### Bubble Composition Helpers

```{r bubble-composition-helpers}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 2 | Diversity, composition and co-occurrence
#   composition: plotting helpers
# ==========================================================================================
bubble_pack_layout <- function(values, canvas = 1.85, padding = 0.04) {
    values <- as.numeric(values)
    if (length(values) == 0) {
        return(tibble::tibble(x0 = numeric(), y0 = numeric(), r = numeric()))
    }

    values[!is.finite(values) | values < 0] <- 0
    if (all(values == 0)) values <- rep(1, length(values))

    ord <- order(values, decreasing = TRUE)
    values <- values[ord]
    radii <- sqrt(values / max(values))

    x <- numeric(length(values))
    y <- numeric(length(values))
    x[1] <- 0
    y[1] <- 0

    if (length(values) > 1) {
        spiral_step <- max(radii) * 0.55 + 0.18
        spiral <- seq(0, 260 * pi, by = 0.12)
        for (i in 2:length(values)) {
            placed <- FALSE
            for (t in spiral) {
                cand <- c(spiral_step * t * cos(t), spiral_step * t * sin(t))
                distances <- sqrt((x[1:(i - 1)] - cand[1])^2 + (y[1:(i - 1)] - cand[2])^2)
                if (all(distances >= radii[1:(i - 1)] + radii[i] + padding)) {
                    x[i] <- cand[1]
                    y[i] <- cand[2]
                    placed <- TRUE
                    break
                }
            }
            if (!placed) {
                angle <- i * 2.399963
                base <- max(sqrt(x[1:(i - 1)]^2 + y[1:(i - 1)]^2), na.rm = TRUE) +
                    radii[i] + padding
                x[i] <- base * cos(angle)
                y[i] <- base * sin(angle)
            }
        }
    }

    xmin <- min(x - radii)
    xmax <- max(x + radii)
    ymin <- min(y - radii)
    ymax <- max(y + radii)
    span <- max(xmax - xmin, ymax - ymin)
    scale_factor <- if (is.finite(span) && span > 0) canvas / span else 1
    center_x <- (xmax + xmin) / 2
    center_y <- (ymax + ymin) / 2

    out <- tibble::tibble(
        x0 = (x - center_x) * scale_factor,
        y0 = (y - center_y) * scale_factor,
        r = radii * scale_factor
    )
    out[order(ord), , drop = FALSE]
}

circle_polygon_df <- function(df, n_points = 72) {
    if (nrow(df) == 0) {
        return(tibble::tibble())
    }

    theta <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n_points)
    df <- df |>
        dplyr::select(x0, y0, r, Developmental_Stage, Taxon, label, text_size)

    purrr::pmap_dfr(df, function(x0, y0, r, Developmental_Stage, Taxon, label, text_size) {
        tibble::tibble(
            x = x0 + r * cos(theta),
            y = y0 + r * sin(theta),
            bubble_id = paste(Developmental_Stage, Taxon, x0, y0, r, sep = "_"),
            Developmental_Stage = Developmental_Stage,
            Taxon = Taxon
        )
    })
}

build_rank_bubble_df <- function(rank_col, top_n = 10) {
    if (!rank_col %in% colnames(taxa_df)) {
        return(tibble::tibble())
    }

    rank_matrix <- aggregate_by_rank(t(counts), taxa_df, rank_col)
    relative_rank <- sweep(rank_matrix, 1, rowSums(rank_matrix), "/")
    relative_rank[is.na(relative_rank)] <- 0

    top_taxa <- colMeans(relative_rank) |>
        sort(decreasing = TRUE) |>
        head(top_n) |>
        names()

    sample_meta <- data.frame(sample_data(ps), stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
    sample_meta$sample_id <- rownames(sample_meta)
    sample_meta <- sample_meta[, intersect(c("sample_id", "Developmental_Stage"), names(sample_meta)), drop = FALSE]

    as.data.frame(relative_rank) |>
        dplyr::mutate(sample_id = rownames(relative_rank)) |>
        tidyr::pivot_longer(
            cols = -sample_id,
            names_to = "Taxon",
            values_to = "RelativeAbundance"
        ) |>
        dplyr::mutate(
            Taxon = dplyr::if_else(is.na(Taxon) | Taxon == "", "Unclassified", Taxon),
            Taxon = dplyr::if_else(Taxon %in% top_taxa, Taxon, "Other")
        ) |>
        dplyr::left_join(sample_meta, by = "sample_id") |>
        dplyr::filter(Developmental_Stage %in% c("Seeds", "Seedlings")) |>
        dplyr::summarise(
            RelativeAbundance = mean(RelativeAbundance, na.rm = TRUE),
            .by = c(Developmental_Stage, Taxon)
        ) |>
        dplyr::group_by(Developmental_Stage) |>
        dplyr::mutate(RelativeAbundance = RelativeAbundance / sum(RelativeAbundance, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
        dplyr::ungroup() |>
        dplyr::mutate(
            Developmental_Stage = factor(Developmental_Stage, levels = c("Seeds", "Seedlings")),
            Taxon = factor(Taxon, levels = c(top_taxa, "Other"))
        )
}

plot_rank_bubble <- function(bubble_df, rank_label, palette, output_file, stage, label_width = 12) {
    if (nrow(bubble_df) == 0) {
        return(list(status = "skipped_no_data"))
    }

    bubble_df <- bubble_df |>
        dplyr::filter(Developmental_Stage == stage)

    if (nrow(bubble_df) == 0) {
        return(list(status = "skipped_no_data"))
    }

    packed_df <- bubble_df |>
        dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(RelativeAbundance), Taxon) |>
        (\(df) dplyr::bind_cols(df, bubble_pack_layout(df$RelativeAbundance)))() |>
        dplyr::mutate(
            label = paste0(
                stringr::str_wrap(as.character(Taxon), width = label_width),
                "\n",
                scales::percent(RelativeAbundance, accuracy = 0.1)
            ),
            text_size = dplyr::case_when(
                r >= 0.48 ~ 4.2,
                r >= 0.33 ~ 3.6,
                r >= 0.22 ~ 3.0,
                TRUE ~ 2.4
            )
        )

    polygon_df <- circle_polygon_df(packed_df)

    p <- ggplot() +
        geom_polygon(
            data = polygon_df,
            aes(x = x, y = y, group = bubble_id, fill = Taxon),
            color = "white",
            linewidth = 0.8,
            alpha = 0.96
        ) +
        geom_text(
            data = packed_df,
            aes(x = x0, y = y0, label = label, size = text_size),
            color = "black",
            lineheight = 0.9,
            fontface = "bold"
        ) +
        scale_size_identity() +
        scale_fill_manual(values = palette, drop = FALSE) +
        coord_equal(xlim = c(-1.05, 1.05), ylim = c(-1.05, 1.05), clip = "off") +
        labs(
            x = NULL,
            y = NULL,
            fill = rank_label,
            title = paste(rank_label, "Composition Bubble Chart by", stage)
        ) +
        theme_void() +
        theme(
            legend.position = "bottom",
            plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
            plot.margin = margin(12, 18, 12, 18)
        )

    save_nature_figure(file.path(figures_dir, output_file), p, kind = "wide")
    readr::write_csv(packed_df, file.path(tables_dir, sub("\\.tiff$", ".csv", output_file)))
    list(status = "completed", plot = p, data = packed_df)
}
```

### Publication-ready Metadata Overview

```{r metadata-overview-publication}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 1 | Data and filtering
#   per-study table of the filtered dataset
# ==========================================================================================
# From tools/make_metadata_overview.R. One row per study with seed/seedling counts and
# per-sample sequencing depth and richness, for the FILTERED dataset (what the analysis
# used); raw-metadata totals go in the footnote. Written as CSV and as a paste-ready
# Markdown table.
overview_ref <- function(x) {
    x <- as.character(x); bad <- !validUTF8(x)
    x[bad] <- iconv(x[bad], from = "macroman", to = "UTF-8")      # metadata is Mac Roman
    s <- stringr::str_replace(x, "^([^_]+).*", "\\1")              # keeps accented surnames
    y <- stringr::str_extract(x, "(19|20)\\d{2}")
    ifelse(is.na(y), s, paste0(s, " et al. ", y))
}
overview_country <- function(x) stringr::str_trim(stringr::str_replace(as.character(x), ":.*$", ""))

ov_md <- as(sample_data(ps), "data.frame")
ov_md$reads <- sample_sums(ps)
ov_md$observed <- phyloseq::estimate_richness(ps, measures = "Observed")$Observed

ov_tab <- ov_md |>
    dplyr::mutate(Reference = overview_ref(Author), Country = overview_country(Geography)) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
        Reference    = paste(sort(unique(Reference)), collapse = "; "),
        Country      = paste(sort(unique(Country)), collapse = "; "),
        n_species    = dplyr::n_distinct(Scientific_Name),
        Species      = paste(sort(unique(Scientific_Name)), collapse = "; "),
        Seeds        = sum(Developmental_Stage == "Seeds"),
        Seedlings    = sum(Developmental_Stage == "Seedlings"),
        Total        = dplyr::n(),
        median_reads = round(median(reads)),
        median_asvs  = round(median(observed)),
        .by = study_alias) |>
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(Total)) |>
    dplyr::rename(Study = study_alias)

ov_tab <- dplyr::bind_rows(ov_tab, tibble::tibble(
    Study = "All studies",
    Reference = sprintf("%d references", dplyr::n_distinct(overview_ref(ov_md$Author))),
    Country = sprintf("%d countries", dplyr::n_distinct(overview_country(ov_md$Geography))),
    n_species = dplyr::n_distinct(ov_md$Scientific_Name), Species = "-",
    Seeds = sum(ov_md$Developmental_Stage == "Seeds"),
    Seedlings = sum(ov_md$Developmental_Stage == "Seedlings"),
    Total = nrow(ov_md),
    median_reads = round(median(ov_md$reads)), median_asvs = round(median(ov_md$observed))))

readr::write_csv(ov_tab, file.path(tables_dir, "metadata_overview_publication.csv"))

ov_fmt <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "d", big.mark = ",")
ov_disp <- ov_tab |>
    dplyr::mutate(Species = ifelse(n_species > 3 & Study != "All studies",
                                   sprintf("%d species", n_species), Species),
                  dplyr::across(c(Seeds, Seedlings, Total, median_reads, median_asvs), ov_fmt)) |>
    dplyr::select(Study, Reference, Country, `Host species` = Species, Seeds, Seedlings,
                  Total, `Median reads` = median_reads, `Median ASVs` = median_asvs)

ov_raw_n <- if (exists("raw_sample_count")) raw_sample_count else NA_integer_
writeLines(c(
    "Table 1. Metadata overview for the compiled seed and seedling microbiome dataset.", "",
    paste0("| ", paste(names(ov_disp), collapse = " | "), " |"),
    paste0("|", paste(rep("---", ncol(ov_disp)), collapse = "|"), "|"),
    apply(ov_disp, 1, \(r) paste0("| ", paste(r, collapse = " | "), " |")), "",
    sprintf(paste("Samples are those retained after quality filtering (n = %s; %s ASVs).",
                  "Median reads and median ASVs are per sample. Sub-national location is",
                  "preserved in the raw metadata but collapsed to country here."),
            ov_fmt(nrow(ov_md)), ov_fmt(ntaxa(ps)))),
    file.path(tables_dir, "metadata_overview_publication.md"))

knitr::kable(ov_disp, caption = "Metadata overview (filtered dataset)")
```

### Taxonomic Composition by Study, Cultivar and Stage

```{r taxa-strips-by-study}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 2 | Diversity, composition and co-occurrence
#   composition: mean relative abundance by study, host species and plant family
# ==========================================================================================
# Replaces the six circle-packing bubble charts (phylum/family/genus x seeds/seedlings).
# One merged figure per rank: every study stacked in a single column, each strip one
# cultivar x stage. Pooling all samples made the composition mostly a description of
# PRJEB45079 (72% of samples); per-study strips show whether a seed-to-seedling shift is
# general or one study's result - and here it is not consistent across studies.
#
# Abundance is the MEAN OF PER-SAMPLE relative abundances, so each sample carries equal
# weight regardless of sequencing depth.
# `row_col` chooses what each strip represents: Cultivar (the default), Plant_Family or
# Scientific_Name. Studies remain the facet in every case, so each variant reads as
# "composition of X, stratified by project".
build_taxa_strips <- function(ps, rank_col, rank_name, threshold, figures_dir, tables_dir,
                              row_col = "Cultivar", row_name = "cultivar") {
    # npg first (goes to the most abundant taxa), then the IGV palette, which is built
    # for many categories - the threshold can expose 50+ genera.
    # the document palette without the two stage colours, which mean seeds and seedlings
    many <- unique(c(FIGURE_PALETTE$categorical, ggsci::pal_igv("default")(51)))
    font <- "Helvetica"

    sd_df <- as(sample_data(ps), "data.frame"); sd_df$sample_id <- rownames(sd_df)
    tax <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    otu <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
    if (!taxa_are_rows(ps)) otu <- t(otu)

    # Zero-count samples have no composition; left in they pull strip means below 100%.
    depth <- colSums(otu)
    otu <- otu[, depth > 0, drop = FALSE]; depth <- depth[depth > 0]
    rel <- sweep(otu, 2, depth, "/")

    rank_of <- tax[[rank_col]]
    rank_of[is.na(rank_of) | rank_of == "" | stringr::str_detect(rank_of, "^unassigned")] <- "Unassigned"
    agg <- rowsum(rel, group = rank_of)

    # Plant family is derived from Scientific_Name through the same family_map used by the
    # composition and beta-diversity figures, so all three agree by construction.
    sd_df$Plant_Family <- if (exists("family_map")) {
        family_map$Family[match(sd_df$Scientific_Name, family_map$Scientific_Name)]
    } else NA_character_

    long <- as.data.frame(as.table(agg), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
        setNames(c("Taxon", "sample_id", "rel")) |>
        dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(sd_df, sample_id, study_alias, Author, Cultivar,
                                       Scientific_Name, Plant_Family, Developmental_Stage),
                         by = "sample_id") |>
        # PRJNA649549 records no cultivar at all; dropping blanks removed the study.
        # Hosts outside family_map land here too rather than vanishing.
        dplyr::mutate(row_val = as.character(.data[[row_col]]),
                      row_val = ifelse(is.na(row_val) | row_val == "", "not reported", row_val))

    # TOP-N RULE: the TOP_TAXA_N taxa by overall mean relative abundance, matching the
    # phylum/genus composition bars so "Other" means the same thing everywhere.
    #
    # This replaced a threshold rule (shown if it reached `threshold` in at least one
    # strip). That rule existed to protect taxa which dominate a single study but are
    # rare overall - Acidobacteriota reaches ~45% in alfalfa seeds yet is not top-15
    # globally, and it now falls into "Other". The trade is deliberate: the threshold
    # exposed 38 families and 51 genera, which is unreadable as a strip. `low_n` and the
    # per-strip CSV still record everything, so nothing is lost from the data, only from
    # the picture. Phylum is unaffected - only 9 phyla clear any sensible cut.
    strip_means <- long |>
        dplyr::summarise(m = mean(rel), .by = c(study_alias, row_val, Developmental_Stage, Taxon))
    keep <- strip_means |>
        dplyr::filter(Taxon != "Unassigned") |>
        dplyr::summarise(mx = max(m), overall = mean(m), .by = Taxon) |>
        dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(overall)) |>
        head(TOP_TAXA_N) |>
        dplyr::pull(Taxon)

    ref_of <- sd_df |>
        dplyr::mutate(ref = {
            a <- as.character(Author); bad <- !validUTF8(a)
            a[bad] <- iconv(a[bad], from = "macroman", to = "UTF-8")   # file is Mac Roman
            s <- stringr::str_replace(a, "^([^_]+).*", "\\1")
            y <- stringr::str_extract(a, "(19|20)\\d{2}")
            ifelse(is.na(y), s, paste0(s, " et al. ", y))
        }) |>
        dplyr::summarise(ref = paste(sort(unique(ref)), collapse = "; "), .by = study_alias) |>
        # Facet labels carry the reference only - the BioProject accession is metadata a
        # reader does not need on the figure. Chandel et al. 2022 contributed two
        # projects, so a reference shared by more than one study gets a/b suffixes;
        # without that the two would silently collapse into a single facet.
        dplyr::arrange(ref, study_alias) |>
        dplyr::mutate(n_ref = dplyr::n(), idx = seq_len(dplyr::n()), .by = ref) |>
        dplyr::mutate(study_lab = ifelse(n_ref > 1, paste0(ref, letters[idx]), ref)) |>
        dplyr::select(study_alias, ref, study_lab)

    grp <- long |>
        # Unassigned reads are unknown, not rare - keep them as their own category
        # rather than inflating "Other".
        dplyr::mutate(Taxon = dplyr::case_when(Taxon %in% keep ~ Taxon,
                                               Taxon == "Unassigned" ~ "Unassigned",
                                               .default = "Other")) |>
        dplyr::summarise(rel = sum(rel), .by = c(sample_id, study_alias, row_val,
                                                 Developmental_Stage, Taxon)) |>
        dplyr::summarise(rel = mean(rel), n = dplyr::n_distinct(sample_id),
                         .by = c(study_alias, row_val, Developmental_Stage, Taxon)) |>
        dplyr::mutate(
            Taxon = factor(Taxon, levels = c(keep, "Other", "Unassigned")),
            # Full stage words: truncating to 4 characters made "Seeds" and "Seedlings"
            # identical, collapsing both stages onto one row at 200%.
            Stage = factor(ifelse(Developmental_Stage == "Seeds", "Seed", "Seedling"),
                           levels = c("Seed", "Seedling")),
            # row_key keeps cultivar AND stage so the two stages stay on separate rows;
            # row_lab is what is printed - the stage is shown by shape, not text.
            # Must include the study: "undefined|Seedling" occurs in three studies, and a
            # study-less key made them share one label, printing the wrong n on each.
            row_key = paste(study_alias, row_val, Stage, sep = "|"),
            row_lab = sprintf("%s (n=%d)%s", row_val, n, ifelse(n < 3, " *", ""))) |>
        dplyr::left_join(ref_of, by = "study_alias")

    totals <- grp |> dplyr::summarise(tot = sum(rel), .by = c(study_alias, row_key))
    if (any(abs(totals$tot - 1) > 0.02)) {
        stop("taxa strips: a strip does not sum to 100% - duplicate row labels?")
    }

    study_order <- grp |>
        dplyr::distinct(study_lab, row_lab, n) |>
        dplyr::summarise(n = sum(n), .by = study_lab) |>
        dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n)) |> dplyr::pull(study_lab)
    grp$study_lab <- factor(grp$study_lab, levels = study_order)

    pal <- setNames(rep(many, length.out = length(keep)), keep)
    pal[["Other"]] <- "#9E9E9E"
    pal[["Unassigned"]] <- "#DDDDDD"
    # Genus names include long SILVA group labels (e.g. Burkholderia-Caballeronia-
    # Paraburkholderia) that clipped at 4+ legend columns.
    legend_cols <- c(phylum = 5, class = 4, family = 4, genus = 3)[[rank_name]]
    n_legend_rows <- ceiling((length(keep) + 2) / legend_cols)
    n_strips <- dplyr::n_distinct(paste(grp$study_alias, grp$row_key))

    # Cultivar then stage, so each cultivar's seed and seedling strips sit together.
    key_levels <- grp |> dplyr::distinct(row_key, row_val, Stage) |>
        dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(row_val), dplyr::desc(Stage)) |> dplyr::pull(row_key)
    grp$row_key <- factor(grp$row_key, levels = unique(key_levels))
    lab_map <- grp |> dplyr::distinct(row_key, row_lab)
    lab_map <- setNames(lab_map$row_lab, as.character(lab_map$row_key))
    markers <- grp |> dplyr::distinct(study_lab, row_key, Stage)

    p <- ggplot(grp, aes(x = rel, y = row_key, fill = Taxon)) +
        geom_col(width = 0.78, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2,
                 position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
        # Stage marker just left of each strip: circle = seed, triangle = seedling.
        geom_point(data = markers, aes(x = -0.022, y = row_key, shape = Stage),
                   inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 2.3, colour = "grey10") +
        scale_shape_manual(values = c(Seed = 16, Seedling = 17), name = NULL) +
        scale_y_discrete(labels = function(k) lab_map[k]) +
        coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
        facet_grid(rows = vars(study_lab), scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
        scale_fill_manual(values = pal, name = NULL) +
        scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
                           expand = expansion(mult = c(0.04, 0.01)), position = "top") +
        labs(x = "Mean relative abundance", y = NULL) +
        guides(shape = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(size = 3.2)),
               fill = guide_legend(order = 2, ncol = legend_cols, byrow = TRUE,
                                   keywidth = unit(11, "pt"), keyheight = unit(11, "pt"))) +
        theme_classic(base_size = 11, base_family = font) +
        theme(strip.placement = "outside",
              strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", colour = NA),
              strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0, face = "bold", size = 9.5,
                                               family = font, margin = margin(2, 6, 2, 6)),
              axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8.5, colour = "grey10"),
              axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9.5, colour = "grey30"),
              axis.title.x = element_text(size = 10.5, colour = "grey20"),
              axis.line.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
              panel.spacing.y = unit(4, "pt"),
              legend.position = "bottom",
              legend.box = "vertical",
              legend.text = element_text(size = 9.5, colour = "grey15"),
              plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA))

    tag <- if (identical(row_col, "Cultivar")) "" else paste0("_by_", row_name)
    out <- file.path(figures_dir, sprintf("fig_taxa_strips_%s%s.tiff", rank_name, tag))
    ggsave(out, p, width = 12, height = 2.2 + 0.24 * n_strips + 0.2 * n_legend_rows, dpi = 300,
           compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
    readr::write_csv(dplyr::select(grp, study_alias, ref, row_val, Stage,
                                   n, Taxon, rel),
                     file.path(tables_dir, sprintf("taxa_strips_%s%s.csv", rank_name, tag)))
    print(p)
    list(status = "completed", file = out, strips = n_strips, taxa = length(keep),
         low_n = sum(dplyr::distinct(grp, study_alias, row_key, n)$n < 3))
}

strip_threshold <- get_config_value(c("taxonomy_analysis", "strip_other_threshold"), 0.03)
taxa_strip_results <- list(
    # Default: one strip per cultivar, faceted by study.
    # class, where the coarsest rank shown used to be phylum
    class  = build_taxa_strips(ps, "Class",  "class",  strip_threshold, figures_dir, tables_dir),
    family = build_taxa_strips(ps, "Family", "family", strip_threshold, figures_dir, tables_dir),
    genus  = build_taxa_strips(ps, "Genus",  "genus",  strip_threshold, figures_dir, tables_dir),

    # Same composition stratified by host instead of cultivar, study still the facet.
    # Cultivar is study-specific, so those strips cannot be compared across projects;
    # plant family and host species are shared vocabularies and can be.
    # NOTE ON NAMING: the first token is the BACTERIAL rank, the token after "_by_" is the
    # HOST grouping. So fig_taxa_strips_family_by_plant_family.tiff is bacterial family
    # composition per plant family - the two "family"s mean different things, and the
    # captions say so explicitly.
    class_plant_family  = build_taxa_strips(ps, "Class", "class", strip_threshold,
                                            figures_dir, tables_dir,
                                            "Plant_Family", "plant_family"),
    family_plant_family = build_taxa_strips(ps, "Family", "family", strip_threshold,
                                            figures_dir, tables_dir,
                                            "Plant_Family", "plant_family"),
    genus_plant_family  = build_taxa_strips(ps, "Genus", "genus", strip_threshold,
                                            figures_dir, tables_dir,
                                            "Plant_Family", "plant_family"),
    class_host_species  = build_taxa_strips(ps, "Class", "class", strip_threshold,
                                            figures_dir, tables_dir,
                                            "Scientific_Name", "host_species"),
    family_host_species = build_taxa_strips(ps, "Family", "family", strip_threshold,
                                            figures_dir, tables_dir,
                                            "Scientific_Name", "host_species"),
    genus_host_species  = build_taxa_strips(ps, "Genus", "genus", strip_threshold,
                                            figures_dir, tables_dir,
                                            "Scientific_Name", "host_species")
)
for (nm in names(taxa_strip_results)) {
    r <- taxa_strip_results[[nm]]
    cat(sprintf("  taxa strips %-7s %s | %d taxa (top %d by overall abundance) | %d strips (%d with n < 3)\n",
                nm, r$status, r$taxa, TOP_TAXA_N, r$strips, r$low_n))
}

# Register the strip figures' legends alongside Figure 1 and rewrite the legends file,
# so figure_legends.md always matches what this render produced.
if (exists("write_figure_legends")) {
    if (!exists("FIGURE_LEGENDS")) FIGURE_LEGENDS <- list()
    ts <- taxa_strip_results
    FIGURE_LEGENDS[["Figure 2"]] <- list(
        file = sprintf("figures/fig_taxa_strips_%s.tiff", c("class", "family", "genus")),
        title = paste("Taxonomic composition of seed and seedling microbiota by study,",
                      "cultivar and developmental stage."),
        panels = c(
            a = sprintf("Class level (%d classes shown).", ts$class$taxa),
            b = sprintf("Family level (%d families shown).", ts$family$taxa),
            c = sprintf("Genus level (%d genera shown).", ts$genus$taxa)),
        footer = paste(
            "Each horizontal bar is one cultivar at one developmental stage within a study;",
            "studies are grouped in rows labelled by BioProject and reference, ordered by",
            "number of samples. Bar segments give the mean of per-sample relative abundances,",
            "so every sample carries equal weight. Circles mark seed and triangles seedling",
            "samples; n is the number of samples and * marks bars based on fewer than three.",
            sprintf("The %d most abundant taxa overall; everything else pooled as Other",
                    TOP_TAXA_N),
            "are shown individually; all others are pooled as Other, and reads without an",
            "assignment at that rank are shown as Unassigned. Samples with no reads after",
            "filtering are excluded. Panels a-c are supplied as separate files.")
    )
    write_figure_legends(FIGURE_LEGENDS, file.path(tables_dir, "figure_legends.md"))
    cat("  Figure legends updated with Figure 2 (taxonomic strips)\n")
}
```

## Core Microbiome Analysis

```{r core-microbiome}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS - | NOT IN THE METHODOLOGY TEXT
#   core microbiome
# ==========================================================================================
compute_core_microbiome <- function(ps, detection = 0.1, prevalence = 0.75,
                                     group_col = NULL, output_dir, tables_dir) {
    tryCatch({
        # ── 1. Global core taxa (all samples) ──────────────────────────────
        bac_core <- microbiome::core(ps,
                                     detection = detection,
                                     prevalence = prevalence,
                                     include.lowest = FALSE)
        bac_ctaxa <- taxa_names(bac_core)

        cat("\n=== Core Microbiome (All Samples) ===\n")
        cat("Core taxa (detection =", detection, ", prevalence =", prevalence, "):",
            length(bac_ctaxa), "\n")

        # ── 2. Per-sample prevalence & mean relative abundance ─────────────
        meta_df <- microbiome::meta(ps)
        asv <- otu_table(ps)
        taxo <- tibble::rownames_to_column(as.data.frame(tax_table(ps)), "ASV")

        # Presence-absence
        asv_pa <- 1 * ((asv > 0) == 1)

        # Occupancy (prevalence as fraction)
        asv_prev <- rowSums(asv_pa) / ncol(asv_pa)

        # Mean relative abundance (proportion)
        asv_rel <- apply(vegan::decostand(asv, method = "total", MARGIN = 2), 1, mean)

        # Combine into table
        asv_prev_rel <- tibble::rownames_to_column(
            as.data.frame(cbind(asv_prev, asv_rel)), "ASV")
        colnames(asv_prev_rel)[2:3] <- c("prevalence", "mean_rel_abundance")

        # Merge with taxonomy
        asv_prev_rel_taxo <- merge(taxo, asv_prev_rel, by = "ASV")

        # Classify: Core vs Flexible
        asv_prev_rel_taxo <- asv_prev_rel_taxo |>
            dplyr::mutate(
                classification = ifelse(ASV %in% bac_ctaxa, "Core", "Flexible")
            )

        # ── 3. Per-group core taxa (if grouping variable provided) ─────────
        group_core_list <- list()
        if (!is.null(group_col) && group_col %in% colnames(sample_data(ps))) {
            categories <- unique(na.omit(sample_data(ps)[[group_col]]))
            categories <- categories[nchar(categories) > 0]

            for (item in categories) {
                cat("  Identifying core taxa for", item, "...\n")
                bh.subset <- subset_samples(ps, get(group_col) == item)
                bh.subset <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(bh.subset) > 0, bh.subset)

                if (nsamples(bh.subset) >= 3) {
                    subset.core <- microbiome::core_members(bh.subset,
                                                            detection = detection,
                                                            prevalence = prevalence,
                                                            include.lowest = TRUE)
                    group_core_list[[item]] <- subset.core
                    cat("    No. of core taxa in", item, ":", length(subset.core), "\n")
                }
            }
        }

        # ── 4. Save full core microbiome table ─────────────────────────────
        # Convert percentages for output
        asv_prev_rel_taxo_out <- asv_prev_rel_taxo |>
            dplyr::mutate(
                prevalence_pct = prevalence * 100,
                mean_rel_abundance_pct = mean_rel_abundance * 100
            ) |>
            dplyr::arrange(desc(prevalence), desc(mean_rel_abundance))

        write.csv(asv_prev_rel_taxo_out,
                  file.path(tables_dir, "core_microbiome.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

        # ── 5. Scatter plot: Prevalence vs Relative Abundance (Fig 4B Style) ──────
        color_core <- c("Core" = FIGURE_PALETTE$categorical[6], "Flexible" = FIGURE_PALETTE$categorical[2])

        # Count taxa per category
        counts_df <- asv_prev_rel_taxo |>
            dplyr::count(classification, name = "n_taxa")

        # Core taxa labels for repelling
        core_for_label <- asv_prev_rel_taxo |>
            dplyr::filter(classification == "Core")

        p_scatter <- ggplot(asv_prev_rel_taxo,
                            aes(x = mean_rel_abundance, y = prevalence * 100)) +
            geom_point(aes(color = classification), size = 2, alpha = 0.95) +
            geom_text_repel(
                data = core_for_label,
                aes(label = ASV, color = classification),
                size = 2.5, max.overlaps = 30, show.legend = FALSE
            ) +
            geom_text(
                data = counts_df |> dplyr::filter(classification == "Core"),
                aes(x = 1e-4, y = 10, label = paste0("Core Taxa: ", n_taxa), fontface = "bold"),
                size = 3.5, inherit.aes = FALSE
            ) +
            # Abundance-Occupancy Relationship thresholds
            geom_hline(yintercept = prevalence * 100, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
            geom_vline(xintercept = detection, linetype = "dotted", color = "black") +
            scale_x_log10(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 0.001)) +
            scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 101)) +
            scale_color_manual(values = color_core) +
            labs(
                x = "Mean Relative Abundance [%] (log-scale)",
                y = "Occupancy / Prevalence [%]",
                color = "Core Classification",
                title = "Abundance-Occupancy Plot"
            ) +
            theme_pipeline_occupancy() +
            theme(legend.position = "right")

        save_nature_figure(file.path(output_dir, "core_microbiome_abundance_occupancy.tiff"),
                           p_scatter, kind = "standard")

        # ── 6. Stacked bar: Core vs Flexible proportion ────────────────────
        df_bar <- asv_prev_rel_taxo |>
            dplyr::group_by(classification) |>
            dplyr::summarise(
                n_taxa = dplyr::n(),
                rel_ab = sum(mean_rel_abundance * 100),
                .groups = "drop"
            ) |>
            dplyr::mutate(
                classification = factor(classification, levels = c("Flexible", "Core"))
            )

        color_bar <- c("Core" = FIGURE_PALETTE$categorical[6], "Flexible" = FIGURE_PALETTE$categorical[2])

        p_bar <- ggplot(df_bar,
                        aes(x = "", y = rel_ab, fill = classification)) +
            geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack", width = 0.25) +
            geom_text(
                aes(label = n_taxa, fontface = "bold", colour = classification),
                position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 4
            ) +
            scale_fill_manual(values = color_bar) +
            scale_color_manual(values = c("Core" = "white", "Flexible" = "white")) +
            coord_flip() +
            labs(
                x = NULL,
                y = "Total Relative Abundance [%]",
                fill = "",
                title = "Core vs Flexible Taxa"
            ) +
            theme_pipeline_classic() +
            theme(
                axis.text.y = element_blank(),
                axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
                legend.position = "bottom"
            )

        save_nature_figure(file.path(output_dir, "core_microbiome_bar.tiff"),
                           p_bar, kind = "compact")

        # ── 7. Per-group core scatter plots (if grouping variable) ─────────
        if (length(group_core_list) > 0) {
            for (grp_name in names(group_core_list)) {
                grp_ctaxa <- group_core_list[[grp_name]]
                grp_df <- asv_prev_rel_taxo |>
                    dplyr::mutate(
                        grp_core = ifelse(ASV %in% grp_ctaxa, "Core", "Flexible"),
                        grp_core = factor(grp_core, levels = c("Flexible", "Core"))
                    )

                grp_counts <- grp_df |> dplyr::count(grp_core, name = "n_taxa")
                grp_core_label <- grp_df |> dplyr::filter(grp_core == "Core")

                p_grp <- ggplot(grp_df,
                                aes(x = mean_rel_abundance * 100, y = prevalence * 100)) +
                    geom_point(aes(color = grp_core), size = 2, alpha = 0.95) +
                    geom_text_repel(
                        data = grp_core_label,
                        aes(label = ASV, color = grp_core),
                        size = 2.5, max.overlaps = 20, show.legend = FALSE
                    ) +
                    geom_hline(yintercept = prevalence * 100, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
                    geom_vline(xintercept = detection, linetype = "dotted", color = "black") +
                    scale_x_log10(breaks = c(10, 1, 0.1, 0.01, 0.001),
                                  labels = c(10, 1, 0.1, 0.01, 0.001)) +
                    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 101)) +
                    scale_color_manual(values = color_core) +
                    labs(
                        x = "Relative abundance [%]",
                        y = "Prevalence [%]",
                        color = "",
                        title = paste0(grp_name, " (n = ", length(grp_ctaxa), " core taxa)")
                    ) +
                    theme_pipeline_occupancy() +
                    theme(legend.position = "none")

                ggsave(file.path(output_dir, paste0("core_microbiome_",
                                                     make.names(grp_name), ".tiff")),
                       p_grp, width = 6, height = 5, dpi = 300)
            }
        }

        # ── 8. Summary table of core taxa ──────────────────────────────────
        core_summary <- asv_prev_rel_taxo_out |>
            dplyr::filter(classification == "Core") |>
            dplyr::arrange(desc(prevalence_pct), desc(mean_rel_abundance_pct))

        if (nrow(core_summary) > 0) {
            readr::write_csv(core_summary,
                             file.path(tables_dir, "core_taxa_list.csv"))
            knitr::kable(head(core_summary, 20),
                         caption = paste0("Core Taxa (Top 20 of ", nrow(core_summary), ")"))
        }

        list(status = "completed", n_core = length(bac_ctaxa),
             n_groups = length(group_core_list))
    }, error = function(e) {
        message("Core microbiome error: ", conditionMessage(e))
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

cat("Computing core microbiome (seed microbiome meta-analysis abundance-occupancy approach)...\n")
# Use thresholds from analysis_config.json (seed microbiome meta-analysis uses 50% prevalence, 0.1% abundance)
core_prev <- config$taxonomy_analysis$core_prevalence_threshold
if (is.null(core_prev)) core_prev <- 0.5

core_det <- config$taxonomy_analysis$core_abundance_threshold
if (is.null(core_det)) core_det <- 0.001

core_result <- compute_core_microbiome(ps, detection = core_det, prevalence = core_prev,
                                        group_col = group_col,
                                        output_dir = figures_dir, tables_dir = tables_dir)
cat("  Core microbiome:", core_result$status, "\n")
if (core_result$status == "completed") {
    cat("  Core taxa:", core_result$n_core, "\n")
    cat("  Group-level analyses:", core_result$n_groups, "\n")
}
```

## Indicator Species Analysis

```{r indicator-species}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 3 | Taxon-stage associations
#   step 1 of 2: indicator analysis (IndVal.g, 999 permutations)
# ==========================================================================================
perform_indicator_species <- function(ps, group_col, output_dir, tables_dir) {
    if (is.null(group_col) || !(group_col %in% colnames(sample_data(ps)))) {
        cat("Indicator species: skipped — no grouping variable\n")
        return(list(status = "skipped_no_group"))
    }

    tryCatch({
        meta_df <- as.data.frame(sample_data(ps))
        keep <- !is.na(meta_df[[group_col]])
        ps_sub <- prune_samples(keep, ps)
        meta_sub <- meta_df[keep, , drop = FALSE]

        otu <- as(otu_table(ps_sub), "matrix")
        if (taxa_are_rows(ps_sub)) otu <- t(otu)

        # Convert to relative abundance for indicator analysis
        rel_abund <- sweep(otu, 1, rowSums(otu), "/")
        rel_abund[is.na(rel_abund)] <- 0

        # Multipatt: indicator value analysis
        set.seed(123)
        indval_result <- indicspecies::multipatt(
            rel_abund,
            meta_sub[[group_col]],
            func = "IndVal.g",
            control = how(nperm = 999)
        )

        # Extract significant indicators (p < 0.05) via $sign slot
        indval_summary <- as.data.frame(indval_result$sign)
        sig_indicators <- indval_summary[which(!is.na(indval_summary$p.value) & indval_summary$p.value < 0.05), ]
        # Derive a single group label: the group combination with indicator value = 1
        group_cols <- grep("^s\\.", colnames(sig_indicators), value = TRUE)
        if (length(group_cols) > 0) {
            sig_indicators$group <- apply(sig_indicators[, group_cols, drop = FALSE], 1,
                                          function(x) paste(sub("^s\\.", "", group_cols[x == 1]), collapse = "+"))
        } else {
            sig_indicators$group <- "unknown"
        }
        sig_indicators$stat <- indval_result$sign[rownames(sig_indicators), "stat"]

        cat("\n=== Indicator Species Results ===\n")
        cat("Total significant indicators (p < 0.05):", nrow(sig_indicators), "\n")

        if (nrow(sig_indicators) > 0) {
            # Add taxonomy information
            tax_df <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps_sub), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
            sig_indicators$taxon_id <- rownames(sig_indicators)

            if ("Genus" %in% colnames(tax_df)) {
                sig_indicators$genus <- tax_df[sig_indicators$taxon_id, "Genus"]
                sig_indicators$genus[is.na(sig_indicators$genus) | sig_indicators$genus == ""] <-
                    sig_indicators$taxon_id
            } else {
                sig_indicators$genus <- sig_indicators$taxon_id
            }

            # Save full results
            write.csv(sig_indicators,
                      file.path(tables_dir, "indicator_species_significant.csv"),
                      row.names = FALSE)

            # Plot top indicators
            top_n <- min(20, nrow(sig_indicators))
            top_ind <- sig_indicators[order(sig_indicators$stat, decreasing = TRUE)[1:top_n], ]

            p <- ggplot(top_ind,
                        aes(x = reorder(genus, stat), y = stat, fill = group)) +
                geom_col() +
                coord_flip() +
                scale_fill_manual(values = get_palette(length(unique(top_ind$group)),
                                                       "wildagain", "alpha_diversity")) +
                labs(
                    x = "Indicator Taxon",
                    y = "Indicator Value (IndVal.g)",
                    fill = "Group",
                    title = paste0("Top ", top_n, " Indicator Species")
                ) +
                theme_pipeline_classic() +
                theme(legend.position = "bottom")

            save_nature_figure(file.path(output_dir, "indicator_species_plot.tiff"),
                               p, kind = "standard")

            # Also run phi coefficient analysis
            set.seed(123)
            phi_result <- indicspecies::multipatt(
                rel_abund,
                meta_sub[[group_col]],
                func = "r.g",
                control = how(nperm = 999)
            )
            phi_summary <- as.data.frame(phi_result$sign)
            sig_phi <- phi_summary[which(!is.na(phi_summary$p.value) & phi_summary$p.value < 0.05), ]

            if (nrow(sig_phi) > 0) {
                write.csv(sig_phi,
                          file.path(tables_dir, "indicator_species_phi.csv"),
                          row.names = FALSE)
                cat("Significant phi indicators:", nrow(sig_phi), "\n")
            }
        }

        list(status = "completed", n_indicators = nrow(sig_indicators))
    }, error = function(e) {
        message("Indicator species error: ", conditionMessage(e))
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

cat("Running indicator species analysis...\n")
if (!is.null(group_col)) {
    indicator_result <- perform_indicator_species(ps, group_col, figures_dir, tables_dir)
    cat("  Indicator species:", indicator_result$status, "\n")
    if (indicator_result$status == "completed") {
        cat("  Significant indicators:", indicator_result$n_indicators, "\n")
    }
}
```

```{r generalist-specialist}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 5, 6, 7 | see the parts marked below
#   CLAM (5), two-step host screen (6), Fisher tests and breadth vs abundance (7)
# ==========================================================================================
# Generalist / specialist classification of genera, two ways, written to
# tables/generalist_specialist_genus.csv for the dendrogram in Part 2.
#
# Genus level, not ASV: 98.8% of ASVs occur in a single study, so an ASV's "specialism"
# would only say which study it came from.
#
# 1. Stage (seeds vs seedlings): the multinomial species classification method, CLAM
#    (Chazdon et al. 2011, Ecology 92:1332), vegan::clamtest(). Run on the studies that
#    sampled both stages only - pooled over all studies, every genus seen in a
#    seedling-only study is called a seedling specialist because nobody sequenced the
#    seeds. It is run again within each of those studies, and the table records in how
#    many the genus got the same class, because one study holds most of the samples.
# 2. Host breadth: Levins' niche breadth B = 1 / sum(p^2) across host plant species,
#    against a null that reshuffles the table keeping its row sums, column sums and
#    number of zeros (quasiswap; the EcolUtils::spec.gen approach). B above the null
#    interval is a host generalist, below it a host specialist. Each host is first
#    reduced to one average sample of `host_breadth_depth` reads (mean relative abundance
#    x depth, rounded), so a host with 700 samples weighs the same as one with 4.
#
# 3. Host breadth by presence/absence, in two screens (16S only; there is no ITS here).
#    Each taxon is present or absent on each host species. Screen one finds how many hosts
#    make a taxon broad: a null that redraws each host's taxa at random, keeping the
#    host's own richness, gives the expected number of taxa at every breadth k, and the
#    threshold is the smallest k above the expected breadth at which more taxa are
#    observed than the null mean. Screen two removes "pseudo-generalists", broad taxa
#    whose hosts are all close relatives: the mean pairwise phylogenetic distance (MPD)
#    of a taxon's hosts is compared with that of every possible set of k hosts. With 16
#    hosts all such sets can be listed (12,870 at most), so the one-sided p-values for
#    clustering and for dispersion are exact, each Benjamini-Hochberg corrected. It was
#    first done with 1,000 random draws, whose smallest possible p (0.001) could not
#    survive correction over 1,700 taxa, so that nothing was ever called clustered. A
#    z-score against the same null is kept, with its normal-theory q (`q_clustered_z`),
#    for comparison: the null is skewed, and that approximation calls far more taxa. Generalist = at or above the threshold and not significantly clustered;
#    specialist = one host; intermediate = the rest. Done for genera (added to the genus
#    table) and for ASVs (a table of their own).
#
# Limits, for the methods text: CLAM and the null both treat reads as individuals, which
# overstates significance; and host is largely tied to study, which neither removes.

# METHODS 6 | host tree, one tip per species
#' The host tree with one tip per species, named with spaces. TimeTree returns subspecies
#' and varieties as tips of their own; host_phylosignal.R reduces it the same way.
read_host_species_tree <- function(path) {
    tree <- if (grepl("\\.(nexus|nex)$", path, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
        ape::read.nexus(path)
    } else ape::read.tree(path)
    tips <- gsub("_", " ", gsub("'", "", tree$tip.label))
    species <- sub("^(\\S+ \\S+).*$", "\\1", tips)
    for (sp in unique(species)) {
        if (sum(species == sp) > 1 && !ape::is.monophyletic(tree, tree$tip.label[species == sp])) {
            stop("tips of ", sp, " do not form a clade in the host tree")
        }
    }
    tree <- ape::keep.tip(tree, tree$tip.label[!duplicated(species)])
    tree$tip.label <- species[!duplicated(species)]
    tree
}

# METHODS 6 | breadth null (screen 1) and host-relatedness null (screen 2)
#' The two screens. `present`: taxon x host logical matrix. `host_distance`: host x host
#' divergence times. Returns the per-taxon table, the breadth null and the threshold.
host_double_screen <- function(present, host_distance, n_iter, fdr) {
    present <- present[rowSums(present) > 0, , drop = FALSE]
    n_taxa <- nrow(present)
    n_host <- ncol(present)
    n_hosts <- rowSums(present)
    richness <- colSums(present)

    # screen one: how many taxa would sit at each breadth if hosts drew taxa at random
    null_counts <- replicate(n_iter, {
        drawn <- unlist(lapply(richness, function(t) sample.int(n_taxa, t)))
        tabulate(tabulate(drawn, nbins = n_taxa), nbins = n_host)
    })
    # counted before the table is built: inside tibble() `n_hosts` would be the new column
    observed_counts <- tabulate(n_hosts, nbins = n_host)
    breadth <- tibble::tibble(n_hosts = seq_len(n_host),
                              observed = observed_counts,
                              null_mean = rowMeans(null_counts),
                              null_lower = apply(null_counts, 1, stats::quantile, 0.025),
                              null_upper = apply(null_counts, 1, stats::quantile, 0.975))
    expected_breadth <- sum(richness) / n_taxa
    broad <- breadth$n_hosts > expected_breadth & breadth$observed > breadth$null_mean
    threshold <- if (any(broad)) min(breadth$n_hosts[broad]) else NA_integer_

    # screen two: are a taxon's hosts closer relatives than k hosts would be by chance?
    # Every set of k hosts is listed where that is feasible, which makes the test exact;
    # with more hosts than that allows, k hosts are drawn at random n_iter times.
    host_distance <- host_distance[colnames(present), colnames(present)]
    mpd <- function(i) mean(host_distance[i, i][lower.tri(diag(length(i)))])
    max_listed <- 1e5
    null_mpd <- lapply(seq_len(n_host), function(k) {
        if (k < 2) return(NA_real_)
        if (choose(n_host, k) <= max_listed) return(utils::combn(n_host, k, FUN = mpd))
        replicate(n_iter, mpd(sample.int(n_host, k)))
    })
    taxa <- purrr::map(seq_len(n_taxa), function(i) {
        k <- n_hosts[[i]]
        if (k < 2) return(tibble::tibble(host_mpd_my = NA_real_, host_mpd_z = NA_real_,
                                         p_clustered = NA_real_, p_dispersed = NA_real_))
        observed <- mpd(which(present[i, ]))
        null <- null_mpd[[k]]
        # the listed null contains the taxon's own host set, so p is never zero; a drawn
        # null does not, hence the +1. The tolerance guards equal MPDs against rounding.
        drawn <- choose(n_host, k) > max_listed
        tail_p <- function(hits) (sum(hits) + drawn) / (length(null) + drawn)
        tibble::tibble(host_mpd_my = observed,
                       host_mpd_z = if (stats::sd(null) > 0) {
                           (observed - mean(null)) / stats::sd(null)
                       } else NA_real_,
                       p_clustered = tail_p(null <= observed + 1e-9),
                       p_dispersed = tail_p(null >= observed - 1e-9))
    }) |> purrr::list_rbind() |>
        dplyr::mutate(taxon = rownames(present), n_hosts = unname(n_hosts),
                      q_clustered = stats::p.adjust(p_clustered, method = "BH"),
                      q_dispersed = stats::p.adjust(p_dispersed, method = "BH"),
                      q_clustered_z = stats::p.adjust(stats::pnorm(host_mpd_z), method = "BH"),
                      pseudo_generalist = !is.na(threshold) & n_hosts >= threshold &
                          dplyr::coalesce(q_clustered < fdr, FALSE),
                      screen_class = dplyr::case_when(
                          n_hosts == 1 ~ "Specialist",
                          !is.na(threshold) & n_hosts >= threshold & !pseudo_generalist ~ "Generalist",
                          TRUE ~ "Intermediate")) |>
        dplyr::select(taxon, n_hosts, host_mpd_my, host_mpd_z, q_clustered, q_dispersed,
                      q_clustered_z, pseudo_generalist, screen_class)
    list(taxa = taxa, breadth = breadth, threshold = threshold,
         expected_breadth = expected_breadth)
}

# METHODS 7 | Fisher's exact tests by rank, top genera, breadth vs abundance
#' How host generalist and host specialist ASVs differ in composition. `asv`: the per-ASV
#' table of host_double_screen(); `otu`: ASV x sample counts; `tax`: taxonomy matrix;
#' `host`: host species of each sample. Three tables:
#'   tests             - per rank and taxon, Fisher's exact test of generalist against
#'                       specialist ASVs inside and outside the taxon, BH-corrected within
#'                       rank; `exclusive_to` marks taxa found in one group only
#'   top_genera        - genera ranked by host breadth (host species, then host genera),
#'                       with their mean relative abundance
#'   breadth_abundance - within the phyla richest in ASVs, does an ASV found on more hosts
#'                       reach a higher abundance where it occurs? Linear regression of
#'                       log10 abundance on breadth, and a one-sided Spearman correlation
generalist_specialist_composition <- function(asv, otu, tax, host, top_genera, major_phyla) {
    blank <- function(x) is.na(x) | x == "" |
        grepl("^(Unassigned|unidentified|uncultured|metagenome)$", x, ignore.case = TRUE)
    groups <- c("Generalist", "Specialist")
    cls <- dplyr::filter(asv, screen_class %in% groups)
    totals <- table(factor(cls$screen_class, levels = groups))

    ranks <- c(Phylum = "Phyla", Class = "Class", Order = "Order", Family = "Family",
               Genus = "Genus")
    tests <- purrr::imap(ranks, function(column, rank) {
        taxon <- unname(tax[cls$taxon, column])
        taxon[blank(taxon)] <- "Unassigned"
        counts <- table(taxon, factor(cls$screen_class, levels = groups))
        purrr::map(rownames(counts), function(tx) {
            inside <- counts[tx, ]
            test <- stats::fisher.test(rbind(inside, totals - inside))
            tibble::tibble(rank = rank, taxon = tx, generalists = inside[["Generalist"]],
                           specialists = inside[["Specialist"]],
                           odds_ratio = unname(test$estimate), p = test$p.value)
        }) |> purrr::list_rbind() |>
            dplyr::mutate(q = stats::p.adjust(p, method = "BH"),
                          exclusive_to = dplyr::case_when(specialists == 0 ~ "Generalists",
                                                          generalists == 0 ~ "Specialists",
                                                          TRUE ~ "")) |>
            dplyr::arrange(q, p)
    }) |> purrr::list_rbind()

    # mean of per-sample relative abundances, as in the composition figures
    rel <- sweep(otu, 2, pmax(colSums(otu), 1), "/")
    genus <- tax[rownames(otu), "Genus"]
    named <- !blank(genus)
    genus_counts <- rowsum(otu[named, , drop = FALSE], genus[named])
    found_on <- function(groups) rowSums(sapply(split(seq_len(ncol(otu)), groups), function(i) {
        rowSums(genus_counts[, i, drop = FALSE]) > 0
    }))
    top <- tibble::tibble(
        Genus = rownames(genus_counts),
        Phylum = as.character(tapply(tax[rownames(otu), "Phyla"][named], genus[named],
                                     function(x) names(sort(table(x), decreasing = TRUE))[1])[Genus]),
        n_asvs = as.integer(table(genus[named])[Genus]),
        n_hosts = unname(found_on(host)),
        n_hostg = unname(found_on(sub(" .*$", "", host))),
        # over the samples with reads: a sample emptied by the feature filter has no
        # composition, and counted as zero it lowered every mean (as in chunk `top-phyla`)
        mean_relative_abundance_pct =
            100 * unname(rowMeans(rowsum(rel[named, colSums(otu) > 0, drop = FALSE], genus[named])))) |>
        dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n_hosts), dplyr::desc(n_hostg),
                       dplyr::desc(mean_relative_abundance_pct)) |>
        dplyr::mutate(rank = dplyr::row_number(), .before = 1) |>
        dplyr::slice_head(n = top_genera)

    # abundance where present: the mean over the samples in which the ASV was detected
    per_asv <- tibble::tibble(taxon = rownames(otu), Phylum = unname(tax[rownames(otu), "Phyla"]),
                              nonzero = rowSums(rel) / pmax(rowSums(otu > 0), 1)) |>
        dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(asv, taxon, n_hosts), dplyr::join_by(taxon)) |>
        dplyr::filter(!blank(Phylum), nonzero > 0)
    phyla <- names(sort(table(per_asv$Phylum), decreasing = TRUE))
    phyla <- phyla[seq_len(min(major_phyla, length(phyla)))]
    breadth_abundance <- purrr::map(phyla, function(ph) {
        d <- dplyr::filter(per_asv, Phylum == ph)
        # abundance spans orders of magnitude, so the fit on log10 is the one to read;
        # the fit on the abundance itself is reported beside it
        raw <- summary(stats::lm(nonzero ~ n_hosts, data = d))
        fit <- summary(stats::lm(log10(nonzero) ~ n_hosts, data = d))
        rho <- suppressWarnings(stats::cor.test(d$n_hosts, d$nonzero, method = "spearman",
                                                alternative = "greater"))
        tibble::tibble(Phylum = ph, n_asvs = nrow(d),
                       slope_raw_per_host = raw$coefficients["n_hosts", "Estimate"],
                       r2_raw = raw$r.squared,
                       lm_raw_p = raw$coefficients["n_hosts", "Pr(>|t|)"],
                       slope_log10_per_host = fit$coefficients["n_hosts", "Estimate"],
                       r2 = fit$r.squared, lm_p = fit$coefficients["n_hosts", "Pr(>|t|)"],
                       spearman_rho = unname(rho$estimate),
                       spearman_p_one_sided = rho$p.value)
    }) |> purrr::list_rbind() |>
        dplyr::mutate(lm_raw_q = stats::p.adjust(lm_raw_p, method = "BH"),
                      lm_q = stats::p.adjust(lm_p, method = "BH"),
                      spearman_q = stats::p.adjust(spearman_p_one_sided, method = "BH"))

    list(tests = tests, top_genera = top, breadth_abundance = breadth_abundance)
}

# METHODS 5 | CLAM by stage; also calls the host screen (6) and the comparison (7)
perform_generalist_specialist <- function(ps, group_col, stage_levels, study_col, host_col,
                                          tables_dir, specialization, alpha, coverage_limit,
                                          breadth_depth, breadth_probs, nperm,
                                          host_tree_path = NULL, screen_iter = 1000,
                                          screen_fdr = 0.05, top_genera = 25,
                                          major_phyla = 5) {
    meta_df <- as(sample_data(ps), "data.frame")
    needed <- c(group_col, study_col, host_col)
    if (!all(needed %in% colnames(meta_df))) {
        cat("Generalist/specialist: skipped - metadata lacks",
            paste(setdiff(needed, colnames(meta_df)), collapse = ", "), "\n")
        return(list(status = "skipped_no_group"))
    }
    stage <- factor(meta_df[[group_col]], levels = stage_levels)
    study <- as.character(meta_df[[study_col]])
    host <- as.character(meta_df[[host_col]])
    both <- names(which(tapply(stage, study, function(x) all(table(x) > 0))))
    if (length(stage_levels) != 2 || length(both) == 0 || dplyr::n_distinct(host) < 2) {
        cat("Generalist/specialist: skipped - needs a study with both stages and two hosts\n")
        return(list(status = "skipped_design"))
    }

    tryCatch({
        otu <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
        if (!taxa_are_rows(ps)) otu <- t(otu)
        tax <- as(tax_table(ps), "matrix")
        genus <- tax[, "Genus"]
        named <- !is.na(genus) & genus != "" &
            !grepl("^(Unassigned|unidentified|uncultured|metagenome)$", genus, ignore.case = TRUE)
        counts <- rowsum(otu[named, , drop = FALSE], genus[named])    # genus x sample
        phylum <- tapply(tax[named, "Phyla"], genus[named],
                         function(x) names(sort(table(x), decreasing = TRUE))[1])

        # --- 1. stage: CLAM ---------------------------------------------------------
        clam <- function(keep) {
            x <- t(counts[, keep, drop = FALSE])
            x <- x[, colSums(x) > 0, drop = FALSE]
            r <- vegan::clamtest(x, stage[keep], coverage.limit = coverage_limit,
                                 specialization = specialization, alpha = alpha)
            totals <- r[, paste0("Total_", stage_levels)]
            tibble::tibble(Genus = as.character(r$Species),
                           reads_1 = totals[[1]], reads_2 = totals[[2]],
                           class = as.character(r$Classes))
        }
        pooled <- clam(study %in% both)
        per_study <- purrr::map(both, function(s) {
            dplyr::select(clam(study == s), Genus, class) |> dplyr::mutate(study = s)
        }) |> purrr::list_rbind()
        agreement <- per_study |>
            dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(pooled, Genus, pooled_class = class),
                              dplyr::join_by(Genus)) |>
            dplyr::summarise(n_studies_tested = sum(class != "Too_rare"),
                             n_studies_agree = sum(class == pooled_class & class != "Too_rare"),
                             .by = Genus)
        stage_tab <- pooled |>
            dplyr::rename(stage_class = class) |>
            dplyr::rename_with(~ paste0("reads_", stage_levels), c(reads_1, reads_2)) |>
            dplyr::left_join(agreement, dplyr::join_by(Genus)) |>
            dplyr::left_join(tidyr::pivot_wider(per_study, names_from = study,
                                                values_from = class,
                                                names_prefix = "stage_class_"),
                             dplyr::join_by(Genus))

        # --- 2. host breadth: Levins' B against a quasiswap null ----------------------
        rel <- sweep(counts, 2, pmax(colSums(otu), 1), "/")
        host_mean <- sapply(split(seq_len(ncol(rel)), host),
                            function(i) rowMeans(rel[, i, drop = FALSE]))    # genus x host
        host_counts <- round(t(host_mean) * breadth_depth)                 # host x genus
        host_counts <- host_counts[, colSums(host_counts) > 0, drop = FALSE]
        levins <- function(m) 1 / colSums(sweep(m, 2, colSums(m), "/")^2)
        observed <- levins(host_counts)
        set.seed(123)
        null <- simulate(vegan::nullmodel(host_counts, "quasiswap_count"), nsim = nperm)
        null_b <- apply(null, 3, levins)                                   # genus x nperm
        bounds <- apply(null_b, 1, stats::quantile, probs = breadth_probs)
        host_tab <- tibble::tibble(
            Genus = colnames(host_counts),
            levins_b = unname(observed),
            levins_b_standardised = (levins_b - 1) / (nrow(host_counts) - 1),
            null_lower = bounds[1, ], null_upper = bounds[2, ],
            host_class = dplyr::case_when(levins_b > null_upper ~ "Generalist",
                                          levins_b < null_lower ~ "Specialist",
                                          TRUE ~ "Neither"))

        # --- 3. host breadth by presence/absence: the double screening -----------------
        screens <- NULL
        if (is.null(host_tree_path) || !file.exists(host_tree_path)) {
            cat("Host double screening: skipped - no host tree (inputs.host_tree)\n")
        } else {
            host_tree <- read_host_species_tree(host_tree_path)
            if (!all(unique(host) %in% host_tree$tip.label)) {
                stop("hosts missing from the host tree: ",
                     paste(setdiff(unique(host), host_tree$tip.label), collapse = ", "))
            }
            # divergence time of two hosts: half the path between their tips
            host_distance <- stats::cophenetic(host_tree) / 2
            host_genus <- sub(" .*$", "", host)
            screen_one <- function(m) {
                by_host <- function(groups) sapply(split(seq_len(ncol(m)), groups),
                                                   function(i) rowMeans(m[, i, drop = FALSE] > 0))
                s <- host_double_screen(by_host(host) > 0, host_distance, screen_iter, screen_fdr)
                # the host genus on which the taxon is most often found: the highest share
                # of that genus's samples, so a heavily sampled host does not win by size
                share <- by_host(host_genus)
                s$taxa$representative_host_genus <-
                    colnames(share)[max.col(share[s$taxa$taxon, , drop = FALSE],
                                            ties.method = "first")]
                s
            }
            set.seed(123)
            screens <- list(genus = screen_one(counts), ASV = screen_one(otu))
        }

        out <- tibble::tibble(Genus = rownames(counts), Phylum = as.character(phylum[Genus]),
                              n_hosts_present = unname(rowSums(host_mean > 0)[Genus])) |>
            dplyr::left_join(stage_tab, dplyr::join_by(Genus)) |>
            dplyr::left_join(host_tab, dplyr::join_by(Genus)) |>
            # below one read in every host's average sample: too rare to give a breadth
            dplyr::mutate(host_class = dplyr::coalesce(host_class, "Too_rare")) |>
            dplyr::arrange(Phylum, Genus)
        if (!is.null(screens)) {
            out <- dplyr::left_join(out, dplyr::select(screens$genus$taxa, -n_hosts),
                                    dplyr::join_by(Genus == taxon))
            readr::write_csv(
                screens$ASV$taxa |>
                    dplyr::mutate(Phylum = unname(tax[taxon, "Phyla"]),
                                  Genus = unname(tax[taxon, "Genus"])) |>
                    dplyr::select(ASV = taxon, Phylum, Genus, dplyr::everything()),
                file.path(tables_dir, "generalist_specialist_asv_host_screen.csv"))
            readr::write_csv(
                purrr::imap(screens, function(s, unit) {
                    dplyr::mutate(s$breadth, unit = unit, threshold = s$threshold,
                                  expected_breadth = s$expected_breadth, .before = 1)
                }) |> purrr::list_rbind(),
                file.path(tables_dir, "generalist_specialist_breadth_null.csv"))
            composition <- generalist_specialist_composition(screens$ASV$taxa, otu, tax, host,
                                                             top_genera, major_phyla)
            readr::write_csv(composition$tests,
                             file.path(tables_dir, "generalist_specialist_composition_tests.csv"))
            readr::write_csv(composition$top_genera,
                             file.path(tables_dir, "generalist_specialist_top_genera.csv"))
            readr::write_csv(composition$breadth_abundance,
                             file.path(tables_dir, "generalist_specialist_breadth_abundance.csv"))
            # taxa found in one group only, reported on their own
            readr::write_csv(dplyr::filter(composition$tests, exclusive_to != ""),
                             file.path(tables_dir, "generalist_specialist_exclusive_taxa.csv"))
            # significantly clustered taxa with the host genus that most often carries
            # them; the table has no rows when nothing is clustered after correction
            readr::write_csv(
                purrr::imap(screens, function(s, unit) {
                    s$taxa |> dplyr::filter(dplyr::coalesce(q_clustered < screen_fdr, FALSE)) |>
                        dplyr::transmute(unit = unit, taxon, n_hosts, host_mpd_my, host_mpd_z,
                                         q_clustered, pseudo_generalist,
                                         representative_host_genus)
                }) |> purrr::list_rbind(),
                file.path(tables_dir, "generalist_specialist_clustered_taxa.csv"))
        }
        readr::write_csv(out, file.path(tables_dir, "generalist_specialist_genus.csv"))

        summary_tab <- dplyr::bind_rows(
            dplyr::count(pooled, class, name = "n_genera") |>
                dplyr::mutate(analysis = "stage_CLAM", scope = "both-stage studies pooled"),
            dplyr::count(per_study, study, class, name = "n_genera") |>
                dplyr::mutate(analysis = "stage_CLAM") |> dplyr::rename(scope = study),
            dplyr::count(out, class = host_class, name = "n_genera") |>
                dplyr::mutate(analysis = "host_breadth_Levins", scope = "all studies"),
            # n_genera counts taxa: genera in the genus rows, ASVs in the ASV rows
            purrr::imap(screens, function(s, unit) {
                dplyr::bind_rows(
                    dplyr::count(s$taxa, class = screen_class, name = "n_genera"),
                    tibble::tibble(class = "Pseudo-generalist (in Intermediate)",
                                   n_genera = sum(s$taxa$pseudo_generalist))) |>
                    dplyr::mutate(analysis = "host_double_screen",
                                  scope = sprintf("%s level, threshold %s hosts", unit,
                                                  s$threshold))
            }) |> purrr::list_rbind(),
            # n_genera counts taxa of that rank here
            if (!is.null(screens)) {
                composition$tests |>
                    dplyr::summarise(`differs, q < 0.05` = sum(q < 0.05),
                                     `only in generalists` = sum(exclusive_to == "Generalists"),
                                     `only in specialists` = sum(exclusive_to == "Specialists"),
                                     .by = rank) |>
                    tidyr::pivot_longer(-rank, names_to = "class", values_to = "n_genera") |>
                    dplyr::mutate(analysis = "composition_Fisher_ASV",
                                  scope = paste(rank, "level"))
            }) |>
            dplyr::select(analysis, scope, class, n_genera)
        readr::write_csv(summary_tab, file.path(tables_dir, "generalist_specialist_summary.csv"))

        cat("\n=== Generalist / specialist genera ===\n")
        cat("Stage (CLAM), studies with both stages:", paste(both, collapse = ", "), "\n")
        print(table(pooled$class))
        cat("Host breadth (Levins' B,", nrow(host_counts), "hosts,", nperm, "null tables):\n")
        print(table(out$host_class))
        for (unit in names(screens)) {
            cat(sprintf("Host double screening, %s level: generalist threshold = %s hosts, %d pseudo-generalists removed\n",
                        unit, screens[[unit]]$threshold,
                        sum(screens[[unit]]$taxa$pseudo_generalist)))
            print(table(screens[[unit]]$taxa$screen_class))
        }
        list(status = "completed", n_genera = nrow(out))
    }, error = function(e) {
        message("Generalist/specialist error: ", conditionMessage(e))
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

cat("Running generalist/specialist analysis...\n")
if (!is.null(group_col)) {
    gs_cfg <- function(key, default) get_config_value(c("generalist_specialist", key), default)
    gs_result <- perform_generalist_specialist(
        ps, group_col,
        stage_levels = get_config_value(c("differential_abundance", "groups"), NULL),
        study_col = gs_cfg("study_group", "study_alias"),
        host_col = gs_cfg("host_group", "Scientific_Name"),
        tables_dir = tables_dir,
        specialization = gs_cfg("clam_specialization", 2 / 3),
        alpha = gs_cfg("clam_alpha", 0.005),
        coverage_limit = gs_cfg("clam_coverage_limit", 10),
        breadth_depth = gs_cfg("host_breadth_depth", 1000),
        breadth_probs = gs_cfg("host_breadth_probs", c(0.025, 0.975)),
        nperm = get_config_value(c("analysis", "permutations"), 999),
        host_tree_path = if (is.null(get_config_value(c("inputs", "host_tree"), NULL))) NULL else
            resolve_path(base_dir, get_config_value(c("inputs", "host_tree"), NULL)),
        screen_iter = gs_cfg("screen_iterations", 1000),
        screen_fdr = gs_cfg("screen_fdr", 0.05),
        top_genera = gs_cfg("top_genera", 25),
        major_phyla = gs_cfg("major_phyla", 5))
    cat("  Generalist/specialist:", gs_result$status, "\n")
}
```

## Analysis Results

### Alpha Diversity Analysis (wild-again Figure1.Rmd + seedling_meta_analysis integration)

#### Diversity Metrics Calculation

```{r alpha-diversity}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 2 | Diversity, composition and co-occurrence
#   alpha diversity: indices on unrarefied counts (reported values: chunk rarefied-alpha)
# ==========================================================================================
compute_alpha_diversity <- function(ps, counts_matrix, tree, group_col = NULL, output_dir, tables_dir) {
    # Calculate alpha diversity metrics using phyloseq
    richness <- phyloseq::estimate_richness(
        ps,
        measures = c("Observed", "Shannon")
    )

    # Calculate Evenness (from seedling_meta_analysis.qmd)
    richness$Evenness <- ifelse(
        richness$Observed > 1,
        richness$Shannon / log(richness$Observed),
        NA_real_
    )

    # Calculate Faith's PD (phylogenetic diversity)
    pd_results <- NULL
    if (!is.null(tree) && !is.null(phy_tree(ps, errorIfNULL = FALSE))) {
        tryCatch({
            otu_for_pd <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
            if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) otu_for_pd <- t(otu_for_pd)
            pd_results <- picante::pd(otu_for_pd, tree, include.root = FALSE)
            richness$Faith_PD <- pd_results$PD[match(rownames(richness), rownames(pd_results))]
            richness$Phylogenetic_Richness <- pd_results$SR[match(rownames(richness), rownames(pd_results))]
        }, error = function(e) {
            message("Warning: Could not calculate Faith's PD: ", conditionMessage(e))
        })
    }

    # Add metadata if group column specified
    if (!is.null(group_col) && group_col %in% colnames(sample_data(ps))) {
        alpha_df <- cbind(as.data.frame(sample_data(ps)), richness)

        # Check normality
        cat("\n=== Normality Tests ===\n")
        cat("Observed ASV Richness:\n")
        print(shapiro.test(richness$Observed))
        cat("\nShannon Index:\n")
        print(shapiro.test(richness$Shannon))

        # Non-parametric test (Kruskal-Wallis)
        if (length(unique(alpha_df[[group_col]])) > 1) {
            kt_obs <- kruskal.test(Observed ~ get(group_col), alpha_df)
            kt_sh <- kruskal.test(Shannon ~ get(group_col), alpha_df)

            cat("\n=== Kruskal-Wallis Tests ===\n")
            cat("Observed ~", group_col, ":", kt_obs$p.value, "\n")
            cat("Shannon ~", group_col, ":", kt_sh$p.value, "\n")

            # Pairwise comparisons
            wt_obs <- pairwise.wilcox.test(
                alpha_df$Observed,
                as.factor(alpha_df[[group_col]]),
                p.adjust.method = "bonf"
            )

            wt_sh <- pairwise.wilcox.test(
                alpha_df$Shannon,
                as.factor(alpha_df[[group_col]]),
                p.adjust.method = "bonf"
            )

            # Save pairwise comparisons
            saveRDS(wt_obs, file.path(output_dir, "pairwise_observed.rds"))
            saveRDS(wt_sh, file.path(output_dir, "pairwise_shannon.rds"))
        }
    }

    # Save alpha diversity table
    write.csv(richness, file.path(tables_dir, "alpha_diversity.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

    # Summary statistics
    metrics_to_summarize <- c("Observed", "Shannon", "Evenness")
    if (!is.null(richness$Faith_PD)) {
        metrics_to_summarize <- c(metrics_to_summarize, "Faith_PD", "Phylogenetic_Richness")
    }

    summary_stats <- data.frame(
        Metric = metrics_to_summarize,
        Mean = vapply(richness[, metrics_to_summarize, drop = FALSE], mean, numeric(1), na.rm = TRUE),
        Median = vapply(richness[, metrics_to_summarize, drop = FALSE], median, numeric(1), na.rm = TRUE),
        SD = vapply(richness[, metrics_to_summarize, drop = FALSE], sd, numeric(1), na.rm = TRUE),
        IQR = vapply(richness[, metrics_to_summarize, drop = FALSE], IQR, numeric(1), na.rm = TRUE)
    )

    write.csv(summary_stats, file.path(tables_dir, "alpha_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
    knitr::kable(summary_stats, caption = "Alpha Diversity Summary Statistics")

    list(status = "completed", n_samples = nrow(richness), alpha_df = richness)
}

# Determine primary grouping variable from config
group_col <- config$analysis$primary_group
if (!is.null(group_col) && group_col %in% colnames(sample_data(ps))) {
    cat("Computing alpha diversity grouped by:", group_col, "\n")
    alpha_result <- compute_alpha_diversity(ps, counts, phylo_tree, group_col, diversity_dir, tables_dir)
} else {
    cat("Computing alpha diversity (no grouping variable)\n")
    alpha_result <- compute_alpha_diversity(ps, counts, phylo_tree, NULL, diversity_dir, tables_dir)
}
cat("  Alpha diversity:", alpha_result$status, "\n")
```
