#### Alpha Diversity Visualization

<!-- removed: alpha-diversity-plots - Part 1 plot_alpha_diversity + plot_variable_alpha driver. Alpha diversity is now represented only by the two richness figures; see tables/alpha_diversity_findings.csv for the statistics these carried. -->

### Rarefied Alpha Diversity

```{r rarefied-alpha}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 2 | Diversity, composition and co-occurrence
#   alpha diversity: richness, Shannon, Pielou's evenness at 500 and 1,000 reads
# ==========================================================================================
#' Kruskal-Wallis test of each rarefied index against each grouping variable, with the
#' H-based effect size epsilon squared, (H - k + 1) / (n - k). `rarefied_df`: one row per
#' sample, the three `*_rarefied` indices and the metadata. Plant family is not a
#' metadata column: it follows from the host species, through `family_map`.
rarefied_alpha_tests <- function(rarefied_df, rarefaction_depth) {
    if (exists("family_map") && "Scientific_Name" %in% names(rarefied_df)) {
        rarefied_df$Plant_Family <- family_map$Family[match(rarefied_df$Scientific_Name,
                                                            family_map$Scientific_Name)]
    }
    # study (study_alias, Author) and country (Geography) are not tested as grouping
    # variables, at the user's request: study is a confounder here, handled by the
    # within-study and stratified tests, and country is kept as description only
    # host genus, not host species, as the user asked (2026-10-20): the host levels analysed are cultivar, genus and plant family
    if ("Scientific_Name" %in% names(rarefied_df)) rarefied_df$Host_Genus <- sub(" .*$", "", rarefied_df$Scientific_Name)
    # host attributes are plant family and host genus only, at the user's request (2026-10-22)
    variables <- intersect(c("Developmental_Stage", "Plant_Family", "Host_Genus"), names(rarefied_df))
    metrics <- c("Observed_rarefied", "Shannon_rarefied", "Evenness_rarefied")
    tests <- list()
    for (v in variables) {
        dv <- rarefied_df[!is.na(rarefied_df[[v]]) & rarefied_df[[v]] != "", , drop = FALSE]
        if (dplyr::n_distinct(dv[[v]]) < 2) next
        for (metric in metrics) {
            kt <- stats::kruskal.test(dv[[metric]] ~ factor(dv[[v]]))
            # n and k count what the test used: evenness is NA for single-ASV samples
            # and kruskal.test drops those
            used <- dv[!is.na(dv[[metric]]), , drop = FALSE]
            k <- dplyr::n_distinct(used[[v]])
            n <- nrow(used)
            H <- unname(kt$statistic)
            tests[[length(tests) + 1]] <- data.frame(
                depth = rarefaction_depth, variable = v, metric = sub("_rarefied$", "", metric),
                groups = dplyr::n_distinct(dv[[v]]), n = n, H = H, df = unname(kt$parameter),
                p = kt$p.value, epsilon_sq = (H - k + 1) / (n - k))
        }
    }
    if (length(tests)) do.call(rbind, tests) else data.frame()
}

compute_rarefied_alpha <- function(ps, rarefaction_depth = NULL, group_col = NULL,
                                    output_dir, tables_dir) {
    tryCatch({
        otu <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
        if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) otu <- t(otu)

        # Rarefaction depth. The previous rule, min(target, min(rowSums(otu))), let the
        # shallowest sample dictate the depth for every other sample - and because two
        # samples in the filtered object carry zero reads, it collapsed the depth to 0,
        # rarefied everything to nothing and returned all-zero richness and Shannon for
        # all 1,886 samples. The failure was invisible: the tryCatch below swallowed the
        # downstream error, so rarefied_observed.tiff and rarefied_shannon.tiff were
        # simply never written while the captions for them stayed in the index.
        # Standard practice instead: rarefy to the configured depth and drop the samples
        # that cannot reach it.
        depths <- rowSums(otu)
        if (is.null(rarefaction_depth)) {
            nonzero <- depths[depths > 0]
            if (!length(nonzero)) {
                cat("Rarefaction: every sample has zero reads - skipped\n")
                return(list(status = "skipped_no_reads"))
            }
            rarefaction_depth <- min(nonzero)
        }
        keep <- depths >= rarefaction_depth
        if (sum(keep) < 2) {
            cat("Rarefaction: fewer than 2 samples reach depth", rarefaction_depth,
                "- skipped\n")
            return(list(status = "skipped_insufficient_depth",
                        depth = rarefaction_depth, retained = sum(keep)))
        }
        cat(sprintf("Rarefying to depth %d: %d of %d samples retained, %d below depth\n",
                    rarefaction_depth, sum(keep), length(depths), sum(!keep)))
        otu <- otu[keep, , drop = FALSE]
        ps <- prune_samples(rownames(otu), ps)

        # Rarefy all samples to the same depth
        set.seed(123)
        otu_rarefied <- t(apply(otu, 1, function(x) {
            rrarefy(x, sample = rarefaction_depth)
        }))
        rownames(otu_rarefied) <- rownames(otu)

        # Calculate alpha diversity on rarefied data.
        # vegan:: is mandatory here. THREE loaded packages export diversity() and
        # igraph's wins the search path: igraph::diversity(graph, weights, vids) has no
        # `index` argument, so the bare call failed with "unused argument (index =
        # "shannon")" - inside the tryCatch, so it was swallowed and this function
        # silently produced nothing. Same masking trap as the dplyr verbs in CLAUDE.md.
        richness_rarefied <- rowSums(otu_rarefied > 0)
        shannon_rarefied <- vegan::diversity(otu_rarefied, index = "shannon")
        # Pielou's evenness, so each rarefaction depth carries the same three indices
        # as the unrarefied table (compute_alpha_diversity). Evenness is undefined for a
        # single-ASV sample, as there.
        evenness_rarefied <- ifelse(richness_rarefied > 1,
                                    shannon_rarefied / log(richness_rarefied), NA_real_)

        rarefied_df <- data.frame(
            sample_id = rownames(otu_rarefied),
            Observed_rarefied = richness_rarefied,
            Shannon_rarefied = shannon_rarefied,
            Evenness_rarefied = evenness_rarefied,
            rarefaction_depth = rarefaction_depth,
            stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )

        # Add metadata
        if (!is.null(group_col) && group_col %in% colnames(sample_data(ps))) {
            meta_df <- as.data.frame(sample_data(ps))
            rarefied_df <- merge(rarefied_df, meta_df,
                                 by.x = "sample_id", by.y = "row.names", all.x = TRUE)

            # Statistical tests on rarefied data
            if (length(unique(rarefied_df[[group_col]])) > 1) {
                kt_obs_r <- kruskal.test(Observed_rarefied ~ get(group_col), rarefied_df)
                kt_sh_r <- kruskal.test(Shannon_rarefied ~ get(group_col), rarefied_df)

                cat("\n=== Rarefied Alpha Diversity: Kruskal-Wallis Tests ===\n")
                cat("Observed (rarefied) ~", group_col, ":", kt_obs_r$p.value, "\n")
                cat("Shannon (rarefied) ~", group_col, ":", kt_sh_r$p.value, "\n")
            }

            # Rarefied boxplots removed: alpha diversity is represented by the two
            # richness figures alone. The rarefied VALUES are still computed and
            # written per depth, because those figures are drawn from them, and the
            # Kruskal-Wallis tests below are still tabulated.

            rare_metrics <- c("Observed_rarefied", "Shannon_rarefied", "Evenness_rarefied")
            rare_tests <- rarefied_alpha_tests(rarefied_df, rarefaction_depth)
            # Per-group summary of every index at this depth, for reporting.
            rare_summary <- purrr::map(rare_metrics, function(metric) {
                rarefied_df |>
                    # .env: rarefied_df has its own rarefaction_depth COLUMN, which would
                    # otherwise be picked up and return one row per sample
                    dplyr::summarise(depth = .env$rarefaction_depth,
                                     metric = sub("_rarefied$", "", .env$metric),
                                     n = sum(!is.na(.data[[metric]])),
                                     median = median(.data[[metric]], na.rm = TRUE),
                                     q25 = unname(quantile(.data[[metric]], 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)),
                                     q75 = unname(quantile(.data[[metric]], 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)),
                                     mean = mean(.data[[metric]], na.rm = TRUE),
                                     sd = sd(.data[[metric]], na.rm = TRUE),
                                     .by = dplyr::all_of(group_col))
            }) |> purrr::list_rbind()
            readr::write_csv(rare_summary,
                             file.path(tables_dir,
                                       sprintf("rarefied_alpha_summary_depth%d.csv",
                                               rarefaction_depth)))
            if (nrow(rare_tests)) {
                readr::write_csv(rare_tests,
                                 file.path(tables_dir,
                                           sprintf("rarefied_alpha_tests_depth%d.csv",
                                                   rarefaction_depth)))
                cat(sprintf("    %d Kruskal-Wallis tests tabulated\n", nrow(rare_tests)))
            }
        }

        write.csv(rarefied_df,
                  file.path(tables_dir,
                            sprintf("rarefied_alpha_diversity_depth%d.csv", rarefaction_depth)),
                  row.names = FALSE)

        list(status = "completed", rarefaction_depth = rarefaction_depth,
             n_samples = nrow(rarefied_df))
    }, error = function(e) {
        message("Rarefied alpha error: ", conditionMessage(e))
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

cat("Computing rarefied alpha diversity...\n")
# Two depths, because the choice is a real trade-off and the reader should see both:
#   500  - the config's min_library_size, keeps 1,851 of 1,886 samples (98.1%)
#   1000 - stricter, keeps 1,760 (93.3%), so richness is estimated from twice the reads
# If the stage difference holds at both, it is not an artefact of the depth chosen.
# Read from filters.rarefaction_depths so Part 2 draws exactly the depths written here;
# the first (shallowest) is the primary depth.
rare_depths <- sort(unique(as.integer(config$filters$rarefaction_depths)))
if (!length(rare_depths)) stop("config filters.rarefaction_depths is empty")

rarefied_alpha_results <- lapply(rare_depths, function(dp) {
    r <- compute_rarefied_alpha(ps, rarefaction_depth = dp, group_col = group_col,
                                figures_dir, tables_dir)
    cat(sprintf("  Rarefied alpha (depth %d): %s\n", dp, r$status))
    if (identical(r$status, "completed")) {
        cat(sprintf("    retained %d samples\n", r$n_samples))
    }
    r
})
names(rarefied_alpha_results) <- paste0("depth", rare_depths)
# kept for the downstream status block, which reports the primary depth
rarefied_alpha_result <- rarefied_alpha_results[[1]]
```

### Alpha Diversity Findings

```{r alpha-findings}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 2 | Diversity, composition and co-occurrence
#   alpha diversity: Kruskal-Wallis tests and effect sizes, overall and within study
# ==========================================================================================
# Table of record for every alpha-diversity test: unrarefied ("none") and each
# rarefaction depth, for all three indices. "overall" rows test each grouping variable
# across all samples. Per-study rows test developmental stage within each study that
# sampled both stages: study is a confounder in a meta-analysis, and the pooled stage
# test is dominated by the largest study. Part 2 reads this table to annotate the
# alpha-diversity figure instead of recomputing anything.
alpha_metrics <- c("Observed", "Shannon", "Evenness")
stage_levels <- config$differential_abundance$groups

kw_row <- function(d, scope, depth, variable, metric) {
    d <- d[!is.na(d[[variable]]) & d[[variable]] != "" & !is.na(d[[metric]]), , drop = FALSE]
    k <- dplyr::n_distinct(d[[variable]])
    if (k < 2) return(NULL)
    kt <- stats::kruskal.test(d[[metric]] ~ factor(d[[variable]]))
    H <- unname(kt$statistic); n <- nrow(d)
    out <- data.frame(scope = scope, depth = depth, variable = variable, metric = metric,
                      groups = k, n = n, H = H, df = unname(kt$parameter), p = kt$p.value,
                      # (H - k + 1) / (n - k): the H-based effect size already used in
                      # the audit's TableS1 under this column name
                      epsilon_sq = (H - k + 1) / (n - k),
                      seed_median = NA_real_, seedling_median = NA_real_,
                      direction = NA_character_)
    if (identical(variable, group_col)) {
        out$seed_median <- median(d[[metric]][d[[variable]] == stage_levels[1]])
        out$seedling_median <- median(d[[metric]][d[[variable]] == stage_levels[2]])
        out$direction <- dplyr::case_when(out$seedling_median > out$seed_median ~ "increase",
                                          out$seedling_median < out$seed_median ~ "decrease",
                                          .default = "none")
    }
    out
}

alpha_findings_result <- tryCatch({
    if (is.null(group_col) || is.null(alpha_result$alpha_df)) stop("no grouping variable or alpha table")
    alpha_by_depth <- list(none = cbind(as(sample_data(ps), "data.frame"), alpha_result$alpha_df))
    for (dp in rare_depths) {
        f <- file.path(tables_dir, sprintf("rarefied_alpha_diversity_depth%d.csv", dp))
        if (!file.exists(f)) next
        d <- read.csv(f, check.names = FALSE)
        names(d) <- sub("_rarefied$", "", names(d))
        alpha_by_depth[[as.character(dp)]] <- d
    }
    alpha_findings <- purrr::imap(alpha_by_depth, function(d, depth) {
        # plant family follows from the host species; it is not a metadata column
        if (exists("family_map") && "Scientific_Name" %in% names(d)) {
            d$Plant_Family <- family_map$Family[match(d$Scientific_Name, family_map$Scientific_Name)]
        }
        # study and country are not in this list, and host is taken as genus: see rarefied_alpha_tests()
        if ("Scientific_Name" %in% names(d)) d$Host_Genus <- sub(" .*$", "", d$Scientific_Name)
        vars <- intersect(c(group_col, "Plant_Family", "Host_Genus"), names(d))
        overall <- purrr::map(vars, function(v) {
            purrr::map(alpha_metrics, function(m) kw_row(d, "overall", depth, v, m)) |>
                purrr::list_rbind()
        }) |> purrr::list_rbind()
        per_study <- purrr::map(split(d, d$study_alias), function(ds) {
            purrr::map(alpha_metrics, function(m) {
                kw_row(ds, ds$study_alias[1], depth, group_col, m)
            }) |> purrr::list_rbind()
        }) |> purrr::list_rbind()
        dplyr::bind_rows(overall, per_study)
    }) |> purrr::list_rbind()
    readr::write_csv(alpha_findings, file.path(tables_dir, "alpha_diversity_findings.csv"))
    list(status = "completed", n_tests = nrow(alpha_findings))
}, error = function(e) {
    message("Alpha findings error: ", conditionMessage(e))
    list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
})
cat("  Alpha diversity findings:", alpha_findings_result$status, "\n")
```

```{r alpha-stage-by-stratum}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 2 | Diversity, composition and co-occurrence
#   alpha diversity: stage effect within each plant family and cultivar, and across them
# ==========================================================================================
# The stage tests above are made across all samples and within each study. Here the same
# contrast is made inside each plant family and each host genus that holds both stages
# (host attributes are plant family and host genus only, at the user's request (2026-10-22)), and
# then tested across them, with the design of the genus-level stage analysis (chunk
# `stage-effects-by-stratum`) and its settings (`stage_effects` in the config):
#   within a stratum   Kruskal-Wallis test of seeds against seedlings, with the effect size
#                      epsilon squared, (H - k + 1) / (n - k), BH-FDR across strata; and
#                      Hedges' g, seedlings minus seeds
#   across strata      random-effects meta-analysis of Hedges' g (REML): Knapp-Hartung for
#                      plant families, a random effect of study above cultivar; Cochran's Q
#                      tests whether the effect differs among the strata, I2 says how much
# Cultivars are taken within host species, as there. Every depth is kept: unrarefied and
# each rarefaction depth. As everywhere here, this does not remove study: a stratum's
# seeds and seedlings can come from different studies, which the table records.
perform_alpha_stage_by_stratum <- function(alpha_by_depth, group_col, stage_levels, study_col,
                                           host_col, family_map, strata, nested_in_study,
                                           within_host, excluded_levels, min_samples, min_strata,
                                           metrics, tables_dir) {
    if (!requireNamespace("metafor", quietly = TRUE)) {
        cat("Alpha stage effects by stratum: skipped - metafor is not installed\n")
        return(list(status = "skipped_no_metafor"))
    }
    by_stratum <- purrr::imap(alpha_by_depth, function(d, depth) {
        d$Plant_Family <- family_map$Family[match(d[[host_col]], family_map$Scientific_Name)]
        d$Host_Genus <- sub(" .*$", "", d[[host_col]])
        stage <- factor(d[[group_col]], levels = stage_levels)
        study <- as.character(d[[study_col]])
        purrr::map(intersect(strata, names(d)), function(variable) {
            stratum <- as.character(d[[variable]])
            stratum[is.na(stratum) | stratum == "" | stratum %in% excluded_levels] <- NA
            if (variable %in% within_host) {
                stratum <- ifelse(is.na(stratum), NA, sprintf("%s (%s)", stratum, d[[host_col]]))
            }
            purrr::map(sort(unique(stats::na.omit(stratum))), function(level) {
                purrr::map(metrics, function(metric) {
                    inside <- !is.na(stratum) & stratum == level & !is.na(stage) & !is.na(d[[metric]])
                    seeds <- d[[metric]][inside & stage == stage_levels[1]]
                    seedlings <- d[[metric]][inside & stage == stage_levels[2]]
                    if (min(length(seeds), length(seedlings)) < min_samples) return(NULL)
                    kt <- stats::kruskal.test(list(seeds, seedlings))
                    H <- unname(kt$statistic)
                    n <- length(seeds) + length(seedlings)
                    es <- metafor::escalc(measure = "SMD", m1i = mean(seedlings), sd1i = stats::sd(seedlings),
                                          n1i = length(seedlings), m2i = mean(seeds),
                                          sd2i = stats::sd(seeds), n2i = length(seeds))
                    tibble::tibble(
                        depth = depth, variable = variable, stratum = level, metric = metric,
                        plant_family = paste(sort(unique(d$Plant_Family[inside])), collapse = "; "),
                        main_study = names(which.max(table(study[inside]))),
                        n_seeds = length(seeds), n_seedlings = length(seedlings),
                        studies_with_both = length(intersect(study[inside & stage == stage_levels[1]],
                                                             study[inside & stage == stage_levels[2]])),
                        seed_median = stats::median(seeds), seedling_median = stats::median(seedlings),
                        H = H, p = kt$p.value, epsilon_sq = (H - 2 + 1) / (n - 2),
                        hedges_g = as.numeric(es$yi), variance = as.numeric(es$vi))
                }) |> purrr::list_rbind()
            }) |> purrr::list_rbind()
        }) |> purrr::list_rbind()
    }) |> purrr::list_rbind()
    if (!nrow(by_stratum)) return(list(status = "skipped_design"))
    by_stratum <- by_stratum |>
        dplyr::mutate(q = stats::p.adjust(p, method = "BH"), .by = c(depth, variable, metric), .after = p) |>
        dplyr::mutate(ci_low = hedges_g - stats::qnorm(0.975) * sqrt(variance),
                      ci_high = hedges_g + stats::qnorm(0.975) * sqrt(variance))

    pooled <- by_stratum |>
        dplyr::filter(is.finite(hedges_g), is.finite(variance), variance > 0) |>
        dplyr::filter(dplyr::n() >= min_strata, .by = c(depth, variable, metric)) |>
        dplyr::group_split(depth, variable, metric) |>
        purrr::map(function(d) {
            # a study level needs at least one study with two strata to be estimable
            with_study <- d$variable[1] %in% nested_in_study &&
                dplyr::n_distinct(d$main_study) < nrow(d) && dplyr::n_distinct(d$main_study) > 1
            fit <- tryCatch(if (with_study) {
                metafor::rma.mv(yi = hedges_g, V = variance, data = d, method = "REML",
                                random = ~ 1 | main_study / stratum, test = "t")
            } else {
                metafor::rma(yi = d$hedges_g, vi = d$variance, method = "REML", test = "knha")
            }, error = function(e) NULL)
            if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)
            w <- 1 / d$variance
            typical <- (length(w) - 1) * sum(w) / (sum(w)^2 - sum(w^2))
            between <- if (with_study) sum(fit$sigma2) else fit$tau2
            tibble::tibble(depth = d$depth[1], variable = d$variable[1], metric = d$metric[1],
                           n_strata = nrow(d), n_studies = dplyr::n_distinct(d$main_study),
                           n_strata_same_direction = sum(sign(d$hedges_g) == sign(fit$b[1])),
                           pooled_g = fit$b[1], ci_low = fit$ci.lb, ci_high = fit$ci.ub, p = fit$pval,
                           # do the strata differ from one another?
                           Q = fit$QE, Q_df = nrow(d) - 1, Q_p = fit$QEp,
                           i2 = 100 * between / (between + typical),
                           model = if (with_study) "study / stratum" else "stratum")
        }) |> purrr::list_rbind()
    readr::write_csv(by_stratum, file.path(tables_dir, "alpha_stage_effect_by_stratum.csv"))
    readr::write_csv(pooled, file.path(tables_dir, "alpha_stage_effect_pooled.csv"))
    cat(sprintf("  %d stage tests within strata (%d plant families, %d host genera); %d pooled estimates\n",
                nrow(by_stratum), dplyr::n_distinct(by_stratum$stratum[by_stratum$variable == "Plant_Family"]),
                dplyr::n_distinct(by_stratum$stratum[by_stratum$variable == "Host_Genus"]), nrow(pooled)))
    list(status = "completed", n_tests = nrow(by_stratum))
}

alpha_stage_strata_result <- tryCatch({
    if (is.null(group_col) || is.null(alpha_result$alpha_df)) stop("no grouping variable or alpha table")
    # the same per-sample values the table of record above was built from
    alpha_by_depth <- list(none = cbind(as(sample_data(ps), "data.frame"), alpha_result$alpha_df))
    for (dp in rare_depths) {
        f <- file.path(tables_dir, sprintf("rarefied_alpha_diversity_depth%d.csv", dp))
        if (!file.exists(f)) next
        d <- read.csv(f, check.names = FALSE)
        names(d) <- sub("_rarefied$", "", names(d))
        alpha_by_depth[[as.character(dp)]] <- d
    }
    se_cfg <- function(key, default) get_config_value(c("stage_effects", key), default)
    perform_alpha_stage_by_stratum(
        alpha_by_depth, group_col, stage_levels,
        study_col = get_config_value(c("generalist_specialist", "study_group"), "study_alias"),
        host_col = get_config_value(c("generalist_specialist", "host_group"), "Scientific_Name"),
        family_map = family_map,
        strata = se_cfg("strata", c("Plant_Family", "Host_Genus")),
        nested_in_study = se_cfg("strata_nested_in_study", "Host_Genus"),
        within_host = se_cfg("strata_within_host", character()),
        excluded_levels = se_cfg("strata_excluded_levels", "undefined"),
        min_samples = se_cfg("min_samples_per_stage", 3), min_strata = se_cfg("min_strata", 2),
        metrics = alpha_metrics, tables_dir = tables_dir)
}, error = function(e) {
    message("Alpha stage effects by stratum error: ", conditionMessage(e))
    list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
})
cat("  Alpha stage effects by stratum:", alpha_stage_strata_result$status, "\n")
```

### Faith's Phylogenetic Diversity

```{r faiths-pd}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS - | NOT IN THE METHODOLOGY TEXT
#   Faith's phylogenetic diversity
# ==========================================================================================
compute_faiths_pd <- function(ps, output_path) {
    if (is.null(phy_tree(ps, errorIfNULL = FALSE))) {
        return(list(status = "skipped_no_tree"))
    }
    
    tryCatch({
        otu <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
        if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) otu <- t(otu)
        tree <- phy_tree(ps)
        
        pd_result <- pd(otu, tree, include.root = FALSE)
        pd_df <- data.frame(
            sample_id = rownames(pd_result),
            faith_pd = pd_result$PD,
            phylogenetic_richness = pd_result$SR,
            stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
        
        write.csv(pd_df, output_path, row.names = FALSE)
        list(status = "completed", n_samples = nrow(pd_df))
    }, error = function(e) {
        message("Faith's PD error: ", conditionMessage(e))
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

cat("Computing Faith's PD...\n")
faith_pd_result <- compute_faiths_pd(ps, file.path(diversity_dir, "faith_pd.csv"))
cat("  Faith's PD:", faith_pd_result$status, "\n")
```

### Beta Diversity Analysis (wild-again Figure2.Rmd approach)

#### UniFrac Distances

```{r unifrac}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS - | NOT IN THE METHODOLOGY TEXT
#   UniFrac distances
# ==========================================================================================
compute_unifrac <- function(ps, output_dir) {
    if (is.null(phy_tree(ps, errorIfNULL = FALSE))) {
        return(list(status = "skipped_no_tree"))
    }

    tryCatch({
        start_parallel_cluster()

        # Unweighted UniFrac
        uw <- get_beta_distance(ps, "unifrac", output_dir)

        # Weighted UniFrac
        w <- get_beta_distance(ps, "wunifrac", output_dir)

        # Full CSV distance matrices are optional because as.matrix() can double
        # memory for large sample sets. RDS preserves the compact dist object.
        write_distance_matrix_csv(uw, file.path(output_dir, "unifrac_unweighted_distance.csv"))
        write_distance_matrix_csv(w, file.path(output_dir, "unifrac_weighted_distance.csv"))

        list(status = "completed", n_samples = nsamples(ps))
    }, error = function(e) {
        message("UniFrac error: ", conditionMessage(e))
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

cat("Computing UniFrac distances...\n")
unifrac_result <- compute_unifrac(ps_beta, diversity_dir)
cat("  UniFrac:", unifrac_result$status, "\n")
```

#### PERMANOVA (adonis2)

```{r permanova}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS - | NOT IN THE METHODOLOGY TEXT
#   PERMANOVA on raw-count dissimilarities (reported: chunk beta-diversity-css)
# ==========================================================================================
subset_beta_to_stages <- function(ps, stages = c("Seeds", "Seedlings")) {
    if (!"Developmental_Stage" %in% colnames(sample_data(ps))) {
        return(ps)
    }
    meta_df <- as.data.frame(sample_data(ps))
    keep <- !is.na(meta_df$Developmental_Stage) & meta_df$Developmental_Stage %in% stages
    ps_sub <- prune_samples(keep, ps)
    prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps_sub) > 0, ps_sub)
}

perform_permanova <- function(ps, group_col, output_dir, tables_dir) {
    if (is.null(group_col) || !(group_col %in% colnames(sample_data(ps)))) {
        cat("PERMANOVA: skipped — no grouping variable\n")
        return(list(status = "skipped_no_group"))
    }

    tryCatch({
        meta_df <- as.data.frame(sample_data(ps))
        # Filter out NAs in grouping variable
        keep <- !is.na(meta_df[[group_col]])
        ps_sub <- prune_samples(keep, ps)
        meta_sub <- meta_df[keep, , drop = FALSE]

        # Bray-Curtis distance; reused across PERMANOVA, NMDS, and PCoA.
        dist_bc <- get_beta_distance(ps_sub, "bray", output_dir)

        # PERMANOVA with config-driven permutations
        n_perm <- config$analysis$permutations
        if (is.null(n_perm)) n_perm <- 999
        set.seed(123)
        permanova_result <- vegan::adonis2(
            dist_bc ~ get(group_col),
            data = meta_sub,
            permutations = n_perm,
            parallel = parallel_config$n_threads
        )

        cat("\n=== PERMANOVA Results ===\n")
        print(permanova_result)

        # Save results
        write.csv(as.data.frame(permanova_result),
                  file.path(tables_dir, "permanova_results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

        list(status = "completed", result = permanova_result)
    }, error = function(e) {
        message("PERMANOVA error: ", conditionMessage(e))
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

perform_permanova_stage_subset <- function(ps, group_col, output_dir, tables_dir) {
    ps_stage <- subset_beta_to_stages(ps)
    if (nsamples(ps_stage) < 4) {
        return(list(status = "skipped_too_few_samples"))
    }
    result <- perform_permanova(ps_stage, group_col, output_dir, tables_dir)
    if (identical(result$status, "completed")) {
        dest <- file.path(tables_dir, "permanova_results_stage_subset.csv")
        if (file.exists(dest)) file.remove(dest)
        file.rename(
            file.path(tables_dir, "permanova_results.csv"),
            dest
        )
    }
    result
}

cat("Running PERMANOVA...\n")
permanova_result <- list(status = "not_run")
permanova_stage_result <- list(status = "not_run")
if (!is.null(group_col)) {
    permanova_result <- perform_permanova(ps_beta, group_col, diversity_dir, tables_dir)
    cat("  PERMANOVA:", permanova_result$status, "\n")
    permanova_stage_result <- perform_permanova_stage_subset(ps_beta, group_col, diversity_dir, tables_dir)
    cat("  PERMANOVA (stage subset):", permanova_stage_result$status, "\n")
}
```


### Beta Diversity (CSS-normalised, all filtered features)

```{r beta-diversity-css}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 2 | Diversity, composition and co-occurrence
#   beta diversity: CSS, Bray-Curtis (ASV and genus), PCoA, PERMANOVA alone and marginal
# ==========================================================================================
# Beta diversity at two units of analysis, both using every feature retained by QC
# (no top-N subset):
#   primary     - all filtered ASVs, the finest unit the data supports
#   sensitivity - all genera, the unit that is comparable across studies
#
# The reported PERMANOVA is at ASV level. Read it as a variance partition over the
# compiled samples, not as a cross-study core claim: 57.4% of ASVs occur in a single
# study and carry 24.7% of the reads, and no ASV is shared by five or more of the
# eight studies, so part of any ASV-level term is study identity rather than biology.
# analysis_results/validation/claim_evidence_register_verified.csv (CR5) records the
# same finding independently and marks cross-study ASV claims refuted_at_asv_level.
# Agglomerated to genus the study-private units carry just 1.2% of reads, so the genus
# row below is the check on whether the unit changes the stage conclusion (it does not:
# stage explains 1.5% at genus level against 1.6% at ASV level). Ordination figures are
# drawn at genus level.
#
# CSS (cumulative sum scaling; Paulson et al. 2013) scales each sample by the sum of
# counts up to a data-driven quantile, so a few dominant features cannot set the
# scaling factor. Sequencing depth spans 65-fold across these studies, which is the
# situation CSS is built for. Distances use the CSS-normalised counts as they are, with
# no log transform on top.
if (!requireNamespace("metagenomeSeq", quietly = TRUE)) {
    message("metagenomeSeq not installed - skipping CSS beta diversity")
} else {

css_ps <- prune_samples(sample_sums(ps) > 0, ps)
css_counts <- as(otu_table(css_ps), "matrix")
if (!taxa_are_rows(css_ps)) css_counts <- t(css_counts)        # features x samples
css_tax <- as.data.frame(as(tax_table(css_ps), "matrix"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
css_md_all <- data.frame(sample_data(css_ps), check.names = FALSE)

# Host genus is not a metadata column either; it is the first word of Scientific_Name. It is
# added here, before the sample tables of the two units are taken from css_md_all.
if ("Scientific_Name" %in% names(css_md_all)) css_md_all$Host_Genus <- sub(" .*$", "", css_md_all$Scientific_Name)
# Plant family is not a metadata column; it is derived from Scientific_Name through the
# same family_map used for the composition figures, so the two agree by construction.
# Hosts outside the map fall to "Other" and are excluded from the family tests below.
if (exists("family_map") && "Scientific_Name" %in% names(css_md_all)) {
    css_md_all$Family <- family_map$Family[match(css_md_all$Scientific_Name,
                                                 family_map$Scientific_Name)]
    css_md_all$Family[is.na(css_md_all$Family)] <- ""
    cat(sprintf("  plant family: %d samples mapped to %d families, %d unmapped\n",
                sum(css_md_all$Family != ""),
                dplyr::n_distinct(css_md_all$Family[css_md_all$Family != ""]),
                sum(css_md_all$Family == "")))
}

# Every genus, no abundance cap. ASVs without a genus call cannot be placed, so they
# are dropped rather than lumped into one meaningless "unassigned" unit; they are
# 0.1% of reads. Species rank is not offered: only 50.9% of reads carry a genuine
# binomial and the labels that exist are biased to cultured reference taxa.
css_blank <- function(x) is.na(x) | x == "" |
    grepl("^(Unassigned|unidentified|uncultured|metagenome)$", x, ignore.case = TRUE)
has_genus <- !css_blank(css_tax$Genus)
cat(sprintf("  genus agglomeration: %d ASVs -> %d genera (%d ASVs lack a genus call)\n",
            sum(has_genus), dplyr::n_distinct(css_tax$Genus[has_genus]), sum(!has_genus)))
genus_counts <- rowsum(css_counts[has_genus, , drop = FALSE],
                       group = css_tax$Genus[has_genus])

# CSS needs >= 2 non-zero units per sample, and no distance is meaningful for a sample
# holding a single unit either. The threshold bites harder after agglomeration, so each
# unit keeps its own sample set and reports its own n.
css_normalise <- function(mat, label) {
    keep <- colSums(mat > 0) >= 2 & colSums(mat) > 0
    if (any(!keep)) cat(sprintf("  %s: dropping %d sample(s) with fewer than 2 units\n",
                                label, sum(!keep)))
    m <- mat[, keep, drop = FALSE]
    m <- m[rowSums(m) > 0, , drop = FALSE]
    mr <- metagenomeSeq::newMRexperiment(m)
    pq <- metagenomeSeq::cumNormStatFast(mr)
    out <- metagenomeSeq::MRcounts(metagenomeSeq::cumNorm(mr, p = pq), norm = TRUE, log = FALSE)
    cat(sprintf("  %s CSS: %d units x %d samples (quantile p = %.3f)\n",
                label, nrow(out), ncol(out), pq))
    list(mat = out, md = css_md_all[colnames(out), , drop = FALSE])
}
CSS <- list(genus = css_normalise(genus_counts, "genus"),
            asv   = css_normalise(css_counts,   "ASV"))

CSS$genus$bray <- vegan::vegdist(t(CSS$genus$mat), method = "bray")
CSS$asv$bray   <- vegan::vegdist(t(CSS$asv$mat),   method = "bray")
saveRDS(CSS$genus$bray, file.path(cache_dir, "bray_css_genus.rds"))
saveRDS(CSS$asv$bray,   file.path(cache_dir, "bray_css_all_features.rds"))

# The raw and CSS count matrices are no longer needed - only the distances and the
# sample metadata are. Dropping them here keeps the forked adonis2 workers small.
rm(css_counts, genus_counts); invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

# ── PERMANOVA ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# `Author` is deliberately absent: it is collinear with study_alias and returns
# df = 0, F = -Inf, p = NA in the marginal model. Country (Geography) is not a term, at the
# user's request: it is kept as a description of the dataset only.
# Host is taken as genus: host genus, not host species, as the user asked (2026-10-20): the host levels analysed are cultivar, genus and plant family.
css_nperm   <- get_config_value(c("analysis", "permutations"), 999)
# host attributes are plant family and host genus only, at the user's request (2026-10-22)
css_terms <- intersect(c("Developmental_Stage", "Family", "Host_Genus", "study_alias"), names(css_md_all))

# adonis2(parallel = n) FORKS the whole R session per worker. By this point the session
# holds ps, ps0, ps_decontam, both CSS matrices and both distance matrices, and every
# permutation that writes triggers a copy-on-write page. At 4 workers this drove the
# machine into swap and one model ran for three hours; at 2 workers free memory still
# fell to ~28 MB. Serial it is. A permutation test is CPU-bound, so the arithmetic is
# slower - but nothing like as slow as paging, which is what actually cost the time.
css_threads <- 1L
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

# These 13 models are the slowest thing in the document by a wide margin, and they are a
# pure function of the two distance matrices, the term list and the permutation count.
# Cache on exactly that signature so figure-only edits re-render in minutes instead of
# recomputing everything. Any change to the data, terms or permutations misses the cache
# and recomputes, so the cache can never silently serve stale statistics.
css_perm_cache <- file.path(cache_dir, "permanova_css_by_unit.rds")
css_perm_sig <- list(transform = "css", terms = css_terms, nperm = css_nperm,
                     asv = dim(CSS$asv$mat), genus = dim(CSS$genus$mat),
                     asv_samples = colnames(CSS$asv$mat),
                     genus_samples = colnames(CSS$genus$mat))
css_cached <- if (file.exists(css_perm_cache)) readRDS(css_perm_cache) else NULL

if (!is.null(css_cached) && identical(css_cached$sig, css_perm_sig)) {
    css_permanova <- css_cached$table
    cat(sprintf("  PERMANOVA: reusing %d cached rows (inputs unchanged)\n", nrow(css_permanova)))
} else {

adonis_one <- function(D, md, term) {
    keep <- !is.na(md[[term]]) & md[[term]] != ""
    dd <- droplevels(data.frame(g = factor(md[[term]][keep])))
    if (nlevels(dd$g) < 2) return(NULL)
    set.seed(123)
    a <- vegan::adonis2(as.dist(as.matrix(D)[keep, keep]) ~ g, data = dd,
                        permutations = css_nperm, parallel = css_threads)
    data.frame(unit = NA_character_, model = "univariate", term = term, df = a$Df[1],
               R2 = a$R2[1], F = a$F[1], p = a$`Pr(>F)`[1], n = sum(keep))
}
css_rows <- list()
for (tm in css_terms) {
    r <- adonis_one(CSS$asv$bray, CSS$asv$md, tm)
    if (is.null(r)) next
    r$unit <- "ASV"
    css_rows[[length(css_rows) + 1]] <- r
    cat(sprintf("  ASV   univariate %-20s R2=%.4f F=%.2f p=%.3f n=%d\n",
                tm, r$R2, r$F, r$p, r$n))
}
gm <- CSS$asv$md
# Family is nested within Scientific_Name - every species maps to exactly one family -
# so once species is in the model Family has no degrees of freedom left and returns
# df = 0, F = Inf, p = NA. That is the same collinearity that keeps Author out. Family
# is therefore reported univariately only, and excluded from the marginal model.
css_marg_terms <- setdiff(css_terms, "Family")
css_keep <- complete.cases(gm[, css_marg_terms]) &
            apply(gm[, css_marg_terms] != "", 1, all)
set.seed(123)
css_marg <- vegan::adonis2(
    as.formula(paste("as.dist(as.matrix(CSS$asv$bray)[css_keep, css_keep]) ~",
                     paste(css_marg_terms, collapse = " + "))),
    data = droplevels(gm[css_keep, css_marg_terms, drop = FALSE]),
    permutations = css_nperm, by = "margin", parallel = css_threads)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(css_marg) - 2)) {
    css_rows[[length(css_rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(unit = "ASV", model = "marginal",
        term = rownames(css_marg)[i], df = css_marg$Df[i], R2 = css_marg$R2[i],
        F = css_marg$F[i], p = css_marg$`Pr(>F)`[i], n = sum(css_keep))
    cat(sprintf("  ASV   marginal   %-20s R2=%.4f F=%.2f p=%.3f n=%d\n",
                rownames(css_marg)[i], css_marg$R2[i], css_marg$F[i],
                css_marg$`Pr(>F)`[i], sum(css_keep)))
}
# The ordination figures are drawn from the genus distances, so the genus univariate set
# is computed too: a figure must carry the statistic for the matrix it was drawn from,
# not the ASV statistic, or the annotation contradicts the picture. The ASV rows above
# remain the reported result; these are the figure annotations and the unit sensitivity.
for (tm in css_terms) {
    r <- adonis_one(CSS$genus$bray, CSS$genus$md, tm)
    if (is.null(r)) next
    r$unit <- "genus"
    css_rows[[length(css_rows) + 1]] <- r
    cat(sprintf("  genus univariate %-20s R2=%.4f F=%.2f p=%.3f n=%d\n",
                tm, r$R2, r$F, r$p, r$n))
}
css_permanova <- do.call(rbind, css_rows)
saveRDS(list(sig = css_perm_sig, table = css_permanova), css_perm_cache)
cat(sprintf("  PERMANOVA: computed and cached %d rows\n", nrow(css_permanova)))

}   # end cache gate

readr::write_csv(css_permanova, file.path(diversity_dir, "permanova_css_by_unit.csv"))

# ── Ordination figures ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Every ordination carries its own PERMANOVA beneath the subtitle. `unit` must match the
# distance matrix the plot was drawn from, otherwise the annotation would describe a
# different analysis from the picture above it.
css_stat_line <- function(unit, term) {
    r <- css_permanova[css_permanova$unit == unit &
                       css_permanova$model == "univariate" &
                       css_permanova$term == term, ]
    if (!nrow(r)) return(NA_character_)
    sprintf("PERMANOVA: R² = %.2f%%, F = %.1f, df = %d, p = %.3f (%d permutations)",
            100 * r$R2[1], r$F[1], r$df[1], r$p[1], css_nperm)
}

css_pcoa_plot <- function(D, md, var, title, dist_label, unit_label, n_units,
                          stat_unit = "genus") {
    # The study legend names references, not accessions.
    if (var == "study_alias" && "Author" %in% names(md)) {
        md[[var]] <- as_study_ref(md[[var]], md$study_alias, md$Author)
    }
    keep <- !is.na(md[[var]]) & md[[var]] != ""
    cm <- cmdscale(as.dist(as.matrix(D)[keep, keep]), k = 2, eig = TRUE)
    ev <- 100 * cm$eig[1:2] / sum(cm$eig[cm$eig > 0])
    d <- data.frame(PCoA1 = cm$points[, 1], PCoA2 = cm$points[, 2],
                    grp = factor(md[[var]][keep]))
    # One shape throughout - a filled circle. Varying the shape as well as the fill
    # made the legend harder to read, not easier: at this point size a triangle and a
    # diamond are near-indistinguishable, so colour alone carries group identity and
    # `distinct_palette()` guarantees the colours are separable.
    # No confidence ellipses either: with 20-odd cultivars they overlapped so heavily
    # they hid the points, and ellipses around small groups implied precision that is
    # not there.
    ggplot(d, aes(PCoA1, PCoA2, fill = grp)) +
        geom_point(shape = 21, size = 2.5, colour = "grey20", stroke = 0.3) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = distinct_palette(nlevels(d$grp)), name = NULL) +
        labs(x = sprintf("PCoA 1 (%.1f%%)", ev[1]),
             y = sprintf("PCoA 2 (%.1f%%)", ev[2]), title = title,
             subtitle = {
                 sub <- sprintf("%s, CSS-normalised, %d %s; n = %d",
                                dist_label, n_units, unit_label, sum(keep))
                 st <- css_stat_line(stat_unit, var)
                 if (is.na(st)) sub else paste(sub, st, sep = "\n")
             }) +
        guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3.6), ncol = 1)) +
        theme_classic(base_size = 12, base_family = "Helvetica") +
        theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
              plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5, colour = "grey30"),
              legend.text = element_text(size = 10), legend.key.size = unit(12, "pt"),
              plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA))
}

css_vars <- c(Developmental_Stage = "developmental stage", Family = "plant family",
              study_alias = "study", Host_Genus = "host genus",
              Author = "reference")
css_vars <- css_vars[names(css_vars) %in% names(css_md_all)]
css_n_genus <- nrow(CSS$genus$mat)
for (v in names(css_vars)) {
    ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, sprintf("pcoa_css_bray_genus_by_%s.tiff", tolower(v))),
           css_pcoa_plot(CSS$genus$bray, CSS$genus$md, v,
                         paste("Community structure by", css_vars[[v]]),
                         "Bray-Curtis", "genera", css_n_genus),
           width = 8.6, height = 6.2, dpi = 300, compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
}
# No Jaccard ordination. Jaccard is presence/absence, and binarising with `> 0` throws
# away exactly what CSS normalisation computed - a scaling factor cannot turn a zero
# into a non-zero, so "CSS-normalised Jaccard" is just raw occurrence data wearing the
# CSS label. Bray-Curtis on the CSS matrix is the only ordination that actually uses
# the transformation, so it is the only one drawn here.

# Unit-of-analysis sensitivity: genus beside ASV, same stage contrast, same colours.
css_r2_note <- function(u) {
    st <- css_stat_line(u, "Developmental_Stage")
    if (is.na(st)) "" else st
}
css_panel_a <- css_pcoa_plot(CSS$genus$bray, CSS$genus$md, "Developmental_Stage",
                             "Genus level", "Bray-Curtis", "genera", css_n_genus,
                             stat_unit = "genus") + labs(tag = "a")
css_panel_b <- css_pcoa_plot(CSS$asv$bray, CSS$asv$md, "Developmental_Stage",
                             "ASV level", "Bray-Curtis", "ASVs", nrow(CSS$asv$mat),
                             stat_unit = "ASV") + labs(tag = "b")
ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "pcoa_css_stage_unit_sensitivity.tiff"),
       (css_panel_a | css_panel_b) +
           patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
           theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
                 plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 9.5, colour = "grey25")),
       width = 13.6, height = 5.8, dpi = 300, compression = "lzw", bg = "white")

cat("  CSS beta diversity:", length(css_vars) + 1, "figures\n")

}
```

```{r pcoa-by-stage}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 2 | Diversity, composition and co-occurrence
#   beta diversity: seeds and seedlings ordinated apart, and host structure tested within each
# ==========================================================================================
# The ordinations above place every sample in one space. Here the seed samples and the
# seedling samples are ordinated separately, so that host structure can be looked at
# within a stage without the stage contrast setting the axes. It is done at genus level
# and at ASV level: same distances (Bray-Curtis of CSS-normalised counts, cached by the
# chunk above) and the same method (cmdscale, variance explained over the positive
# eigenvalues) as css_pcoa_plot(). Coordinates of the two stages are on different axes and
# cannot be compared with each other. Part 2 draws the figures from the tables written:
# diversity/pcoa_css_<unit>_by_stage.csv and permanova_css_<unit>_by_stage.csv.
PCOA_STAGE_UNITS <- c(genus = "bray_css_genus.rds", asv = "bray_css_all_features.rds")
pcoa_by_stage <- function(unit, cache_file) {
    dist_file <- file.path(cache_dir, cache_file)
    if (!file.exists(dist_file)) stop("no cached CSS ", unit, " distances: run chunk beta-diversity-css")
    stage_distance <- as.matrix(readRDS(dist_file))
    stage_md <- as(sample_data(ps), "data.frame")
    if (!all(rownames(stage_distance) %in% rownames(stage_md))) stop("cached distances name unknown samples")
    stage_md <- stage_md[rownames(stage_distance), , drop = FALSE]
    stage_md$Plant_Family <- family_map$Family[match(stage_md$Scientific_Name, family_map$Scientific_Name)]
    pcoa_stage_coords <- purrr::map(config$differential_abundance$groups, function(stage) {
        keep <- !is.na(stage_md[[group_col]]) & stage_md[[group_col]] == stage
        cm <- cmdscale(as.dist(stage_distance[keep, keep]), k = 2, eig = TRUE)
        explained <- 100 * cm$eig[1:2] / sum(cm$eig[cm$eig > 0])
        tibble::tibble(sample_id = rownames(stage_distance)[keep], stage = stage,
                       PCoA1 = cm$points[, 1], PCoA2 = cm$points[, 2],
                       variance_1 = explained[1], variance_2 = explained[2],
                       n_samples = sum(keep),
                       Scientific_Name = stage_md$Scientific_Name[keep],
                       Cultivar = stage_md$Cultivar[keep],
                       Plant_Family = stage_md$Plant_Family[keep],
                       study_alias = stage_md$study_alias[keep])
    }) |> purrr::list_rbind()
    readr::write_csv(pcoa_stage_coords, file.path(diversity_dir, sprintf("pcoa_css_%s_by_stage.csv", unit)))

    # The tests that go with those ordinations: within each stage, how much of the variation
    # does host genus, host species, cultivar (within host species), plant family or study
    # explain (PERMANOVA, each alone)? Dispersion (PERMDISP) is not tested, at the user's
    # request (2026-10-20).
    # Same distances, same number of permutations and seed as the tests on all samples.
    stage_md$host_genus <- sub(" .*$", "", stage_md$Scientific_Name)
    stage_md$cultivar_in_host <- ifelse(
        is.na(stage_md$Cultivar) | stage_md$Cultivar %in% c("", "undefined"), NA,
        sprintf("%s (%s)", stage_md$Cultivar, stage_md$Scientific_Name))
    # host genus, not host species, as the user asked (2026-10-20): the host levels analysed are cultivar, genus and plant family
    # host attributes are plant family and host genus only, at the user's request (2026-10-22)
    stage_terms <- c(host_genus = "Host genus", Plant_Family = "Plant family", study_alias = "Study")
    stage_permutations <- get_config_value(c("analysis", "permutations"), 999)
    pcoa_stage_tests <- purrr::map(config$differential_abundance$groups, function(stage) {
        purrr::imap(stage_terms, function(label, column) {
            keep <- !is.na(stage_md[[group_col]]) & stage_md[[group_col]] == stage &
                !is.na(stage_md[[column]]) & stage_md[[column]] != ""
            groups <- factor(stage_md[[column]][keep])
            if (nlevels(groups) < 2) return(NULL)
            distances <- as.dist(stage_distance[keep, keep])
            set.seed(123)
            fit <- vegan::adonis2(distances ~ groups, permutations = stage_permutations)
            tibble::tibble(stage = stage, term = label, n_samples = sum(keep), n_groups = nlevels(groups),
                           df = fit$Df[1], R2 = fit$R2[1], F = fit$F[1], p = fit$`Pr(>F)`[1])
        }) |> purrr::list_rbind()
    }) |> purrr::list_rbind()
    readr::write_csv(pcoa_stage_tests, file.path(diversity_dir, sprintf("permanova_css_%s_by_stage.csv", unit)))
    cat("  ", unit, "level\n")
    print(as.data.frame(dplyr::mutate(pcoa_stage_tests, dplyr::across(where(is.double), ~ signif(.x, 3)))),
          row.names = FALSE)
    print(as.data.frame(dplyr::distinct(pcoa_stage_coords, stage, n_samples, variance_1, variance_2)),
          row.names = FALSE)
    nrow(pcoa_stage_coords)
}
pcoa_by_stage_result <- tryCatch({
    list(status = "completed", n_samples = purrr::imap(PCOA_STAGE_UNITS, function(file, unit) pcoa_by_stage(unit, file)))
}, error = function(e) {
    message("PCoA by stage error: ", conditionMessage(e))
    list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
})
cat("  PCoA by stage:", pcoa_by_stage_result$status, "\n")
```

#### NMDS Ordination

```{r nmds}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS - | NOT IN THE METHODOLOGY TEXT
#   NMDS ordination
# ==========================================================================================
compute_nmds <- function(ps, group_col = NULL, output_dir) {
    tryCatch({
        dist_bc <- get_beta_distance(ps, "bray", output_dir)

        # NMDS with 2 dimensions, try multiple starts
        set.seed(123)
        nmds_result <- metaMDS(dist_bc, k = 2, try = 50, trymax = 100, trace = 0)

        # Extract scores
        scores_df <- data.frame(
            Sample = rownames(nmds_result$points),
            NMDS1 = nmds_result$points[, 1],
            NMDS2 = nmds_result$points[, 2],
            stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )

        # Add metadata
        if (!is.null(group_col) && group_col %in% colnames(sample_data(ps))) {
            meta_df <- as.data.frame(sample_data(ps))
            scores_df <- merge(scores_df, meta_df, by.x = "Sample", by.y = "row.names", all.x = TRUE)
        }

        # Stress value
        stress <- nmds_result$stress
        cat("NMDS stress:", round(stress, 3), "\n")

        # Plot
        p <- ggplot(scores_df, aes(x = NMDS1, y = NMDS2, color = .data[[group_col]])) +
            geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.95) +
            labs(
                x = "NMDS1",
                y = "NMDS2",
                color = group_col,
                title = paste0("NMDS Ordination (Stress = ", round(stress, 3), ")")
            ) +
            theme_pipeline_classic() +
            theme(legend.position = "right") +
            guides(color = guide_legend(ncol = 1))

        # Save
        save_nature_figure(file.path(output_dir, "nmds_plot.tiff"), p, kind = "standard")
        write.csv(scores_df, file.path(output_dir, "nmds_data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

        # Shepard diagram
        shepard <- Shepard(dist_bc, nmds_result$points)
        p_shep <- plot(shepard, type = "p", pch = 16, cex = 0.7,
                       main = "Shepard Diagram", xlab = "Observed Dissimilarity",
                       ylab = "Ordination Distance")
        ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "nmds_shepard.tiff"),
               recordPlot(), width = 6.5, height = 5.0, dpi = 300)

        list(status = "completed", stress = stress)
    }, error = function(e) {
        message("NMDS error: ", conditionMessage(e))
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

cat("Computing NMDS ordination...\n")
nmds_result <- compute_nmds(ps_beta, group_col, diversity_dir)
cat("  NMDS:", nmds_result$status, "\n")
```

#### PCoA Ordination

```{r pcoa}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS - | NOT IN THE METHODOLOGY TEXT
#   PCoA of raw-count Bray-Curtis and Jaccard dissimilarities
# ==========================================================================================
compute_pcoa <- function(ps, distance_method, output_dir) {
    tryCatch({
        # Calculate distance matrix
        if (distance_method %in% c("unifrac", "wunifrac")) {
            if (is.null(phy_tree(ps, errorIfNULL = FALSE))) {
                return(list(status = "skipped_no_tree"))
            }
            dist_mat <- get_beta_distance(ps, distance_method, output_dir)
        } else if (distance_method == "bray") {
            dist_mat <- get_beta_distance(ps, "bray", output_dir)
        } else if (distance_method == "jaccard") {
            dist_mat <- get_beta_distance(ps, "jaccard", output_dir)
        } else {
            dist_mat <- get_beta_distance(ps, distance_method, output_dir)
        }

        # PCoA
        pcoa_result <- cmdscale(dist_mat, k = 2, eig = TRUE)

        # Extract variance explained
        var_explained <- round(pcoa_result$eig / sum(pcoa_result$eig) * 100, 2)

        # Create data frame for plotting
        pcoa_df <- data.frame(
            Sample = rownames(pcoa_result$points),
            PCoA1 = pcoa_result$points[, 1],
            PCoA2 = pcoa_result$points[, 2],
            stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )

        # Add metadata
        if (!is.null(group_col) && group_col %in% colnames(sample_data(ps))) {
            meta_df <- as.data.frame(sample_data(ps))
            pcoa_df <- merge(pcoa_df, meta_df, by.x = "Sample", by.y = "row.names", all.x = TRUE)
        } else {
            return(list(status = "skipped_no_group"))
        }

        # ── 1. Create a plot with color = Scientific_Name and shape = Developmental_Stage (Beta Diversity) ──
        if ("Scientific_Name" %in% colnames(sample_data(ps)) && "Developmental_Stage" %in% colnames(sample_data(ps))) {
            p_spec <- ggplot(pcoa_df, aes(x = PCoA1, y = PCoA2,
                                          color = Scientific_Name,
                                          shape = Developmental_Stage)) +
                geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.95) +
                scale_shape_manual(values = c(1, 16, 2, 3)) +
                labs(
                    x = paste0("PCoA1 (", var_explained[1], "%)"),
                    y = paste0("PCoA2 (", var_explained[2], "%)"),
                    color = "Plant Species", shape = "Stage",
                    title = paste0("PCoA (", distance_method, ")")
                ) +
                theme_pipeline_classic() +
                theme(
                    legend.position = "right",
                    legend.text = element_text(face = "bold.italic")
                ) +
                guides(color = guide_legend(ncol = 1, order = 1),
                       shape = guide_legend(ncol = 1, order = 2))
            # figure retired: see the beta-diversity-css chunk (CSS, all filtered features)
            if (FALSE) save_nature_figure(
file.path(output_dir, paste0("pcoa_", distance_method, "_species.tiff")),
                               p_spec, kind = "wide")
        }

        # ── 2. Standard PCoA plot using primary group ──
        p <- ggplot(pcoa_df, aes(x = PCoA1, y = PCoA2, color = .data[[group_col]])) +
            geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.95) +
            labs(
                x = paste0("PCoA1 (", var_explained[1], "%)"),
                y = paste0("PCoA2 (", var_explained[2], "%)"),
                color = group_col,
                title = paste0("PCoA (", distance_method, ")")
            ) +
            theme_pipeline_classic() +
            theme(legend.position = "right") +
            guides(color = guide_legend(ncol = 1))

        # Save standard PCoA
        # figure retired: see the beta-diversity-css chunk (CSS, all filtered features)
        if (FALSE) save_nature_figure(
file.path(output_dir, paste0("pcoa_", distance_method, ".tiff")),
                           p, kind = "standard")
        write.csv(pcoa_df, file.path(output_dir, paste0("pcoa_", distance_method, ".csv")), row.names = FALSE)

        list(status = "completed", var_explained = var_explained)
    }, error = function(e) {
        message("PCoA error: ", conditionMessage(e))
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

compute_pcoa_rank <- function(ps, distance_method, output_dir, suffix, title_suffix) {
    tryCatch({
        if (distance_method %in% c("unifrac", "wunifrac")) {
            if (is.null(phy_tree(ps, errorIfNULL = FALSE))) {
                return(list(status = "skipped_no_tree"))
            }
            dist_mat <- get_beta_distance(ps, distance_method, output_dir)
        } else {
            dist_mat <- get_beta_distance(ps, distance_method, output_dir)
        }

        pcoa_result <- cmdscale(dist_mat, k = 2, eig = TRUE)
        var_explained <- round(pcoa_result$eig / sum(pcoa_result$eig) * 100, 2)
        pcoa_df <- data.frame(
            Sample = rownames(pcoa_result$points),
            PCoA1 = pcoa_result$points[, 1],
            PCoA2 = pcoa_result$points[, 2],
            stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )

        if (!is.null(group_col) && group_col %in% colnames(sample_data(ps))) {
            meta_df <- as.data.frame(sample_data(ps))
        pcoa_df <- merge(pcoa_df, meta_df, by.x = "Sample", by.y = "row.names", all.x = TRUE)
        }

        p <- ggplot(pcoa_df, aes(x = PCoA1, y = PCoA2, color = .data[[group_col]])) +
            geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.95) +
            labs(
                x = paste0("PCoA1 (", var_explained[1], "%)"),
                y = paste0("PCoA2 (", var_explained[2], "%)"),
                color = group_col,
                title = paste0("PCoA (", distance_method, ") ", title_suffix)
            ) +
            theme_pipeline_classic() +
            theme(legend.position = "right") +
            guides(color = guide_legend(ncol = 1))

        # figure retired: see the beta-diversity-css chunk (CSS, all filtered features)

        if (FALSE) save_nature_figure(
            file.path(output_dir, paste0("pcoa_", distance_method, "_", suffix, ".tiff")),
            p, kind = "standard"
        )
        write.csv(
            pcoa_df,
            file.path(output_dir, paste0("pcoa_", distance_method, "_", suffix, ".csv")),
            row.names = FALSE
        )

        list(status = "completed", var_explained = var_explained)
    }, error = function(e) {
        message("PCoA rank error: ", conditionMessage(e))
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

# Compute PCoA for different distance methods
distance_methods <- c("bray", "jaccard")
if (!is.null(phy_tree(ps_beta, errorIfNULL = FALSE))) {
    distance_methods <- c(distance_methods, "unifrac", "wunifrac")
}

for (dm in distance_methods) {
    cat("Computing PCoA with", dm, "distance...\n")
    pcoa_result <- compute_pcoa(ps_beta, dm, diversity_dir)
    cat("  PCoA", dm, ":", pcoa_result$status, "\n")
    if (dm %in% c("bray", "jaccard")) {
        cat("Computing PCoA with", dm, "distance at OTUID level...\n")
        pcoa_otuid_result <- compute_pcoa_rank(ps_beta_otuid, dm, diversity_dir, suffix = "otuid", title_suffix = "OTUID level")
        cat("  PCoA", dm, "OTUID:", pcoa_otuid_result$status, "\n")

        cat("Computing PCoA with", dm, "distance at genus level...\n")
        pcoa_genus_result <- compute_pcoa_rank(ps_beta_genus, dm, diversity_dir, suffix = "genus", title_suffix = "Genus level")
        cat("  PCoA", dm, "Genus:", pcoa_genus_result$status, "\n")
    }
}
```

#### Multi-variable Assessment

```{r variable-assessment, results='asis', fig.show='hold', out.width='32%'}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS - | NOT IN THE METHODOLOGY TEXT
#   per-variable screen on raw counts (reported: chunk beta-diversity-css)
# ==========================================================================================
# Host is taken as genus: host genus, not host species, as the user asked (2026-10-20): the host levels analysed are cultivar, genus and plant family.
selected_assessment_vars <- c(
    "Developmental_Stage",
    "Host_Genus",
    "study_alias",
    "Author"
)
ps_assessment <- ps
sample_data(ps_assessment)$Host_Genus <- sub(" .*$", "", sample_data(ps_assessment)$Scientific_Name)

safe_file_label <- function(x) {
    x <- iconv(x, from = "", to = "UTF-8", sub = "")
    x <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", x)
    x <- gsub("^_+|_+$", "", x)
    tolower(x)
}

clean_group_values <- function(x) {
    x <- iconv(as.character(x), from = "", to = "UTF-8", sub = "")
    x[x == "" | is.na(x)] <- NA_character_
    x
}

named_variable_palette <- function(levels, context = "alpha_diversity") {
    levels <- sort(unique(levels))
    pal <- get_palette(length(levels), "wildagain", context)
    if (length(pal) < length(levels)) {
        pal <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(POISON_FROG_GRADIENT)(length(levels))
    }
    names(pal) <- levels
    pal
}

prepare_variable_samples <- function(ps, variable, min_group_n = 3) {
    meta_df <- data.frame(sample_data(ps), stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
    meta_df$sample_id <- rownames(meta_df)
    meta_df$group <- clean_group_values(meta_df[[variable]])
    meta_df <- meta_df[!is.na(meta_df$group), , drop = FALSE]

    group_counts <- meta_df |>
        dplyr::count(group, name = "n") |>
        dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n), group)

    keep_groups <- group_counts$group[group_counts$n >= min_group_n]
    meta_keep <- meta_df[meta_df$group %in% keep_groups, , drop = FALSE]

    list(
        metadata = meta_keep,
        group_counts = group_counts,
        kept_groups = keep_groups,
        status = if (length(keep_groups) >= 2 && nrow(meta_keep) >= 4) "ready" else "skipped_sparse"
    )
}


plot_variable_pcoa <- function(dist_sub, meta_sub, variable, output_dir) {
    safe_var <- safe_file_label(variable)
    pcoa_result <- cmdscale(dist_sub, k = 2, eig = TRUE)
    var_explained <- round(pcoa_result$eig / sum(pcoa_result$eig) * 100, 2)
    pcoa_df <- data.frame(
        sample_id = rownames(pcoa_result$points),
        PCoA1 = pcoa_result$points[, 1],
        PCoA2 = pcoa_result$points[, 2],
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ) |>
        dplyr::left_join(
            meta_sub[, intersect(c("sample_id", "group", "Developmental_Stage"), colnames(meta_sub)), drop = FALSE],
            by = "sample_id"
        )

    n_groups <- dplyr::n_distinct(pcoa_df$group)
    pal <- named_variable_palette(pcoa_df$group, "beta_diversity")

    p <- ggplot(pcoa_df, aes(x = PCoA1, y = PCoA2, color = group)) +
        geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.95) +
        scale_color_manual(values = pal) +
        labs(
            x = paste0("PCoA1 (", var_explained[1], "%)"),
            y = paste0("PCoA2 (", var_explained[2], "%)"),
            color = variable,
            title = paste("Genus-level Bray-Curtis community clustering by", variable)
        ) +
        theme_pipeline_classic() +
        theme(legend.position = "right") +
        guides(color = guide_legend(ncol = 1))

    pcoa_uses_stage_facets <- "Developmental_Stage" %in% colnames(pcoa_df)
    if (pcoa_uses_stage_facets) {
        p <- p + facet_wrap(~Developmental_Stage, nrow = 1)
    }

    pcoa_kind <- if (pcoa_uses_stage_facets) "wide" else "standard"
    # Figures have one home: analysis_results/figures/. Writing the TIFF to output_dir
    # put five uncompressed 12 MB ordinations into diversity/ alongside the data.
    # The coordinate CSV stays in output_dir, where the other diversity data lives.
    save_nature_figure(file.path(figures_dir, paste0("pcoa_bray_genus_by_", safe_var, ".tiff")),
                       p, kind = pcoa_kind)
    readr::write_csv(pcoa_df, file.path(output_dir, paste0("pcoa_bray_genus_by_", safe_var, ".csv")))
}

subset_stage_for_pcoa <- function(meta_df, stages = c("Seeds", "Seedlings")) {
    stage_col <- "Developmental_Stage"
    if (!stage_col %in% colnames(meta_df)) {
        return(meta_df)
    }

    meta_df |>
        dplyr::filter(.data[[stage_col]] %in% stages) |>
        dplyr::mutate(
            Developmental_Stage = factor(.data[[stage_col]], levels = stages)
        )
}

subset_phyloseq_to_stages <- function(ps_obj, stages = c("Seeds", "Seedlings")) {
    stage_col <- "Developmental_Stage"
    if (!stage_col %in% colnames(sample_data(ps_obj))) {
        return(ps_obj)
    }

    ps_sub <- subset_samples(ps_obj, Developmental_Stage %in% c("Seeds", "Seedlings"))
    prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps_sub) > 0, ps_sub)
}

drop_invalid_distance_samples <- function(dist_obj, meta_df) {
    dist_mat <- as.matrix(dist_obj)
    keep_ids <- intersect(rownames(dist_mat), meta_df$sample_id)
    dist_mat <- dist_mat[keep_ids, keep_ids, drop = FALSE]
    meta_df <- meta_df[match(keep_ids, meta_df$sample_id), , drop = FALSE]

    if (nrow(dist_mat) == 0 || nrow(meta_df) == 0) {
        return(list(dist = as.dist(matrix(numeric(0), nrow = 0, ncol = 0)), meta = meta_df))
    }

    bad_rows <- apply(dist_mat, 1, function(x) any(!is.finite(x)))
    bad_groups <- is.na(meta_df$group)
    keep <- !(bad_rows | bad_groups)
    dist_mat <- dist_mat[keep, keep, drop = FALSE]
    meta_df <- meta_df[keep, , drop = FALSE]

    list(dist = as.dist(dist_mat), meta = meta_df)
}

assess_metadata_variable <- function(ps_alpha, variable,
                                     beta_stats_dist, pcoa_bray_dist,
                                     figures_dir, diversity_dir, tables_dir,
                                     min_group_n = 3) {
    use_stage_subset <- variable != "Developmental_Stage"
    ps_alpha_use <- if (use_stage_subset) subset_phyloseq_to_stages(ps_alpha) else ps_alpha

    prepared <- prepare_variable_samples(ps_alpha_use, variable, min_group_n = min_group_n)
    counts_tbl <- prepared$group_counts |>
        dplyr::mutate(variable = variable, kept = group %in% prepared$kept_groups, .before = 1)

    if (prepared$status != "ready") {
        return(list(
            status = prepared$status,
            counts = counts_tbl,
            alpha = tibble::tibble(),
            beta = tibble::tibble()
        ))
    }

    meta_sub <- prepared$metadata
    sample_ids <- meta_sub$sample_id

    rich <- phyloseq::estimate_richness(ps_alpha_use, measures = c("Observed", "Shannon"))
    alpha_df <- data.frame(sample_id = rownames(rich), rich, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::inner_join(
            meta_sub[, intersect(c("sample_id", "group", "Developmental_Stage"), colnames(meta_sub)), drop = FALSE],
            by = "sample_id"
        )

    alpha_tests <- tibble::tibble(
        variable = variable,
        metric = c("Observed", "Shannon"),
        test = "Kruskal-Wallis",
        statistic = c(
            unname(kruskal.test(Observed ~ group, data = alpha_df)$statistic),
            unname(kruskal.test(Shannon ~ group, data = alpha_df)$statistic)
        ),
        p_value = c(
            kruskal.test(Observed ~ group, data = alpha_df)$p.value,
            kruskal.test(Shannon ~ group, data = alpha_df)$p.value
        ),
        n_samples = nrow(alpha_df),
        n_groups = dplyr::n_distinct(alpha_df$group)
    )

    # alpha boxplots removed: alpha diversity is represented by the two richness figures

    beta_sample_ids <- intersect(sample_ids, labels(beta_stats_dist))
    if (length(beta_sample_ids) < 4) {
        return(list(
            status = "skipped_sparse",
            counts = counts_tbl,
            alpha = alpha_tests,
            beta = tibble::tibble()
        ))
    }

    dist_matrix <- as.matrix(beta_stats_dist)
    beta_meta <- data.frame(
        group = factor(meta_sub$group[match(beta_sample_ids, meta_sub$sample_id)]),
        sample_id = beta_sample_ids,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    beta_clean <- drop_invalid_distance_samples(
        as.dist(dist_matrix[beta_sample_ids, beta_sample_ids, drop = FALSE]),
        beta_meta
    )
    dist_sub <- beta_clean$dist
    beta_meta <- beta_clean$meta

    if (nrow(beta_meta) < 4 || dplyr::n_distinct(beta_meta$group) < 2) {
        return(list(
            status = "skipped_sparse",
            counts = counts_tbl,
            alpha = alpha_tests,
            beta = tibble::tibble()
        ))
    }

    n_perm <- config$analysis$permutations
    if (is.null(n_perm)) n_perm <- 999
    set.seed(123)
    permanova_result <- vegan::adonis2(
        dist_sub ~ group,
        data = beta_meta,
        permutations = n_perm,
        parallel = parallel_config$n_threads
    )

    # dispersion (PERMDISP) is not tested, at the user's request (2026-10-20)
    beta_tests <- tibble::tibble(
        variable = variable,
        method = "PERMANOVA",
        distance = "bray_asv",
        statistic = unname(as.data.frame(permanova_result)[1, "F"]),
        r2 = unname(as.data.frame(permanova_result)[1, "R2"]),
        p_value = unname(as.data.frame(permanova_result)[1, "Pr(>F)"]),
        n_samples = length(beta_sample_ids),
        n_groups = dplyr::n_distinct(beta_meta$group)
    )

    pcoa_meta_sub <- subset_stage_for_pcoa(meta_sub)
    pcoa_sample_ids <- intersect(pcoa_meta_sub$sample_id, labels(pcoa_bray_dist))

    if (length(pcoa_sample_ids) < 4 || dplyr::n_distinct(pcoa_meta_sub$group) < 2) {
        return(list(
            status = "completed_no_pcoa",
            counts = counts_tbl,
            alpha = alpha_tests,
            beta = beta_tests
        ))
    }

    pcoa_dist_matrix <- as.matrix(pcoa_bray_dist)
    pcoa_meta_sub <- pcoa_meta_sub[match(pcoa_sample_ids, pcoa_meta_sub$sample_id), , drop = FALSE]
    pcoa_clean <- drop_invalid_distance_samples(
        as.dist(pcoa_dist_matrix[pcoa_sample_ids, pcoa_sample_ids, drop = FALSE]),
        pcoa_meta_sub
    )
    pcoa_dist_sub <- pcoa_clean$dist
    pcoa_meta_sub <- pcoa_clean$meta

    if (nrow(pcoa_meta_sub) < 4 || dplyr::n_distinct(pcoa_meta_sub$group) < 2) {
        return(list(
            status = "completed_no_pcoa",
            counts = counts_tbl,
            alpha = alpha_tests,
            beta = beta_tests
        ))
    }

    plot_variable_pcoa(pcoa_dist_sub, pcoa_meta_sub, variable, diversity_dir)

    list(
        status = "completed",
        counts = counts_tbl,
        alpha = alpha_tests,
        beta = beta_tests
    )
}
```

#### UMAP Representation (wild-again utils/UMAP approach)

```{r umap}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS - | NOT IN THE METHODOLOGY TEXT
#   UMAP ordination
# ==========================================================================================
compute_umap <- function(ps, group_col = NULL, output_dir) {
    if (!requireNamespace("umap", quietly = TRUE)) {
        cat("UMAP package not installed, skipping\n")
        return(list(status = "skipped_no_umap"))
    }

    tryCatch({
        # Transform count data
        otu <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
        if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) {
            otu <- t(otu)
        }

        # Apply CLR transformation
        otu_clr <- microbiome::transform(otu, "clr")

        # Remove NA columns (if any)
        otu_clr <- otu_clr[, colSums(is.na(otu_clr)) == 0]

        # Run UMAP
        umap_result <- umap::umap(otu_clr, n_components = 2)

        # Create data frame
        umap_df <- data.frame(
            Sample = rownames(otu_clr),
            UMAP1 = umap_result$layout[, 1],
            UMAP2 = umap_result$layout[, 2],
            stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )

        # Add metadata
        if (!is.null(group_col) && group_col %in% colnames(sample_data(ps))) {
            meta_df <- as.data.frame(sample_data(ps))
            umap_df <- merge(umap_df, meta_df, by.x = "Sample", by.y = "row.names", all.x = TRUE)
        }

        # Plot
        p <- ggplot(umap_df, aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2, color = .data[[group_col]])) +
            geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.95) +
            labs(
                x = "UMAP1",
                y = "UMAP2",
                color = group_col,
                title = "UMAP Ordination (CLR-transformed)"
            ) +
            theme_pipeline_classic() +
            theme(legend.position = "right") +
            guides(color = guide_legend(ncol = 1))

        # Save
        save_nature_figure(file.path(output_dir, "umap.tiff"), p, kind = "standard")
        write.csv(umap_df, file.path(output_dir, "umap_data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

        list(status = "completed", n_samples = nrow(umap_df))
    }, error = function(e) {
        message("UMAP error: ", conditionMessage(e))
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

if (!is.null(group_col)) {
    cat("Computing UMAP...\n")
    umap_result <- compute_umap(ps_beta, group_col, figures_dir)
    cat("  UMAP:", umap_result$status, "\n")
}
```
