### Differential Abundance Analysis (DESeq2)

```{r deseq2}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 3 | Taxon-stage associations
#   step 1 of 2: DESeq2 screen of ASVs (poscounts size factors)
# ==========================================================================================
run_deseq2 <- function(ps, group_col, g1, g2, output_path) {
    if (!requireNamespace("DESeq2", quietly = TRUE)) {
        return(list(status = "skipped_missing_deseq2"))
    }
    
    tryCatch({
        sd <- data.frame(sample_data(ps), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
        if (!(group_col %in% colnames(sd))) {
            return(list(status = "skipped_no_group_column"))
        }
        
        keep <- sd[[group_col]] %in% c(g1, g2)
        if (sum(keep) < 4) {
            return(list(status = "skipped_too_few_samples"))
        }
        
        ps_sub <- prune_samples(keep, ps)
        # Samples with zero total counts give NA size factors and abort
        # estimateSizeFactors(type = "poscounts") with
        # "all(!is.na(value)) is not TRUE". Three such samples survive filtering here
        # - the same three for which Shannon is undefined (n = 1883, not 1886).
        n_before <- nsamples(ps_sub)
        ps_sub <- prune_samples(sample_sums(ps_sub) > 0, ps_sub)
        n_dropped <- n_before - nsamples(ps_sub)
        if (n_dropped > 0) {
            cat("  dropped", n_dropped, "zero-count sample(s) before DESeq2\n")
        }
        ps_sub <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps_sub) > 0, ps_sub)
        
        sample_data(ps_sub)[[group_col]] <- factor(
            sample_data(ps_sub)[[group_col]],
            levels = c(g2, g1)
        )
        
        # DESeq2 wants countData as features x samples. A phyloseq otu_table may be
        # stored either way, so transpose only when taxa are NOT already the rows -
        # an unconditional t() here silently failed every run with
        # "ncol(countData) == nrow(colData) is not TRUE" and left
        # differential_abundance/ empty.
        otu_mat <- as(otu_table(ps_sub), "matrix")
        if (!taxa_are_rows(ps_sub)) otu_mat <- t(otu_mat)

        dds <- DESeq2::DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
            countData = otu_mat,
            colData = data.frame(sample_data(ps_sub)),
            design = as.formula(paste("~", group_col))
        )
        dds <- DESeq2::estimateSizeFactors(dds, type = "poscounts")
        dds <- DESeq2::DESeq(dds, quiet = TRUE)
        
        res <- DESeq2::results(dds, contrast = c(group_col, g1, g2))
        res_df <- as.data.frame(res)
        res_df$feature_id <- rownames(res_df)
        res_df <- res_df[order(res_df$padj), ]
        
        write.csv(res_df, output_path, row.names = FALSE)
        list(
            status = "completed",
            n_features = nrow(res_df),
            # adjusted p and fold change together, as the screen and the volcano apply them
            n_significant = sum(res_df$padj < get_config_value(c("stage_effects", "deseq2_fdr"), 0.05) &
                                    abs(res_df$log2FoldChange) >
                                        get_config_value(c("stage_effects", "deseq2_min_log2fc"), 1),
                                na.rm = TRUE)
        )
    }, error = function(e) {
        # cat() not message(): the YAML sets `message: false`, so message() output is
        # discarded and a failure here shows only as status "failed" with no reason.
        cat("  DESeq2 error:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

da_groups <- config$differential_abundance$groups
group_col <- config$analysis$primary_group

if (!is.null(da_groups) && length(da_groups) == 2) {
    cat("Running DESeq2 (", da_groups[1], "vs", da_groups[2], ")...\n")
    deseq2_result <- run_deseq2(
        ps, group_col, da_groups[1], da_groups[2],
        file.path(da_dir, "deseq2_results.csv")
    )
    cat("  DESeq2:", deseq2_result$status, "\n")
    if (deseq2_result$status == "completed") {
        cat("  Features:", deseq2_result$n_features, "\n")
        cat("  Significant (padj < 0.05, |log2 fold change| > 1):", deseq2_result$n_significant, "\n")
    }
} else {
    cat("No differential abundance groups specified, skipping DESeq2\n")
    deseq2_result <- list(status = "skipped_no_groups")
}
```

### Volcano Plot (DESeq2 Results)

```{r volcano-plot}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 3 | Taxon-stage associations
#   step 1 of 2: volcano plot of the DESeq2 screen
# ==========================================================================================
plot_volcano <- function(ps, deseq2_result, da_dir, figures_dir) {
    if (is.null(deseq2_result) || deseq2_result$status != "completed") {
        return(list(status = "skipped_no_deseq2"))
    }

    tryCatch({
        res_path <- file.path(da_dir, "deseq2_results.csv")
        if (!file.exists(res_path)) {
            return(list(status = "skipped_no_results_file"))
        }

        res_df <- readr::read_csv(res_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

        # Add genus labels from taxonomy
        tax_df <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
        res_df <- res_df |>
            dplyr::mutate(
                genus = dplyr::if_else(
                    feature_id %in% rownames(tax_df),
                    tax_df[feature_id, "Genus"],
                    feature_id
                ),
                genus = dplyr::if_else(is.na(genus) | genus == "", feature_id, genus)
            )

        # Classify direction
        res_df <- res_df |>
            dplyr::mutate(
                direction = dplyr::case_when(
                    is.na(padj) ~ "NS",
                    padj >= 0.05 ~ "NS",
                    log2FoldChange > 1 ~ "Up",
                    log2FoldChange < -1 ~ "Down",
                    .default = "NS"
                ),
                direction = factor(direction, levels = c("Up", "Down", "NS"))
            )

        # up is higher in seedlings, down higher in seeds: the two stage colours
        direction_colors <- c("Up" = FIGURE_PALETTE$seedlings, "Down" = FIGURE_PALETTE$seeds, "NS" = "grey70")

        # Top significant taxa for labelling
        top_sig <- res_df |>
            dplyr::filter(direction != "NS") |>
            dplyr::arrange(padj) |>
            head(15)

        p <- ggplot(res_df, aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(padj), color = direction)) +
            geom_point(alpha = 0.95, size = 1.5) +
            geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
            geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
            scale_color_manual(values = direction_colors) +
            ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
                data = top_sig,
                aes(label = genus),
                size = 3, max.overlaps = 20, show.legend = FALSE
            ) +
            labs(
                x = "log2 Fold Change",
                y = "-log10(adjusted p-value)",
                color = "Direction",
                title = "Volcano Plot (DESeq2)"
            ) +
            theme_pipeline_classic() +
            theme(legend.position = "bottom")

        save_nature_figure(file.path(figures_dir, "volcano_deseq2.tiff"),
                           p, kind = "standard")

        n_up <- sum(res_df$direction == "Up", na.rm = TRUE)
        n_down <- sum(res_df$direction == "Down", na.rm = TRUE)
        cat("  Volcano plot: Up =", n_up, ", Down =", n_down, "\n")

        list(status = "completed", n_up = n_up, n_down = n_down)
    }, error = function(e) {
        message("Volcano plot error: ", conditionMessage(e))
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

cat("Generating volcano plot...\n")
volcano_result <- plot_volcano(ps, deseq2_result, da_dir, figures_dir)
cat("  Volcano:", volcano_result$status, "\n")
```

### ANCOM-BC2 Differential Abundance

```{r ancombc}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS - | NOT IN THE METHODOLOGY TEXT
#   ANCOM-BC2
# ==========================================================================================
run_ancombc2 <- function(ps, group_col, output_path) {
    if (!requireNamespace("microbiomeMarker", quietly = TRUE)) {
        return(list(status = "skipped_missing_package"))
    }

    tryCatch({
        sd <- data.frame(sample_data(ps), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
        if (!(group_col %in% colnames(sd))) {
            return(list(status = "skipped_no_group_column"))
        }

        groups <- unique(na.omit(sd[[group_col]]))
        if (length(groups) < 2) {
            return(list(status = "skipped_fewer_than_2_groups"))
        }

        # Run ANCOM-BC2
        ancom_result <- microbiomeMarker::run_ancombc2(
            ps,
            group = group_col,
            p_adj_cutoff = 0.05,
            pairwise = FALSE
        )

        # Extract results
        res_df <- as.data.frame(microbiomeMarker::marker_table(ancom_result))

        if (nrow(res_df) > 0) {
            # Add taxonomy labels
            tax_df <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
            res_df <- res_df |>
                dplyr::mutate(
                    genus = dplyr::if_else(
                        feature %in% rownames(tax_df),
                        tax_df[feature, "Genus"],
                        feature
                    ),
                    genus = dplyr::if_else(is.na(genus) | genus == "", feature, genus)
                )
        }

        readr::write_csv(res_df, output_path)

        list(
            status = "completed",
            n_features = nrow(res_df),
            n_significant = sum(res_df$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
        )
    }, error = function(e) {
        message("ANCOM-BC2 error: ", conditionMessage(e))
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

cat("Running ANCOM-BC2...\n")

        ps, group_col,
        file.path(da_dir, "ancombc2_results.csv")
    )
    cat("  ANCOM-BC2:", ancombc_result$status, "\n")
    if (ancombc_result$status == "completed") {
        cat("  Significant features:", ancombc_result$n_significant, "\n")
    }
} else {
    ancombc_result <- list(status = "skipped_no_group")
}
```

### Stage effect within each plant family and cultivar

```{r stage-effects-by-stratum}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 3 | Taxon-stage associations
#   step 2 of 2: CLR, Hedges' g per plant family and cultivar, random-effects pooling
# ==========================================================================================
# Does a genus shift between seeds and seedlings in the same direction in every plant
# family, and in every cultivar? The indicator analysis and DESeq2 above pool all samples.
# Here the stage difference is estimated inside each stratum (a plant family, or a
# cultivar) that has both stages, and the per-stratum estimates are then pooled.
#
# Genera: those holding an ASV that both DESeq2 and the indicator analysis call
#   stage-associated (the consensus of the two pooled methods).
# Abundance: centred log-ratio of genus counts within each sample, so that the comparison
#   is not driven by the other genera in the sample.
# Per stratum: Hedges' g, seedlings minus seeds (metafor::escalc, measure "SMD"), where the
#   genus is detected in at least `min_prevalence` of the stratum's samples.
# Pooled: random-effects meta-analysis (REML) with a t-based test, BH-FDR over genera.
#   Plant families span studies, so they are pooled as independent (Knapp-Hartung).
#   Cultivars sit inside studies - several cultivars of one study share its laboratory and
#   sequencing run - so for a variable listed in `strata_nested_in_study` a random effect
#   of study is added above that of stratum (metafor::rma.mv), which stops cultivars of
#   one study being counted as independent evidence.
#   A variable listed in `strata_within_host` is taken within host species: "sativus" is
#   the cultivar label of both a carrot and a radish in the metadata, and pooled under the
#   one name they would be compared as if they were one plant.
#
# Sensitivity: each pooled estimate is refitted with every stratum left out in turn. Two
#   cultivars of one study hold most of the samples and a few small strata give extreme
#   effects, so the question is whether any single stratum carries a result. The pooled
#   table records the range of the leave-one-out estimates and how often the sign flips or
#   the 95% interval moves on or off zero.
#
# What this does NOT do: remove study. A plant family's seeds and seedlings can come from
# different studies; the per-stratum table records how many studies supplied each stage
# and how many supplied both, so that such strata can be told apart.
perform_stage_effects <- function(ps, group_col, stage_levels, study_col, host_col, family_map,
                                  strata, nested_in_study, within_host, excluded_levels, deseq_path,
                                  indicator_path, tables_dir, deseq_fdr, deseq_lfc,
                                  min_samples, min_prevalence, pseudocount, min_strata) {
    needed <- c(deseq_path, indicator_path)
    if (any(!file.exists(needed))) {
        cat("Stage effects: skipped - missing",
            paste(basename(needed[!file.exists(needed)]), collapse = ", "), "\n")
        return(list(status = "skipped_no_input"))
    }
    if (!requireNamespace("metafor", quietly = TRUE)) {
        cat("Stage effects: skipped - metafor is not installed\n")
        return(list(status = "skipped_no_metafor"))
    }
    tryCatch({
        meta_df <- as(sample_data(ps), "data.frame")
        # plant family is not in the metadata; it follows from the host species
        if (!"Plant_Family" %in% names(meta_df)) {
            meta_df$Plant_Family <- family_map$Family[match(meta_df[[host_col]],
                                                            family_map$Scientific_Name)]
        }
        # host genus, the other host attribute stratified by: the first word of the host species
        meta_df$Host_Genus <- sub(" .*$", "", meta_df[[host_col]])
        stage <- factor(meta_df[[group_col]], levels = stage_levels)
        study <- as.character(meta_df[[study_col]])

        otu <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
        if (!taxa_are_rows(ps)) otu <- t(otu)
        tax <- as(tax_table(ps), "matrix")
        genus <- tax[, "Genus"]
        named <- !is.na(genus) & genus != "" &
            !grepl("^(Unassigned|unidentified|uncultured|metagenome)$", genus, ignore.case = TRUE)
        counts <- rowsum(otu[named, , drop = FALSE], genus[named])      # genus x sample
        log_counts <- log(counts + pseudocount)
        clr <- sweep(log_counts, 2, colMeans(log_counts))
        mean_rel <- rowMeans(sweep(counts, 2, pmax(colSums(otu), 1), "/"))

        deseq_all <- readr::read_csv(deseq_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
        deseq <- dplyr::filter(deseq_all, !is.na(padj), padj < deseq_fdr,
                               abs(log2FoldChange) > deseq_lfc)
        indicator <- readr::read_csv(indicator_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
        consensus <- intersect(deseq$feature_id, indicator$taxon_id)
        # step one, the screen: every ASV with what each method said of it
        readr::write_csv(
            deseq_all |>
                dplyr::transmute(
                    ASV = feature_id, Genus = unname(genus[feature_id]), log2FoldChange, padj,
                    deseq2 = feature_id %in% deseq$feature_id,
                    # looked up before `indicator` becomes a column of this table
                    indicator_stage = indicator$group[match(feature_id, indicator$taxon_id)],
                    indicator_value = indicator$stat[match(feature_id, indicator$taxon_id)],
                    indicator = !is.na(indicator_value),
                    screen = dplyr::case_when(deseq2 & indicator ~ "Both",
                                              deseq2 ~ "DESeq2 only",
                                              indicator ~ "Indicator analysis only",
                                              TRUE ~ "Neither")),
            file.path(tables_dir, "stage_screen_asvs.csv"))
        candidates <- sort(unique(genus[intersect(consensus, names(genus)[named])]))
        cat(sprintf("Consensus ASVs: %d, in %d genera\n", length(consensus), length(candidates)))

        # total heterogeneity as a share of total variance, for either kind of model
        i_squared <- function(fit, variance) {
            w <- 1 / variance
            typical <- (length(w) - 1) * sum(w) / (sum(w)^2 - sum(w^2))
            between <- if (inherits(fit, "rma.mv")) sum(fit$sigma2) else fit$tau2
            100 * between / (between + typical)
        }

        one_variable <- function(variable) {
            if (!variable %in% names(meta_df)) {
                cat("  ", variable, ": skipped - not in the metadata\n")
                return(NULL)
            }
            stratum <- as.character(meta_df[[variable]])
            stratum[is.na(stratum) | stratum == "" | stratum %in% excluded_levels] <- NA
            if (variable %in% within_host) {
                stratum <- ifelse(is.na(stratum), NA, sprintf("%s (%s)", stratum, meta_df[[host_col]]))
            }
            usable <- names(which(tapply(stage, stratum, function(x) all(table(x) >= min_samples))))
            if (length(usable) < min_strata) {
                cat("  ", variable, ": skipped - fewer than", min_strata, "levels with both stages\n")
                return(NULL)
            }
            nested <- variable %in% nested_in_study
            per_stratum <- purrr::map(usable, function(level) {
                inside <- !is.na(stratum) & stratum == level
                seeds <- inside & stage == stage_levels[1]
                seedlings <- inside & stage == stage_levels[2]
                prevalence <- rowMeans(counts[candidates, inside, drop = FALSE] > 0)
                keep <- candidates[prevalence >= min_prevalence]
                if (!length(keep)) return(NULL)
                es <- metafor::escalc(
                    measure = "SMD",
                    m1i = rowMeans(clr[keep, seedlings, drop = FALSE]),
                    sd1i = apply(clr[keep, seedlings, drop = FALSE], 1, stats::sd),
                    n1i = rep(sum(seedlings), length(keep)),
                    m2i = rowMeans(clr[keep, seeds, drop = FALSE]),
                    sd2i = apply(clr[keep, seeds, drop = FALSE], 1, stats::sd),
                    n2i = rep(sum(seeds), length(keep)))
                tibble::tibble(
                    Genus = keep, stratum = level,
                    plant_family = paste(sort(unique(meta_df$Plant_Family[inside])), collapse = "; "),
                    main_study = names(which.max(table(study[inside]))),
                    n_seeds = sum(seeds), n_seedlings = sum(seedlings),
                    studies_with_seeds = dplyr::n_distinct(study[seeds]),
                    studies_with_seedlings = dplyr::n_distinct(study[seedlings]),
                    studies_with_both = length(intersect(study[seeds], study[seedlings])),
                    prevalence = unname(prevalence[keep]),
                    hedges_g = as.numeric(es$yi), variance = as.numeric(es$vi))
            }) |> purrr::list_rbind() |>
                dplyr::filter(is.finite(hedges_g), is.finite(variance), variance > 0) |>
                dplyr::mutate(ci_low = hedges_g - stats::qnorm(0.975) * sqrt(variance),
                              ci_high = hedges_g + stats::qnorm(0.975) * sqrt(variance))

            pool <- function(d) {
                # a study level needs at least one study with two strata to be estimable
                with_study <- nested && dplyr::n_distinct(d$main_study) < nrow(d) &&
                    dplyr::n_distinct(d$main_study) > 1
                fit <- if (with_study) {
                    metafor::rma.mv(yi = hedges_g, V = variance, data = d, method = "REML",
                                    random = ~ 1 | main_study / stratum, test = "t")
                } else {
                    metafor::rma(yi = d$hedges_g, vi = d$variance, method = "REML", test = "knha")
                }
                list(fit = fit, with_study = with_study)
            }
            by_genus <- per_stratum |>
                dplyr::filter(dplyr::n() >= min_strata, .by = Genus) |>
                dplyr::group_split(Genus)

            # leave-one-out: only where enough strata remain to pool
            leave_one_out <- by_genus |>
                purrr::keep(function(d) nrow(d) > min_strata) |>
                purrr::map(function(d) {
                    purrr::map(seq_len(nrow(d)), function(i) {
                        fit <- tryCatch(pool(d[-i, ])$fit, error = function(e) NULL)
                        if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)
                        tibble::tibble(Genus = d$Genus[1], omitted_stratum = d$stratum[i],
                                       pooled_g = fit$b[1], ci_low = fit$ci.lb,
                                       ci_high = fit$ci.ub, p = fit$pval)
                    }) |> purrr::list_rbind()
                }) |> purrr::list_rbind()

            pooled <- by_genus |>
                purrr::map(function(d) {
                    fitted <- pool(d)
                    fit <- fitted$fit
                    with_study <- fitted$with_study
                    tibble::tibble(Genus = d$Genus[1], n_strata = nrow(d),
                                   n_studies = dplyr::n_distinct(d$main_study),
                                   n_strata_same_direction = sum(sign(d$hedges_g) == sign(fit$b[1])),
                                   pooled_g = fit$b[1], ci_low = fit$ci.lb, ci_high = fit$ci.ub,
                                   p = fit$pval, i2 = i_squared(fit, d$variance),
                                   model = if (with_study) "study / stratum" else "stratum")
                }) |> purrr::list_rbind() |>
                dplyr::mutate(q = stats::p.adjust(p, method = "BH"),
                              Phylum = unname(tax[match(Genus, genus), "Phyla"]),
                              mean_relative_abundance_pct = 100 * unname(mean_rel[Genus])) |>
                dplyr::left_join(
                    leave_one_out |>
                        dplyr::summarise(loo_g_min = min(pooled_g), loo_g_max = max(pooled_g),
                                         loo_excludes_zero = sum(ci_low > 0 | ci_high < 0),
                                         loo_fits = dplyr::n(), .by = Genus),
                    dplyr::join_by(Genus)) |>
                dplyr::mutate(loo_sign_stable = sign(loo_g_min) == sign(loo_g_max) &
                                  sign(loo_g_min) == sign(pooled_g)) |>
                dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(pooled_g))

            tag <- tolower(variable)
            readr::write_csv(leave_one_out,
                             file.path(tables_dir, sprintf("stage_effect_leave_one_out_by_%s_genus.csv", tag)))
            readr::write_csv(per_stratum, file.path(tables_dir, sprintf("stage_effect_by_%s_genus.csv", tag)))
            readr::write_csv(pooled, file.path(tables_dir, sprintf("stage_effect_pooled_by_%s_genus.csv", tag)))
            cat(sprintf("  %s: %d levels with both stages; %d genera pooled; significant at FDR < 0.05: %d\n",
                        variable, length(usable), nrow(pooled), sum(pooled$q < 0.05)))
            nrow(pooled)
        }
        cat("\n=== Stage effect within plant family and cultivar (genus level) ===\n")
        done <- purrr::compact(purrr::map(purrr::set_names(strata), one_variable))
        if (!length(done)) return(list(status = "skipped_design"))
        list(status = "completed", n_genera = unlist(done))
    }, error = function(e) {
        cat("  Stage effects error:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

cat("Running stage effects within plant family and host genus...\n")
if (!is.null(group_col)) {
    se_cfg <- function(key, default) get_config_value(c("stage_effects", key), default)
    stage_effects_result <- perform_stage_effects(
        ps, group_col,
        stage_levels = get_config_value(c("differential_abundance", "groups"), NULL),
        study_col = get_config_value(c("generalist_specialist", "study_group"), "study_alias"),
        host_col = get_config_value(c("generalist_specialist", "host_group"), "Scientific_Name"),
        family_map = family_map,
        strata = se_cfg("strata", c("Plant_Family", "Host_Genus")),
        nested_in_study = se_cfg("strata_nested_in_study", "Host_Genus"),
        within_host = se_cfg("strata_within_host", character()),
        excluded_levels = se_cfg("strata_excluded_levels", "undefined"),
        deseq_path = file.path(da_dir, "deseq2_results.csv"),
        indicator_path = file.path(tables_dir, "indicator_species_significant.csv"),
        tables_dir = tables_dir,
        deseq_fdr = se_cfg("deseq2_fdr", 0.05), deseq_lfc = se_cfg("deseq2_min_log2fc", 1),
        min_samples = se_cfg("min_samples_per_stage", 3),
        min_prevalence = se_cfg("min_prevalence", 0.1),
        pseudocount = se_cfg("clr_pseudocount", 0.5), min_strata = se_cfg("min_strata", 2))
    cat("  Stage effects:", stage_effects_result$status, "\n")
}
```

### Analyses that live in their own scripts

```{r external-analyses}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 4, 7, 8 | see the parts marked below
#   runs the standalone scripts; each call below is marked with its paragraph
# ==========================================================================================
# Host phylogenetic signal, phylosymbiosis, the generalist and specialist trees, predicted
# traits, predicted gene content, the special groups and the iTOL files each live in a
# script of their own. They are run from here, in dependency order, so that one render of
# this document writes every table and tree that Part 2 draws. The scripts stay the one
# home of their code: nothing is copied into this document.
#
# A step is skipped, not failed, when its script, an input, a program or a package is
# absent - the degrade-don't-fail rule of the Python pipeline's R sidecar. Several steps
# take half an hour to an hour (IQ-TREE, the marginal PERMANOVA, PICRUSt2), so a step is
# rerun only when its script or an input has changed: the MD5 sums of both are kept in
# cache/external_<step>.md5 beside the step's log. Outputs found without such a record
# are adopted as they stand. `external_analyses.force` in the config reruns everything;
# `external_analyses.run: false` (the smoke config) skips the lot.
external_cfg <- function(key, default) get_config_value(c("external_analyses", key), default)
external_tools <- Sys.getenv("SEEDLING_TOOLS_BIN",
                             file.path(path.expand("~"), ".local/share/seedling_tools/bin"))
external_picrust <- Sys.getenv("PICRUST2_BIN",
                               file.path(dirname(external_tools), "miniforge3/envs/picrust2/bin"))
has_program <- function(x) {
    nzchar(Sys.which(x)) || any(file.exists(file.path(c(external_tools, external_picrust), x)))
}
config_file <- normalizePath(config_path)
out <- function(...) file.path(output_dir, ...)
input_file <- function(key) {
    if (is.null(config$inputs[[key]])) NA_character_ else resolve_path(base_dir, config$inputs[[key]])
}
resource <- function(...) {
    file.path(resolve_path(base_dir, get_config_value(c("predicted_traits", "resources_dir"),
                                                      "resources")), ...)
}

run_external <- function(name, script, inputs, outputs, programs = character(),
                         packages = character()) {
    status <- function(state, detail = "") tibble::tibble(step = name, status = state, detail = detail)
    script_path <- file.path(base_dir, script)
    if (!file.exists(script_path)) return(status("skipped", paste("no script:", script)))
    missing <- inputs[is.na(inputs) | !file.exists(inputs)]
    if (length(missing)) {
        return(status("skipped", paste("missing input:", paste(basename(missing), collapse = ", "))))
    }
    absent <- c(programs[!vapply(programs, has_program, logical(1))],
                packages[!vapply(packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)])
    if (length(absent)) return(status("skipped", paste("not installed:", paste(absent, collapse = ", "))))

    stamp <- file.path(cache_dir, sprintf("external_%s.md5", name))
    signature <- unname(tools::md5sum(c(script_path, inputs)))
    if (all(file.exists(outputs)) && !isTRUE(external_cfg("force", FALSE))) {
        if (!file.exists(stamp)) {
            writeLines(signature, stamp)
            return(status("adopted", "outputs already present; inputs recorded"))
        }
        if (identical(readLines(stamp), signature)) return(status("up to date"))
    }
    extension <- tools::file_ext(script)
    interpreter <- switch(extension, R = file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"),
                          py = Sys.which("python3"), sh = "bash")
    arguments <- if (extension == "sh") c(script_path, config_file) else
        c(script_path, "--config", config_file)
    log <- file.path(cache_dir, sprintf("external_%s.log", name))
    started <- Sys.time()
    exit_code <- system2(interpreter, shQuote(arguments), stdout = log, stderr = log)
    minutes <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), started, units = "mins"))
    if (exit_code != 0 || !all(file.exists(outputs))) {
        return(status("failed", paste("see", file.path("cache", basename(log)))))
    }
    writeLines(signature, stamp)
    status("completed", sprintf("%.1f min", minutes))
}

if (!isTRUE(external_cfg("run", TRUE))) {
    cat("Analyses in their own scripts: not run (external_analyses.run is false)\n")
} else {
    screen_asvs <- out("tables", "generalist_specialist_asv_host_screen.csv")
    traits_asv <- out("tables", "predicted_traits_asv.csv")
    host_table <- out("tables", "host_plant_species.csv")
    host_tree <- out("tables", "host_phylosignal_tree.nwk")
    ps_clean_file <- out("setup", "ps_clean.rds")
    tree_of <- function(group) out("trees", group, "tree.nwk")
    # in dependency order: a step's outputs are the inputs of later ones
    external_status <- dplyr::bind_rows(
        # METHODS 4 | Blomberg's K and Pagel's lambda
        run_external("host_phylosignal", "host_phylosignal.R",
                     inputs = c(out("tables", "rarefied_alpha_diversity.csv"), input_file("host_tree")),
                     outputs = c(out("tables", "host_phylosignal.csv"), host_tree,
                                 out("tables", "host_phylosignal_species_means.csv"))),
        # METHODS 4 | Mantel, MRM, marginal PERMANOVA, variance partitioning
        run_external("host_phylosymbiosis", "host_phylosymbiosis.R",
                     inputs = c(out("cache", "bray_css_genus.rds"),
                                out("cache", "bray_css_all_features.rds"), ps_clean_file,
                                host_tree, host_table),
                     outputs = out("tables", c("host_phylosymbiosis_tests.csv",
                                               "host_phylosymbiosis_pairs.csv",
                                               "host_beta_permanova.csv",
                                               "host_beta_variance_partition.csv"))),
        # METHODS 7 | alignment and maximum-likelihood trees
        run_external("generalist_specialist_trees", "generalist_specialist_trees.sh",
                     inputs = c(screen_asvs, input_file("rep_seqs")),
                     outputs = c(tree_of(c("generalists", "specialists", "combined")),
                                 out("trees", "tree_build_summary.csv")),
                     programs = c("muscle", "mafft", "trimal", "iqtree3", "FastTree")),
        # METHODS 8 | BugBase, FAPROTAX, metaTraits
        run_external("predicted_traits", "predicted_traits.py",
                     inputs = c(screen_asvs, input_file("rep_seqs"), input_file("taxonomy"),
                                resource("greengenes", "gg_13_8_otus", "rep_set", "97_otus.fasta"),
                                resource("bugbase", "default_traits_precalculated.txt.gz"),
                                resource("faprotax", "FAPROTAX_1.2.12", "FAPROTAX.txt"),
                                resource("metatraits", "gtdb_genus_summary_all.tsv.gz")),
                     outputs = c(traits_asv, out("tables", "predicted_traits_catalogue.csv")),
                     programs = "vsearch"),
        # METHODS 8 | traits against host breadth
        run_external("predicted_trait_tests", "predicted_trait_tests.R",
                     inputs = c(traits_asv, out("tables", "predicted_traits_catalogue.csv"), screen_asvs),
                     outputs = out("tables", "predicted_trait_breadth_tests.csv")),
        # METHODS 8 | PICRUSt2 KEGG orthologue prediction
        run_external("ko_predict", "ko_predict.sh",
                     inputs = c(screen_asvs, input_file("rep_seqs")),
                     outputs = out("picrust2", c("bac_KO_predicted.tsv.gz",
                                                 "combined_marker_predicted_and_nsti.tsv.gz")),
                     programs = "picrust2_pipeline.py"),
        # METHODS 8 | orthologues against host breadth; KEGG and PGPg
        run_external("ko_breadth_tests", "ko_breadth_tests.R",
                     inputs = c(out("picrust2", c("bac_KO_predicted.tsv.gz",
                                                  "combined_marker_predicted_and_nsti.tsv.gz")),
                                screen_asvs, resource("kegg", "ko00001.json"),
                                resource("pgpg", "pathways_plabase.txt")),
                     outputs = out("tables", c("ko_breadth_tests.csv", "ko_enrichment_summary.csv"))),
        # METHODS 8 | anaerobic, nitrogen-fixing, small-genome groups
        run_external("special_groups", "special_groups.R",
                     inputs = c(ps_clean_file, traits_asv, screen_asvs, host_table),
                     outputs = out("tables", c("special_group_summary.csv",
                                               "special_group_heatmap_matrix.csv",
                                               "special_group_host_order_tests.csv"))),
        # METHODS 8 | traits, orthologue categories and special groups between the stages
        run_external("functional_stage_effects", "functional_stage_effects.R",
                     inputs = c(ps_clean_file, traits_asv, host_table,
                                out("tables", c("predicted_trait_breadth_tests.csv",
                                                "ko_breadth_tests.csv",
                                                "special_group_sample_abundance.csv")),
                                out("picrust2", c("bac_KO_predicted.tsv.gz",
                                                  "combined_marker_predicted_and_nsti.tsv.gz"))),
                     outputs = out("tables", paste0(rep(c("predicted_trait", "ko_category",
                                                           "special_group"), each = 2),
                                                     "_stage_effect_",
                                                     c("by_plant_family", "pooled"), ".csv")),
                     packages = "metafor"),
        # METHODS - | NOT IN THE METHODOLOGY TEXT: iTOL annotation files (trees are drawn in R)
        run_external("generalist_specialist_itol", "generalist_specialist_itol.R",
                     inputs = c(tree_of(c("generalists", "specialists")), screen_asvs, traits_asv,
                                host_table, ps_clean_file),
                     outputs = out("itol", c("generalists", "specialists"), "tree.nwk"),
                     packages = "itol.toolkit"))
    readr::write_csv(external_status, file.path(tables_dir, "external_analyses_status.csv"))
    knitr::kable(external_status, caption = "Analyses run from their own scripts")
}
```

### Co-occurrence Network

```{r cooccurrence-network}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 2 | Diversity, composition and co-occurrence
#   co-occurrence: Spearman network of the 50 most abundant ASVs of each developmental stage
# ==========================================================================================
# One network for seeds and one for seedlings, at the user's request (2026-10-20): within
# each stage, the 50 ASVs with the highest mean relative abundance in that stage, Spearman
# correlations between every pair across that stage's samples, Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted
# within the stage; an edge is |rho| >= 0.6 at adjusted p < 0.05. Samples left with no
# reads by the filter have no composition and are left out. The edges of both stages are
# written to one table (tables/cooccurrence_edges.csv) with a `stage` column; Part 2 draws
# the figure (chunk `fx-fig-cooccurrence`).
build_cooccurrence_network <- function(ps, group_col, top_n = 50, rho_threshold = 0.6, p_threshold = 0.05,
                                       tables_dir) {
    tryCatch({
        otu <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
        if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) otu <- t(otu)                      # samples x ASVs
        otu <- otu[rowSums(otu) > 0, , drop = FALSE]
        rel <- sweep(otu, 1, rowSums(otu), "/")
        stage_of <- as(sample_data(ps), "data.frame")[rownames(rel), group_col]
        tax_df <- as.data.frame(as(tax_table(ps), "matrix"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
        stages <- get_config_value(c("differential_abundance", "groups"), sort(unique(stage_of)))
        edges <- purrr::map(stages, function(stage) {
            r <- rel[!is.na(stage_of) & stage_of == stage, , drop = FALSE]
            m <- r[, order(colMeans(r), decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(min(top_n, ncol(r)))], drop = FALSE]
            ids <- colnames(m)
            genus <- tax_df[ids, "Genus"]
            genus[is.na(genus) | genus == ""] <- ids[is.na(genus) | genus == ""]
            pairs <- utils::combn(ncol(m), 2)
            tests <- apply(pairs, 2, function(ij) {
                ct <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(m[, ij[1]], m[, ij[2]], method = "spearman", exact = FALSE))
                c(unname(ct$estimate), ct$p.value)
            })
            tibble::tibble(stage = stage, taxon1 = genus[pairs[1, ]], taxon2 = genus[pairs[2, ]],
                           taxon1_id = ids[pairs[1, ]], taxon2_id = ids[pairs[2, ]],
                           rho = tests[1, ], p_value = tests[2, ], n_samples = nrow(m)) |>
                dplyr::mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")) |>
                dplyr::filter(!is.na(rho), abs(rho) >= rho_threshold, p_adj < p_threshold)
        }) |> purrr::list_rbind()
        readr::write_csv(edges, file.path(tables_dir, "cooccurrence_edges.csv"))
        summary <- dplyr::summarise(edges, edges = dplyr::n(), asvs = dplyr::n_distinct(c(taxon1_id, taxon2_id)),
                                    samples = dplyr::first(n_samples), .by = stage)
        print(as.data.frame(summary), row.names = FALSE)
        list(status = "completed", n_edges = nrow(edges))
    }, error = function(e) {
        message("Co-occurrence network error: ", conditionMessage(e))
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

cat("Building co-occurrence networks, one per developmental stage...\n")
cooccurrence_result <- build_cooccurrence_network(ps, group_col, top_n = 50, rho_threshold = 0.6,
                                                  p_threshold = 0.05, tables_dir = tables_dir)
cat("  Co-occurrence:", cooccurrence_result$status, "\n")
```

### Rarefaction Curves

```{r rarefaction}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS - | NOT IN THE METHODOLOGY TEXT
#   rarefaction curves
# ==========================================================================================
rarefaction_curves <- function(ps, output_path, n_depths = 10) {
    tryCatch({
        otu <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
        if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) otu <- t(otu)

        max_depth <- max(rowSums(otu))
        min_depth <- min(rowSums(otu))
        
        cat("  Sequencing depth range:", min_depth, "-", max_depth, "\n")
        
        # Use 10% of max depth as minimum, or 100, whichever is smaller
        start_depth <- max(10, min(min_depth, 100))
        depths <- unique(round(seq(start_depth, max_depth, length.out = n_depths)))

        results <- list()
        for (d in depths) {
            for (i in seq_len(nrow(otu))) {
                samp_counts <- otu[i, ]
                total <- sum(samp_counts)
                if (total < d) next

                rarefied <- rarefy(samp_counts, sample = d)
                results[[length(results) + 1]] <- data.frame(
                    sample_id = rownames(otu)[i],
                    depth = d,
                    expected_richness = as.numeric(rarefied),
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
                )
            }
        }

        if (length(results) > 0) {
            rare_df <- purrr::list_rbind(results)
            write.csv(rare_df, output_path, row.names = FALSE)
            list(status = "completed", n_points = nrow(rare_df))
        } else {
            list(status = "skipped_no_data")
        }
    }, error = function(e) {
        message("Rarefaction error: ", conditionMessage(e))
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

cat("Computing rarefaction curves...\n")
rarefaction_result <- rarefaction_curves(
    ps, file.path(diversity_dir, "rarefaction_data.csv")
)
cat("  Rarefaction:", rarefaction_result$status, "\n")
```

### Performance Benchmark (run manually)

Times the two operations that dominate this pipeline's runtime on the current machine:
symmetric eigendecomposition (BLAS-bound; `betadisper` and PCoA) and `adonis2` at several
thread counts. It is **not run during a normal render** (`eval = FALSE`), because it
competes with the analysis for CPU. Run the chunk interactively when the machine is idle,
then set `analysis.threads` in `analysis_config.json` to the fastest row.

```{r performance-benchmark, eval = FALSE}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS - | support code (no analysis)
#   timing benchmark (not evaluated)
# ==========================================================================================
# Measure the two things that dominate this pipeline's runtime, so tuning decisions
# rest on numbers from this machine rather than on general advice.
#
#   Rscript tools/benchmark_performance.R [n_samples]
#
# Run it when nothing else heavy is running - a concurrent render will skew every
# timing here. Default n is 1886, the sample count of the real filtered object.

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
    library(vegan)
})

n <- 1886L   # sample count of the filtered object

si <- sessionInfo()
cat("== environment ==\n")
cat("  R         :", R.version.string, "\n")
cat("  platform  :", R.version$platform, "\n")
cat("  BLAS      :", basename(si$BLAS), "\n")
cat("  LAPACK    :", basename(si$LAPACK), "\n")
cat("  physical  :", system("sysctl -n hw.physicalcpu", intern = TRUE), "cores\n")
cat("  logical   :", system("sysctl -n hw.logicalcpu", intern = TRUE), "cores\n")
cat("  detectCores(logical=TRUE):", parallel::detectCores(logical = TRUE), "\n\n")

# ── 1. BLAS-bound work ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# betadisper does a full PCoA internally and cmdscale eigendecomposes the whole
# distance matrix, so symmetric eigen at this size is a direct proxy for a large
# slice of the pipeline's cost. The reference libRblas is single-threaded;
# libRblas.vecLib.dylib (Apple Accelerate) is multithreaded and ships with R.
cat("== 1. symmetric eigendecomposition,", n, "x", n, "==\n")
set.seed(1)
m <- crossprod(matrix(rnorm(n * 200), nrow = 200))
t_eigen <- system.time(eigen(m, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE))[["elapsed"]]
cat(sprintf("  eigen(): %.1f s\n", t_eigen))
cat(sprintf("  matrix multiply %dx%d: %.1f s\n\n", n, n,
            system.time(m %*% m)[["elapsed"]]))

# ── 2. Permutation tests at varying thread counts ─────────────────────────────
# adonis2 and permutest take `parallel =`. More threads is not automatically
# faster: the 8 logical cores here are 4 physical cores with hyperthreading, and
# these permutations are memory-bandwidth bound.
cat("== 2. adonis2, 999 permutations, by thread count ==\n")
set.seed(1)
comm <- matrix(rpois(n * 100, 3), nrow = n)
grp <- factor(sample(c("Seeds", "Seedlings"), n, replace = TRUE))
d <- vegdist(comm, method = "bray")
df <- data.frame(group = grp)

for (th in unique(c(1L, 2L, 4L, parallel::detectCores(logical = TRUE) - 1L))) {
    set.seed(123)
    el <- system.time(
        vegan::adonis2(d ~ group, data = df, permutations = 999, parallel = th)
    )[["elapsed"]]
    cat(sprintf("  parallel = %-2d : %6.1f s\n", th, el))
}

cat("\n== how to act on this ==\n")
cat("  * If BLAS is libRblas.0.dylib, switch to Apple Accelerate and re-run:\n")
cat("      cd /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/lib\n")
cat("      ln -sf libRblas.vecLib.dylib libRblas.dylib\n")
cat("    Revert with: ln -sf libRblas.0.dylib libRblas.dylib\n")
cat("  * Set analysis.threads in analysis_config.json to whichever row above wins.\n")
```


# Part 2 — All analysis figures

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## About this part
Every analysis figure, from `figures_all.qmd`. It reads the persisted outputs Part 1 just wrote rather than recomputing them, and wraps each figure in `fig_section()` so a missing input records a skip instead of aborting the render. Writes `tables/figure_manifest.csv`.
:::


## What this document is

Every figure in the project is generated here, and only here. It reads the
**persisted outputs** of the analysis pipeline rather than recomputing them, so it
renders in minutes and never touches the 609 MB count table. Each figure is written
into the folder of its analysis under `by_analysis/`; the last two chunks then gather
the tables beside them (`fx-analysis-folders`) and merge the finished figures into the
four figures of the manuscript (`fx-fig-main-figures`, in `by_analysis/00_main_figures/`).
Its inputs:

| Input | Supplies |
| --- | --- |
| `setup/ps_clean.rds` | filtered phyloseq object (1,886 x 2,000) — alpha diversity, composition |
| `setup/ps0.rds` | pre-filter object — QC library sizes |
| `cache/{bray,jaccard}_distance.rds` | beta-diversity distances |
| `diversity/pcoa_*.csv` | ordination coordinates, metadata already joined |
| `diversity/rarefaction_data.csv`, `diversity/umap_data.csv` | rarefaction and UMAP (both switched off in the config, `figures.skip`) |
| `tables/*.csv` | composition, indicator taxa, co-occurrence, the stage screen and stage effects, host generalists and specialists, host phylogenetic signal, special groups |
| `trees/*/tree.nwk` | maximum-likelihood trees of the generalist and specialist ASVs |
| `validation/supplementary/*.csv` | manuscript Fig 1–4 tables of record |

Run the pipeline first if any input is missing:

```
python3 microbiome_analysis.py --config analysis_config.json
quarto render phyloseq_analysis.qmd -P config:analysis_config.json
```

Every figure is wrapped in `fig_section()`, which reports a **skip** and carries on
when an input is absent — the same degrade-don't-fail rule the Python pipeline uses
for a missing `Rscript`. Nothing here recomputes statistics; `permanova_*`,
`permdisp_*` and the audit tables are read as the values of record.

```{r fx-setup}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS - | support code (no analysis)
#   Part 2 setup
# ==========================================================================================
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
    library(phyloseq)
    library(vegan)
    library(ggplot2)
    library(dplyr)
    library(tidyr)
    library(readr)
    library(stringr)
    library(forcats)
    library(tibble)
    library(patchwork)
    library(scales)
    library(purrr)
    library(ggrepel)
    library(RColorBrewer)
    library(jsonlite)
})

resolve_path <- function(base_dir, configured_path) {
    if (startsWith(configured_path, "/")) return(configured_path)
    normalizePath(file.path(base_dir, configured_path), mustWork = FALSE)
}

config_path <- if (exists("params") && !is.null(params$config)) params$config else "analysis_config.json"
if (!file.exists(config_path)) stop("Configuration file not found: ", config_path)
config <- fromJSON(config_path)
base_dir <- dirname(normalizePath(config_path))

RESULTS <- resolve_path(base_dir, config$outputs$directory)
FIGS    <- file.path(RESULTS, "figures")
dir.create(FIGS, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Config-driven grouping, so this notebook follows the same variables as the pipeline.
PRIMARY   <- config$analysis$primary_group
SECONDARY <- config$analysis$secondary_groups
STAGES    <- config$differential_abundance$groups

res <- function(...) file.path(RESULTS, ...)
```

```{r fx-palettes}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS - | support code (no analysis)
#   Part 2 palettes
# ==========================================================================================
# Font. Every figure is set in one sans-serif family, Helvetica as Nature asks (config
# figures.font_family): the themes take it as their base family and the text drawn by
# geoms as their default. Text that names no family is drawn in the device's own
# sans-serif font, which is checked to be the same.
FIGURE_FONT <- if (is.null(config$figures$font_family)) "Helvetica" else config$figures$font_family
ggplot2::update_geom_defaults("text", list(family = FIGURE_FONT))
ggplot2::update_geom_defaults("label", list(family = FIGURE_FONT))
if (requireNamespace("systemfonts", quietly = TRUE) &&
    !identical(systemfonts::match_fonts("sans")$path, systemfonts::match_fonts(FIGURE_FONT)$path)) {
    message("Font: the device's sans-serif font is not ", FIGURE_FONT, "; text without a named family will differ")
}
# Palette and themes lifted from phyloseq_analysis.R / phyloseq_analysis.qmd so
# figures produced here are visually identical to the pipeline's.
# The same palette as Part 1, from the config's `palette` section: the colours of the
# figures of the Cell Reports manuscript the user works from. Seeds orange, seedlings teal,
# and those two colours mean nothing else. The sequential and diverging ramps and the
# named roles below replace the ColorBrewer and viridis scales used before.
FIGURE_PALETTE <- config$palette
if (is.null(FIGURE_PALETTE)) stop("the config has no `palette` section")
STAGE_PELLET     <- c("Seeds" = FIGURE_PALETTE$seeds, "Seedlings" = FIGURE_PALETTE$seedlings)
NATURE_THICK     <- c(unname(STAGE_PELLET), FIGURE_PALETTE$categorical)
PRIMARY_PELLET   <- NATURE_THICK[1:4]
CORE_PELLET      <- c("Biomarker" = FIGURE_PALETTE$categorical[6], "Core" = FIGURE_PALETTE$categorical[2],
                      "Flexible" = FIGURE_PALETTE$categorical[3])
PIPELINE_BAR_FILL <- FIGURE_PALETTE$bar
PALETTE_SEQUENTIAL <- FIGURE_PALETTE$sequential            # low to high
PALETTE_CONTRAST   <- FIGURE_PALETTE$sequential_contrast   # low to high, wider range of lightness
PALETTE_DIVERGING  <- FIGURE_PALETTE$diverging             # low, middle, high
# Host generalists and specialists, kept out of every other categorical scale.
HOST_BREADTH_COLOURS <- c(generalist = FIGURE_PALETTE$host_generalist,
                          specialist = FIGURE_PALETTE$host_specialist)
INK <- "#1f1f1f"

get_palette <- function(n) {
    if (n <= length(PRIMARY_PELLET)) return(PRIMARY_PELLET[seq_len(n)])
    # Extend with thick colours, not the pastel RColorBrewer "Set3".
    rep(NATURE_THICK, length.out = n)
}

theme_nature_base <- function(base_size = 8) {
    theme_classic(base_size = base_size, base_family = FIGURE_FONT) %+replace%
        theme(
            text = element_text(colour = "black"),
            axis.title = element_text(colour = "black", size = base_size),
            axis.text = element_text(colour = "black", size = base_size - 1),
            legend.text = element_text(colour = "black", size = base_size - 1),
            legend.title = element_text(colour = "black", size = base_size),
            strip.text = element_text(size = base_size - 1, face = "bold"),
            strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "white"),
            panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = INK, linewidth = 0.35),
            panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.2, colour = "#d9d9d9"),
            panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
            plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = base_size + 1),
            plot.subtitle = element_text(size = base_size - 1),
            plot.margin = margin(4, 4, 4, 4)
        )
}
theme_pipeline_classic  <- function(base_size = 8) theme_nature_base(base_size)
theme_pipeline_faceted  <- function(base_size = 8) theme_nature_base(base_size)
theme_set(theme_nature_base())

figure_size <- function(kind = c("standard", "wide", "square", "tall", "compact")) {
    switch(match.arg(kind),
        standard = list(width = 7.0, height = 5.1),
        wide     = list(width = 8.8, height = 5.1),
        square   = list(width = 6.6, height = 6.0),
        tall     = list(width = 6.9, height = 7.0),
        compact  = list(width = 6.4, height = 4.6))
}

save_nature_figure <- function(filename, plot, kind = "standard", dpi = 300, ...) {
    dims <- figure_size(kind)
    # LZW is lossless, so the figures are bit-identical in content but a fraction of
    # the size. Uncompressed 300 dpi TIFFs were running 13-15 MB each, 449 MB total.
    ggsave(filename, plot, width = dims$width, height = dims$height, dpi = dpi,
           compression = "lzw", ...)
    invisible(filename)
}

safe_file_label <- function(x) tolower(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", x))

# Plant families in one order, and so one colour each, in the dendrogram and the ordinations.
PCOA_FAMILY_ORDER <- c("Brassicaceae", "Fabaceae", "Apiaceae", "Asteraceae", "Solanaceae", "Poaceae")
# Host groups (plant family, host genus, host species, cultivar) take the palette's colours
# in an order that sets the first ones far apart (config palette.host_contrast), then the
# rest of the palette. The groups with the most samples are given the first colours. The
# list leaves out the palette's rust, which is too near the seed colour.
HOST_COLOUR_POOL <- unique(c(unlist(FIGURE_PALETTE$host_contrast), setdiff(NATURE_THICK, STAGE_PELLET),
                             FIGURE_PALETTE$pastel))
# One colour scheme for the hosts, the same in every figure: plant families take the first
# colours, in the order above, and host genera the saturated colours of config
# palette.host_genus (none of them a family, stage or pale colour, so every genus stands
# out against white), the genera with the most samples first. So a ring of the dendrogram
# and the points of an ordination that stand for the same host have the same colour, and
# one key serves both.
host_colours <- function() {
    hosts <- read_csv(res("tables", "host_plant_species.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::filter(grepl("^[A-Z][a-z]+ [a-z]+$", Species))                    # not the totals row
    families <- c(PCOA_FAMILY_ORDER, sort(setdiff(hosts$Family, PCOA_FAMILY_ORDER)))
    genera <- names(sort(tapply(hosts$Total, sub(" .*$", "", hosts$Species), sum), decreasing = TRUE))
    genus_pool <- unique(c(unlist(FIGURE_PALETTE$host_genus), HOST_COLOUR_POOL[-seq_along(families)]))
    if (length(families) > length(HOST_COLOUR_POOL) || length(genera) > length(genus_pool)) {
        stop("more hosts than colours in the palette")
    }
    list(family = setNames(HOST_COLOUR_POOL[seq_along(families)], families),
         genus = setNames(genus_pool[seq_along(genera)], genera))
}
# the plant-family colours on their own, for the figures that show no other host level
HOST_FAMILY_COLOURS <- setNames(HOST_COLOUR_POOL[seq_along(PCOA_FAMILY_ORDER)], PCOA_FAMILY_ORDER)
# Panel letters: bold, 8 pt, at the top left of the panel, in the case set in the config
# (figures.panel_letter_case, "upper" or "lower"). Every letter drawn goes through
# panel_letter(), and a panel heading through panel_title(), so the case is set in one place.
PANEL_LETTER_SIZE <- 8
PANEL_LETTER_CASE <- if (is.null(config$figures$panel_letter_case)) "upper" else config$figures$panel_letter_case
panel_letter <- function(x) if (identical(PANEL_LETTER_CASE, "lower")) tolower(x) else toupper(x)
panel_title <- function(letter, heading = NULL) paste(c(panel_letter(letter), heading), collapse = "   ")
```

```{r fx-fig-registry}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS - | support code (no analysis)
#   fig_section(): draw a figure, or record a skip
# ==========================================================================================
# Every figure registers here. A section that cannot run records a skip and its
# reason instead of aborting the render, so one missing input never costs the
# other 36 figures.
FIG_LOG <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
FIG_LOG$rows <- list()

record <- function(name, status, reason = NA_character_, file = NA_character_) {
    FIG_LOG$rows[[length(FIG_LOG$rows) + 1]] <- tibble(
        figure = name, status = status, reason = reason,
        file = if (is.na(file)) NA_character_ else basename(file))
    invisible(NULL)
}

# Figures listed under `figures.skip` in the config are not drawn: they belong to analyses
# that are not in the methodology and whose outputs the user had removed (2026-10-08).
# Delete a name from that list to have the figure back.
FIG_SWITCHED_OFF <- if (is.null(config$figures$skip)) character() else config$figures$skip

#' Run a figure block, requiring `needs` to exist first.
fig_section <- function(name, needs = character(), expr) {
    if (name %in% FIG_SWITCHED_OFF) {
        message("SKIP ", name, " - switched off in the config (figures.skip)")
        record(name, "skipped", "switched off in the config")
        return(invisible(NULL))
    }
    missing <- needs[!file.exists(needs)]
    if (length(missing)) {
        reason <- paste("missing:", paste(basename(missing), collapse = ", "))
        message("SKIP ", name, " - ", reason)
        record(name, "skipped", reason)
        return(invisible(NULL))
    }
    out <- tryCatch(force(expr), error = function(e) {
        message("FAIL ", name, " - ", conditionMessage(e))
        record(name, "failed", conditionMessage(e))
        NULL
    })
    if (!is.null(out)) {
        record(name, "written", NA_character_, if (is.character(out)) out[1] else NA_character_)
        message("OK   ", name)
    }
    invisible(out)
}

# Where a result belongs: the folder of the config's `analysis_folders` section whose file
# list claims it (wildcards allowed), or NA. `path` is relative to the outputs directory.
analysis_folder_for <- function(path) {
    for (folder in names(config$analysis_folders$folders)) {
        patterns <- config$analysis_folders$folders[[folder]]$files
        if (any(vapply(patterns, function(p) grepl(utils::glob2rx(p), path), logical(1)))) {
            return(folder)
        }
    }
    NA_character_
}

# A figure is written into its analysis folder, beside that analysis's tables, and
# nowhere else. One that no folder claims falls back to figures/.
fig <- function(name) {
    file <- paste0(name, ".tiff")
    folder <- analysis_folder_for(file.path("figures", file))
    if (is.na(folder)) return(file.path(FIGS, file))
    target <- file.path(RESULTS, config$analysis_folders$directory, folder)
    dir.create(target, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
    file.path(target, file)
}
```

```{r fx-load-core}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS - | support code (no analysis)
#   load the filtered phyloseq object
# ==========================================================================================
PS_CLEAN <- res("setup", "ps_clean.rds")
PS0      <- res("setup", "ps0.rds")

ps <- if (file.exists(PS_CLEAN)) readRDS(PS_CLEAN) else NULL
if (!is.null(ps)) {
    # as.data.frame() on a sample_data object keeps the phyloseq class, which dplyr
    # verbs reject ("no applicable method for 'mutate'"). Coerce to a plain tibble.
    meta <- as(sample_data(ps), "data.frame")
    meta$sample_id <- rownames(meta)
    meta <- as_tibble(meta)
    cat(sprintf("ps_clean: %d samples x %d taxa\n", nsamples(ps), ntaxa(ps)))
} else {
    meta <- NULL
    cat("ps_clean.rds absent - object-derived figures will be skipped\n")
}
```

```{r fx-fig-alluvial-stage}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 2 | Diversity, composition and co-occurrence
#   figures: composition alluvials (Sankey), at genus and class level, and seedling-vs-seed
# ==========================================================================================
# Seed-to-seedling composition as an alluvial (Sankey-style) diagram.
#
# IMPORTANT, and stated in the caption: seeds and seedlings are DIFFERENT samples, not
# paired ones. A ribbon links the same genus name at the two stages - it does not show
# that those cells persisted, were inherited or were transmitted. With unpaired samples
# "composition at each stage" is the strongest claim available, so the figure never says
# "transition". Groups are restricted to those holding both stages; a group with one
# stage has no transition to draw.

# Built once for every genus figure in this chunk: the per-sample genus table collapsed
# to one shared set of top genera, and one genus -> colour map. Choosing the genera and
# colours inside each figure let the same genus change colour between the family and
# host-species alluvials (Erwinia green in one, brown in the other).
#' The per-sample relative abundance of the top taxa of one rank, with one colour each.
#' `rank_col`: a column of the taxonomy table. Returns NULL without a dataset.
alluvial_taxa <- function(rank_col, n_top = TOP_TAXA_N) {
    if (is.null(ps)) return(NULL)
    otu <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
    if (!taxa_are_rows(ps)) otu <- t(otu)
    tx <- as.data.frame(as(tax_table(ps), "matrix"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    blank <- function(x) is.na(x) | x == "" |
        grepl("^(Unassigned|unidentified|uncultured|metagenome)$", x, ignore.case = TRUE)
    g <- !blank(tx[[rank_col]])
    gen <- rowsum(otu[g, , drop = FALSE], group = tx[[rank_col]][g])
    md <- as(sample_data(ps), "data.frame")
    keep <- colSums(gen) > 0 & md[[PRIMARY]] %in% STAGES
    gen <- gen[, keep, drop = FALSE]; md <- md[keep, , drop = FALSE]
    rel <- sweep(gen, 2, colSums(gen), "/")

    # Top taxa by the mean of study x stage means, so no single large study picks them.
    study_stage <- interaction(md$study_alias, md[[PRIMARY]], drop = TRUE)
    ss_mean <- rowsum(t(rel), study_stage) / as.vector(table(study_stage))
    top <- names(sort(colMeans(ss_mean), decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(min(n_top, nrow(rel)))]
    # the document palette without the two stage colours: the bars here are the stages
    taxon_colours <- unique(c(setdiff(NATURE_THICK, STAGE_PELLET), FIGURE_PALETTE$pastel))
    pal <- stats::setNames(c(taxon_colours[seq_along(top)], "#9E9E9E"), c(top, "Other"))

    rel_top <- rbind(rel[top, , drop = FALSE],
                     Other = colSums(rel[!rownames(rel) %in% top, , drop = FALSE]))
    long <- as.data.frame(as.table(rel_top), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
        setNames(c("Taxon", "sample_id", "rel")) |>
        dplyr::left_join(tibble::tibble(
            sample_id = rownames(md), Stage = md[[PRIMARY]], study = md$study_alias,
            Scientific_Name = md$Scientific_Name,
            Plant_Family = dplyr::coalesce(
                family_map$Family[match(md$Scientific_Name, family_map$Scientific_Name)],
                "Other")), by = "sample_id")
    list(long = long, top = top, pal = pal)
}
.genus <- alluvial_taxa("Genus")
GENUS_LONG <- .genus$long
GENUS_TOP <- .genus$top
GENUS_PAL <- .genus$pal
# The same view at class level, the rank of the other composition figures. Fewer classes
# are named than genera (config taxonomy_analysis.sankey_class_taxa): the rest are slivers,
# and with them the legend would not fit in two rows at a readable size.
CLASS_TAXA <- alluvial_taxa("Class", if (is.null(config$taxonomy_analysis$sankey_class_taxa)) 9 else
    config$taxonomy_analysis$sankey_class_taxa)

# Study means per group x stage x genus, restricted to studies that sampled BOTH stages
# of that group. A plain mean over samples would let Chesneau et al. 2022 (1,352 of 1,886
# samples) speak for Brassicaceae and Fabaceae; a mean over every study would build the
# seed and seedling bars from different studies (Chandel et al. 2022a/b and Nunes et al.
# 2022 sampled seedlings only), so the stage contrast would partly be a study contrast.
# Pairing within study removes both, and every contributing study counts equally.
paired_study_means <- function(group_col, long = GENUS_LONG) {
    long |>
        dplyr::mutate(grp = .data[[group_col]]) |>
        dplyr::filter(!is.na(grp), grp != "") |>
        dplyr::summarise(rel = mean(rel), .by = c(Plant_Family, grp, study, Stage, Taxon)) |>
        dplyr::filter(dplyr::n_distinct(Stage) == 2, .by = c(grp, study))
}

# Returns the plot, or a character reason when there is nothing to draw, which the
# caller records as a skip so the figure manifest still accounts for it.
# No title is drawn into the artwork: what the figure shows is said in its legend.
build_alluvial <- function(group_col, group_name, width = 11, height = 6.2,
                           taxa = list(long = GENUS_LONG, pal = GENUS_PAL), rank = "genus",
                           base_size = 11, legend_rows = NULL, panel_gap = 2) {
    if (!requireNamespace("ggalluvial", quietly = TRUE)) return("ggalluvial not installed")
    per_study <- paired_study_means(group_col, taxa$long)
    if (!nrow(per_study)) return(sprintf("no %s has a study sampling both stages", group_name))

    # Panels in family order, so host species of one family sit together.
    lab <- per_study |>
        dplyr::summarise(k = dplyr::n_distinct(study), .by = c(Plant_Family, grp)) |>
        dplyr::arrange(Plant_Family, grp) |>
        dplyr::mutate(label = if (group_col == "Plant_Family")
                                  sprintf("%s\n(n = %d)", grp, k)
                              else sprintf("%s\n%s, n = %d", grp, Plant_Family, k))
    d <- per_study |>
        dplyr::summarise(rel = mean(rel), .by = c(grp, Stage, Taxon)) |>
        dplyr::mutate(rel = rel / sum(rel), .by = c(grp, Stage)) |>
        dplyr::mutate(grp = factor(lab$label[match(grp, lab$grp)], levels = lab$label),
                      Stage = factor(Stage, levels = STAGES),
                      Taxon = factor(Taxon, levels = names(taxa$pal)))

    p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = Stage, stratum = Taxon, alluvium = Taxon,
                       y = rel, fill = Taxon)) +
        # Wider strata pull the two bars toward each other: the centres are a fixed unit
        # apart on a discrete axis, so the only way to close the gap is to widen the bars.
        ggalluvial::geom_flow(alpha = 0.55, width = 0.46, curve_type = "sigmoid") +
        ggalluvial::geom_stratum(width = 0.46, colour = "grey25", linewidth = 0.25) +
        facet_wrap(~grp, nrow = if (nrow(lab) > 8) 2 else 1) +
        # trim the outer padding too, so the pair sits compactly in each panel
        scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = 0.08)) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = taxa$pal) +
        scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent,
                           expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
        labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean relative abundance", fill = NULL) +
        guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = legend_rows, byrow = TRUE)) +
        theme_classic(base_size = base_size, base_family = "Helvetica") +
        theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey94", colour = NA),
              strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = base_size - 2,
                                        margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2)),
              axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"),
              # the two stage names of one panel must not run into those of the next
              axis.text.x = element_text(size = base_size - 3),
              legend.text = element_text(size = base_size - 1.5, colour = "black"),
              # tight panel gutters: the ribbons carry the comparison, so wide gaps
              # between families only push the panels apart and shrink the flows
              panel.spacing = unit(panel_gap, "pt"),
              legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.size = unit(base_size - 1, "pt"),
              legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0), legend.box.spacing = unit(3, "pt"),
              plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA))
    list(plot = p, groups = nrow(lab), width = width, height = height)
}

# Sized in inches by the caller rather than through save_nature_figure(), whose fixed
# kinds top out at 8.8 in wide - too narrow for six to twelve alluvial panels.
fig_section("fig_alluvial_genus_by_plant_family", needs = PS_CLEAN, {
    a <- build_alluvial("Plant_Family", "plant family", width = 7.2, height = 4.7, base_size = 9,
                        legend_rows = 4, panel_gap = 8)
    if (is.character(a)) record("fig_alluvial_genus_by_plant_family", "skipped", a) else {
        print(a$plot)
        ggsave(fig("fig_alluvial_genus_by_plant_family"), a$plot,
               width = a$width, height = a$height, dpi = 600,
               device = if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) ragg::agg_tiff else "tiff",
               compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
    }
})

# The class-level Sankey: the composition figure of the manuscript, at the rank of the
# other composition figures.
fig_section("fig_alluvial_class_by_plant_family", needs = PS_CLEAN, {
    # drawn at the page width it is used at in main Figure 2, so the type is not shrunk;
    # the classes sit in two rows under the bars
    a <- build_alluvial("Plant_Family", "plant family", width = 7.2, height = 3.9, taxa = CLASS_TAXA,
                        rank = "class", base_size = 10, legend_rows = 2, panel_gap = 8)
    if (is.character(a)) record("fig_alluvial_class_by_plant_family", "skipped", a) else {
        print(a$plot)
        ggsave(fig("fig_alluvial_class_by_plant_family"), a$plot,
               width = a$width, height = a$height, dpi = 600,
               device = if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) ragg::agg_tiff else "tiff",
               compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
    }
})

# Supplementary: the same view per host species, for those carrying both stages.
fig_section("fig_alluvial_genus_by_host_species", needs = PS_CLEAN, {
    a <- build_alluvial("Scientific_Name", "host species", width = 7.2, height = 6.8, base_size = 8,
                        legend_rows = 4, panel_gap = 6)
    if (is.character(a)) record("fig_alluvial_genus_by_host_species", "skipped", a) else {
        print(a$plot)
        ggsave(fig("fig_alluvial_genus_by_host_species"), a$plot,
               width = a$width, height = a$height, dpi = 600,
               device = if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) ragg::agg_tiff else "tiff",
               compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
    }
})

# Seedling relative to seed per host species: the same paired study means and the same
# genera as the alluvials, as a log2 ratio. Genera absent at one stage need a floor;
# 1e-4 (0.01%) is stated in the caption, because a ratio against a near-zero stage mostly
# reflects that floor rather than a measured change.
fig_section("fig_genus_seedling_vs_seed_by_species", needs = PS_CLEAN, {
    pseudo <- 1e-4
    seed <- STAGES[1]; sdlg <- STAGES[2]
    dd <- paired_study_means("Scientific_Name") |>
        dplyr::filter(Taxon != "Other") |>
        dplyr::summarise(rel = mean(rel), n_studies = dplyr::n_distinct(study),
                         .by = c(Plant_Family, grp, Stage, Taxon)) |>
        tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Stage, values_from = rel) |>
        dplyr::mutate(log2FC = log2((.data[[sdlg]] + pseudo) / (.data[[seed]] + pseudo)),
                      peak = pmax(.data[[seed]], .data[[sdlg]])) |>
        dplyr::rename(Scientific_Name = grp)
    readr::write_csv(dd, res("tables", "genus_seedling_vs_seed_by_species.csv"))

    rows <- dd |> dplyr::distinct(Plant_Family, Scientific_Name) |>
        dplyr::arrange(Plant_Family, Scientific_Name)
    dd <- dd |> dplyr::mutate(
        Scientific_Name = factor(Scientific_Name, levels = rev(rows$Scientific_Name)),
        Taxon = factor(Taxon, levels = GENUS_TOP),
        fc = pmax(pmin(log2FC, 6), -6))
    p <- ggplot(dd, aes(x = Taxon, y = Scientific_Name)) +
        geom_point(aes(size = peak, fill = fc), shape = 21, colour = "grey30", stroke = 0.25) +
        facet_grid(Plant_Family ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
        scale_fill_gradient2(low = STAGE_PELLET[[seed]], mid = "grey95", high = STAGE_PELLET[[sdlg]],
                             midpoint = 0, limits = c(-6, 6), breaks = c(-6, -3, 0, 3, 6),
                             labels = c("-6", "-3", "0", "+3", "+6"),
                             # ASCII only: the default pdf device cannot encode <= / >=
                             name = "log2(seedling / seed)\ncapped at +/-6") +
        scale_size_area(max_size = 6, limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0.01, 0.25, 0.5, 1),
                        labels = scales::percent, name = "Peak mean\nrelative abundance") +
        labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
        theme_pipeline_classic(8) +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, face = "italic"),
              axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"),
              strip.placement = "outside",
              strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1, face = "bold"),
              strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey94", colour = NA),
              panel.spacing.y = unit(2, "pt"))
    print(p)
    save_nature_figure(fig("fig_genus_seedling_vs_seed_by_species"), p, "standard")
})
```

```{r fx-fig-composition-dendrogram}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 2 | Diversity, composition and co-occurrence
#   figure: composition_dendrogram
# ==========================================================================================
# Composition as a circular dendrogram of the hosts. Each tip is one host plant genus at
# one developmental stage (config taxonomy_analysis.dendrogram_min_samples or more samples);
# seeds and seedlings of a genus are separate tips, so the two stages are told apart. The tips are clustered on their mean genus-level composition
# (Bray-Curtis between the mean relative-abundance profiles, average linkage), the seed
# tips and the seedling tips each on their own, and the two trees are joined at the root:
# one stage to each side of the circle. The clustering is a display of the composition
# drawn round it and not a test. From the centre:
# a ring for the stage, a ring for the plant family and a ring for the host genus, the
# composition in per cent at class level and at genus level as stacked bars, and the
# number of samples of the tip; the host is read from the rings. The classes and genera named are those of the
# Sankey figures (chunk `fx-fig-alluvial-stage`). Plant family takes the colours it has
# in the ordinations set under this panel in main Figure 2. The palette has fewer colours
# than the rings and bars have categories, so colours recur between them; each ring and
# each set of bars has its own key, titled with the variable alone: which ring or bar it
# is goes in the caption. The tree is given a large share of the radius, so that its
# branching can be read.
# Host is largely tied to study: tips of one study can cluster for that reason alone.
fig_section("composition_dendrogram", needs = PS_CLEAN, {
    setting <- function(key, default) {
        value <- config$taxonomy_analysis[[key]]
        if (is.null(value)) default else value
    }
    min_samples <- setting("dendrogram_min_samples", 3)
    genera_named <- head(GENUS_TOP, setting("dendrogram_genera", 10))
    classes_named <- CLASS_TAXA$top

    otu <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
    if (!taxa_are_rows(ps)) otu <- t(otu)
    tx <- as.data.frame(as(tax_table(ps), "matrix"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    md <- as(sample_data(ps), "data.frame")
    blank <- function(x) is.na(x) | x == "" |
        grepl("^(Unassigned|unidentified|uncultured|metagenome)$", x, ignore.case = TRUE)
    by_rank <- function(rank) rowsum(otu, ifelse(blank(tx[[rank]]), "Unassigned", tx[[rank]]))
    keep <- colSums(otu) > 0 & md[[PRIMARY]] %in% STAGES
    relative <- function(counts) sweep(counts[, keep, drop = FALSE], 2, colSums(otu)[keep], "/")
    genus <- relative(by_rank("Genus"))
    class <- relative(by_rank("Class"))
    md <- md[keep, , drop = FALSE]

    hosts <- read_csv(res("tables", "host_plant_species.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
    samples <- tibble(
        sample = rownames(md), stage = md[[PRIMARY]], species = md$Scientific_Name,
        family = hosts$Family[match(md$Scientific_Name, hosts$Species)]) |>
        # a tip is one host genus at one stage (host attributes are plant family and host genus only, at the user's request (2026-10-22))
        dplyr::mutate(host_genus = sub(" .*$", "", species),
                      tip = paste(host_genus, stage, sep = "|"))
    tips <- samples |>
        dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), species = paste(sort(unique(species)), collapse = "; "),
                         .by = c(tip, stage, host_genus, family)) |>
        dplyr::filter(n >= min_samples)
    samples <- dplyr::filter(samples, tip %in% tips$tip)
    tip_means <- function(rel) {                       # taxon x tip, mean of per-sample values
        sums <- rowsum(t(rel[, samples$sample, drop = FALSE]), samples$tip)
        t(sums / as.vector(table(samples$tip)[rownames(sums)]))
    }
    genus_means <- tip_means(genus)
    class_means <- tip_means(class)
    # Seeds and seedlings are clustered apart and the two trees joined at the root, so each
    # stage keeps its own side of the circle. With fewer than two tips at a stage there is
    # nothing to cluster within it, and all tips are clustered together.
    cluster <- function(ids) ape::as.phylo(stats::hclust(
        vegan::vegdist(t(genus_means[, ids, drop = FALSE]), method = "bray"), method = "average"))
    by_stage <- split(tips$tip, factor(tips$stage, STAGES))
    tr <- if (length(by_stage) == 2 && all(lengths(by_stage) >= 2)) {
        parts <- lapply(by_stage, cluster)
        depths <- vapply(parts, function(part) max(ape::node.depth.edgelength(part)), numeric(1))
        for (i in seq_along(parts)) parts[[i]]$root.edge <- 1.1 * max(depths) - depths[[i]]
        parts[[1]] + parts[[2]]
    } else cluster(tips$tip)
    # tip data for the tree: the first column is the tip name
    tips <- tips |>
        dplyr::mutate(shown = format(n, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)) |>
        dplyr::relocate(tip)
    pool <- unique(c(setdiff(NATURE_THICK, STAGE_PELLET), FIGURE_PALETTE$pastel))
    families <- c(intersect(PCOA_FAMILY_ORDER, tips$family), sort(setdiff(tips$family, PCOA_FAMILY_ORDER)))
```
