```{r fx-fig-composition-dendrogram}
    # Contrast. The palette has about twenty colours and the figure about forty categories,
    # so colours cannot all differ; they are set so that what stands side by side differs.
    # The two rings take the host colours of every figure (host_colours()), so they share
    # no colour and match the ordinations. The two sets of bars share no colour either: classes take strong, dark
    # tones and genera lighter ones (config palette.class_bars and palette.genus_bars),
    # and each set runs through different hues. Rings and bars may share a colour.
    host_scheme <- host_colours()
    genus_ring <- host_scheme$genus[sort(names(host_scheme$genus))]   # every genus: the key serves b and c too
    class_colours <- unique(c(unlist(FIGURE_PALETTE$class_bars), pool))[seq_along(classes_named)]
    genus_colours <- setdiff(unique(c(unlist(FIGURE_PALETTE$genus_bars), pool)),
                             class_colours)[seq_along(genera_named)]

    `%<+%` <- ggtree::`%<+%`
    p <- ggtree::ggtree(tr, layout = "fan", open.angle = 14, linewidth = 0.25) %<+% tips
    depth <- max(p$data$x)
    round_tree <- dplyr::arrange(dplyr::filter(p$data, isTip), y)$label
    # Radial positions, as shares of the tree's depth. A ring of tiles is centred `offset`
    # beyond the ring before it; bars start `offset` beyond and are `bar_depth` long at 100%.
    ring_step <- 0.075; bar_gap <- 0.08; bar_depth <- 0.36
    key <- function(order, ncol = 1, italic = FALSE) guide_legend(
        order = order, ncol = ncol,
        theme = theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 5.5, colour = "black",
                                                 face = if (italic) "italic" else "plain")))
    # a ring of one tile per tip; its data may not share a column name with the tree data
    ring <- function(column, colours, title, order, offset, ncol = 1, italic = FALSE) list(
        ggnewscale::new_scale_fill(),
        ggtreeExtra::geom_fruit(data = tibble(label = tips$tip, ring_value = factor(tips[[column]], names(colours))),
                                geom = geom_tile, mapping = aes(y = label, fill = ring_value),
                                width = 0.06 * depth, offset = offset, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15),
        # A level with no tip (a host with too few samples) would have an empty key. This layer
        # draws nothing, its positions being missing, but holds every level, so that each
        # keeps its colour in the key, which also serves the ordinations under this panel.
        geom_tile(data = tibble(ring_value = factor(names(colours), names(colours))),
                  mapping = aes(x = NA_real_, y = NA_real_, fill = ring_value), inherit.aes = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE),
        scale_fill_manual(values = colours, name = title, drop = FALSE, guide = key(order, ncol, italic)))
    # the composition of each tip in per cent, as stacked bars with a radial axis
    stacked <- function(means, named, colours, title, order, offset) {
        shown <- rbind(means[named, , drop = FALSE],
                       Other = pmax(1 - colSums(means[named, , drop = FALSE]), 0))
        long <- as.data.frame(as.table(100 * shown), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
            setNames(c("taxon", "label", "share")) |>
            dplyr::mutate(taxon = factor(taxon, levels = rev(c(named, "Other"))))
        list(ggnewscale::new_scale_fill(),
             ggtreeExtra::geom_fruit(data = long, geom = geom_col,
                                     mapping = aes(y = label, x = share, fill = taxon), orientation = "y",
                                     width = 0.86, pwidth = bar_depth, offset = offset,
                                     axis.params = list(axis = "x", text.size = 1.4, nbreak = 3, vjust = 1,
                                                        line.size = 0.15)),
             scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(c(colours, "grey88"), c(named, "Other")), name = title,
                               breaks = c(named, "Other"), guide = key(order)))
    }
    p <- p +
        ring("stage", STAGE_PELLET[STAGES], "Stage", 1, ring_step) +
        ring("family", host_scheme$family[families], "Plant family", 2,
             ring_step, ncol = 2) +
        ring("host_genus", genus_ring, "Host genus", 3,
             ring_step, ncol = 2, italic = TRUE) +
        stacked(class_means, classes_named, class_colours, "Bacterial class", 4,
                bar_gap) +
        stacked(genus_means, genera_named, genus_colours,
                "Bacterial genus", 5, bar_gap)
    # The sample numbers go just beyond the outer bars, whose edge is read off the built
    # plot. They stand outside the plotting circle, and the margins are their room.
    outer_edge <- max(vapply(ggplot2::ggplot_build(p)$data, function(layer) {
        max(c(layer$xmax, layer$x, -Inf), na.rm = TRUE)
    }, numeric(1)))
    p <- p +
        ggtree::geom_tiplab(aes(label = shown), size = 5 / ggplot2::.pt,
                            offset = outer_edge - depth + 0.04 * depth) +
        theme(legend.position = "right", legend.key.size = unit(6, "pt"),
              legend.text = element_text(size = 5.5, colour = "black"),
              legend.title = element_text(size = 6, face = "bold"),
              legend.spacing.y = unit(1, "pt"), legend.margin = margin(1, 0, 1, 2),
              legend.box.spacing = unit(0, "pt"), plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
    # The polar panel keeps its outer rim empty, so the circle is drawn on a square larger
    # than the space it is given, the empty rim falling off the page; the keys stand in a
    # column of their own to its right. Sizes in inches.
    page <- c(width = 7.2, height = 5.3); keys_from <- 5.55; square <- 6.05
    keys <- ggpubr::get_legend(p)
    p <- cowplot::ggdraw() +
        cowplot::draw_plot(p + theme(legend.position = "none"),
                           x = (keys_from - square) / 2 / page[["width"]],
                           y = (page[["height"]] - square) / 2 / page[["height"]],
                           width = square / page[["width"]], height = square / page[["height"]]) +
        cowplot::draw_grob(keys, x = keys_from / page[["width"]], y = 0,
                           width = 1 - keys_from / page[["width"]], height = 1)
    readr::write_csv(
        # in the order of the tips round the tree
        tips[match(round_tree, tips$tip), ] |>
            dplyr::select(stage, family, host_genus, host_species = species, n) |>
            dplyr::bind_cols(tibble::as_tibble(t(100 * class_means[classes_named, round_tree])),
                             tibble::as_tibble(t(100 * genus_means[genera_named, round_tree]))),
        res("tables", "composition_dendrogram_tips.csv"))
    print(p)
    # double-column width (183 mm), 600 dpi, drawn with ragg for sharp type
    ggsave(fig("composition_dendrogram"), p, width = page[["width"]], height = page[["height"]], dpi = 600,
           device = if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) ragg::agg_tiff else "tiff",
           compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
})
```

```{r fx-fig-alpha-indices}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 2 | Diversity, composition and co-occurrence
#   figure: alpha_indices_by_stage_rarefied
# ==========================================================================================
# Alpha-diversity indices by developmental stage at each rarefaction depth, one row per
# index. The test printed in each panel is read from tables/alpha_diversity_findings.csv
# (Part 1), not recomputed here.
.depths <- sort(unique(as.integer(config$filters$rarefaction_depths)))
.findings <- res("tables", "alpha_diversity_findings.csv")
fig_section("alpha_indices_by_stage_rarefied",
            needs = c(res("tables", sprintf("rarefied_alpha_diversity_depth%d.csv", .depths)),
                      .findings), {
    index_labels <- c(Observed = "Observed ASV richness", Shannon = "Shannon",
                      Evenness = "Pielou's evenness")
    d <- purrr::map(.depths, function(dp) {
        read_csv(res("tables", sprintf("rarefied_alpha_diversity_depth%d.csv", dp)),
                 show_col_types = FALSE) |>
            dplyr::select(sample_id, stage = dplyr::all_of(PRIMARY),
                          dplyr::ends_with("_rarefied")) |>
            dplyr::mutate(depth = dp)
    }) |> list_rbind() |>
        tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::ends_with("_rarefied"), names_to = "metric",
                            values_to = "value") |>
        dplyr::mutate(metric = sub("_rarefied$", "", metric)) |>
        dplyr::filter(metric %in% names(index_labels), stage %in% STAGES, !is.na(value))
    # column strips carry the sample counts, which differ between depths
    depth_labels <- d |> dplyr::filter(metric == "Observed") |>
        dplyr::summarise(lab = sprintf("%s reads (%s seeds, %s seedlings)", comma(depth[1]),
                                       comma(sum(stage == STAGES[1])),
                                       comma(sum(stage == STAGES[2]))), .by = depth)
    as_panel <- function(x) dplyr::mutate(x,
        depth = factor(depth, levels = depth_labels$depth, labels = depth_labels$lab),
        metric = factor(metric, levels = names(index_labels), labels = index_labels))
    ann <- read_csv(.findings, show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = cols(depth = "c")) |>
        dplyr::filter(scope == "overall", variable == PRIMARY,
                      depth %in% as.character(.depths), metric %in% names(index_labels)) |>
        # plotmath, so the label needs no non-ASCII glyph on any device
        dplyr::mutate(depth = as.integer(depth),
                      label = sprintf('italic(p)~"%s"*","~~epsilon^2=="%.3f"',
                                      ifelse(p < 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("= %.3f", p)),
                                      # the estimator dips just below 0 when there is
                                      # no effect; print that as 0
                                      pmax(epsilon_sq, 0))) |>
        as_panel()
    p <- ggplot(as_panel(d), aes(x = factor(stage, levels = STAGES), y = value)) +
        geom_boxplot(aes(fill = stage), outlier.size = 0.3, outlier.alpha = 0.4,
                     linewidth = 0.3, width = 0.6) +
        geom_text(data = ann, aes(x = 1.5, y = Inf, label = label), parse = TRUE,
                  vjust = 1.5, size = 2.4) +
        facet_grid(metric ~ depth, scales = "free_y", switch = "y") +
        scale_fill_manual(values = STAGE_PELLET) +
        # headroom above the boxes for the test label
        scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.22))) +
        labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
        theme_pipeline_faceted() +
        theme(legend.position = "none", strip.placement = "outside",
              strip.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(b = 3)))
    print(p)
    # double-column width (183 mm), and short enough to be joined with the stage screen
    ggsave(fig("alpha_indices_by_stage_rarefied"), p, width = 7.2, height = 5.6, dpi = 600,
           device = if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) ragg::agg_tiff else "tiff",
           compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
})
```

```{r fx-fig-alpha-richness-faceted}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 2 | Diversity, composition and co-occurrence
#   figures: alpha richness and evenness by species, at 500 and 1,000 reads
# ==========================================================================================
# Observed richness by host species, at each rarefaction depth. Both depths are shown because the stage contrast in richness
# depends on which is chosen - Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.0095 at 500 reads but p = 0.958 at
# 1000, while Shannon holds at both. The pair is a depth-sensitivity comparison, not two
# views of one result. Statistics are in tables/alpha_diversity_findings.csv.
# Depths from the config, the same list Part 1 rarefied to.
# The same layout is drawn for Pielou's evenness. Evenness is a 0-1 proportion, so its
# axis is linear and its medians keep two decimals; it is undefined for a single-ASV
# sample, and those samples are left out of that figure.
.alpha_by_species <- list(
    richness = list(col = "Observed_rarefied", label = "Observed ASV richness",
                    title = "Bacterial ASV richness by plant family and species",
                    log = TRUE, digits = 0),
    evenness = list(col = "Evenness_rarefied", label = "Pielou's evenness",
                    title = "Bacterial community evenness by plant family and species",
                    log = FALSE, digits = 2))
.jobs <- expand.grid(dp = sort(unique(as.integer(config$filters$rarefaction_depths))),
                     nm = names(.alpha_by_species), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
for (.i in seq_len(nrow(.jobs))) {
    .dp <- .jobs$dp[.i]; .nm <- .jobs$nm[.i]; .m <- .alpha_by_species[[.nm]]
    .src <- res("tables", sprintf("rarefied_alpha_diversity_depth%d.csv", .dp))

    fig_section(sprintf("alpha_%s_by_species_depth%d", .nm, .dp), needs = .src, {
        d <- read_csv(.src, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
            dplyr::filter(!is.na(Scientific_Name), Scientific_Name != "",
                          !is.na(study_alias), study_alias != "",
                          !is.na(.data[[.m$col]])) |>
            dplyr::mutate(value = .data[[.m$col]],
                          accession = study_alias,
                          study_alias = as_study_ref(study_alias, study_alias, Author),
                          # the axis label, a/b suffix included, so the table below names
                          # Chandel et al. 2022a and 2022b exactly as the axis does
                          reference = study_alias,
                          Plant_Family = family_map$Family[match(Scientific_Name,
                                                                 family_map$Scientific_Name)],
                          Plant_Family = dplyr::coalesce(Plant_Family, "Other"),
                          # Seeds column first, in developmental order
                          dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(PRIMARY), ~ factor(.x, levels = STAGES)))
        # One median per species AND stage, drawn only in that stage's column. A median
        # pooled over both stages was drawn in both columns, so it sat nowhere near the
        # data (Medicago sativa seeds ~180 ASVs, line at ~14) and appeared in columns
        # with no samples at all.
        med <- d |> dplyr::summarise(m = median(value),
                                     .by = c(Scientific_Name, dplyr::all_of(PRIMARY)))
        d$Scientific_Name <- order_by_median(d$Scientific_Name, d$value)
        med$Scientific_Name <- factor(med$Scientific_Name, levels = levels(d$Scientific_Name))
        # Row strips read left to right as plant family then species, so the host taxonomy
        # is nested and legible without a legend; the study/reference axis moves to the
        # right so the two labelled edges do not compete.
        med$Plant_Family <- d$Plant_Family[match(med$Scientific_Name, d$Scientific_Name)]
        d$Plant_Family <- order_by_median(d$Plant_Family, d$value)
        med$Plant_Family <- factor(med$Plant_Family, levels = levels(d$Plant_Family))
        p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = value, y = study_alias)) +
            # Box and whisker per study within each species row, points over the top.
            # The boxes carry the quartiles the jitter alone could not show.
            geom_boxplot(aes(group = study_alias), orientation = "y", width = 0.55,
                         outlier.shape = NA, fill = NA, colour = "grey35",
                         linewidth = 0.3) +
            geom_jitter(aes(colour = Scientific_Name), alpha = 0.85, size = 1.0,
                        height = 0.18) +
            geom_vline(data = med, aes(xintercept = m), linewidth = 0.5, colour = "black") +
            # free_y only: the two stage columns share one x axis, so a position means the
            # same richness in both - the comparison this figure exists to make
            facet_grid(Plant_Family + Scientific_Name ~ .data[[PRIMARY]],
                       scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
            (if (.m$log) scale_x_log10() else scale_x_continuous()) +
            # Study labels on the right; the left axis carries no ticks, only the title
            # "Plant family", which names what the two strip columns on that side encode.
            scale_y_discrete(position = "right") +
            scale_colour_manual(values = distinct_palette(nlevels(d$Scientific_Name))) +
            labs(x = sprintf("%s (rarefied to %d reads)", .m$label, .dp),
                 y = "Study",
                 title = .m$title,
                 subtitle = sprintf("Rarefied to %d reads, n = %d. Boxes are per-study quartiles; black lines are species medians at each stage.",
                                    .dp, nrow(d))) +
            theme_pipeline_faceted() +
            theme(strip.placement = "outside",
                  # margin keeps the family strip off the species strip; without it they
                  # render as one run-together string ("SolanaceaeSolanum lycopersicum")
                  strip.text.y.left = element_text(size = 6, angle = 0, hjust = 1,
                                                   margin = margin(r = 5, l = 5)),
                  strip.background.y = element_rect(fill = "grey95", colour = NA),
                  panel.spacing.y = unit(2, "pt"),
                  axis.text.y.right = element_text(size = 6),
                  axis.title.y.right = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold",
                                                    margin = margin(l = 6)),
                  legend.position = "none")

        # Contributing-studies panel, moved here from the cultivar figure when that was
        # retired, so the reference/accession/sample-count summary survives.
        auth <- d |>
            dplyr::summarise(Samples = dplyr::n(),
                             Species = dplyr::n_distinct(Scientific_Name),
                             Seeds = sum(.data[[PRIMARY]] == "Seeds", na.rm = TRUE),
                             Seedlings = sum(.data[[PRIMARY]] == "Seedlings", na.rm = TRUE),
                             Median = round(median(value), .m$digits),
                             # the accession, not the relabelled study column - that now
                             # holds the reference and would duplicate the first column
                             .by = c(reference, accession)) |>
            dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(Samples))
        readr::write_csv(auth, res("tables",
                         sprintf("alpha_%s_species_studies_depth%d.csv", .nm, .dp)))

        # One monospaced string per row with fixed field widths. Positioning seven columns
        # by x coordinate kept colliding once the reference and accession were both long
        # ("Chesneau et al. 2022PRJEB450791344"); fixed widths cannot overlap by
        # construction, whatever the content.
        # Field widths sized to the panel: patchwork aligns this table to the plot panel
        # above, which the two left strip columns have narrowed, so a 77-character row
        # overflowed and clipped after "Species". 64 characters fits.
        # The reference is padded with str_pad(), not sprintf's %-20s: sprintf pads by
        # BYTES, so "Acuña" (n-tilde is two bytes) came out a column short and shifted
        # every field after it.
        row_fmt <- "%s %-11s %5s %4s %5s %5s %5s"
        pad_ref <- function(x) stringr::str_pad(x, 20, side = "right")
        hdr <- sprintf(row_fmt, pad_ref("Reference"), "Accession", "n", "Spp",
                       "Seed", "Sdlg", "Med")
        body <- auth |>
            dplyr::mutate(txt = sprintf(row_fmt, pad_ref(reference), accession, Samples,
                                        Species, Seeds, Seedlings,
                                        formatC(Median, format = "f", digits = .m$digits))) |>
            dplyr::pull(txt)
        long <- data.frame(row = seq_along(c(hdr, body)) - 1L, txt = c(hdr, body))
        tab <- ggplot(long, aes(0, -row, label = txt)) +
            geom_text(aes(fontface = ifelse(row == 0, "bold", "plain")),
                      hjust = 0, size = 2.5, family = "mono") +
            geom_hline(yintercept = -0.5, linewidth = 0.4) +
            scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.02, 1.05)) +
            # clip = "off": the row is drawn as one string, so if it runs a few characters
            # past the panel edge it must still render rather than losing a column.
            coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
            labs(title = "Contributing studies") +
            theme_void(base_size = 11) +
            theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, family = "Helvetica",
                                            margin = margin(b = 4)),
                  plot.margin = margin(4, 8, 2, 8))

        left_title <- ggplot() +
            annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, label = "Plant family", angle = 90,
                     size = 3.6, fontface = "bold", family = "Helvetica") +
            # the strip is narrower than the rotated text is tall, so an unclipped panel
            # is what keeps the "y" descender ("Plant familv" when clipped)
            coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
            theme_void()
        # Height split sized to the ink: the plot carries 16 faceted rows, the table 9
        # lines. At 6:1.1 the table held ~22% of the canvas for ~8% of the content and
        # squeezed the plot; at 9:1 with a larger face the rows collided because nine
        # lines no longer fitted the height. 7:1.2 at size 2.5 clears both.
        combined <- ((left_title | p) + patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(0.035, 1))) /
                    tab + patchwork::plot_layout(heights = c(7, 1.2))
        print(combined)
        save_nature_figure(fig(sprintf("alpha_%s_by_species_depth%d", .nm, .dp)),
                           combined, "tall")
    })
}
```

```{r fx-fig-tree-genus}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 | see the parts marked below
#   tree figures and host_phylosignal; each figure below is marked
# ==========================================================================================
# Phylogenetic tree of the most abundant genera, with their abundance at each stage.
# The tree is the pipeline's own (QIIME2, built from this study's ASV sequences), pruned
# to one tip per genus: that genus's most abundant ASV. No tree is inferred here.
# The tip labels in tree.nexus carry literal single quotes ('a4e1...'), which is why they
# match no ASV id as read; they are stripped before matching.
TREE_FILE <- resolve_path(base_dir, config$inputs$tree)
TREE_TOP_GENERA <- 50
# Genera left out of all three trees. Akkermansia is a gut bacterium that dominates the
# seeds of a single study (Cui wheat) and is a suspected contaminant. This removes it
# from the tree figures only; it is still in the filtered dataset and every statistic.
TREE_EXCLUDE_GENERA <- c("Akkermansia")
# Colours for phyla and genera in the trees. The two stage colours are left out because
# they mean seeds and seedlings in the stage rings, and within one figure phyla take the
# first colours and genera the ones after, so no colour stands for two things - with a
# shared palette the same purple was Proteobacteria in one ring and Enterobacter in the
# next, and the rings could not be read against the legends.
TREE_TAXON_COLOURS <- setdiff(NATURE_THICK, c(STAGE_PELLET, HOST_BREADTH_COLOURS,
                                              FIGURE_PALETTE$stage_generalist))
# One colour per phylum, fixed across the three trees: the phyla with the most ASVs are
# named and any other phylum is grey. Genera take the colours after these.
TREE_PHYLA_SHOWN <- 7
TREE_PHYLUM_COLOURS <- if (is.null(ps)) character() else {
    .phyla <- as(tax_table(ps), "matrix")[, "Phyla"]
    .phyla <- names(sort(table(.phyla[.phyla != ""]), decreasing = TRUE))
    .phyla <- .phyla[seq_len(min(TREE_PHYLA_SHOWN, length(.phyla)))]
    setNames(TREE_TAXON_COLOURS[seq_along(.phyla)], .phyla)
}
TREE_GENUS_COLOURS <- TREE_TAXON_COLOURS[-seq_len(TREE_PHYLA_SHOWN)]
# Genera named in a genus ring: those with the most ASVs in that tree; the rest are grey.
TREE_GENERA_SHOWN <- 11
# One ring per stage, each on its own colour scale running from near-white to that
# stage's colour, with a colour bar as its legend - so the legend shows exactly what the
# ring is drawn in. Drawn as opacity with a solid-colour key, the pale tiles in the rings
# matched nothing in the legend. Both stages share one range, so the rings compare tile
# for tile. The ring width is given outright, as a share (`rel_width`) of the tree's
# depth: a one-column ring has no x extent for geom_fruit to scale. Offsets are measured
# from where the previous ring starts, so the second ring is pushed out by the first
# ring's width - at a fixed small offset it was drawn on top of the first.
tree_stage_rings <- function(data, value, what, depth, rel_width, first_offset,
                             trans = "identity", border = NA, horizontal = FALSE) {
    top <- max(data[[value]])
    width <- rel_width * depth
    bar <- if (horizontal) {
        function(i) guide_colourbar(order = 10 + i, direction = "horizontal",
                                    title.position = "top", barwidth = unit(60, "pt"),
                                    barheight = unit(6, "pt"))
    } else {
        function(i) guide_colourbar(order = 10 + i, barwidth = unit(6, "pt"),
                                    barheight = unit(34, "pt"))
    }
    purrr::imap(STAGES, function(s, i) list(
        ggnewscale::new_scale_fill(),
        ggtreeExtra::geom_fruit(data = dplyr::filter(data, stage == s), geom = geom_tile,
                                mapping = aes(y = label, fill = .data[[value]]),
                                width = width,
                                offset = if (i == 1) first_offset else rel_width + 0.012,
                                colour = border, linewidth = 0.2),
        scale_fill_gradient(low = "grey97", high = STAGE_PELLET[[s]], trans = trans,
                            limits = c(0, top), name = sprintf("%s\n%s", s, what),
                            guide = bar(i))))
}
# An outer ring of bars round the tree: each ASV's mean relative abundance, the seed and
# seedling bars stacked, in the stage colours. The bars are solid, so they get a
# solid-colour key of their own, separate from the gradient bars of the prevalence rings,
# and a radial axis so the bar lengths can be read. `offset` has to clear the ring before
# it, whose width geom_fruit does not account for.
tree_stage_bars <- function(data, value, what, offset, pwidth = 0.28) list(
    ggnewscale::new_scale_fill(),
    ggtreeExtra::geom_fruit(data = data, geom = geom_col,
                            mapping = aes(y = label, x = .data[[value]], fill = stage),
                            orientation = "y", pwidth = pwidth, offset = offset,
                            axis.params = list(axis = "x", text.size = 1.6, nbreak = 3,
                                               vjust = 1),
                            grid.params = list(linewidth = 0.15)),
    scale_fill_manual(values = STAGE_PELLET, name = sprintf("Outer bars:\n%s", what),
                      guide = guide_legend(order = 20, ncol = 1)))
# Per-ASV prevalence and mean relative abundance at each stage, one row per ASV.
tree_stage_wide <- function(d) {
    dplyr::left_join(
        tidyr::pivot_wider(dplyr::select(d, label, stage, prevalence),
                           names_from = stage, values_from = prevalence),
        tidyr::pivot_wider(dplyr::select(d, label, stage, mean_rel),
                           names_from = stage, values_from = mean_rel,
                           names_prefix = "mean_rel_abundance_"),
        dplyr::join_by(label))
}
# METHODS - | NOT IN THE METHODOLOGY TEXT: figure: tree_genus_by_stage
fig_section("tree_genus_by_stage", needs = c(PS_CLEAN, TREE_FILE), {
    otu <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
    if (!taxa_are_rows(ps)) otu <- t(otu)
    tax <- as_tibble(as(tax_table(ps), "matrix"), rownames = "asv") |>
        dplyr::mutate(id = sub("^ASV [0-9]+ : ", "", asv), reads = rowSums(otu)[asv]) |>
        dplyr::filter(!is.na(Genus), Genus != "",
                      !grepl("^(Unassigned|unidentified|uncultured|metagenome)$", Genus,
                             ignore.case = TRUE),
                      !Genus %in% TREE_EXCLUDE_GENERA)
    # mean of per-sample relative abundances, as in the composition figures
    rel <- sweep(otu, 2, pmax(colSums(otu), 1), "/")
    genus_rel <- rowsum(rel[tax$asv, , drop = FALSE], tax$Genus)
    sample_stage <- meta[[PRIMARY]][match(colnames(genus_rel), meta$sample_id)]
    abund <- purrr::map(STAGES, function(s) {
        tibble(Genus = rownames(genus_rel), stage = s,
               mean_rel = rowMeans(genus_rel[, sample_stage == s, drop = FALSE]))
    }) |> list_rbind()
    top <- names(sort(rowMeans(genus_rel), decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(min(TREE_TOP_GENERA,
                                                                          nrow(genus_rel)))]
    reps <- tax |> dplyr::filter(Genus %in% top) |>
        dplyr::slice_max(reads, n = 1, by = Genus, with_ties = FALSE)

    tr <- if (grepl("\\.(nexus|nex)$", TREE_FILE, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
        ape::read.nexus(TREE_FILE)
    } else ape::read.tree(TREE_FILE)
    tr$tip.label <- gsub("'", "", tr$tip.label)
    reps <- reps |> dplyr::filter(id %in% tr$tip.label)
    tr <- ape::keep.tip(tr, reps$id)
    tr <- phangorn::midpoint(tr)
    # SILVA's compound genus names ("Allorhizobium-Neorhizobium-Pararhizobium-Rhizobium")
    # do not fit round a circular tree; the first name stands for the group. Short
    # compound names ("Escherichia-Shigella") are kept whole.
    reps$label <- ifelse(nchar(reps$Genus) > 25, sub("-.*$", " group", reps$Genus), reps$Genus)
    tr$tip.label <- reps$label[match(tr$tip.label, reps$id)]

    tips <- reps |> dplyr::select(label, Genus, Phylum = Phyla)
    abund <- abund |> dplyr::inner_join(tips, dplyr::join_by(Genus)) |>
        dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * mean_rel, stage = factor(stage, levels = STAGES))
    readr::write_csv(abund |> dplyr::select(Genus, Phylum, stage, mean_rel),
                     res("tables", "tree_genus_by_stage.csv"))

    `%<+%` <- ggtree::`%<+%`
    # branch.length = "none": a dendrogram of the branching order with every tip on one
    # circle, so labels and rings line up; branch lengths are in the tree file.
    # One ring per stage in that stage's colour; opacity carries abundance on a shared
    # scale, so the two rings compare tile for tile. sqrt, because a few genera hold
    # most of the reads.
    p <- ggtree::ggtree(tr, layout = "fan", open.angle = 10, branch.length = "none",
                        linewidth = 0.3) %<+% tips
    depth <- max(p$data$x)
    p <- p +
        ggtree::geom_tippoint(aes(colour = Phylum), size = 1.5) +
        scale_colour_manual(values = TREE_PHYLUM_COLOURS, na.value = "grey60",
                            name = "Phylum", guide = guide_legend(order = 1, ncol = 2)) +
        tree_stage_rings(abund, "pct", "mean relative abundance (%)", depth,
                         rel_width = 0.09, first_offset = 0.09, trans = "sqrt",
                         border = "white", horizontal = TRUE)
    p <- p + ggtree::geom_tiplab(aes(label = label), size = 1.9, fontface = "italic",
                                 offset = 0.33 * depth) +
        ggtree::hexpand(0.5) +
        labs(title = "Phylogeny of the most abundant genera in seeds and seedlings",
             subtitle = sprintf("%d genera, one tip per genus (its most abundant ASV). Inner ring: seeds; outer ring: seedlings.",
                                ape::Ntip(tr))) +
        theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "horizontal",
              legend.key.size = unit(8, "pt"),
              legend.text = element_text(size = 6), legend.title = element_text(size = 6.5),
              plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9, hjust = 0.5),
              plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 6.5, hjust = 0.5))
    print(p)
    save_nature_figure(fig("tree_genus_by_stage"), p, "square")
})

# The whole tree: every ASV that passed filtering, too many to name, so tips carry no
# labels. Branch tips are coloured by phylum; the rings, from the centre, give each ASV's
# genus and its prevalence (share of that stage's samples in which it was detected) in
# seeds and in seedlings.
# METHODS - | NOT IN THE METHODOLOGY TEXT: figure: tree_asv_by_stage
fig_section("tree_asv_by_stage", needs = c(PS_CLEAN, TREE_FILE), {
    otu <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
    if (!taxa_are_rows(ps)) otu <- t(otu)
    tax <- as_tibble(as(tax_table(ps), "matrix"), rownames = "asv") |>
        dplyr::mutate(label = sub("^ASV [0-9]+ : ", "", asv)) |>
        dplyr::filter(!Genus %in% TREE_EXCLUDE_GENERA)
    sample_stage <- meta[[PRIMARY]][match(colnames(otu), meta$sample_id)]
    # mean of per-sample relative abundances, as in the composition figures
    rel <- sweep(otu, 2, pmax(colSums(otu), 1), "/")
    prev <- purrr::map(STAGES, function(s) {
        tibble(label = tax$label, stage = s,
               prevalence = 100 * rowMeans(otu[tax$asv, sample_stage == s, drop = FALSE] > 0),
               mean_rel = 100 * rowMeans(rel[tax$asv, sample_stage == s, drop = FALSE]))
    }) |> list_rbind() |>
        dplyr::mutate(stage = factor(stage, levels = STAGES))

    tr <- if (grepl("\\.(nexus|nex)$", TREE_FILE, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
        ape::read.nexus(TREE_FILE)
    } else ape::read.tree(TREE_FILE)
    tr$tip.label <- gsub("'", "", tr$tip.label)
    tr <- ape::keep.tip(tr, intersect(tax$label, tr$tip.label))
    tr <- phangorn::midpoint(tr)

    shown <- names(TREE_PHYLUM_COLOURS)
    tips <- tax |> dplyr::filter(label %in% tr$tip.label) |>
        dplyr::mutate(Phylum = factor(ifelse(Phyla %in% shown, Phyla, "Other"),
                                      levels = c(shown, "Other")),
                      # a missing or placeholder genus is not a genus to name in the ring
                      Genus = ifelse(is.na(Genus) | grepl("^(|Unassigned|unidentified|uncultured|metagenome)$",
                                                          Genus, ignore.case = TRUE),
                                     "Unassigned", Genus),
                      # long compound SILVA names shortened as in the genus tree
                      Genus_label = ifelse(nchar(Genus) > 25, sub("-.*$", " group", Genus), Genus),
                      Genus_shown = forcats::fct_other(
                          Genus_label, keep = names(sort(table(Genus_label[Genus != "Unassigned"]),
                                                         decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(TREE_GENERA_SHOWN)],
                          other_level = "Other genera")) |>
        dplyr::select(label, Phylum, Genus, Genus_shown)
    prev <- dplyr::filter(prev, label %in% tr$tip.label)
    wide <- tree_stage_wide(prev)
    wide$found_in <- dplyr::case_when(wide[[STAGES[1]]] > 0 & wide[[STAGES[2]]] > 0 ~ "both stages",
                                      wide[[STAGES[1]]] > 0 ~ paste(STAGES[1], "only"),
                                      .default = paste(STAGES[2], "only"))
    readr::write_csv(dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(tips, -Genus_shown), wide,
                                      dplyr::join_by(label)),
                     res("tables", "tree_asv_by_stage.csv"))
    n_found <- table(wide$found_in)
    genera <- setdiff(levels(tips$Genus_shown), "Other genera")
    genus_colours <- c(setNames(TREE_GENUS_COLOURS[seq_along(genera)], genera),
                       "Other genera" = "grey88")

    `%<+%` <- ggtree::`%<+%`
    # branch.length = "none", as in the genus figure: a few very long branches otherwise
    # squeeze the rest of the tree into the centre, far from the rings.
    p <- ggtree::ggtree(tr, layout = "fan", open.angle = 8, branch.length = "none",
                        linewidth = 0.12, colour = "grey35") %<+% tips
    # a one-column ring has no x extent for geom_fruit to scale, so its width is given
    genus_ring_width <- 0.05 * max(p$data$x)
    p <- p +
        ggtree::geom_tippoint(aes(colour = Phylum), size = 0.3) +
        scale_colour_manual(values = c(TREE_PHYLUM_COLOURS, Other = "grey60"),
                            name = "Phylum (tips)",
                            guide = guide_legend(order = 1, ncol = 2,
                                                 override.aes = list(size = 2))) +
        # no `data`: the genus column is already on the tree, joined with the tips above
        ggtreeExtra::geom_fruit(geom = geom_tile, mapping = aes(fill = Genus_shown),
                                width = genus_ring_width, offset = 0.04) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = genus_colours, name = "Genus (ring 1)",
                          guide = guide_legend(order = 2, ncol = 2)) +
        tree_stage_rings(prev, "prevalence", "prevalence (% of samples)",
                         max(p$data$x), rel_width = 0.05, first_offset = 0.065,
                         trans = "sqrt") +
        tree_stage_bars(prev, "mean_rel", "mean relative abundance (%)", offset = 0.075) +
        labs(title = "Phylogenetic tree of all filtered ASVs in seeds and seedlings",
             subtitle = sprintf("%s ASVs: %s in both stages, %s in %s, %s in %s.\nRings, from the centre: genus, seeds, seedlings. Outer bars: mean relative abundance.",
                                comma(ape::Ntip(tr)), comma(n_found[["both stages"]]),
                                comma(n_found[[paste(STAGES[1], "only")]]), tolower(paste(STAGES[1], "only")),
                                comma(n_found[[paste(STAGES[2], "only")]]), tolower(paste(STAGES[2], "only")))) +
        theme(legend.position = "right", legend.box = "vertical",
              legend.key.size = unit(8, "pt"),
              legend.text = element_text(size = 6), legend.title = element_text(size = 6.5),
              plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9, hjust = 0.5),
              plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 6.5, hjust = 0.5))
    print(p)
    save_nature_figure(fig("tree_asv_by_stage"), p, "square")
})

# The prevalent ASVs only, with phylum and genus as rings of their own (innermost first:
# phylum, genus, seeds, seedlings). The threshold is the config's core prevalence, 50% of
# samples. No ASV reaches that across all samples pooled - the most widespread one is in
# 41.7% - because 98.8% of ASVs occur in a single study. It is therefore applied within
# study: an ASV is kept if it is in at least 50% of the samples of at least one study.
TREE_MIN_PREVALENCE <- config$taxonomy_analysis$core_prevalence_threshold
# METHODS - | NOT IN THE METHODOLOGY TEXT: figure: tree_asv_prevalent_by_stage
fig_section("tree_asv_prevalent_by_stage", needs = c(PS_CLEAN, TREE_FILE), {
    otu <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
    if (!taxa_are_rows(ps)) otu <- t(otu)
    tax <- as_tibble(as(tax_table(ps), "matrix"), rownames = "asv") |>
        dplyr::mutate(label = sub("^ASV [0-9]+ : ", "", asv),
                      overall = rowMeans(otu[asv, , drop = FALSE] > 0)) |>
        dplyr::filter(!Genus %in% TREE_EXCLUDE_GENERA)
    sample_study <- meta$study_alias[match(colnames(otu), meta$sample_id)]
    by_study <- sapply(split(seq_len(ncol(otu)), sample_study),
                       function(i) rowMeans(otu[, i, drop = FALSE] > 0))
    tax$n_studies <- rowSums(by_study[tax$asv, , drop = FALSE] >= TREE_MIN_PREVALENCE)
    tax <- dplyr::filter(tax, n_studies >= 1)
    if (nrow(tax) < 3) stop(sprintf("only %d ASVs reach %.0f%% prevalence in a study",
                                    nrow(tax), 100 * TREE_MIN_PREVALENCE))
    sample_stage <- meta[[PRIMARY]][match(colnames(otu), meta$sample_id)]
    # mean of per-sample relative abundances, as in the composition figures
    rel <- sweep(otu, 2, pmax(colSums(otu), 1), "/")
    prev <- purrr::map(STAGES, function(s) {
        tibble(label = tax$label, stage = s,
               prevalence = 100 * rowMeans(otu[tax$asv, sample_stage == s, drop = FALSE] > 0),
               mean_rel = 100 * rowMeans(rel[tax$asv, sample_stage == s, drop = FALSE]))
    }) |> list_rbind() |>
        dplyr::mutate(stage = factor(stage, levels = STAGES))

    tr <- if (grepl("\\.(nexus|nex)$", TREE_FILE, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
        ape::read.nexus(TREE_FILE)
    } else ape::read.tree(TREE_FILE)
    tr$tip.label <- gsub("'", "", tr$tip.label)
    tr <- ape::keep.tip(tr, intersect(tax$label, tr$tip.label))
    tr <- phangorn::midpoint(tr)

    tips <- tax |> dplyr::filter(label %in% tr$tip.label) |>
        dplyr::mutate(Genus = ifelse(is.na(Genus) | Genus == "", "Unassigned", Genus),
                      # the genera with the most ASVs are named, the rest grouped
                      Genus_shown = forcats::fct_other(
                          Genus, keep = names(sort(table(Genus), decreasing = TRUE))[
                              seq_len(min(TREE_GENERA_SHOWN, dplyr::n_distinct(Genus)))],
                          other_level = "Other genera")) |>
        dplyr::select(label, Phylum = Phyla, Genus, Genus_shown, overall, n_studies)
    prev <- dplyr::filter(prev, label %in% tr$tip.label)
    readr::write_csv(tips |> dplyr::select(-Genus_shown) |>
                         dplyr::mutate(overall = 100 * overall) |>
                         dplyr::left_join(tree_stage_wide(prev), dplyr::join_by(label)),
                     res("tables", "tree_asv_prevalent_by_stage.csv"))

    p <- ggtree::ggtree(tr, layout = "fan", open.angle = 10, branch.length = "none",
                        linewidth = 0.3)
    # A one-column ring has no x extent for geom_fruit to scale, so its tile width is
    # given outright, as a share of the tree's depth.
    ring_width <- 0.07 * max(p$data$x)
    genera <- setdiff(levels(tips$Genus_shown), "Other genera")
    genus_colours <- c(setNames(TREE_GENUS_COLOURS[seq_along(genera)], genera),
                       "Other genera" = "grey70")
    taxon_ring <- function(column, title, order, colours) list(
        ggnewscale::new_scale_fill(),
        ggtreeExtra::geom_fruit(data = tips, geom = geom_tile,
                                mapping = aes(y = label, fill = .data[[column]]),
                                width = ring_width, offset = 0.06, colour = "white",
                                linewidth = 0.2),
        scale_fill_manual(values = colours, na.value = "grey60",
                          name = title, guide = guide_legend(order = order, ncol = 1)))
    p <- p +
        taxon_ring("Phylum", "Phylum (ring 1)", 1, TREE_PHYLUM_COLOURS) +
        taxon_ring("Genus_shown", "Genus (ring 2)", 2, genus_colours) +
        tree_stage_rings(prev, "prevalence", "prevalence (% of samples)",
                         max(p$data$x), rel_width = 0.07, first_offset = 0.09,
                         border = "white") +
        tree_stage_bars(prev, "mean_rel", "mean relative abundance (%)", offset = 0.1) +
        labs(title = "Phylogenetic tree of the most prevalent ASVs in seeds and seedlings",
             subtitle = sprintf("%d ASVs present in at least %.0f%% of the samples of at least one study.\nRings, from the centre: phylum, genus, seeds, seedlings. Outer bars: mean relative abundance.",
                                ape::Ntip(tr), 100 * TREE_MIN_PREVALENCE)) +
        theme(legend.position = "right", legend.box = "vertical",
              legend.key.size = unit(8, "pt"),
              legend.text = element_text(size = 6), legend.title = element_text(size = 6.5),
              plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9, hjust = 0.5),
              plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 6.5, hjust = 0.5))
    print(p)
    save_nature_figure(fig("tree_asv_prevalent_by_stage"), p, "square")
})

# Generalist and specialist genera on the genus tree, to show whether either kind of
# specialism follows phylogeny. The classes are Part 1's (chunk `generalist-specialist`,
# tables/generalist_specialist_genus.csv); nothing is tested here. One tip per genus that
# got a stage class, its most abundant ASV, as in the genus tree above. Inner ring: stage
# class from the CLAM test. Second ring: host class from the two-stage host screening
# (column `screen_class`: generalist = at or above the breadth threshold and not clustered
# on the host tree; specialist = one host species; intermediate = the rest). It replaced
# the Levins' B class the ring first showed, so that the figure uses the same host classes
# as the trees and tables that follow from the screening. Outside them, a
# heatmap with one column per host plant genus gives the host context: on which hosts the
# genus was found, shaded by its mean relative abundance there. Cells for hosts where it
# was absent are drawn in a faint grey, not left blank, so that a column can be followed
# round the tree to its name. The colour scale is logarithmic and runs through several
# hues (viridis, darkest = most abundant): over half the detected cells are below 0.1% and
# the top one is 86%, so on a square-root scale in a single hue nearly every cell was the
# same pale shade.
# A stage class is drawn as a full-length bar only where the genus got that class in at
# least two studies on their own, and as a half-length bar otherwise. Most genera occur in
# one study, and without this the figure shows a whole clade of "seed specialists" that is
# the 12 seed samples of a single study. It was first shown by fading the unsupported
# tiles, but faded navy, red and tan could not be told apart, nor from the greys beside
# them; every class is now a solid colour.
SPECIALIST_TABLE <- res("tables", "generalist_specialist_genus.csv")
# Tips that carry a name: the most abundant genera. All of them do not fit round the tree.
TREE_LABELLED_GENERA <- 40
# Seed and seedling specialists take the stage colours. The seven classes of the two rings
# are chosen to be told apart at a glance, within a ring and between the rings: the two
# stage colours and navy in the first; the two host-breadth colours and grey in the second.
TREE_STAGE_GENERALIST_COLOUR <- FIGURE_PALETTE$stage_generalist
TREE_HOST_CLASS_COLOURS <- c("Host generalist" = HOST_BREADTH_COLOURS[["generalist"]],
                             "Host specialist" = HOST_BREADTH_COLOURS[["specialist"]],
                             "Intermediate" = "grey78")
# Bar length of a stage class, by how many studies give the genus that class on their own.
TREE_STAGE_SUPPORT_LENGTH <- c("Two or more studies" = 1, "One study or none" = 0.5)
# Range of the heatmap's colour scale, in per cent mean relative abundance. Anything
# detected below the lower limit is drawn in the lowest colour.
TREE_HOST_ABUNDANCE_LIMITS <- c(0.01, 100)
# METHODS 5 | figure: tree_generalist_specialist_genus (CLAM class and host screen, genus level)
fig_section("tree_generalist_specialist_genus", needs = c(PS_CLEAN, TREE_FILE, SPECIALIST_TABLE), {
    stage_names <- c(setNames(sprintf("%s specialist", sub("s$", "", STAGES)),
                              paste0("Specialist_", STAGES)),
                     Generalist = "Stage generalist")
    stage_colours <- c(setNames(unname(STAGE_PELLET[STAGES]), stage_names[seq_along(STAGES)]),
                       "Stage generalist" = TREE_STAGE_GENERALIST_COLOUR)
    host_names <- c(Generalist = "Host generalist", Specialist = "Host specialist",
                    Intermediate = "Intermediate")
    cls <- read_csv(SPECIALIST_TABLE, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::filter(stage_class %in% names(stage_names), !Genus %in% TREE_EXCLUDE_GENERA) |>
        dplyr::mutate(stage_class = factor(stage_names[stage_class], levels = stage_names),
                      host_class = factor(host_names[screen_class], levels = host_names),
                      support = factor(ifelse(n_studies_agree >= 2,
                                              names(TREE_STAGE_SUPPORT_LENGTH)[1],
                                              names(TREE_STAGE_SUPPORT_LENGTH)[2]),
                                       levels = names(TREE_STAGE_SUPPORT_LENGTH)))

    otu <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
    if (!taxa_are_rows(ps)) otu <- t(otu)
    tax <- as_tibble(as(tax_table(ps), "matrix"), rownames = "asv") |>
        dplyr::mutate(id = sub("^ASV [0-9]+ : ", "", asv), reads = rowSums(otu)[asv]) |>
        dplyr::filter(Genus %in% cls$Genus)
    # mean of per-sample relative abundances, as in the composition figures
    rel <- sweep(otu, 2, pmax(colSums(otu), 1), "/")
    genus_by_sample <- rowsum(rel[tax$asv, , drop = FALSE], tax$Genus)
    genus_rel <- rowMeans(genus_by_sample)
    # the same, within each host plant genus (the first word of the host species name)
    sample_host <- sub(" .*$", "", meta[[config$generalist_specialist$host_group]][
        match(colnames(genus_by_sample), meta$sample_id)])
    host_rel <- sapply(split(seq_len(ncol(genus_by_sample)), sample_host),
                       function(i) rowMeans(genus_by_sample[, i, drop = FALSE]))
    reps <- tax |> dplyr::slice_max(reads, n = 1, by = Genus, with_ties = FALSE)

    tr <- if (grepl("\\.(nexus|nex)$", TREE_FILE, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
        ape::read.nexus(TREE_FILE)
    } else ape::read.tree(TREE_FILE)
    tr$tip.label <- gsub("'", "", tr$tip.label)
    reps <- reps |> dplyr::filter(id %in% tr$tip.label)
    tr <- ape::keep.tip(tr, reps$id)
    tr <- phangorn::midpoint(tr)
    reps$label <- ifelse(nchar(reps$Genus) > 25, sub("-.*$", " group", reps$Genus), reps$Genus)
    tr$tip.label <- reps$label[match(tr$tip.label, reps$id)]

    tips <- reps |> dplyr::select(label, Genus, Phylum = Phyla) |>
        dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(cls, Genus, stage_class, host_class, support),
                         dplyr::join_by(Genus)) |>
        dplyr::mutate(Phylum = ifelse(Phylum %in% names(TREE_PHYLUM_COLOURS), Phylum, "Other"),
                      mean_rel = genus_rel[Genus],
                      shown = ifelse(rank(-mean_rel) <= TREE_LABELLED_GENERA, label, ""))
    hosts <- as_tibble(100 * host_rel[tips$Genus, , drop = FALSE], rownames = "Genus")
    readr::write_csv(tips |> dplyr::select(Genus, Phylum, stage_class, support, host_class) |>
                         dplyr::left_join(hosts, dplyr::join_by(Genus)),
                     res("tables", "tree_generalist_specialist_genus.csv"))
    host_long <- hosts |>
        tidyr::pivot_longer(-Genus, names_to = "host", values_to = "pct") |>
        dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(tips, Genus, label), dplyr::join_by(Genus)) |>
        dplyr::mutate(pct = ifelse(pct > 0, pct, NA_real_))

    `%<+%` <- ggtree::`%<+%`
    # the wider opening holds the host names of the heatmap columns
    p <- ggtree::ggtree(tr, layout = "fan", open.angle = 24, branch.length = "none",
                        linewidth = 0.25) %<+% tips
    depth <- max(p$data$x)
    # the ring data may not share a column name with the tree data it is drawn on
    class_scale <- function(title, order, colours) {
        scale_fill_manual(values = colours, name = title, drop = FALSE,
                          guide = guide_legend(order = order, ncol = 1,
                                               override.aes = list(colour = "grey35")))
    }
    p <- p +
        ggtree::geom_tippoint(aes(colour = Phylum), size = 0.7) +
        scale_colour_manual(values = c(TREE_PHYLUM_COLOURS, Other = "grey60"),
                            name = "Phylum",
                            guide = guide_legend(order = 1, ncol = 2,
                                                 override.aes = list(size = 2))) +
        ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
        ggtreeExtra::geom_fruit(
            data = dplyr::transmute(tips, label, ring_class = stage_class,
                                    ring_length = TREE_STAGE_SUPPORT_LENGTH[as.character(support)]),
            geom = geom_col, mapping = aes(y = label, x = ring_length, fill = ring_class),
            orientation = "y", width = 1, pwidth = 0.13, offset = 0.05, colour = "white",
            linewidth = 0.1) +
        class_scale("Stage class", 2,
                    stage_colours) +
        ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
        ggtreeExtra::geom_fruit(
            data = dplyr::select(tips, label, ring_class = host_class), geom = geom_tile,
            mapping = aes(y = label, fill = ring_class), width = 0.09 * depth,
            offset = 0.07, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
        class_scale("Host class", 3, TREE_HOST_CLASS_COLOURS) +
        ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
        ggtreeExtra::geom_fruit(data = host_long, geom = geom_tile,
                                mapping = aes(y = label, x = host, fill = pct),
                                pwidth = 0.52, offset = 0.05, colour = "white",
                                linewidth = 0.15,
                                axis.params = list(axis = "x", text.size = 1.9,
                                                   text.angle = -78, hjust = 0,
                                                   line.size = 0)) +
        scale_fill_gradientn(colours = PALETTE_CONTRAST, trans = "log10",
                             limits = TREE_HOST_ABUNDANCE_LIMITS, oob = scales::squish,
                             breaks = 10^seq(log10(TREE_HOST_ABUNDANCE_LIMITS[1]),
                                             log10(TREE_HOST_ABUNDANCE_LIMITS[2])),
                             labels = function(x) ifelse(x == TREE_HOST_ABUNDANCE_LIMITS[1],
                                                         paste0("\u2264", x), x),
                             na.value = "grey96",
                             name = "Mean relative abundance\non host genus (%)",
                             guide = guide_colourbar(order = 4, direction = "horizontal",
                                                     barwidth = unit(95, "pt"),
                                                     barheight = unit(8, "pt"))) +
        ggtree::geom_tiplab(aes(label = shown), size = 2.1, fontface = "italic",
                            offset = 1.02 * depth) +
        # With the heatmap the tree needs the full page width, so the legends go beneath it.
        theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "horizontal", legend.box.just = "top",
              legend.title.position = "top",
              legend.key.size = unit(10, "pt"), legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
              legend.title = element_text(size = 8.5, face = "bold"),
              legend.spacing.x = unit(14, "pt"), legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
              legend.box.spacing = unit(2, "pt"), plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 8, 2))
    print(p)
    # double-column width (183 mm), the height set by the square tree plus its legends
    ggsave(fig("tree_generalist_specialist_genus"), p, width = 7.2, height = 8.3, dpi = 300,
           compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
})

# Trees of the host generalist and the host specialist ASVs, one figure each. The classes
# are Part 1's double screening (tables/generalist_specialist_asv_host_screen.csv): a
# generalist is found on at least the threshold number of host species and its hosts are
# not significantly clustered on the host tree; a specialist is found on one host species.
# The trees are the maximum-likelihood trees built by generalist_specialist_trees.sh
# (generalists: MUSCLE, trimAl, IQ-TREE; specialists: MAFFT, trimAl, FastTree), midpoint-
# rooted here for display; nothing is inferred in this document. They were first drawn by
# pruning the pipeline's ASV tree, before those trees existed. Both are annotated alike:
# inner ring phylum, second ring class. On the generalist tree a dot marks branches with
# ultrafast bootstrap support of 95% or more. Outside the rings, the generalist tree
# has a bar per ASV for the number of host species it was found on. Every specialist has
# one host, so its tree shows which instead: one thin ring per host plant family, marked
# where the ASV's host belongs to it. Position carries the family, not colour: with seven
# phyla and eight classes already coloured, six more colours could not be kept apart.
HOST_SCREEN_ASVS <- res("tables", "generalist_specialist_asv_host_screen.csv")
HOST_SCREEN_TREES <- c(Generalist = res("trees", "generalists", "tree.nwk"),
                       Specialist = res("trees", "specialists", "tree.nwk"))
# Ultrafast bootstrap support (%) from which a branch of the generalist tree is marked.
TREE_SUPPORT_SHOWN <- 95
# Plant family of each host, from the host species table Part 1 writes.
HOST_SIGNAL_HOSTS <- res("tables", "host_plant_species.csv")
# Classes named in the class ring: those with the most ASVs over the two trees together,
# so a class has the same colour in both; the rest are grouped.
TREE_CLASSES_SHOWN <- 8
# Soft colours for the class ring, so it cannot be taken for the phylum ring beside it.
TREE_CLASS_COLOURS <- FIGURE_PALETTE$pastel
# Genera named on the generalist tree: the most abundant, each at its most abundant ASV.
TREE_LABELLED_ASV_GENERA <- 20
# METHODS 7 | figures: tree_host_generalists, tree_host_specialists
host_screen_tree <- function(group, outer = c("bars", "families")) {
    outer <- match.arg(outer)
    otu <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
    if (!taxa_are_rows(ps)) otu <- t(otu)
    # mean of per-sample relative abundances, as in the composition figures
    mean_rel <- rowMeans(sweep(otu, 2, pmax(colSums(otu), 1), "/"))
    tax_class <- as(tax_table(ps), "matrix")[, "Class"]
    asv <- read_csv(HOST_SCREEN_ASVS, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::filter(screen_class %in% c("Generalist", "Specialist"),
                      !Genus %in% TREE_EXCLUDE_GENERA) |>
        dplyr::mutate(label = sub("^ASV [0-9]+ : ", "", ASV), Class = unname(tax_class[ASV]),
                      Class = ifelse(is.na(Class) | Class == "", "Unassigned", Class),
                      mean_rel = unname(mean_rel[ASV]))
    classes <- names(sort(table(asv$Class), decreasing = TRUE))
    classes <- classes[seq_len(min(TREE_CLASSES_SHOWN, length(classes)))]
    class_colours <- c(setNames(TREE_CLASS_COLOURS[seq_along(classes)], classes),
                       "Other classes" = "grey88")
    asv <- dplyr::filter(asv, screen_class == group)

    tr <- ape::read.tree(HOST_SCREEN_TREES[[group]])
    tr <- ape::keep.tip(tr, intersect(asv$label, tr$tip.label))
    # support values stay on the branches they belong to when the root moves
    tr <- phangorn::midpoint(tr, node.labels = "support")

    tips <- dplyr::filter(asv, label %in% tr$tip.label)
    # one name per genus, on its most abundant ASV, for the most abundant genera
    named_tips <- tips |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(Genus), Genus != "") |>
        dplyr::mutate(genus_rel = sum(mean_rel), .by = Genus) |>
        dplyr::slice_max(mean_rel, n = 1, by = Genus, with_ties = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::slice_max(genus_rel, n = TREE_LABELLED_ASV_GENERA, with_ties = FALSE)
    tips <- tips |>
        dplyr::mutate(
            ring_phylum = ifelse(Phylum %in% names(TREE_PHYLUM_COLOURS), Phylum, "Other"),
            ring_class = factor(ifelse(Class %in% classes, Class, "Other classes"),
                                levels = intersect(names(class_colours),
                                                   c(Class, "Other classes"))) |> droplevels(),
            # long compound SILVA names do not fit round the tree; the first name stands in
            shown = ifelse(outer == "bars" & label %in% named_tips$label,
                           ifelse(nchar(Genus) > 25, sub("-.*$", " group", Genus), Genus), ""))

    `%<+%` <- ggtree::`%<+%`
    p <- ggtree::ggtree(tr, layout = "fan", open.angle = if (outer == "families") 24 else 12,
                        branch.length = "none", linewidth = 0.2) %<+%
        dplyr::select(tips, label, shown)
    depth <- max(p$data$x)
    # the ring data may not share a column name with the tree data it is drawn on
    ring <- function(column, title, order, colours) list(
        ggnewscale::new_scale_fill(),
        ggtreeExtra::geom_fruit(
            data = dplyr::select(tips, label, ring_value = dplyr::all_of(column)),
            geom = geom_tile, mapping = aes(y = label, fill = ring_value),
            width = 0.08 * depth, offset = 0.06, colour = NA),
        scale_fill_manual(values = colours, name = title,
                          guide = guide_legend(
                              order = order,
                              # phyla in one column, so the keys fit the width at a readable size
                              ncol = if (dplyr::n_distinct(tips[[column]]) <= 4 || column == "ring_phylum") 1 else 2,
                              override.aes = list(colour = "grey35"))))
    p <- p +
        ring("ring_phylum", "Phylum", 1,
             c(TREE_PHYLUM_COLOURS, Other = "grey60")) +
        ring("ring_class", "Class", 2, class_colours)

    if (outer == "bars") {
        p <- p +
            ggtree::geom_nodepoint(aes(subset = !isTip & !is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(label))) &
                                           suppressWarnings(as.numeric(label)) >= TREE_SUPPORT_SHOWN,
                                       shape = "support"), size = 0.5, colour = "black") +
            scale_shape_manual(values = c(support = 16),
                               labels = sprintf("Bootstrap %d%%\nor more", TREE_SUPPORT_SHOWN),
                               name = "Branch support",
                               guide = guide_legend(order = 0, override.aes = list(size = 2))) +
            ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
            ggtreeExtra::geom_fruit(
                data = dplyr::transmute(tips, label, bar_hosts = n_hosts,
                                        bar_key = "Number of host\nplant species"),
                geom = geom_col, mapping = aes(y = label, x = bar_hosts, fill = bar_key),
                orientation = "y", pwidth = 0.3, offset = 0.07,
                axis.params = list(axis = "x", text.size = 3.2, nbreak = 3, vjust = 1),
                grid.params = list(linewidth = 0.15)) +
            scale_fill_manual(values = c("Number of host\nplant species" = "grey25"),
                              name = "Host breadth",
                              guide = guide_legend(order = 3)) +
            ggtree::geom_tiplab(aes(label = shown), size = 3.2, fontface = "italic",
                                offset = 0.5 * depth)
        outer_text <- "Outer bars: number of host plant species the ASV was found on."
    } else {
        hosts <- read_csv(HOST_SIGNAL_HOSTS, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
            dplyr::filter(!grepl("species$", Species)) |>
            dplyr::transmute(host_genus = sub(" .*$", "", Species), Family) |>
            dplyr::distinct()
        found <- tips |>
            dplyr::inner_join(hosts, dplyr::join_by(representative_host_genus == host_genus)) |>
            dplyr::transmute(label, host_family = factor(Family, levels = sort(unique(hosts$Family))),
                             found = "Host")
        if (nrow(found) != nrow(tips)) stop("a specialist ASV has no host plant family")
        p <- p +
            ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
            ggtreeExtra::geom_fruit(
                data = tidyr::complete(found, label, host_family, fill = list(found = "No")),
                geom = geom_tile, mapping = aes(y = label, x = host_family, fill = found),
                pwidth = 0.3, offset = 0.07,
                axis.params = list(axis = "x", text.size = 2.6, text.angle = -78, hjust = 0,
                                   line.size = 0)) +
            scale_fill_manual(values = c(Host = "grey15", No = "grey94"),
                              labels = c(Host = "Host of the ASV", No = "Not its host"),
                              name = "Host family",
                              guide = guide_legend(order = 3, ncol = 1,
                                                   override.aes = list(colour = "grey35")))
        outer_text <- "Outer rings: host plant family, one ring each, marked where the ASV's only host belongs to it."
    }
    # A fan tree leaves a blank band round itself for tip names. The specialist tree has
    # none, so its subtitle and legends are pulled into that band; the generalist tree's
    # names fill it, so there the subtitle and legends are kept clear of them.
    slack <- if (outer == "families") -22 else 10
    # tip names may run past the panel's edge rather than be cut there
    p$coordinates$clip <- "off"
    # no title or subtitle: the legend of the figure says what the tree is. Each tree is
    # drawn 7.2 in wide and set at half that in main Figure 5, so its type is drawn at
    # twice the size it is read at (tip names 5 pt, keys 5.5 and 6.5 pt in the figure)
    p +
        theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "horizontal", legend.box.just = "top",
              legend.title.position = "top", legend.key.size = unit(14, "pt"),
              legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
              legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
              legend.spacing.x = unit(8, "pt"), legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
              legend.box.spacing = unit(slack, "pt"),
              plot.margin = if (outer == "bars") margin(40, 30, 6, 30) else margin(2, 2, 6, 2))
}
fig_section("tree_host_generalists",
            needs = c(PS_CLEAN, HOST_SCREEN_TREES[["Generalist"]], HOST_SCREEN_ASVS), {
    p <- host_screen_tree("Generalist", "bars")
    print(p)
    ggsave(fig("tree_host_generalists"), p, width = 7.2, height = 8.1, dpi = 300,
           compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
})
fig_section("tree_host_specialists",
            needs = c(PS_CLEAN, HOST_SCREEN_TREES[["Specialist"]], HOST_SCREEN_ASVS,
                      HOST_SIGNAL_HOSTS), {
    p <- host_screen_tree("Specialist", "families")
    print(p)
    # taller than wide: with 1,100 tips the tree takes the full page width, and the three
    # legends sit beneath it
    ggsave(fig("tree_host_specialists"), p, width = 7.2, height = 8.3, dpi = 300,
           compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
})

# The host generalist and the host specialist ASVs on ONE tree: the main figure of the
# generalist/specialist analysis. The two trees above show each class on its own; this one
# shows where the classes sit relative to each other. Everything drawn is a stored result:
# the tree is the combined maximum-likelihood tree of generalist_specialist_trees.sh, the
# classes and host breadth are Part 1's two-stage screening, and the predicted oxygen use is
# predicted_traits.py's BugBase table. From the centre outwards: branches and a ring in the
# class colours; phylum; predicted oxygen use (anaerobes are the trait most strongly tied to
# narrow host range); one ring per host plant family, filled where the ASV was detected on
# it; and bars for the number of host species. Intermediate ASVs are in neither class and
# are not on the tree. No title is drawn into the artwork: a main figure takes its caption
# in the manuscript.
COMBINED_TREE <- res("trees", "combined", "tree.nwk")
PREDICTED_TRAITS <- res("tables", "predicted_traits_asv.csv")
BREADTH_ABUNDANCE <- res("tables", "generalist_specialist_breadth_abundance.csv")
# The generalists are the few, so they take the accent colour and the specialists a quiet
# dark one. Oxygen use runs pale to dark blue; none of these is a phylum colour.
HOST_CLASS_COLOURS <- c("Host generalist" = HOST_BREADTH_COLOURS[["generalist"]],
                        "Host specialist" = HOST_BREADTH_COLOURS[["specialist"]])
OXYGEN_COLOURS <- c(unlist(FIGURE_PALETTE$oxygen), "Not predicted" = "white")
# Generalist genera named round the tree: the most abundant, each on its most abundant ASV,
# and no two closer than this share of the circle, so that names never run into each other.
COMBINED_TREE_LABELS <- 12
COMBINED_TREE_LABEL_GAP <- 0.035
# METHODS 7 | figure: tree_generalist_specialist (both classes; rings from paragraphs 6 and 8)
fig_section("tree_generalist_specialist",
            needs = c(PS_CLEAN, COMBINED_TREE, HOST_SCREEN_ASVS, HOST_SIGNAL_HOSTS,
                      PREDICTED_TRAITS, BREADTH_ABUNDANCE), {
    otu <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
    if (!taxa_are_rows(ps)) otu <- t(otu)
    mean_rel <- rowMeans(sweep(otu, 2, pmax(colSums(otu), 1), "/"))
    traits <- read_csv(PREDICTED_TRAITS, show_col_types = FALSE, na = "NA", guess_max = 5000) |>
        dplyr::transmute(ASV, oxygen = dplyr::case_when(
            bugbase_Anaerobic ~ "Anaerobic",
            bugbase_Facultatively_Anaerobic ~ "Facultatively anaerobic",
            bugbase_Aerobic ~ "Aerobic", TRUE ~ "Not predicted"))
    asv <- read_csv(HOST_SCREEN_ASVS, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::filter(screen_class %in% c("Generalist", "Specialist"),
                      !Genus %in% TREE_EXCLUDE_GENERA) |>
        dplyr::left_join(traits, dplyr::join_by(ASV)) |>
        dplyr::mutate(label = sub("^ASV [0-9]+ : ", "", ASV),
                      class_name = factor(paste("Host", tolower(screen_class)),
                                          levels = names(HOST_CLASS_COLOURS)),
                      phylum_name = ifelse(Phylum %in% names(TREE_PHYLUM_COLOURS), Phylum, "Other"),
                      oxygen = factor(dplyr::coalesce(oxygen, "Not predicted"),
                                      levels = names(OXYGEN_COLOURS)),
                      mean_rel = unname(mean_rel[ASV]))

    tr <- ape::read.tree(COMBINED_TREE)
    tr <- ape::keep.tip(tr, intersect(asv$label, tr$tip.label))
    tr <- phangorn::midpoint(tr)
    tips <- dplyr::filter(asv, label %in% tr$tip.label)
    # branches leading only to one class take its colour; mixed ones stay grey
    tr <- ggtree::groupOTU(tr, split(tips$label, tips$class_name), group_name = "branch_class")

    # on which host plant families each ASV was detected
    families <- read_csv(HOST_SIGNAL_HOSTS, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::filter(!grepl("species$", Species))
    sample_family <- families$Family[match(meta[[config$generalist_specialist$host_group]][
        match(colnames(otu), meta$sample_id)], families$Species)]
    detected <- sapply(split(seq_len(ncol(otu)), sample_family),
                       function(i) rowSums(otu[tips$ASV, i, drop = FALSE]) > 0)
    family_long <- tibble::as_tibble(detected) |>
        dplyr::mutate(label = tips$label) |>
        tidyr::pivot_longer(-label, names_to = "host_family", values_to = "found") |>
        dplyr::mutate(found = ifelse(found, "Detected", "Not detected"))

    named <- tips |> dplyr::filter(screen_class == "Generalist", !is.na(Genus), Genus != "") |>
        dplyr::mutate(genus_rel = sum(mean_rel), .by = Genus) |>
        dplyr::slice_max(mean_rel, n = 1, by = Genus, with_ties = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(genus_rel)) |>
        dplyr::transmute(label, shown = ifelse(nchar(Genus) > 25, sub("-.*$", " group", Genus),
                                               Genus))

    `%<+%` <- ggtree::`%<+%`
    p <- ggtree::ggtree(tr, aes(colour = branch_class), layout = "fan", open.angle = 22,
                        branch.length = "none", linewidth = 0.18) +
        scale_colour_manual(values = c(HOST_CLASS_COLOURS, "0" = "grey62"), guide = "none")
    depth <- max(p$data$x)
    # taken in order of abundance, a genus is named only if it stands clear of those named
    position <- p$data$y[match(named$label, p$data$label)] / ape::Ntip(tr)
    kept <- integer()
    for (i in seq_along(position)) {
        if (length(kept) < COMBINED_TREE_LABELS &&
            all(abs(position[i] - position[kept]) > COMBINED_TREE_LABEL_GAP)) kept <- c(kept, i)
    }
    p <- p %<+% named[kept, ]
    key <- function(order, ncol = 1) guide_legend(order = order, ncol = ncol,
                                                  override.aes = list(colour = "grey35"))
    ring <- function(column, width, offset) ggtreeExtra::geom_fruit(
        data = dplyr::select(tips, label, ring_value = dplyr::all_of(column)),
        geom = geom_tile, mapping = aes(y = label, fill = ring_value),
        width = width * depth, offset = offset, colour = NA)
    p <- p +
        ring("class_name", 0.045, 0.04) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = HOST_CLASS_COLOURS,
                          name = "Host class",
                          guide = key(1)) +
        ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
        ring("phylum_name", 0.07, 0.06) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = c(TREE_PHYLUM_COLOURS, Other = "grey60"),
                          name = "Phylum (ring 2)", guide = key(2, 2)) +
        ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
        ring("oxygen", 0.07, 0.075) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = OXYGEN_COLOURS, name = "Predicted oxygen use\n(ring 3)",
                          drop = FALSE, guide = key(3)) +
        ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
        ggtreeExtra::geom_fruit(
            data = family_long, geom = geom_tile,
            mapping = aes(y = label, x = host_family, fill = found), pwidth = 0.3,
            offset = 0.07,
            axis.params = list(axis = "x", text.size = 2.3, text.angle = -78, hjust = 0,
                               line.size = 0)) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = c("Detected" = "grey18", "Not detected" = "grey93"),
                          name = "Host plant family\n(rings 4 to 9)", guide = key(4)) +
        ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
        ggtreeExtra::geom_fruit(
            data = dplyr::select(tips, label, bar_hosts = n_hosts, bar_class = class_name),
            geom = geom_col, mapping = aes(y = label, x = bar_hosts, fill = bar_class),
            orientation = "y", pwidth = 0.2, offset = 0.11,
            axis.params = list(axis = "x", text.size = 2.3, nbreak = 3, vjust = 1),
            grid.params = list(linewidth = 0.15, colour = "grey85")) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = HOST_CLASS_COLOURS, guide = "none") +
        ggtree::geom_tiplab(aes(label = shown), size = 2.5, fontface = "italic",
                            colour = "black", offset = 0.94 * depth) +
        ggtree::hexpand(0.2) +
        theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "horizontal", legend.box.just = "top",
              legend.title.position = "top", legend.key.size = unit(10, "pt"),
              legend.text = element_text(size = 8, colour = "black"),
              legend.title = element_text(size = 8.5, face = "bold", colour = "black"),
              legend.spacing.x = unit(12, "pt"), legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
              legend.box.spacing = unit(8, "pt"), plot.margin = margin(-10, 2, 6, 2))
    readr::write_csv(
        tips |> dplyr::select(ASV, Phylum, Genus, host_class = class_name, n_hosts,
                              predicted_oxygen_use = oxygen) |>
            dplyr::bind_cols(tibble::as_tibble(detected)),
        res("tables", "tree_generalist_specialist.csv"))

    # Beneath the legends, a table of Part 1's stored tests: within each of the phyla
    # richest in ASVs, does an ASV found on more host species reach a higher relative
    # abundance where it occurs? The tests use every ASV of the phylum, the intermediate
    # ones included, so their ASV numbers are larger than the number of tips drawn.
    small_q <- function(q) ifelse(q < 0.001, "< 0.001",
                                  vapply(q, function(v) format(signif(v, 2), scientific = FALSE),
                                         character(1)))
    breadth_stats <- read_csv(BREADTH_ABUNDANCE, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::transmute(row = rev(seq_along(Phylum)), Phylum,
                         ASVs = formatC(n_asvs, format = "d", big.mark = ","),
                         "R\u00b2" = sprintf("%.3f", r2), "Regression q" = small_q(lm_q),
                         "Spearman \u03c1" = sprintf("%.2f", spearman_rho),
                         "Spearman q" = small_q(spearman_q))
    columns <- setNames(c(0.035, 0.34, 0.47, 0.63, 0.79, 0.95), names(breadth_stats)[-1])
    cells <- tidyr::pivot_longer(breadth_stats, -row, names_to = "column", values_to = "text") |>
        dplyr::mutate(x = unname(columns[column]), hjust = ifelse(column == "Phylum", 0, 1))
    rules <- c(nrow(breadth_stats) + c(1.5, 0.5), 0.5)      # above and below the header, and the foot
    stats_table <- ggplot(cells, aes(x, row)) +
        geom_point(data = breadth_stats, aes(x = 0.012, fill = Phylum), shape = 22, size = 3.2,
                   colour = "grey35", stroke = 0.3) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = TREE_PHYLUM_COLOURS, guide = "none") +
        geom_text(aes(label = text, hjust = hjust), size = 8 / .pt, colour = "black") +
        annotate("text", x = unname(columns), y = nrow(breadth_stats) + 1, label = names(columns),
                 hjust = c(0, rep(1, length(columns) - 1)), size = 8 / .pt, fontface = "bold") +
        annotate("segment", x = 0, xend = 0.97, y = rules, yend = rules, linewidth = 0.3) +
        scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.3), expand = c(0, 0)) +
        scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.3, nrow(breadth_stats) + 1.7), expand = c(0, 0)) +
        labs(title = "Host breadth against relative abundance, by phylum (all ASVs of the phylum)") +
        theme_void() +
        theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 8.5, face = "bold", colour = "black",
                                        margin = margin(0, 0, 4, 0)),
              plot.margin = margin(8, 2, 4, 26))
    p <- p / stats_table + patchwork::plot_layout(heights = c(1, 0.13))
    print(p)
    # full page at double-column width (183 mm), 600 dpi, drawn with ragg for sharp type
    ggsave(fig("tree_generalist_specialist"), p, width = 7.2, height = 9.4, dpi = 600,
           device = if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) ragg::agg_tiff else "tiff",
           compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
})

# Host plant phylogeny with each host's alpha diversity beside it: the figure for the test
# of host phylogenetic signal. Nothing is computed here. The tree, the species means and
# the test results are all host_phylosignal.R's outputs, so the figure shows exactly what
# was tested. If closely related hosts had similar diversity, neighbouring tips would
# carry similar values; Blomberg's K and Pagel's lambda in each panel say whether they do.
HOST_SIGNAL_TREE  <- res("tables", "host_phylosignal_tree.nwk")
HOST_SIGNAL_TABLE <- res("tables", "host_phylosignal.csv")
HOST_SIGNAL_MEANS <- res("tables", "host_phylosignal_species_means.csv")
HOST_SIGNAL_INDICES <- c(Observed = "Observed richness (ASVs)", Shannon = "Shannon index",
                         Evenness = "Pielou's evenness")
# The branches and the row bands take the plant-family colours of every figure
# (host_colours(), chunk `fx-palettes`), which leave out the two stage colours.
# METHODS 4 | figure: host_phylosignal
fig_section("host_phylosignal",
            needs = c(HOST_SIGNAL_TREE, HOST_SIGNAL_TABLE, HOST_SIGNAL_MEANS,
                      HOST_SIGNAL_HOSTS), {
    tr <- ape::read.tree(HOST_SIGNAL_TREE)
    stats <- read_csv(HOST_SIGNAL_TABLE, show_col_types = FALSE)
    # one rarefaction depth per figure: the deepest the pipeline wrote
    depth_shown <- max(stats$depth)
    stats <- dplyr::filter(stats, depth == depth_shown)
    means <- read_csv(HOST_SIGNAL_MEANS, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::filter(depth == depth_shown) |>
        dplyr::mutate(stage = factor(stage, levels = STAGES))
    families <- read_csv(HOST_SIGNAL_HOSTS, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::transmute(species = gsub(" ", "_", Species), Family) |>
        dplyr::filter(species %in% tr$tip.label)
    if (!all(tr$tip.label %in% families$species)) stop("a host on the tree has no plant family")

    n_tips <- ape::Ntip(tr)
    root_age <- max(ape::node.depth.edgelength(tr))
```
