```{r fx-fig-tree-genus}
    # Each host's row, and the block of rows each plant family takes, top to bottom.
    tip_y <- ggtree::ggtree(tr)$data |> dplyr::filter(isTip) |>
        dplyr::select(species = label, y)
    bands <- tip_y |> dplyr::inner_join(families, dplyr::join_by(species)) |>
        dplyr::summarise(ymin = min(y) - 0.5, ymax = max(y) + 0.5, .by = Family) |>
        dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(ymin))
    family_colours <- host_colours()$family[bands$Family]   # the host colours of every figure
    # A pale band in the family's colour runs across the tree and all three panels, with a
    # white line between hosts, so a row can be followed from its tip to its points.
    family_rows <- function() list(
        annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = bands$ymin, ymax = bands$ymax,
                 fill = family_colours[bands$Family], alpha = 0.14),
        geom_hline(yintercept = seq_len(n_tips - 1) + 0.5, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5))
    rows <- scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.5, n_tips + 0.5), expand = c(0, 0))
    ages <- pretty(c(0, root_age), n = 4)
    ages <- ages[ages <= root_age]

    # Branches within a family take its colour; the deeper branches joining families are grey.
    tr <- ggtree::groupOTU(tr, split(families$species, families$Family), group_name = "Family")
    p_tree <- ggtree::ggtree(tr, aes(colour = Family), linewidth = 0.55) +
        ggtree::geom_tiplab(aes(label = gsub("_", " ", label)), fontface = "italic",
                            size = 2.6, offset = 0.02 * root_age, colour = "black") +
        scale_colour_manual(values = c(family_colours, "0" = "grey40"),
                            breaks = names(family_colours), name = "Plant family",
                            guide = guide_legend(order = 1, nrow = 2,
                                                 override.aes = list(linewidth = 1.6))) +
        ggtree::theme_tree2() +
        # the axis counts back from the present; the tip names take the space right of it
        scale_x_continuous(breaks = root_age - ages, labels = ages,
                           limits = c(0, 1.8 * root_age), name = "Million years ago") +
        rows +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7), axis.title.x = element_text(size = 7.5,
                                                                                hjust = 0.2),
              plot.margin = margin(4, 0, 4, 4))
    # the bands go underneath the tree, which ggtree() has already drawn
    p_tree$layers <- c(family_rows(), p_tree$layers)

    panel <- function(ix) {
        d <- means |> dplyr::filter(index == ix) |>
            dplyr::inner_join(tip_y, dplyr::join_by(species)) |>
            # the two stages of a host sit just above and below the middle of its row
            dplyr::mutate(y = y + ifelse(stage == STAGES[1], 0.17, -0.17))
        tests <- stats |> dplyr::filter(index == ix) |>
            dplyr::arrange(match(stage, STAGES)) |>
            dplyr::mutate(k_text = sprintf("%s: K = %.2f, P = %.2f", stage, K, K_p),
                          lambda_text = sprintf("%s %.2f", tolower(stage), lambda))
        # one line per stage for K, one line for both lambdas: a panel is too narrow for more
        tests_text <- paste(c(tests$k_text,
                              paste0("λ: ", paste(tests$lambda_text, collapse = ", "))),
                            collapse = "\n")
        ggplot(d, aes(x = mean, y = y)) +
            family_rows() +
            # a white rim keeps two overlapping points apart
            geom_point(aes(fill = stage, size = n), shape = 21, colour = "white",
                       stroke = 0.4) +
            scale_fill_manual(values = STAGE_PELLET, name = "Stage", drop = FALSE,
                              guide = guide_legend(order = 2,
                                                   override.aes = list(size = 3))) +
            scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.2, 3.8), trans = "log10",
                                  breaks = c(3, 30, 300), name = "Samples",
                                  guide = guide_legend(order = 3,
                                                       override.aes = list(fill = "grey30"))) +
            scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.09)) +
            rows +
            labs(x = HOST_SIGNAL_INDICES[[ix]], y = NULL,
                 subtitle = tests_text) +
            theme_pipeline_classic(base_size = 8) +
            theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
                  # value guides only; the bands and white lines already mark the rows
                  panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
                  panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "grey75", linewidth = 0.2),
                  panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.3),
                  plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 6.5, hjust = 0, lineheight = 1.1,
                                               margin = margin(b = 5)),
                  plot.margin = margin(4, 4, 4, 2))
    }
    p <- p_tree + panel("Observed") + panel("Shannon") + panel("Evenness") +
        patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(1.85, 1, 1, 1), guides = "collect") &
        theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 7.5),
              legend.title = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
              legend.key.size = unit(9, "pt"), legend.margin = margin(0, 3, 0, 3),
              legend.key.spacing.x = unit(3, "pt"))
    print(p)
    # double-column width (183 mm)
    ggsave(fig("host_phylosignal"), p, width = 7.2, height = 4.9, dpi = 300,
           compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
})
```

```{r fx-fig-pcoa-by-stage}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 2 | Diversity, composition and co-occurrence
#   figures: pcoa_css_by_stage, pcoa_css_by_stage_study, pcoa_css_asv_by_stage
# ==========================================================================================
# Structure within each stage: the seed samples and the seedling samples, each in its own
# ordination (Part 1, chunk `pcoa-by-stage`, at genus and at ASV level). Nothing is
# computed here. Every panel carries its letter, no heading, and the PERMANOVA of its
# variable within its stage (R2 and p; F is in the table of tests). The
# stage, its number of samples and the variance of the axes are in the axis titles.
#   pcoa_css_by_stage        genus level, by host genus, cultivar and plant family: panels
#                            B to G of main Figure 2, under the dendrogram
#   pcoa_css_by_stage_study  genus level, by study: panels C and D of Figure S2
#   pcoa_css_asv_by_stage    ASV level, by study, host genus, cultivar and plant family:
#                            panels E to L of Figure S2
# Host genus and plant family take the host colours of every figure (host_colours());
# cultivars and studies take the palette by number of samples, the same at both levels.
# A sample with no cultivar on record is left out of the cultivar panels (as it is of the
# cultivar test), so those panels hold fewer samples than the others.
# The two stage colours are not used. Part 1 also tests host species within each stage
# (the table of tests); it is not drawn.
PCOA_NOT_REPORTED <- "Not reported"
PCOA_STUDY_TABLE <- res("tables", "fig1_study_table.csv")
# host attributes are plant family and host genus only, at the user's request (2026-10-22)
PCOA_STAGE_TERMS <- c(study = "Study", host_genus = "Host genus", Plant_Family = "Plant family")
pcoa_stage_file <- function(kind, unit) res("diversity", sprintf("%s_css_%s_by_stage.csv", kind, unit))
PCOA_STAGE_FILE <- pcoa_stage_file("pcoa", "genus")
# the coordinates of one unit, with the labels the panels are coloured by
pcoa_stage_coords <- function(unit) {
    study_names <- if (file.exists(PCOA_STUDY_TABLE)) {
        studies <- read_csv(PCOA_STUDY_TABLE, show_col_types = FALSE)
        setNames(sprintf("%s (%s)", studies$Reference, studies$`Project ID`), studies$`Project ID`)
    } else character()
    read_csv(pcoa_stage_file("pcoa", unit), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::mutate(Plant_Family = dplyr::coalesce(Plant_Family, PCOA_NOT_REPORTED),
                      host_genus = sub(" .*$", "", Scientific_Name),
                      # "sativus" is a cultivar of carrot and of radish: the host goes with the name
                      cultivar = ifelse(is.na(Cultivar) | Cultivar %in% c("", "undefined"), PCOA_NOT_REPORTED,
                                        sprintf("%s (%s)", Cultivar, sub("^(\\w)\\w+ ", "\\1. ", Scientific_Name))),
                      # studies are named as in the overview: reference and accession
                      study = dplyr::coalesce(unname(study_names[study_alias]), study_alias))
}
# the PERMANOVA of Part 1 goes on the panel it belongs to; without the table, no text
pcoa_stage_tests <- function(unit) {
    file <- pcoa_stage_file("permanova", unit)
    if (!file.exists(file)) return(NULL)
    read_csv(file, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::mutate(label = sprintf("R² = %.1f%%, p = %s", 100 * R2, format(p, nsmall = 3)))
}
# One palette per variable for both units. Cultivars and studies take the colours by
# number of samples at genus level, so that those that fill the panels are the furthest
# apart in colour; their keys are alphabetical (cultivar) or by size (study).
pcoa_stage_palettes <- function() {
    units <- c("genus", "asv")[file.exists(pcoa_stage_file("pcoa", c("genus", "asv")))]
    coords <- purrr::map(units, pcoa_stage_coords)
    ranked <- function(column) {
        by_unit <- purrr::map(coords, function(d) names(sort(table(d[[column]][d[[column]] != PCOA_NOT_REPORTED]),
                                                             decreasing = TRUE)))
        values <- unique(unlist(by_unit))
        if (length(values) > length(HOST_COLOUR_POOL)) stop("more groups than colours in the palette: ", column)
        setNames(HOST_COLOUR_POOL[seq_along(values)], values)
    }
    host_scheme <- host_colours()
    list(study = ranked("study"), host_genus = host_scheme$genus,
         Plant_Family = c(host_scheme$family, setNames("white", PCOA_NOT_REPORTED)))
}
pcoa_stage_panel <- function(coords, tests, palette, variable, stage, letter, first_column, key = "none",
                             point_size = 1.3) {
    d <- dplyr::filter(coords, .data$stage == .env$stage, .data[[variable]] != PCOA_NOT_REPORTED) |>
        dplyr::mutate(group = factor(.data[[variable]], levels = names(palette))) |>
        # the largest groups are drawn first, so the small ones are not buried under them
        dplyr::add_count(group, name = "group_size") |> dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(group_size))
    shown <- if (is.null(tests)) NULL else dplyr::filter(tests, .data$term == PCOA_STAGE_TERMS[[variable]],
                                                         .data$stage == .env$stage)
    axis_title <- function(i, share) sprintf("PCoA %d (%.1f%%)", i, share)
    # A square panel with one unit the same length on both axes, so the ordination is not
    # stretched: both axes span the wider of the stage's two ranges, about their centres.
    # The span comes from every sample of the stage, so the panels of a stage share it.
    at_stage <- dplyr::filter(coords, .data$stage == .env$stage)
    span <- 1.06 * max(diff(range(at_stage$PCoA1)), diff(range(at_stage$PCoA2)))
    square <- function(x) mean(range(x)) + c(-0.5, 0.5) * span
    ggplot(d, aes(PCoA1, PCoA2, fill = group)) +
        geom_point(shape = 21, size = point_size, stroke = 0.15, colour = "grey15", alpha = 0.95, show.legend = TRUE) +
        (if (is.null(shown) || !nrow(shown)) NULL else annotate(
            "label", x = -Inf, y = -Inf, label = shown$label[1], hjust = 0, vjust = 0, size = 5.5 / ggplot2::.pt,
            label.size = 0, label.padding = unit(2, "pt"), fill = scales::alpha("white", 0.8))) +
        # the key lists the groups of this unit, at both stages
        scale_fill_manual(values = palette, breaks = intersect(names(palette), coords[[variable]]),
                          name = PCOA_STAGE_TERMS[[variable]], drop = FALSE, guide = key) +
        coord_equal(xlim = square(at_stage$PCoA1), ylim = square(at_stage$PCoA2), expand = FALSE) +
        # ticks every 0.25 on both axes, as the units are the same
        scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_width(0.25)) +
        scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_width(0.25)) +
        labs(x = axis_title(1, d$variance_1[1]),
             y = if (first_column) sprintf("%s (n = %s)\n%s", stage, format(d$n_samples[1], big.mark = ","),
                                           axis_title(2, d$variance_2[1])) else axis_title(2, d$variance_2[1]),
             title = panel_letter(letter)) +
        theme_pipeline_classic(base_size = 7) +
        theme(plot.title = element_text(size = PANEL_LETTER_SIZE, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
              plot.title.position = "plot",
              axis.text = element_text(size = 6, colour = "black"),
              axis.title = element_text(size = 6.5, colour = "black", lineheight = 0.95),
              plot.margin = margin(3, 6, 3, 3))
}
# The panels of one unit: a row for each stage and a column for each variable, lettered
# row by row from `first_letter` (the figures are joined under other panels). `keys`
# names the variables that get a key; the others have theirs elsewhere in the figure.
pcoa_stage_grid <- function(unit, variables, first_letter, keys = list(), point_size = 1.3) {
    coords <- pcoa_stage_coords(unit)
    tests <- pcoa_stage_tests(unit)
    palettes <- pcoa_stage_palettes()
    purrr::imap(intersect(STAGES, coords$stage), function(stage, row) {
        purrr::imap(variables, function(variable, i) pcoa_stage_panel(
            coords, tests, palettes[[variable]], variable, stage,
            letters[first_letter - 1 + (row - 1) * length(variables) + i], i == 1,
            key = if (is.null(keys[[variable]])) "none" else keys[[variable]], point_size = point_size))
    }) |> purrr::list_flatten()
}
pcoa_key <- function(..., italic = FALSE) guide_legend(
    ..., override.aes = list(size = 2, alpha = 1),
    theme = if (italic) theme(legend.text = element_text(face = "italic")) else theme())
PCOA_KEY_THEME <- theme(legend.title = element_text(size = 6.5, face = "bold"),
                        legend.text = element_text(size = 6, colour = "black"), legend.key.size = unit(7, "pt"),
                        legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0), legend.box.spacing = unit(3, "pt"))
save_pcoa <- function(name, p, height) {
    print(p)
    # double-column width (183 mm), 600 dpi, drawn with ragg for sharp type
    ggsave(fig(name), p, width = 7.2, height = height, dpi = 600,
           device = if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) ragg::agg_tiff else "tiff",
           compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
}
# Main Figure 2, panels B to G (panel A is the dendrogram, whose key serves host genus
# and plant family; cultivar is not in the dendrogram and has its key under the panels).
fig_section("pcoa_css_by_stage", needs = PCOA_STAGE_FILE, {
    variables <- c("host_genus", "Plant_Family")
    # no key: host genus and plant family take the colours of the dendrogram's key above.
    # One row of four square panels (seeds, then seedlings), so Figure 2 stays on a page.
    panels <- pcoa_stage_grid("genus", variables, first_letter = 2, point_size = 0.9)
    p <- patchwork::wrap_plots(panels, nrow = 1)
    save_pcoa("pcoa_css_by_stage", p, 2.15)
})
# Figure S2, panels C and D: the same two ordinations by study, side by side. They show
# how far the studies keep apart within a stage, which the host panels of main Figure 2
# cannot be read without.
fig_section("pcoa_css_by_stage_study", needs = PCOA_STAGE_FILE, {
    panels <- pcoa_stage_grid("genus", "study", first_letter = 3, keys = list(study = pcoa_key(ncol = 1)))
    p <- patchwork::wrap_plots(panels, nrow = 1) + patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
        PCOA_KEY_THEME & theme(legend.position = "right", legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 2))
    save_pcoa("pcoa_css_by_stage_study", p, 2.45)
})
# Figure S2, panels E to L: the ordinations at ASV level, by study and by the three host
# variables of main Figure 2. The study key is the one of panels C and D, above them in
# the joined figure; the host keys are under the panels.
fig_section("pcoa_css_asv_by_stage", needs = pcoa_stage_file("pcoa", "asv"), {
    variables <- c("study", "host_genus", "Plant_Family")
    panels <- pcoa_stage_grid("asv", variables, first_letter = 5, point_size = 1.1,
                              keys = list(host_genus = pcoa_key(nrow = 1, order = 1, italic = TRUE),
                                          Plant_Family = pcoa_key(nrow = 1, order = 2)))
    # the three keys one under the other, each within the width of the page
    p <- patchwork::wrap_plots(panels, ncol = length(variables)) + patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
        PCOA_KEY_THEME & theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical", legend.box.just = "left",
                               legend.text = element_text(size = 5.5, colour = "black"),
                               legend.key.size = unit(6, "pt"), legend.key.spacing.x = unit(4, "pt"),
                               legend.spacing.y = unit(1, "pt"))
    save_pcoa("pcoa_css_asv_by_stage", p, 5.0)
})
```

```{r fx-fig-indicator}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 3 | Taxon-stage associations
#   figure: indicator_species_plot (step 1)
# ==========================================================================================
fig_section("indicator_species_plot", needs = res("tables", "indicator_species_significant.csv"), {
    ind <- read_csv(res("tables", "indicator_species_significant.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::filter(!is.na(genus), genus != "") |>
        slice_max(stat, n = 25, with_ties = FALSE) |>
        # one bar per ASV: with the genus alone on the axis, the ASVs of a genus were
        # stacked into one bar and their indicator values summed to more than 1
        mutate(taxon = sprintf("%s (%s)", genus, sub(" :.*$", "", taxon_id)),
               taxon = fct_reorder(taxon, stat))
    p <- ggplot(ind, aes(x = stat, y = taxon, fill = group)) +
        geom_col(colour = INK, linewidth = 0.2, width = 0.75) +

        labs(x = "Indicator value (IndVal.g)", y = NULL, fill = "Enriched in",
             title = "Indicator taxa by developmental stage") +
        theme_pipeline_classic() +
        theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6.5))
    print(p)
    save_nature_figure(fig("indicator_species_plot"), p, "standard")
})
```
