```{r fx-fig-stage-screen}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 3 | Taxon-stage associations
#   figure: stage_screen (step 1: DESeq2 and IndVal.g)
# ==========================================================================================
# Step one of the stage analysis, the screen: every ASV DESeq2 could test, placed by its
# fold change and adjusted p, and marked by what the two pooled methods said of it. The
# ASVs both methods flag are the ones whose genera go on to the stratified analysis
# (fx-fig-stage-heatmap). Nothing is tested here: the classes are Part 1's
# (tables/stage_screen_asvs.csv). DESeq2's contrast is seeds over seedlings; the axis is
# turned round so that right means seedlings, as in the heatmap.
STAGE_SCREEN <- res("tables", "stage_screen_asvs.csv")
# Fold changes beyond this are drawn at the edge: ASVs absent from one stage give values
# several times larger.
STAGE_SCREEN_FOLD_LIMIT <- 10
fig_section("stage_screen", needs = STAGE_SCREEN, {
    cfg <- config$stage_effects
    all_asvs <- read_csv(STAGE_SCREEN, show_col_types = FALSE)
    d <- all_asvs |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj)) |>
        dplyr::mutate(
            fold = -log2FoldChange,
            # an adjusted p of exactly zero is drawn level with the smallest non-zero one
            significance = -log10(pmax(padj, min(padj[padj > 0]))),
            class = dplyr::case_when(
                screen == "Both" & fold > 0 ~ sprintf("Both methods, higher in %s", tolower(STAGES[2])),
                screen == "Both" ~ sprintf("Both methods, higher in %s", tolower(STAGES[1])),
                TRUE ~ screen))
    levels_shown <- c(sprintf("Both methods, higher in %s", tolower(STAGES)), "DESeq2 only",
                      "Indicator analysis only", "Neither")
    counts <- table(factor(d$class, levels = levels_shown))
    keys <- setNames(sprintf("%s (n = %s)", levels_shown, comma(as.integer(counts))), levels_shown)
    d <- d |> dplyr::mutate(class = factor(class, levels = rev(levels_shown))) |> dplyr::arrange(class)
    limit <- STAGE_SCREEN_FOLD_LIMIT
    p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = pmax(pmin(fold, limit), -limit), y = significance,
                       colour = class, size = class, shape = abs(fold) > limit)) +
        geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1) * cfg$deseq2_min_log2fc, linetype = "dashed",
                   colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.3) +
        geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(cfg$deseq2_fdr), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey55",
                   linewidth = 0.3) +
        geom_point(stroke = 0.4) +
        scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c(unname(STAGE_PELLET[STAGES]), "grey20", "grey62", "grey85"),
                                              levels_shown),
                            breaks = levels_shown, labels = keys, name = "Screen") +
        scale_size_manual(values = setNames(c(1.5, 1.5, 0.9, 0.7, 0.6), levels_shown), guide = "none") +
        scale_shape_manual(values = c("FALSE" = 16, "TRUE" = 1), guide = "none") +
        scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-limit, limit), breaks = seq(-limit, limit, by = 5),
                           labels = function(x) ifelse(abs(x) == limit, sprintf("%s%d", ifelse(x < 0, "≤", "≥"), as.integer(x)), x)) +
        scale_y_continuous(trans = "sqrt", expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.04)),
                           breaks = c(0, 5, 20, 50, 100, 200)) +
        labs(x = sprintf("DESeq2 log2 fold change (%s over %s)", tolower(STAGES[2]), tolower(STAGES[1])),
             y = expression(-log[10] ~ "adjusted p")) +
        guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2))) +
        theme_pipeline_classic(base_size = 7.5) +
        theme(panel.border = element_blank(), panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
              axis.line = element_line(colour = INK, linewidth = 0.3),
              axis.text = element_text(colour = "black", size = 7),
              axis.title = element_text(size = 7.5),
              legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(size = 7.5, face = "bold"),
              legend.text = element_text(size = 7, colour = "black"),
              legend.key.size = unit(10, "pt"), plot.margin = margin(4, 4, 4, 4))
    print(p)
    cat(sprintf("ASVs: %d; with a DESeq2 adjusted p and drawn: %d\n", nrow(all_asvs), nrow(d)))
    # double-column width (183 mm), 600 dpi, drawn with ragg for sharp type
    ggsave(fig("stage_screen"), p, width = 7.2, height = 3.4, dpi = 600,
           device = if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) ragg::agg_tiff else "tiff",
           compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
})
```

```{r fx-fig-stage-heatmap}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 3 | Taxon-stage associations
#   figure: stage_effect_heatmap (step 2: Hedges' g)
# ==========================================================================================
# Heatmap of the stage effect within each plant family (C) and within each cultivar (D),
# for the genera the pooled methods call stage-associated. Nothing is estimated here: the
# per-stratum effects and the pooled estimates are Part 1's (chunk
# `stage-effects-by-stratum`). One row per genus and one column per family or cultivar,
# with the pooled estimate, printed, in a column of its own. The colour is Hedges' g,
# running from the seed colour through white to the seedling colour; a dot marks an effect
# whose 95% interval excludes zero and a cross a cell that could not be estimated. A strip above the
# columns gives the plant family, so the cultivars need no key of their own. This replaced
# a forest plot, at the user's request. The rows are the genera estimated in at least
# STAGE_HEAT_MIN_STRATA strata in both analyses; the rest are in the tables.
# host attributes are plant family and host genus only, at the user's request (2026-10-22)
STAGE_HEAT_PANELS <- c("Within plant family" = "plant_family", "Within host genus" = "host_genus")
STAGE_HEAT_MIN_STRATA <- 3
# Effects beyond this take the end colour: a few small strata give far larger values.
STAGE_HEAT_COLOUR_LIMIT <- 2
# the plant-family colours of every figure
STAGE_HEAT_FAMILY_COLOURS <- HOST_FAMILY_COLOURS
stage_effect_file <- function(kind, tag) res("tables", sprintf("stage_effect_%s_%s_genus.csv", kind, tag))
fig_section("stage_effect_heatmap",
            needs = c(stage_effect_file("by", STAGE_HEAT_PANELS),
                      stage_effect_file("pooled_by", STAGE_HEAT_PANELS)), {
    pooled <- purrr::map(STAGE_HEAT_PANELS, function(tag) {
        read_csv(stage_effect_file("pooled_by", tag), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
            dplyr::filter(n_strata >= STAGE_HEAT_MIN_STRATA)
    })
    # rows run from the genus most raised in seedlings (top) to the most raised in seeds
    genera <- pooled[[1]] |> dplyr::filter(Genus %in% pooled[[2]]$Genus) |>
        dplyr::arrange(pooled_g) |> dplyr::pull(Genus)
    n <- length(genera)
    limit <- STAGE_HEAT_COLOUR_LIMIT
    squash <- function(g) pmax(pmin(g, limit), -limit)
    marked <- "95% confidence interval excludes zero"
    absent <- "Not estimated"
    heat_panel <- function(title, letter, first, italic = FALSE) {
        tag <- STAGE_HEAT_PANELS[[title]]
        by <- read_csv(stage_effect_file("by", tag), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
            dplyr::filter(Genus %in% genera) |>
            # "Flavert (Phaseolus vulgaris)" -> "Flavert (P. vulgaris)"
            dplyr::mutate(column = stratum,
                          # a host genus of two families (none here) would take its first family's colour
                          family = factor(sub(";.*$", "", plant_family), levels = names(STAGE_HEAT_FAMILY_COLOURS)))
        columns <- dplyr::distinct(by, family, column) |> dplyr::arrange(family, column) |>
            dplyr::mutate(x = dplyr::row_number())
        pooled_x <- nrow(columns) + 1.35
        cells <- tidyr::expand_grid(Genus = genera, column = columns$column) |>
            dplyr::left_join(dplyr::transmute(by, Genus, column, g = hedges_g,
                                              clear = ci_low > 0 | ci_high < 0),
                             dplyr::join_by(Genus, column)) |>
            dplyr::left_join(columns, dplyr::join_by(column)) |>
            dplyr::mutate(y = match(Genus, genera))
        po <- pooled[[title]] |> dplyr::filter(Genus %in% genera) |>
            dplyr::transmute(y = match(Genus, genera), x = pooled_x, g = pooled_g,
                             clear = dplyr::coalesce(ci_low > 0 | ci_high < 0, FALSE))
        ggplot() +
            geom_tile(data = cells, aes(x, y, fill = squash(g)), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
            geom_tile(data = po, aes(x, y, fill = squash(g)), colour = "grey25", linewidth = 0.3,
                      width = 0.92, height = 0.92) +
            # a pooled estimate whose interval excludes zero carries the same mark as the
            # other cells, set before its value rather than in a corner of the frame
            geom_text(data = po, aes(x + ifelse(clear, 0.12, 0), y, label = sprintf("%+.1f", g),
                                     colour = abs(g) > 0.55 * limit),
                      size = 6 / ggplot2::.pt, show.legend = FALSE) +
            scale_colour_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "white", "FALSE" = "black"), guide = "none") +
            geom_point(data = dplyr::filter(cells, is.na(g)), aes(x, y, shape = absent), size = 1,
                       colour = "grey60", stroke = 0.35) +
            geom_point(data = dplyr::filter(cells, clear), aes(x, y, shape = marked), size = 1.2,
                       fill = "white", colour = "black", stroke = 0.35) +
            geom_point(data = dplyr::filter(po, clear), aes(x - 0.29, y, shape = marked),
                       size = 1, fill = "white", colour = "black", stroke = 0.35) +
            scale_shape_manual(values = setNames(c(21, 4), c(marked, absent)), name = NULL,
                               limits = c(marked, absent),
                               guide = guide_legend(order = 3, ncol = 1,
                                                    override.aes = list(size = 1.8))) +
            scale_fill_gradient2(low = STAGE_PELLET[[STAGES[1]]], mid = "white",
                                 high = STAGE_PELLET[[STAGES[2]]], midpoint = 0,
                                 limits = c(-limit, limit), na.value = "grey96",
                                 name = sprintf("Hedges' g (%s − %s)", tolower(STAGES[2]),
                                                tolower(STAGES[1])),
                                 guide = guide_colourbar(order = 1, direction = "horizontal",
                                                         title.position = "top",
                                                         barwidth = unit(95, "pt"),
                                                         barheight = unit(7, "pt"))) +
            ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
            geom_tile(data = columns, aes(x, n + 0.78, fill = family), height = 0.24,
                      colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
            scale_fill_manual(values = STAGE_HEAT_FAMILY_COLOURS,
                              limits = names(STAGE_HEAT_FAMILY_COLOURS), drop = FALSE,
                              name = "Plant family",
                              # one key serves both panels
                              guide = if (first) guide_legend(order = 2, nrow = 2,
                                                              title.position = "top") else "none") +
            # host genera in italics, "Pooled" upright
            scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(columns$x, pooled_x),
                               labels = if (italic) parse(text = c(sprintf("italic('%s')", columns$column), "'Pooled'"))
                                        else c(columns$column, "Pooled"),
                               limits = c(0.5, pooled_x + 0.5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
            scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq_len(n),
                               labels = ifelse(nchar(genera) > 25, sub("-.*$", " group", genera), genera),
                               limits = c(0.5, n + 0.92), expand = c(0, 0)) +
            labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = sprintf("%s   %s", letter, title)) +
            theme_pipeline_classic(base_size = 7.5) +
            theme(panel.border = element_blank(), panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
                  axis.line = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
                  axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 6.5,
                                             colour = "black"),
                  axis.text.y = if (first) element_text(face = "italic", size = 7.5, colour = "black")
                                else element_blank(),
                  # bold, as the alpha-diversity heatmap above it in main Figure 3
                  plot.title = element_text(size = PANEL_LETTER_SIZE, face = "bold", hjust = 0, colour = "black"),
                  legend.title = element_text(size = 7.5, face = "bold"),
                  legend.text = element_text(size = 7, colour = "black"),
                  legend.key.size = unit(9, "pt"), legend.margin = margin(0, 6, 0, 6),
                  plot.margin = margin(3, 3, 3, 3))
    }
    widths <- purrr::map_dbl(STAGE_HEAT_PANELS, function(tag) {
        dplyr::n_distinct(read_csv(stage_effect_file("by", tag), show_col_types = FALSE)$stratum) + 1.85
    })
    # lettered B and C: in main Figure 4 this figure sits under the phylosymbiosis
    # scatter, panel A (the main-figures chunk at the end of Part 2)
    p <- heat_panel(names(STAGE_HEAT_PANELS)[1], panel_letter("b"), TRUE) +
        heat_panel(names(STAGE_HEAT_PANELS)[2], panel_letter("c"), FALSE, italic = TRUE) +
        patchwork::plot_layout(widths = unname(widths), guides = "collect") &
        theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box.spacing = unit(2, "pt"))
    print(p)
    # double-column width (183 mm), 600 dpi, drawn with ragg for sharp type
    ggsave(fig("stage_effect_heatmap"), p, width = 7.2, height = 2.1 + 0.27 * n, dpi = 600,
           device = if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) ragg::agg_tiff else "tiff",
           compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
})
```

```{r fx-fig-cooccurrence}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 2 | Diversity, composition and co-occurrence
#   figure: cooccurrence_network
# ==========================================================================================
# The networks of the two stages (Part 1, chunk `cooccurrence-network`), seeds in panel A
# above seedlings in panel B, each drawn as its modules: every connected module is laid
# out on its own, on a pale disc whose area is proportional to its number of ASVs. The
# figure carries no descriptive text beyond the panel letters and stages and one key: module
# genera, ASV counts and the size of each network are given in the legend. The modules sit
# on one grid of four columns that
# both panels share, largest first, so that discs line up from panel to panel and a disc
# of a given size means the same number of ASVs in both. Nodes are ASVs, coloured by genus
# (one colour per genus in both panels; past the palette, the rarest genera are grey as
# "Other genera") and sized by degree on one scale; edges are shaded by |rho|. One key, under
# the panels. Nothing is computed here but the layout.
fig_section("cooccurrence_network", needs = res("tables", "cooccurrence_edges.csv"), {
    stopifnot(requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE), requireNamespace("ggforce", quietly = TRUE))
    all_edges <- read_csv(res("tables", "cooccurrence_edges.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::filter(p_adj < 0.05, abs(rho) >= 0.6, taxon1_id != taxon2_id)
    if (!"stage" %in% names(all_edges)) stop("the edge table has no stage column: rerun chunk cooccurrence-network")
    stages <- intersect(STAGES, all_edges$stage)
    genus_of <- dplyr::bind_rows(dplyr::select(all_edges, stage, id = taxon1_id, genus = taxon1),
                                 dplyr::select(all_edges, stage, id = taxon2_id, genus = taxon2)) |>
        dplyr::distinct(stage, id, .keep_all = TRUE)
    pool <- unique(c(setdiff(NATURE_THICK, STAGE_PELLET), FIGURE_PALETTE$pastel))
    ranked <- names(sort(table(genus_of$genus), decreasing = TRUE))
    named <- if (length(ranked) > length(pool)) ranked[seq_len(length(pool) - 1)] else ranked
    genus_colours <- c(setNames(pool[seq_along(named)], named),
                       if (length(ranked) > length(named)) c(`Other genera` = "grey70"))
    graphs <- purrr::map(setNames(stages, stages), function(s) igraph::graph_from_data_frame(
        dplyr::filter(all_edges, stage == s) |> dplyr::select(from = taxon1_id, to = taxon2_id, rho), directed = FALSE))
    # one geometry for both panels: grid, disc scale, node scale and plotting window
    # compact: discs a small gap apart, on the same grid in both panels
    columns <- 4; col_step <- 2.1; row_step <- 2.1; disc_max <- 0.95
    largest <- max(purrr::map_dbl(graphs, function(g) max(table(igraph::components(g)$membership))))
    max_degree <- max(purrr::map_dbl(graphs, function(g) max(igraph::degree(g))))
    n_rows <- max(purrr::map_dbl(graphs, function(g) ceiling(igraph::components(g)$no / columns)))
    window_x <- c(-disc_max - 0.15, col_step * (columns - 1) + disc_max + 0.15)
    window_y <- c(-row_step * (n_rows - 1) - disc_max - 0.15, disc_max + 0.15)
    any_negative <- any(all_edges$rho < 0)
    stage_panel <- function(stage, letter, with_key) {
        g <- graphs[[stage]]
        membership <- igraph::components(g)$membership
        by_size <- as.integer(names(sort(table(membership), decreasing = TRUE)))
        set.seed(42)
        nodes <- purrr::imap(by_size, function(module, i) {
            part <- igraph::induced_subgraph(g, names(membership)[membership == module])
            radius <- disc_max * sqrt(igraph::vcount(part) / largest)
            xy <- igraph::layout_with_fr(part, niter = 2000)
            # centred on the middle of its extent and scaled to fill the disc
            xy <- sweep(xy, 2, (apply(xy, 2, max) + apply(xy, 2, min)) / 2)
            xy <- xy / max(sqrt(rowSums(xy^2)), 1e-9) * radius * 0.78
            tibble(id = igraph::V(part)$name, module = i, radius = radius,
                   x0 = col_step * ((i - 1) %% columns), y0 = -row_step * ((i - 1) %/% columns),
                   x = x0 + xy[, 1], y = y0 + xy[, 2], degree = igraph::degree(part))
        }) |> purrr::list_rbind() |>
            dplyr::left_join(dplyr::filter(genus_of, .data$stage == .env$stage) |> dplyr::select(id, genus),
                             dplyr::join_by(id)) |>
            dplyr::mutate(shown = ifelse(genus %in% named, genus, "Other genera"))
        el <- igraph::as_edgelist(g)
        seg <- tibble(
            x = nodes$x[match(el[, 1], nodes$id)], y = nodes$y[match(el[, 1], nodes$id)],
            xend = nodes$x[match(el[, 2], nodes$id)], yend = nodes$y[match(el[, 2], nodes$id)],
            rho = igraph::E(g)$rho,
            sign = factor(ifelse(igraph::E(g)$rho > 0, "Positive", "Negative"), c("Positive", "Negative")))
        discs <- nodes |>
            dplyr::summarise(name = paste(names(sort(table(genus), decreasing = TRUE)), collapse = ", "),
                             asvs = dplyr::n(), .by = c(module, x0, y0, radius)) |>
            dplyr::mutate(name = stringr::str_wrap(name, 24))
        n_samples <- dplyr::first(all_edges$n_samples[all_edges$stage == stage])
        ggplot() +
            ggforce::geom_circle(data = discs, aes(x0 = x0, y0 = y0, r = radius + 0.12), fill = "grey96",
                                 colour = "grey82", linewidth = 0.25) +
            geom_curve(data = seg, aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend, alpha = abs(rho), linetype = sign),
                       colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.22, curvature = 0.1, ncp = 8) +
            geom_point(data = nodes, aes(x = x, y = y, size = degree, fill = factor(shown, names(genus_colours))),
                       shape = 21, colour = "white", stroke = 0.3) +
            # draws nothing, but holds every genus, so that each keeps its colour in the key
            geom_point(data = tibble(g = factor(names(genus_colours), names(genus_colours))),
                       aes(x = NA_real_, y = NA_real_, fill = g), shape = 21, colour = "white", stroke = 0.3,
                       na.rm = TRUE) +
            scale_fill_manual(values = genus_colours, name = "Genus", drop = FALSE,
                              guide = guide_legend(order = 1, nrow = 3, override.aes = list(size = 2.4),
                                                   theme = theme(legend.text = element_text(face = "italic")))) +
            scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.2, 3.6), limits = c(1, max_degree), name = "Degree",
                                  breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(3),
                                  guide = guide_legend(order = 2, override.aes = list(fill = "grey45"))) +
            scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.25, 0.8), limits = c(0.6, 1), name = "Spearman |ρ|",
                                   breaks = c(0.7, 0.8, 0.9),
                                   guide = guide_legend(order = 3, override.aes = list(linewidth = 0.7))) +
            scale_linetype_manual(values = c(Positive = "solid", Negative = "22"), name = "Correlation", drop = FALSE,
                                  guide = if (any_negative) guide_legend(order = 4) else "none") +
            labs(title = panel_title(letter, stage)) +
            coord_fixed(xlim = window_x, ylim = window_y, expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
            theme_void(base_size = 7) +
            theme(plot.title = element_text(size = PANEL_LETTER_SIZE, face = "bold", hjust = 0, margin = margin(0, 0, 2, 0)),
                  plot.title.position = "plot", plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2),
                  # one key for the figure: the scales are shared, so the last panel carries it
                  legend.position = if (with_key) "bottom" else "none")
    }
    panels <- purrr::imap(stages, function(stage, i) stage_panel(stage, letters[i], with_key = i == length(stages)))
    # the key is the last panel's own (the first has none), set under it
    p <- patchwork::wrap_plots(panels, ncol = 1) &
        theme(legend.box = "horizontal", legend.box.just = "top",
              legend.title = element_text(size = 6.5, face = "bold"), legend.title.position = "top",
              legend.text = element_text(size = 6, colour = "black"),
              legend.key.size = unit(7, "pt"), legend.spacing.x = unit(10, "pt"),
              legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0), legend.box.spacing = unit(4, "pt"))
    print(p)
    # double-column width (183 mm), 600 dpi, drawn with ragg for sharp type
    # as tall as lets each panel span the page width: the window's shape sets the height
    panel_width <- 6.9
    height <- min(9.4, 2 * panel_width * diff(window_y) / diff(window_x) + 0.35 + 0.75)
    ggsave(fig("cooccurrence_network"), p, width = 7.2, height = height, dpi = 600,
           device = if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) ragg::agg_tiff else "tiff",
           compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
})
```

```{r fx-fig-special-groups}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 8 | Predicted traits, gene content and special groups
#   figure: special_group_heatmaps
# ==========================================================================================
# Where the special groups of bacteria occur: one clustered heatmap per group. The groups
# and the matrices are special_groups.R's (tables/special_group_heatmap_matrix.csv); only
# the clustering for display is done here. Rows are the group's taxa, named at the finest
# level they resolve to and found on at least three host genera; columns are host plant
# genera; the colour is the row z-score of log10 mean relative abundance. Rows and columns
# are clustered with Ward's method. A star marks a taxon whose abundance differs among
# host plant orders (Kruskal-Wallis, BH-FDR). All group memberships are predicted traits.
SPECIAL_MATRIX <- res("tables", "special_group_heatmap_matrix.csv")
SPECIAL_ORDER_TESTS <- res("tables", "special_group_host_order_tests.csv")
SPECIAL_GROUP_TITLES <- c(anaerobic = "Predicted anaerobic bacteria",
                          nitrogen_fixing = "Predicted nitrogen-fixing bacteria",
                          small_genome = "Predicted small-genome bacteria")
fig_section("special_group_heatmaps", needs = c(SPECIAL_MATRIX, SPECIAL_ORDER_TESTS), {
    mat <- read_csv(SPECIAL_MATRIX, show_col_types = FALSE)
    tests <- read_csv(SPECIAL_ORDER_TESTS, show_col_types = FALSE)
    z_limit <- max(abs(mat$z))
    heat_panel <- function(g, letter) {
        d <- dplyr::filter(mat, group == g)
        z <- tidyr::pivot_wider(dplyr::select(d, label, host_genus, z), names_from = host_genus,
                                values_from = z) |>
            tibble::column_to_rownames("label") |> as.matrix()
        rows <- stats::hclust(stats::dist(z), method = "ward.D2")
        cols <- stats::hclust(stats::dist(t(z)), method = "ward.D2")
        starred <- tests$label[tests$group == g & tests$q < 0.05]
        # ranks above genus carry a prefix ("f: ", "o: ") and are not set in italics
        # long compound SILVA names are cut to their first name, as on the trees
        row_names <- function(x) {
            short <- ifelse(nchar(x) > 25, sub("-.*$", " group", x), x)
            ifelse(x %in% starred, paste(short, "*"), short)
        }
        d <- d |> dplyr::mutate(label = factor(label, levels = rows$labels[rows$order]),
                                host_genus = factor(host_genus, levels = cols$labels[cols$order]))
        dendro <- function(h, flip) {
            seg <- ggdendro::dendro_data(h)$segments
            n <- length(h$labels)
            g0 <- if (flip) {
                ggplot(seg) + geom_segment(aes(x = -y, y = x, xend = -yend, yend = xend),
                                           linewidth = 0.3) +
                    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.5, n + 0.5), expand = c(0, 0))
            } else {
                ggplot(seg) + geom_segment(aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
                                           linewidth = 0.3) +
                    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.5, n + 0.5), expand = c(0, 0))
            }
            g0 + theme_void() + theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
        }
        heat <- ggplot(d, aes(host_genus, label, fill = z)) +
            geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
            scale_fill_gradient2(low = PALETTE_DIVERGING[1], mid = PALETTE_DIVERGING[2],
                                 high = PALETTE_DIVERGING[3], midpoint = 0, limits = c(-z_limit, z_limit),
                                 name = "Row z-score of log10\nmean relative abundance") +
            scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
            scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0), position = "right", labels = row_names) +
            labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
            theme_pipeline_classic(base_size = 8) +
            theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "italic", size = 7.5),
                  axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7.5), panel.grid = element_blank(),
                  panel.grid.major = element_blank(), plot.margin = margin(0, 4, 2, 0),
                  # one shared colour bar is drawn under the panels instead
                  legend.position = "none")
        # the panel letter only, at the top left as in every figure: the group and its
        # number of taxa are in the figure legend
        patchwork::wrap_elements(
            patchwork::plot_spacer() + dendro(cols, FALSE) + dendro(rows, TRUE) + heat +
                patchwork::plot_layout(ncol = 2, widths = c(0.12, 1), heights = c(0.22, 1)) +
                patchwork::plot_annotation(
                    title = letter, theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = PANEL_LETTER_SIZE, face = "bold",
                                                                            hjust = 0),
                                                  plot.title.position = "plot")))
    }
    shown <- intersect(names(SPECIAL_GROUP_TITLES), unique(mat$group))
    legend_plot <- ggplot(mat, aes(host_genus, label, fill = z)) + geom_tile() +
        scale_fill_gradient2(low = PALETTE_DIVERGING[1], mid = PALETTE_DIVERGING[2],
                             high = PALETTE_DIVERGING[3], midpoint = 0, limits = c(-z_limit, z_limit),
                             name = "Row z-score of log10 mean relative abundance",
                             guide = guide_colourbar(direction = "horizontal",
                                                     title.position = "top",
                                                     barwidth = unit(150, "pt"),
                                                     barheight = unit(8, "pt"))) +
        theme(legend.title = element_text(size = 8.5, face = "bold"),
              legend.text = element_text(size = 8))
    # the panel letter goes in each panel's title: the legend strip is not a panel. The
    # letters start at b: in the supplementary set this figure is joined under panel a
    p <- patchwork::wrap_plots(c(purrr::map2(shown, panel_letter(letters[seq_along(shown) + 1]), heat_panel),
                                 list(patchwork::wrap_elements(ggpubr::get_legend(legend_plot)))),
                               ncol = 1, heights = c(rep(1, length(shown)), 0.22))
    print(p)
    # double-column width (183 mm); one band per group
    ggsave(fig("special_group_heatmaps"), p, width = 7.2, height = 1.1 + 2.2 * length(shown),
           dpi = 300, compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
})
```

```{r fx-fig-functional}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 8 | Predicted traits, gene content and special groups
#   figure: functional_host_breadth_heatmaps
# ==========================================================================================
# Which predicted functions go with a wide or a narrow host range. Nothing is tested here:
# the traits and their tests are predicted_trait_tests.R's, the orthologue counts are
# ko_breadth_tests.R's, and host breadth is Part 1's screen.
#   A  the binary traits most strongly tied to host breadth, in each direction. Columns
#      are ASVs grouped by the number of host species they occur on; the colour is the
#      log2 odds ratio of carrying the trait in that group against all annotated ASVs
#      (0.5 added to every count, so a group with none or all is still finite). A cell
#      with too few annotated ASVs is left grey. The last column prints the fitted odds
#      ratio per doubling of host number, which is the tested quantity.
#   B, C  the orthologue categories with the most orthologues: the share of each
#      category's orthologues enriched in generalists and in specialists, with the count
#      in the cell. The first row is all orthologues, for reference.
TRAIT_TESTS <- res("tables", "predicted_trait_breadth_tests.csv")
TRAITS_BY_ASV <- res("tables", "predicted_traits_asv.csv")
ASV_HOST_BREADTH <- res("tables", "generalist_specialist_asv_host_screen.csv")
KO_SUMMARY <- res("tables", "ko_enrichment_summary.csv")
functional_setting <- function(section, key, default) {
    value <- config[[section]][[key]]
    if (is.null(value)) default else value
}
TRAIT_SOURCES <- c(bugbase = "B", faprotax = "F", metatraits = "M")
# "metatraits_growth_malonate" -> "Growth malonate (M)"
trait_label <- function(x) {
    name <- gsub("_", " ", sub("_ec[0-9_]+$", "", sub("^[a-z]+_", "", x)))
    paste0(toupper(substr(name, 1, 1)), substring(name, 2), " (",
           TRAIT_SOURCES[sub("_.*$", "", x)], ")")
}
# "CE-BACTERIAL_FITNESS" -> "CE: bacterial fitness"; KEGG names are left as they are
tidy_category <- function(x) {
    x <- gsub("_", " ", sub("^([A-Z_]+)-", "\\1: ", gsub("\\|", " / ", x)))
    upper_case <- x == toupper(x)
    x[upper_case] <- paste0(substr(x[upper_case], 1, 1), tolower(substring(x[upper_case], 2)))
    sub("^Ce: ", "CE: ", x)
}
fig_section("functional_host_breadth_heatmaps",
            needs = c(TRAIT_TESTS, TRAITS_BY_ASV, ASV_HOST_BREADTH, KO_SUMMARY), {
    per_direction <- functional_setting("predicted_traits", "heatmap_traits_per_direction", 12)
    breaks <- functional_setting("predicted_traits", "heatmap_host_breaks", c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9))
    min_cell <- functional_setting("predicted_traits", "heatmap_min_asvs_per_cell", 5)
    trait_fdr <- functional_setting("predicted_traits", "fdr", 0.05)
    n_categories <- functional_setting("gene_content", "heatmap_categories", 15)
    exclude <- functional_setting("gene_content", "heatmap_exclude_pattern", "")
    title_theme <- theme(plot.title = element_text(size = PANEL_LETTER_SIZE, face = "bold",
                                                   margin = margin(0, 0, 5, 0)),
                         plot.title.position = "plot")
    bar <- guide_colourbar(direction = "horizontal", title.position = "top",
                           barwidth = unit(130, "pt"), barheight = unit(7, "pt"))

    # ---- A: traits against host breadth
    directions <- c(wide = "More common\non many hosts", narrow = "More common\non few hosts")
    chosen <- read_csv(TRAIT_TESTS, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::filter(status == "tested", type == "binary", q < trait_fdr) |>
        dplyr::mutate(direction = ifelse(odds_ratio_per_doubling > 1, "wide", "narrow")) |>
        dplyr::slice_min(q, n = per_direction, by = direction, with_ties = FALSE)
    upper <- c(breaks[-1] - 1, Inf)
    bin_labels <- ifelse(is.infinite(upper), paste0("≥", breaks),
                         ifelse(upper == breaks, breaks, paste0(breaks, "–", upper)))
    carried <- read_csv(TRAITS_BY_ASV, show_col_types = FALSE, na = "NA", guess_max = 5000) |>
        dplyr::select(ASV, dplyr::all_of(chosen$trait)) |>
        dplyr::inner_join(read_csv(ASV_HOST_BREADTH, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
                              dplyr::select(ASV, n_hosts), dplyr::join_by(ASV)) |>
        tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(ASV, n_hosts), names_to = "trait", values_to = "has") |>
        dplyr::filter(!is.na(has)) |>
        dplyr::mutate(has = as.logical(has),
                      host_group = cut(n_hosts, breaks = c(breaks, Inf), right = FALSE,
                                       labels = bin_labels))
    trait_cells <- carried |>
        dplyr::summarise(n_annotated = dplyr::n(), n_with_trait = sum(has),
                         .by = c(trait, host_group)) |>
        tidyr::complete(trait, host_group, fill = list(n_annotated = 0L, n_with_trait = 0L)) |>
        dplyr::left_join(dplyr::summarise(carried, all_annotated = dplyr::n(),
                                          all_with_trait = sum(has), .by = trait),
                         dplyr::join_by(trait)) |>
        dplyr::mutate(log2_odds_ratio = log2(
            ((n_with_trait + 0.5) / (n_annotated - n_with_trait + 0.5)) /
                ((all_with_trait + 0.5) / (all_annotated - all_with_trait + 0.5))),
            shown = ifelse(n_annotated >= min_cell, log2_odds_ratio, NA_real_)) |>
        dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(chosen, trait, direction, odds_ratio_per_doubling, q),
                         dplyr::join_by(trait)) |>
        dplyr::arrange(direction, dplyr::desc(odds_ratio_per_doubling), host_group)
    readr::write_csv(trait_cells, res("tables", "functional_trait_heatmap_matrix.csv"))

    rows <- chosen |> dplyr::arrange(odds_ratio_per_doubling) |>
        dplyr::mutate(row = factor(trait_label(trait), levels = trait_label(trait)),
                      facet = factor(directions[direction], levels = directions))
    trait_cells <- trait_cells |>
        dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(rows, trait, row, facet), dplyr::join_by(trait))
    limit <- min(3, max(abs(trait_cells$shown), na.rm = TRUE))
    panel_a <- ggplot(trait_cells, aes(host_group, row)) +
        geom_tile(aes(fill = shown), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
        geom_text(data = rows, aes(x = "OR", label = sprintf("%.2f", odds_ratio_per_doubling)),
                  size = 7 / .pt, colour = "black") +
        scale_fill_gradient2(low = PALETTE_DIVERGING[1], mid = PALETTE_DIVERGING[2],
                             high = PALETTE_DIVERGING[3], midpoint = 0, limits = c(-limit, limit),
                             oob = scales::squish, na.value = "grey88", guide = bar,
                             name = paste0(panel_letter("a"), ": log2 odds ratio of carrying the trait\n(grey, too few annotated ASVs)")) +
        # the OR column holds text only, so it needs its half-cell of room added
        scale_x_discrete(limits = c(bin_labels, "OR"), expand = expansion(add = c(0, 0.5))) +
        scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
        facet_grid(facet ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
        labs(x = "Number of host plant species on which the ASV occurs", y = NULL,
             title = sprintf("%s   Predicted traits against host breadth (the %d most significant in each direction)", panel_letter("a"),
                             per_direction)) +
        theme_pipeline_classic(base_size = 8) +
        theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 7.5, colour = "black"),
              axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8, hjust = 0.4),
              strip.text.y = element_text(size = 7.5, face = "bold", angle = 0, hjust = 0),
              strip.background = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank(),
              panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.spacing = unit(5, "pt")) + title_theme

    # ---- B, C: orthologue categories
    classes <- c("Generalist-enriched" = "Generalist-\nenriched",
                 "Specialist-enriched" = "Specialist-\nenriched")
    ko <- read_csv(KO_SUMMARY, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::mutate(n = `Generalist-enriched` + `Specialist-enriched` + Unassigned)
    ko_rows <- function(scheme_name) {
        d <- dplyr::filter(ko, scheme == scheme_name)
        if (nzchar(exclude)) d <- dplyr::filter(d, !grepl(exclude, category))
        dplyr::bind_rows(dplyr::filter(ko, scheme == "all KOs") |>
                             dplyr::mutate(category = "All orthologues"),
                         dplyr::slice_max(d, n, n = n_categories, with_ties = FALSE)) |>
            # a no-break space keeps the count on the line of the name's last word
            dplyr::mutate(row = stringr::str_wrap(
                sprintf("%s\u00a0(%s)", tidy_category(category), format(n, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)), 50),
                row = factor(row, levels = rev(row))) |>
            tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::all_of(names(classes)), names_to = "class",
                                values_to = "orthologues") |>
            dplyr::mutate(share = 100 * orthologues / n, class = factor(classes[class], classes))
    }
    ko_cells <- list(kegg = ko_rows("KEGG level 2"), pgpg = ko_rows("PGPG level 3"))
    top_share <- max(purrr::map_dbl(ko_cells, function(d) max(d$share)))
    ko_panel <- function(d, title, side,
                         key = paste0(panel_letter("b"), ", ", panel_letter("c"),
                                      ": share of the category's\northologues (%), with the number")) {
        ggplot(d, aes(class, row, fill = share)) +
            geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
            geom_text(aes(label = orthologues, colour = share > 0.6 * top_share), size = 7 / .pt) +
            scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "black"), guide = "none") +
            scale_fill_gradientn(colours = PALETTE_SEQUENTIAL, limits = c(0, top_share),
                                 guide = bar, name = key) +
            scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0), position = "top") +
            scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0), position = side) +
            labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = title) +
            theme_pipeline_classic(base_size = 8) +
            theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 7.5, colour = "black", lineheight = 0.85),
                  axis.text.y = element_text(face = ifelse(grepl("^All orthologues", levels(d$row)),
                                                           "bold", "plain")),
                  panel.grid = element_blank(), panel.grid.major = element_blank()) +
            title_theme
    }
    panel_b <- ko_panel(ko_cells$kegg, panel_title("b", "KEGG categories (level 2)"), "left")
    panel_c <- ko_panel(ko_cells$pgpg, panel_title("c", "Plant-growth-promotion categories (PGPg_finder)"), "right") +
        theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 1))
    # The three bands are laid out independently: aligned panel by panel, the trait
    # heatmap would be squeezed to the width of the two narrow category heatmaps.
    colour_bar <- function(plot) ggpubr::get_legend(
        plot + theme(legend.title = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
                     legend.text = element_text(size = 7.5)))
    no_legend <- theme(legend.position = "none")
    p <- patchwork::wrap_plots(
        panel_a + no_legend,
        patchwork::wrap_elements(full = (panel_b | panel_c) & no_legend),
        patchwork::wrap_elements(full = patchwork::wrap_plots(colour_bar(panel_a),
                                                              colour_bar(panel_b), nrow = 1)),
        ncol = 1, heights = c(nrow(rows) + 3, 1.6 * (n_categories + 2.2), 3.4))
    print(p)
    # double-column width (183 mm), 600 dpi, drawn with ragg for sharp type
    ggsave(fig("functional_host_breadth_heatmaps"), p, width = 7.2, height = 9.2, dpi = 600,
           device = if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) ragg::agg_tiff else "tiff",
           compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
})
# The KEGG panel on its own, for the supplementary set. The trait tests and the
# plant-growth-promotion functions have panels of their own in main Figure 5, and the
# supplementary figures do not repeat data that a main figure shows. It reuses the panel
# built above, so it is skipped or fails with it.
fig_section("ko_kegg_category_heatmap", needs = c(TRAIT_TESTS, TRAITS_BY_ASV, ASV_HOST_BREADTH, KO_SUMMARY), {
    p <- ko_panel(ko_cells$kegg, NULL, "left",
                  key = "Share of the category's orthologues (%), with the number of orthologues") +
        theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
              legend.text = element_text(size = 7.5), plot.margin = margin(4, 110, 4, 40))
    print(p)
    # double-column width (183 mm), 600 dpi, drawn with ragg for sharp type
    ggsave(fig("ko_kegg_category_heatmap"), p, width = 7.2, height = 4.4, dpi = 600,
           device = if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) ragg::agg_tiff else "tiff",
           compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
})
```

```{r fx-fig-functional-stage}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 8 | Predicted traits, gene content and special groups
#   figure: functional_stage_heatmaps
# ==========================================================================================
# The developmental-stage context of the three functional analyses, in one figure drawn
# like the stage heatmap of the genera. Nothing is estimated here: the effects are
# functional_stage_effects.R's. One row per function and one column per plant family, with
# the pooled estimate, printed, in a framed column of its own. The colour is Hedges' g
# (seedlings minus seeds), from the seed colour through white to the seedling colour; a
# dot marks an effect whose 95% interval excludes zero and a cross a cell that could not
# be estimated. The rows are those of the host-breadth figure above, so the two read
# together: the same 24 traits, and the same orthologue categories.
functional_stage_file <- function(prefix, kind) {
    res("tables", sprintf("%s_stage_effect_%s.csv", prefix, kind))
}
# plant families in the order of the host phylogeny figure
FUNCTIONAL_FAMILY_ORDER <- c("Brassicaceae", "Fabaceae", "Apiaceae", "Asteraceae", "Solanaceae",
                             "Poaceae")
FUNCTIONAL_STAGE_LIMIT <- 2          # effects beyond this take the end colour
FUNCTIONAL_STAGE_MARKS <- c(clear = "95% confidence interval excludes zero",
                            absent = "Not estimated")

#' One heatmap. `rows`: feature, label and, optionally, block (a facet), top row first.
#' `families`: the columns to draw, so that panels of one figure can share them.
#' `column_order`: the columns in a given order, for strata that are not plant families.
stage_function_panel <- function(by, pooled, rows, title = NULL, label_side = "left",
                                 families = unique(by$plant_family), column_order = NULL) {
    limit <- FUNCTIONAL_STAGE_LIMIT
    columns <- if (!is.null(column_order)) c(column_order, "Pooled") else
        c(intersect(FUNCTIONAL_FAMILY_ORDER, families),
          setdiff(sort(families), FUNCTIONAL_FAMILY_ORDER), "Pooled")
    if (!"block" %in% names(rows)) rows$block <- ""
    cells <- dplyr::bind_rows(
        tidyr::expand_grid(feature = rows$feature, plant_family = setdiff(columns, "Pooled")) |>
            dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(by, feature, plant_family, g = hedges_g, ci_low, ci_high),
                             dplyr::join_by(feature, plant_family)),
        tibble(feature = rows$feature, plant_family = "Pooled") |>
            dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(pooled, feature, g = pooled_g, ci_low, ci_high),
                             dplyr::join_by(feature))) |>
        dplyr::left_join(rows, dplyr::join_by(feature)) |>
        dplyr::mutate(x = factor(plant_family, levels = columns),
                      y = factor(label, levels = rev(unique(rows$label))),
                      block = factor(block, levels = unique(rows$block)),
                      clear = !is.na(g) & (ci_low > 0 | ci_high < 0),
                      pooled = plant_family == "Pooled")
    ggplot(cells, aes(x, y)) +
        geom_tile(aes(fill = pmax(pmin(g, limit), -limit)), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
        geom_tile(data = dplyr::filter(cells, pooled, !is.na(g)), fill = NA, colour = "grey25",
                  linewidth = 0.3, width = 0.92, height = 0.92) +
        # a pooled estimate whose interval excludes zero carries the same mark as the other
        # cells, set before its value rather than in a corner of the frame
        geom_text(data = dplyr::filter(cells, pooled, !is.na(g)),
                  aes(label = sprintf("%+.1f", g), colour = abs(g) > 0.55 * limit),
                  size = 6 / ggplot2::.pt, show.legend = FALSE,
                  position = position_nudge(x = ifelse(dplyr::filter(cells, pooled, !is.na(g))$clear, 0.12, 0))) +
        scale_colour_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "white", "FALSE" = "black"), guide = "none") +
        geom_point(data = dplyr::filter(cells, is.na(g)), aes(shape = FUNCTIONAL_STAGE_MARKS[["absent"]]),
                   size = 1, colour = "grey60", stroke = 0.35) +
        geom_point(data = dplyr::filter(cells, clear, !pooled),
                   aes(shape = FUNCTIONAL_STAGE_MARKS[["clear"]]), size = 1.2, fill = "white",
                   colour = "black", stroke = 0.35) +
        geom_point(data = dplyr::filter(cells, clear, pooled),
                   aes(shape = FUNCTIONAL_STAGE_MARKS[["clear"]]), size = 0.9, fill = "white",
                   colour = "black", stroke = 0.35, position = position_nudge(x = -0.29)) +
        scale_shape_manual(values = setNames(c(21, 4), unname(FUNCTIONAL_STAGE_MARKS)), name = NULL,
                           limits = unname(FUNCTIONAL_STAGE_MARKS), drop = FALSE,
                           guide = guide_legend(order = 2, ncol = 1, override.aes = list(size = 1.8))) +
        scale_fill_gradient2(low = STAGE_PELLET[[STAGES[1]]], mid = "white",
                             high = STAGE_PELLET[[STAGES[2]]], midpoint = 0,
                             limits = c(-limit, limit), na.value = "grey96",
                             name = sprintf("Hedges' g (%s − %s)", tolower(STAGES[2]),
                                            tolower(STAGES[1])),
                             guide = guide_colourbar(order = 1, direction = "horizontal",
                                                     title.position = "top",
                                                     barwidth = unit(95, "pt"),
                                                     barheight = unit(7, "pt"))) +
        scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0), drop = FALSE) +
        scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0), position = label_side) +
        facet_grid(block ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
        labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = title) +
        theme_pipeline_classic(base_size = 7.5) +
        theme(panel.border = element_blank(), panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
              strip.placement = "outside",
              panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.line = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
              axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 7, colour = "black"),
              axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7.5, colour = "black", lineheight = 0.85),
              strip.text.y.left = if (all(rows$block == "")) element_blank() else
                  element_text(size = 7.5, face = "bold", angle = 90),
              strip.background = element_blank(), panel.spacing = unit(5, "pt"),
              plot.title = element_text(size = PANEL_LETTER_SIZE, face = "bold", margin = margin(0, 0, 5, 0),
                                        hjust = if (label_side == "left") 0 else 1),
              plot.title.position = "plot",
              legend.position = "bottom", legend.box.spacing = unit(2, "pt"),
              legend.title = element_text(size = 7.5, face = "bold"),
              legend.text = element_text(size = 7, colour = "black"),
              legend.key.size = unit(9, "pt"), legend.margin = margin(0, 6, 0, 6),
              plot.margin = margin(3, 3, 3, 3))
}
fig_section("functional_stage_heatmaps",
            needs = c(functional_stage_file(c("predicted_trait", "ko_category", "special_group"),
                                            "by_plant_family"),
                      functional_stage_file(c("predicted_trait", "ko_category", "special_group"),
                                            "pooled"),
                      res("tables", "functional_trait_heatmap_matrix.csv"), KO_SUMMARY), {
    n_categories <- functional_setting("gene_content", "heatmap_categories", 15)
    exclude <- functional_setting("gene_content", "heatmap_exclude_pattern", "")
    effects <- function(prefix, kind) read_csv(functional_stage_file(prefix, kind),
                                               show_col_types = FALSE)
    # A: the traits of the host-breadth figure, in its order
    traits_shown <- read_csv(res("tables", "functional_trait_heatmap_matrix.csv"),
                             show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::distinct(trait, direction, odds_ratio_per_doubling) |>
        dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(odds_ratio_per_doubling)) |>
        dplyr::transmute(feature = trait, label = stringr::str_wrap(trait_label(trait), 38),
                         block = ifelse(direction == "wide", "More common on many hosts",
                                        "More common on few hosts"))
    # the plant families of the trait analysis give every panel its columns
    families <- unique(effects("predicted_trait", "by_plant_family")$plant_family)
    # B, C: the categories of the host-breadth figure, those with the most orthologues
    largest <- function(scheme_name) {
        d <- read_csv(KO_SUMMARY, show_col_types = FALSE) |> dplyr::filter(scheme == scheme_name) |>
            dplyr::mutate(n = `Generalist-enriched` + `Specialist-enriched` + Unassigned)
        if (nzchar(exclude)) d <- dplyr::filter(d, !grepl(exclude, category))
        dplyr::slice_max(d, n, n = n_categories, with_ties = FALSE) |>
            dplyr::transmute(feature = category,
                             label = stringr::str_wrap(tidy_category(category), 32))
    }
    ko_panel <- function(scheme_name, title) stage_function_panel(
        dplyr::filter(effects("ko_category", "by_plant_family"), scheme == scheme_name),
        dplyr::filter(effects("ko_category", "pooled"), scheme == scheme_name),
        largest(scheme_name), title, "right", families) +
        # room on the left for the slanted family names, which lean out of the panel
        theme(plot.margin = margin(3, 3, 3, 30))
    # D: the special groups
    group_titles <- c(anaerobic = "Predicted anaerobic bacteria",
                      nitrogen_fixing = "Predicted nitrogen-fixing bacteria",
                      small_genome = "Predicted small-genome bacteria")
    groups_by <- effects("special_group", "by_plant_family")
    groups_shown <- tibble(feature = intersect(names(group_titles), groups_by$feature)) |>
        dplyr::mutate(label = unname(group_titles[feature]))

    panel_a <- stage_function_panel(effects("predicted_trait", "by_plant_family"),
                                    effects("predicted_trait", "pooled"), traits_shown,
                                    panel_title("a", "Predicted traits"), families = families)
    panel_b <- ko_panel("KEGG level 2", panel_title("b", "KEGG categories (level 2)"))
    panel_c <- ko_panel("PGPG level 3", panel_title("c", "Plant-growth-promotion categories"))
    panel_d <- stage_function_panel(groups_by, effects("special_group", "pooled"), groups_shown,
                                    panel_title("d", "Special groups"), families = families)
    # Two columns, labels on the outside and the heat blocks side by side. The columns are
    # laid out independently, and the one legend is drawn beneath both.
    no_legend <- theme(legend.position = "none")
    column <- function(top, bottom, heights) patchwork::wrap_elements(
        full = patchwork::wrap_plots(top + no_legend, bottom + no_legend, ncol = 1, heights = heights))
    p <- patchwork::wrap_plots(
        patchwork::wrap_plots(column(panel_a, panel_d, c(nrow(traits_shown) + 1, nrow(groups_shown) + 0.4)),
                              column(panel_b, panel_c, c(1, 1)), nrow = 1, widths = c(1.02, 1)),
        patchwork::wrap_elements(full = ggpubr::get_legend(panel_a)),
        ncol = 1, heights = c(1, 0.06))
    print(p)
    # double-column width (183 mm), 600 dpi, drawn with ragg for sharp type
    ggsave(fig("functional_stage_heatmaps"), p, width = 7.2, height = 8.9, dpi = 600,
           device = if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) ragg::agg_tiff else "tiff",
           compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
})
```

```{r fx-fig-alpha-stage-strata}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 2 | Diversity, composition and co-occurrence
#   figure: alpha_stage_effect_heatmap
# ==========================================================================================
# The stage effect on alpha diversity within each plant family (B) and each host genus (C),
# with the estimate pooled across them. Nothing is estimated here: the effects are Part
# 1's (chunk `alpha-stage-by-stratum`). It is drawn with the panel of the functional stage
# heatmap above, which is why it sits here and not with the other alpha figures: Hedges'
# g from the seed colour to the seedling colour, a dot where the 95% interval excludes
# zero, a cross where a stratum could not be estimated, the pooled estimate framed.
ALPHA_STRATA_FILE <- res("tables", "alpha_stage_effect_by_stratum.csv")
ALPHA_STRATA_POOLED <- res("tables", "alpha_stage_effect_pooled.csv")
ALPHA_INDEX_LABELS <- c(Observed = "Observed richness", Shannon = "Shannon diversity",
                        Evenness = "Pielou's evenness")
fig_section("alpha_stage_effect_heatmap", needs = c(ALPHA_STRATA_FILE, ALPHA_STRATA_POOLED), {
    depth_label <- function(depth) dplyr::case_when(
        depth == "none" ~ "Unrarefied",
        TRUE ~ paste(format(suppressWarnings(as.integer(depth)), big.mark = ","), "reads"))
    # the rarefied depths first, shallowest (the primary depth) on top, then unrarefied
    depth_rank <- function(depth) ifelse(depth == "none", Inf, suppressWarnings(as.numeric(depth)))
    by <- read_csv(ALPHA_STRATA_FILE, show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = cols(depth = col_character())) |>
        dplyr::mutate(feature = paste(depth, metric),
                      # "Flavert (Phaseolus vulgaris)" -> "Flavert (P. vulgaris)"
                      column = sub("\\((\\w)\\w+ ", "(\\1. ", stratum))
    pooled <- read_csv(ALPHA_STRATA_POOLED, show_col_types = FALSE,
                       col_types = cols(depth = col_character())) |>
        dplyr::mutate(feature = paste(depth, metric))
    rows <- dplyr::distinct(by, depth, metric, feature) |>
        dplyr::mutate(metric = factor(metric, levels = names(ALPHA_INDEX_LABELS))) |>
        dplyr::arrange(depth_rank(depth), metric) |>
        dplyr::transmute(feature, label = unname(ALPHA_INDEX_LABELS[as.character(metric)]),
                         block = depth_label(depth))
    panel <- function(variable_name, title, column_order = NULL) stage_function_panel(
        dplyr::filter(by, variable == variable_name) |>
            dplyr::transmute(feature, plant_family = column, hedges_g, ci_low, ci_high),
        dplyr::filter(pooled, variable == variable_name), rows, title, column_order = column_order)
    # host genera side by side with the other genera of their plant family (host attributes are plant family and host genus only, at the user's request (2026-10-22))
    genus_order <- dplyr::filter(by, variable == "Host_Genus") |>
        dplyr::distinct(column, family = plant_family) |>
        dplyr::arrange(match(family, FUNCTIONAL_FAMILY_ORDER), column) |> dplyr::pull(column)
    family_order <- intersect(FUNCTIONAL_FAMILY_ORDER, by$column[by$variable == "Plant_Family"])
    # lettered B and C: in main Figure 3 this figure sits under the host phylogeny with
    # alpha diversity, panel A, so that the alpha-diversity panels are in one figure
    panel_a <- panel("Plant_Family", panel_title("b", "Within plant family"), family_order)
    panel_b <- panel("Host_Genus", panel_title("c", "Within host genus"), genus_order) +
        theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), strip.text.y.left = element_blank(),
              axis.text.x = element_text(face = "italic"))
    p <- panel_a + panel_b +
        patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(length(family_order) + 1, length(genus_order) + 1),
                               guides = "collect") &
        theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box.spacing = unit(2, "pt"))
    print(p)
    # double-column width (183 mm), 600 dpi, drawn with ragg for sharp type
    ggsave(fig("alpha_stage_effect_heatmap"), p, width = 7.2, height = 2.0 + 0.26 * nrow(rows),
           dpi = 600, device = if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) ragg::agg_tiff else "tiff",
           compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
})
```

```{r fx-fig-host-breadth-panels}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 4, 7, 8 | see the parts marked below
#   figures: host_phylosymbiosis_scatter, host_breadth_top_genera, three volcano plots
# ==========================================================================================
# Panels of the main figures that had tables but no figure. Nothing is estimated here:
# every value is read from a table Part 1 or its scripts wrote. Each is drawn at the size
# of its place in a main figure (chunk `fx-fig-main-figures`), and carries no panel letter.
PANEL_THEME <- theme_pipeline_classic(base_size = 7.5) +
    # the title starts clear of the panel letter the main figure sets in the corner
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold", hjust = 0, margin = margin(1, 0, 4, 18)),
          plot.title.position = "plot",
          legend.title = element_text(size = 7.5, face = "bold"), legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
          legend.key.size = unit(8, "pt"), axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"))
save_panel <- function(name, p, width, height) {
    print(p)
    ggsave(fig(name), p, width = width, height = height, dpi = 600,
           device = if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) ragg::agg_tiff else "tiff",
           compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
}
BREADTH_CLASS_COLOURS <- c("Generalist-enriched" = HOST_BREADTH_COLOURS[["generalist"]],
                           "Specialist-enriched" = HOST_BREADTH_COLOURS[["specialist"]],
                           "Unassigned" = "grey80")

# METHODS 4 | figure: host_phylosymbiosis_scatter
fig_section("host_phylosymbiosis_scatter",
            needs = res("tables", c("host_phylosymbiosis_pairs.csv", "host_phylosymbiosis_tests.csv")), {
    units <- c(genus = "Genera", ASV = "ASVs")
    # one facet per unit and stage: genera then ASVs, seeds then seedlings
    facet_of <- function(unit, stage) factor(
        paste(units[unit], tolower(stage), sep = ", "),
        levels = as.vector(t(outer(units, tolower(STAGES), paste, sep = ", "))))
    pairs <- read_csv(res("tables", "host_phylosymbiosis_pairs.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::mutate(panel = facet_of(unit, stage))
    tests <- read_csv(res("tables", "host_phylosymbiosis_tests.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::mutate(panel = facet_of(unit, stage),
                      # the tests sit under the panel's name, clear of the points
                      label = sprintf("**%s**<br><span style='font-size:6pt'>Mantel r = %.2f, p = %.3f<br>MRM R² = %.2f, p = %.3f</span>",
                                      panel, mantel_r, mantel_p, mrm_r2, mrm_p))
    strip_labels <- setNames(tests$label, as.character(tests$panel))
    p <- ggplot(pairs, aes(divergence_my, mean_bray)) +
        geom_point(aes(fill = between_study_share), shape = 21, size = 1.3, stroke = 0.2,
                   colour = "grey25", alpha = 0.9) +
        geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
        # from light grey, not white, so that pairs from one study still show against the panel
        scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("grey88", PIPELINE_BAR_FILL, FIGURE_PALETTE$stage_generalist),
                            limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1),
                            name = "Share of sample pairs from different studies",
                            # the colour bar lies along the top, clear of the panel letter at the left
                            guide = guide_colourbar(direction = "horizontal", title.position = "left",
                                                    barwidth = unit(80, "pt"), barheight = unit(5, "pt"))) +
        facet_wrap(~ panel, nrow = 1, labeller = as_labeller(strip_labels)) +
        labs(x = "Host divergence time (million years)",
             y = "Mean Bray–Curtis dissimilarity\nbetween host species") +
        PANEL_THEME + theme(strip.text = ggtext::element_markdown(size = 7.5, lineheight = 1.1,
                                                                  margin = margin(0, 0, 2, 0)),
                            strip.background = element_blank(),
                            legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "right",
                            legend.title = element_text(size = 7, face = "bold", vjust = 0.9),
                            # room at the right for the last label of the bar
                            legend.margin = margin(0, 12, 0, 0), legend.box.spacing = unit(2, "pt"))
    save_panel("host_phylosymbiosis_scatter", p, 7.2, 2.95)
})

# METHODS 7 | figure: host_breadth_top_genera
fig_section("host_breadth_top_genera", needs = res("tables", "generalist_specialist_top_genera.csv"), {
    top <- read_csv(res("tables", "generalist_specialist_top_genera.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::mutate(label = ifelse(nchar(Genus) > 25, sub("-.*$", " group", Genus), Genus),
                      label = factor(label, levels = label[order(rank)]),
                      log_abundance = log10(mean_relative_abundance_pct))
    # the abundance axis on the right is the count axis rescaled
    most <- max(top$n_hosts)
    span <- range(top$log_abundance)
    to_count <- function(x) (x - span[1]) / diff(span) * most
    bars <- tidyr::pivot_longer(top, c(n_hostg, n_hosts), names_to = "measure", values_to = "hosts") |>
        dplyr::mutate(measure = factor(c(n_hostg = "Host genera", n_hosts = "Host species")[measure],
                                       levels = c("Host genera", "Host species")))
    p <- ggplot(bars, aes(label, hosts)) +
        geom_col(aes(fill = measure), position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7) +
        geom_point(data = top, aes(y = to_count(log_abundance), shape = "Mean relative abundance"),
                   colour = FIGURE_PALETTE$abundance, size = 1.6) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = c("Host genera" = FIGURE_PALETTE$host_genera,
                                     "Host species" = FIGURE_PALETTE$host_species), name = NULL) +
        scale_shape_manual(values = 18, name = NULL) +
        scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05)), name = "Number of hosts",
                           sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / most * diff(span) + span[1],
                                               name = "log10 mean relative\nabundance (%)")) +
        labs(x = NULL) +
        PANEL_THEME +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "italic", size = 7),
              legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "right",
              legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0), legend.box.spacing = unit(2, "pt"))
    save_panel("host_breadth_top_genera", p, 7.2, 2.5)
})

# METHODS 8 | figures: trait_numeric_volcano, trait_binary_volcano
TRAIT_SOURCE_COLOURS <- unlist(FIGURE_PALETTE$trait_sources)
trait_tests_for_volcano <- function() {
    read_csv(TRAIT_TESTS, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::filter(status == "tested", !is.na(q)) |>
        dplyr::mutate(source = factor(sub(" .*$", "", resource), levels = names(TRAIT_SOURCE_COLOURS)),
                      name = sub(" \\([BFM]\\)$", "", trait_label(trait)),
                      significance = -log10(pmax(q, 1e-300)))
}
trait_volcano <- function(d, x, x_title, title, n_labels = 6) {
    fdr <- functional_setting("predicted_traits", "fdr", 0.05)
    named <- dplyr::slice_max(dplyr::filter(d, q < fdr), significance, n = n_labels, with_ties = FALSE)
    ggplot(d, aes(.data[[x]], significance)) +
        geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(fdr), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.3) +
        geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.3) +
        geom_point(aes(colour = source, alpha = q < fdr), size = 1) +
        ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = named, aes(label = name), size = 5.5 / ggplot2::.pt,
                                 min.segment.length = 0, segment.size = 0.2, max.overlaps = Inf,
                                 box.padding = 0.4, force = 3, seed = 1) +
        scale_colour_manual(values = TRAIT_SOURCE_COLOURS, drop = FALSE, name = NULL) +
        scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 0.9, `FALSE` = 0.3), guide = "none") +
        scale_y_continuous(trans = "sqrt", expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.06))) +
        labs(x = x_title, y = expression(-log[10] ~ "adjusted p"), title = title) +
        PANEL_THEME + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.margin = margin(-4, 0, 0, 0))
}
fig_section("trait_numeric_volcano", needs = TRAIT_TESTS, {
    d <- dplyr::filter(trait_tests_for_volcano(), type == "numeric")
    p <- trait_volcano(d, "spearman_rho", "Spearman ρ with number of host species",
                       "Numeric traits", n_labels = 4)
    save_panel("trait_numeric_volcano", p, 2.4, 2.7)
})
fig_section("trait_binary_volcano", needs = TRAIT_TESTS, {
    d <- dplyr::filter(trait_tests_for_volcano(), type == "binary") |>
        dplyr::mutate(log2_or = pmax(pmin(log2(odds_ratio_per_doubling), 4), -4))
    p <- trait_volcano(d, "log2_or", "log2 odds ratio per doubling of host number",
                       "Binary traits", n_labels = 5)
    save_panel("trait_binary_volcano", p, 2.4, 2.7)
})

# METHODS 8 | figure: ko_volcano
fig_section("ko_volcano", needs = res("tables", "ko_breadth_tests.csv"), {
    ko <- read_csv(res("tables", "ko_breadth_tests.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::filter(!is.na(q), is.finite(log2_odds_ratio)) |>
        dplyr::mutate(significance = -log10(pmax(q, 1e-300)),
                      shown = pmax(pmin(log2_odds_ratio, 5), -5),
                      enrichment = factor(enrichment, levels = names(BREADTH_CLASS_COLOURS)))
    counts <- table(ko$enrichment)
    p <- ggplot(dplyr::arrange(ko, enrichment != "Unassigned"), aes(shown, significance)) +
        geom_point(aes(colour = enrichment), size = 0.35, alpha = 0.6) +
        scale_colour_manual(values = BREADTH_CLASS_COLOURS, name = NULL,
                            labels = sprintf("%s (%s)", names(counts), format(as.integer(counts), big.mark = ",")),
                            guide = guide_legend(ncol = 1, override.aes = list(size = 1.6, alpha = 1))) +
        scale_y_continuous(trans = "sqrt", expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.06))) +
        labs(x = "log2 odds ratio per doubling of host number", y = expression(-log[10] ~ "adjusted p"),
             title = "KEGG orthologues") +
        PANEL_THEME + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.margin = margin(-4, 0, 0, 0))
    save_panel("ko_volcano", p, 2.4, 2.7)
})

# METHODS 8 | figures: trait_breadth_forest, ko_function_bars
# The same two sets of tests as the volcano plots above, drawn so that the functions can
# be read by name: the traits most strongly tied to host breadth with their odds ratios,
# and the plant-growth-promotion functions with the share of their orthologues enriched
# in host generalists and in host specialists. These two are panels D and E of main
# Figure 5; the volcano plots are kept as supplementary figures.

#' A predicted trait's name as a reader would write it: "metatraits_growth_malonate" ->
#' "Growth on malonate". The source is shown by colour, not in the name.
trait_name <- function(x) {
    n <- tolower(gsub("_", " ", sub("_ec[0-9_]+$", "", sub("^[a-z]+_", "", x))))
    n <- sub("^growth ", "growth on ", n)
    n <- sub("^assimilation ", "assimilation of ", n)
    n <- sub("^degradation ", "degradation of ", n)
    n <- sub("^builds acid from ", "acid production from ", n)
    n <- sub("^enzyme activity (.*)$", "\\1 activity", n)
    n <- sub("^electron acceptor (.*)$", "\\1 as electron acceptor", n)
    n <- sub("^carbon source (.*)$", "\\1 as carbon source", n)
    n <- gsub("\\bd glucose\\b", "D-glucose", n)
    n <- gsub("\\b(\\d) hydroxy", "\\1-hydroxy", n)
    n <- sub("n acetyl beta glucosaminidase", "N-acetyl-β-glucosaminidase", n)
    n <- gsub("\\bbeta ", "β-", n)
    n <- sub("^gram negative$", "Gram-negative", n)
    # a capital for a Latin first letter only: a Greek beta stays as it is
    ifelse(grepl("^[a-z]", n), paste0(toupper(substr(n, 1, 1)), substring(n, 2)), n)
}

fig_section("trait_breadth_forest", needs = TRAIT_TESTS, {
    per_direction <- functional_setting("predicted_traits", "forest_traits_per_direction", 10)
    fdr <- functional_setting("predicted_traits", "fdr", 0.05)
    limit <- 32                                   # odds ratios beyond this are drawn at the edge
    shown <- read_csv(TRAIT_TESTS, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::filter(status == "tested", type == "binary", q < fdr) |>
        dplyr::mutate(direction = ifelse(odds_ratio_per_doubling > 1, "wide", "narrow")) |>
        dplyr::slice_min(q, n = per_direction, by = direction, with_ties = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::arrange(odds_ratio_per_doubling) |>
        dplyr::mutate(name = trait_name(trait), name = factor(name, levels = unique(name)),
                      source = factor(sub(" .*$", "", resource), levels = names(TRAIT_SOURCE_COLOURS)),
                      low = pmax(or_ci_low, 1 / limit), high = pmin(or_ci_high, limit),
                      estimate = pmax(pmin(odds_ratio_per_doubling, limit), 1 / limit))
    p <- ggplot(shown, aes(estimate, name, colour = source)) +
        geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.3) +
        geom_segment(aes(x = low, xend = high, yend = name), linewidth = 0.5) +
        geom_point(size = 1.5) +
        scale_colour_manual(values = TRAIT_SOURCE_COLOURS, drop = FALSE, name = NULL) +
        scale_x_continuous(trans = "log2", breaks = c(1 / 16, 1 / 4, 1, 4, 16),
                           labels = c("1/16", "1/4", "1", "4", "16")) +
        labs(x = "Odds ratio per doubling of host number\n(left: few hosts; right: many hosts)", y = NULL) +
        PANEL_THEME +
        theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6.5), legend.position = "bottom",
              legend.margin = margin(-4, 0, 0, 0))
    save_panel("trait_breadth_forest", p, 3.6, 3.0)
})

fig_section("ko_function_bars", needs = KO_SUMMARY, {
    n_functions <- functional_setting("gene_content", "function_bars", 12)
    functions <- read_csv(KO_SUMMARY, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::filter(scheme == "PGPG level 3") |>
        dplyr::mutate(n = `Generalist-enriched` + `Specialist-enriched` + Unassigned) |>
        dplyr::slice_max(n, n = n_functions, with_ties = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::mutate(generalist = 100 * `Generalist-enriched` / n,
                      specialist = 100 * `Specialist-enriched` / n,
                      name = stringr::str_wrap(tidy_category(category), 30),
                      name = factor(name, levels = name[order(generalist - specialist)]))
    bars <- dplyr::bind_rows(
        dplyr::transmute(functions, name, class = "Generalist-enriched", share = generalist,
                         count = `Generalist-enriched`),
        dplyr::transmute(functions, name, class = "Specialist-enriched", share = -specialist,
                         count = `Specialist-enriched`))
    reach <- max(abs(bars$share)) * 1.22
    p <- ggplot(bars, aes(share, name, fill = class)) +
        geom_col(width = 0.72) +
        geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey25", linewidth = 0.3) +
        geom_text(aes(label = count, hjust = ifelse(share < 0, 1.15, -0.15)), size = 5.5 / ggplot2::.pt) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = BREADTH_CLASS_COLOURS[c("Specialist-enriched", "Generalist-enriched")],
                          breaks = c("Specialist-enriched", "Generalist-enriched"), name = NULL) +
        scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-reach, reach), labels = function(x) abs(x)) +
        labs(x = "Share of the function's orthologues (%)", y = NULL) +
        PANEL_THEME +
        theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6.5, lineheight = 0.85), legend.position = "bottom",
              legend.margin = margin(-4, 0, 0, 0))
    save_panel("ko_function_bars", p, 3.6, 3.0)
})
```
