```{r fx-fig-supplementary-panels}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 2, 6, 7 | see the parts marked below
#   figures: beta_variance_explained, host_breadth_null, host_class_composition
# ==========================================================================================
# Supplementary figures for result tables that had none: the variance in community
# structure explained by each variable, the null model behind the host-breadth threshold,
# and the taxa that differ between host generalists and specialists. Nothing is computed
# here: every value is read from a table Part 1 or its scripts wrote.

#' Labels made unique within a facet and ordered by a value there, for a faceted axis.
#' The part after "___" is removed again when the axis is drawn.
tidytext_order <- function(label, by, within) {
    key <- paste(label, within, sep = "___")
    factor(key, levels = unique(key[order(within, by)]))
}

# METHODS 2 | figure: beta_variance_explained
BETA_TERM_LABELS <- c(Developmental_Stage = "Developmental stage", Family = "Plant family",
                      Host_Genus = "Host genus")
fig_section("beta_variance_explained",
            needs = c(res("diversity", "permanova_css_by_unit.csv"),
                      res("tables", "host_beta_variance_partition.csv")), {
    # A: each variable on its own. Study is left out, as in the tables.
    alone <- read_csv(res("diversity", "permanova_css_by_unit.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::filter(model == "univariate", term %in% names(BETA_TERM_LABELS)) |>
        dplyr::mutate(variable = factor(BETA_TERM_LABELS[term], levels = rev(unname(BETA_TERM_LABELS))),
                      unit = factor(ifelse(unit == "ASV", "ASVs", "Genera"), levels = c("Genera", "ASVs")))
    panel_a <- ggplot(alone, aes(100 * R2, variable, fill = unit)) +
        geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7) +
        geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", 100 * R2)), position = position_dodge(width = 0.75),
                  hjust = -0.15, size = 5.5 / ggplot2::.pt) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = c(Genera = FIGURE_PALETTE$categorical[3], ASVs = FIGURE_PALETTE$bar),
                          name = NULL, guide = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)) +
        scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.14))) +
        labs(x = "Variance explained alone (PERMANOVA R², %)", y = NULL, title = panel_letter("a")) +
        PANEL_THEME + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.margin = margin(-4, 0, 0, 0),
                            plot.title = element_text(size = PANEL_LETTER_SIZE, face = "bold", margin = margin(0, 0, 3, 0)))
    # B: what host and stage explain alone and together (adjusted R2)
    fractions <- read_csv(res("tables", "host_beta_variance_partition.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::filter(fraction != "unexplained") |>
        dplyr::mutate(part = dplyr::case_when(
                          grepl("^(genus|family|cultivar) alone$", fraction) ~ "Host alone",
                          fraction == "stage alone" ~ "Stage alone",
                          TRUE ~ "Shared"),
                      model = sprintf("%s, host as %s", ifelse(unit == "ASV", "ASVs", "Genera"), host_level)) |>
        dplyr::summarise(share = 100 * sum(pmax(adj_R2, 0)), .by = c(model, part)) |>
        dplyr::mutate(part = factor(part, levels = c("Shared", "Stage alone", "Host alone")))
    panel_b <- ggplot(fractions, aes(share, model, fill = part)) +
        geom_col(width = 0.65) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = c("Host alone" = FIGURE_PALETTE$categorical[1],
                                     "Stage alone" = FIGURE_PALETTE$categorical[7], "Shared" = "grey75"),
                          name = NULL, guide = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE, nrow = 1)) +
        scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
        labs(x = "Variance explained (adjusted R², %)", y = NULL, title = panel_letter("b")) +
        PANEL_THEME + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.margin = margin(-4, 0, 0, 0),
                            plot.title = element_text(size = PANEL_LETTER_SIZE, face = "bold", margin = margin(0, 0, 3, 0)))
    save_panel("beta_variance_explained", panel_a + panel_b, 7.2, 2.4)
})

# METHODS 6 | figure: host_breadth_null
fig_section("host_breadth_null", needs = res("tables", "generalist_specialist_breadth_null.csv"), {
    null <- read_csv(res("tables", "generalist_specialist_breadth_null.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::mutate(panel = factor(ifelse(unit == "ASV", "ASVs", "Genera"), levels = c("ASVs", "Genera")))
    thresholds <- dplyr::distinct(null, panel, threshold)
    p <- ggplot(null, aes(n_hosts)) +
        geom_col(aes(y = observed, fill = "Observed"), width = 0.75) +
        geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = null_lower, ymax = null_upper, colour = "Null model (mean and 95% range)"),
                      width = 0.3, linewidth = 0.35) +
        geom_point(aes(y = null_mean, colour = "Null model (mean and 95% range)"), size = 1) +
        geom_vline(data = thresholds, aes(xintercept = threshold - 0.5), linetype = "dashed",
                   colour = "grey35", linewidth = 0.35) +
        geom_text(data = thresholds, aes(x = threshold - 0.3, y = Inf, label = "generalist threshold"),
                  hjust = 0, vjust = 1.4, size = 5.5 / ggplot2::.pt, colour = "grey25") +
        facet_wrap(~ panel, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
        scale_fill_manual(values = c(Observed = FIGURE_PALETTE$bar), name = NULL) +
        scale_colour_manual(values = c("Null model (mean and 95% range)" = FIGURE_PALETTE$categorical[6]),
                            name = NULL) +
        scale_y_continuous(trans = "sqrt", expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
        scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1, 16, 2)) +
        labs(x = "Number of host plant species on which the taxon occurs", y = "Number of taxa") +
        # panel names at the left, clear of the threshold label at the top of each panel
        PANEL_THEME + theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
                            strip.background = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
                            legend.margin = margin(-4, 0, 0, 0))
    save_panel("host_breadth_null", p, 7.2, 2.9)
})

# METHODS 7 | figure: host_class_composition
fig_section("host_class_composition",
            needs = res("tables", c("generalist_specialist_composition_tests.csv",
                                    "generalist_specialist_breadth_abundance.csv")), {
    fdr <- functional_setting("generalist_specialist", "screen_fdr", 0.05)
    ranks <- c("Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus")
    tests <- read_csv(res("tables", "generalist_specialist_composition_tests.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        # each ASV sits in one taxon of a rank, so the rank totals are the class sizes
        dplyr::mutate(share_generalists = 100 * generalists / sum(generalists),
                      share_specialists = 100 * specialists / sum(specialists), .by = rank) |>
        dplyr::filter(!is.na(q), q < fdr, taxon != "Unassigned") |>
        dplyr::mutate(rank = factor(rank, levels = ranks),
                      label = ifelse(nchar(taxon) > 28, sub("-.*$", " group", taxon), taxon),
                      label = tidytext_order(label, share_generalists - share_specialists, rank))
    shares <- tidyr::pivot_longer(tests, c(share_generalists, share_specialists), names_to = "class",
                                  values_to = "share") |>
        dplyr::mutate(class = ifelse(class == "share_generalists", "Host generalists", "Host specialists"))
    panel_a <- ggplot(shares, aes(share, label)) +
        geom_line(aes(group = label), colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.4) +
        geom_point(aes(colour = class), size = 1.5) +
        facet_grid(rank ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
        scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) sub("___.*$", "", x)) +
        scale_colour_manual(values = c("Host generalists" = HOST_BREADTH_COLOURS[["generalist"]],
                                       "Host specialists" = HOST_BREADTH_COLOURS[["specialist"]]), name = NULL) +
        scale_x_continuous(trans = "sqrt", breaks = c(0, 1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 75)) +
        labs(x = "Share of the class's ASVs in the taxon (%)", y = NULL, title = panel_letter("b")) +
        PANEL_THEME +
        theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6.5, face = "italic"),
              strip.text.y = element_text(size = 7, face = "bold", angle = 0, hjust = 0),
              strip.background = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
              legend.margin = margin(-4, 0, 0, 0),
              plot.title = element_text(size = PANEL_LETTER_SIZE, face = "bold", margin = margin(0, 0, 3, 0)))
    abundance <- read_csv(res("tables", "generalist_specialist_breadth_abundance.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::mutate(Phylum = factor(Phylum, levels = Phylum[order(spearman_rho)]),
                      result = ifelse(spearman_q < fdr, "q < 0.05", "not significant"))
    panel_b <- ggplot(abundance, aes(spearman_rho, Phylum, fill = result)) +
        geom_col(width = 0.65) +
        # the bar's own value first, then the number of ASVs it rests on
        geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("\u03c1 = %.2f (%s ASVs)", spearman_rho,
                                      format(n_asvs, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE))), hjust = -0.05,
                  size = 5.5 / ggplot2::.pt) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = c("q < 0.05" = FIGURE_PALETTE$bar, "not significant" = "grey75"), name = NULL) +
        scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.75))) +
        labs(x = "Spearman ρ between host number\nand relative abundance", y = NULL, title = panel_letter("c")) +
        PANEL_THEME + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.margin = margin(-4, 0, 0, 0),
                            plot.title = element_text(size = PANEL_LETTER_SIZE, face = "bold", margin = margin(0, 0, 3, 0)))
    save_panel("host_class_composition", panel_a + panel_b + patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(1.55, 1)),
               7.2, 4.6)
})
```

```{r fx-fig-study-overview}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 1 | Data and filtering
#   figure: study_overview (the overview figure)
# ==========================================================================================
# One-figure overview of the compiled dataset, panels A-F: where the samples come from
# (map and country shares), the seed/seedling split, how many each study contributes at
# each stage, and the host genera sampled at each stage. Everything describes the
# filtered dataset in ps_clean.rds.
# Colours: seeds orange and seedlings teal wherever stage is shown; countries take
# other colours, shared by the map and the pie so one legend serves both.
OVERVIEW_STUDIES <- res("tables", "metadata_overview_publication.csv")
OVERVIEW_TOP_HOSTS <- 12
fig_section("study_overview", needs = c(PS_CLEAN, OVERVIEW_STUDIES), {
    # sized for a 183 mm double-column page: no text under 6 pt, 8 pt panel letters, all
    # of it black. Journal style for the bar panels: axis lines only, no frame and no
    # gridlines - every bar carries its own number - and tight margins, so the panels sit
    # close together.
    OVERVIEW_LABEL_SIZE <- 6 / ggplot2::.pt        # geom_text sizes are in mm; this is 6 pt
    panel_theme <- theme_pipeline_classic(base_size = 7.5) +
        theme(panel.border = element_blank(), panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
              axis.text = element_text(colour = "black", size = 6.5),
              axis.line = element_line(colour = INK, linewidth = 0.3),
              axis.ticks = element_line(colour = INK, linewidth = 0.3),
              axis.ticks.length = unit(1.5, "pt"), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
              axis.title.x = element_text(size = 7, margin = margin(t = 1)),
              # the top margin holds the panel letter clear of the first bar's name
              plot.margin = margin(8, 3, 1, 2))
    void_theme <- theme_void(base_size = 7.5) + theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 1, 0, 1))
    d <- meta |>
        dplyr::mutate(country = stringr::str_trim(sub(":.*$", "", Geography)),
                      host_genus = sub(" .*$", "", Scientific_Name),
                      stage = factor(.data[[PRIMARY]], levels = STAGES))

    # --- A, B: geography -----------------------------------------------------------
    by_country <- d |> dplyr::count(country, name = "n") |>
        dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n)) |>
        dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n),
                      key = sprintf("%s (%s%%, n = %s)", country,
                                    ifelse(pct < 1, sprintf("%.1f", pct), sprintf("%.0f", pct)),
                                    comma(n)),
                      key = factor(key, levels = key))
    country_colours <- setNames(
        rep(setdiff(NATURE_THICK, STAGE_PELLET), length.out = nrow(by_country)),
        levels(by_country$key))
    world <- ggplot2::map_data("world") |> dplyr::filter(region != "Antarctica") |>
        dplyr::left_join(by_country, dplyr::join_by(region == country))
    unmatched <- setdiff(by_country$country, world$region)
    if (length(unmatched)) stop("countries not on the map: ", paste(unmatched, collapse = ", "))
    p_map <- ggplot(world, aes(long, lat, group = group, fill = key)) +
        geom_polygon(colour = "grey35", linewidth = 0.12) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = country_colours, na.value = "grey93", guide = "none") +
        coord_quickmap(expand = FALSE) +
        void_theme
    p_pie_country <- ggplot(by_country, aes(x = 1, y = n, fill = key)) +
        geom_col(width = 1, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
        coord_polar(theta = "y", direction = -1) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = country_colours, name = "Country") +
        void_theme +
        theme(legend.position = "left", legend.key.size = unit(6, "pt"),
              legend.text = element_text(size = 6, colour = "black"),
              legend.title = element_text(size = 7, face = "bold", colour = "black"),
              legend.key.spacing.y = unit(0, "pt"),
              legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0), legend.box.spacing = unit(0, "pt"))

    # --- D: samples per study, by stage ---------------------------------------------
    refs <- read_csv(OVERVIEW_STUDIES, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::select(study_alias = Study, Reference)
    # two accessions share "Chandel et al. 2022"; the accession keeps them apart
    by_study <- d |> dplyr::count(study_alias, stage, name = "n") |>
        dplyr::left_join(refs, dplyr::join_by(study_alias)) |>
        dplyr::mutate(study = sprintf("%s (%s)", dplyr::coalesce(Reference, study_alias),
                                      study_alias),
                      study = fct_reorder(study, n, .fun = sum))
    # Horizontal bars, like E and F: the study names read straight, where upright bars
    # needed them slanted under the axis and a third of the panel went on labels. Each
    # bar ends in its two counts, so no stage key is needed - panel C names the colours.
    study_counts <- by_study |>
        tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = stage, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
        dplyr::mutate(total = .data[[STAGES[1]]] + .data[[STAGES[2]]],
                      lab = sprintf("%s / %s", comma(.data[[STAGES[1]]]),
                                    comma(.data[[STAGES[2]]])))
    p_study <- ggplot(by_study, aes(x = n, y = study)) +
        # reversed, so the segments run in the order of the counts: seeds, then seedlings
        geom_col(aes(fill = stage), width = 0.75, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
        geom_text(data = study_counts, aes(x = total, label = lab), hjust = -0.08,
                  size = OVERVIEW_LABEL_SIZE) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = STAGE_PELLET, guide = "none") +
        scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.45)), labels = comma,
                           breaks = c(0, 500, 1000)) +
        labs(x = sprintf("Samples (%s / %s)", tolower(STAGES[1]), tolower(STAGES[2])),
             y = NULL) +
        panel_theme

    # --- C: stage split -------------------------------------------------------------
    by_stage <- d |> dplyr::count(stage, name = "n") |>
        dplyr::mutate(lab = sprintf("%s\n%.0f%%\nn = %s", stage, 100 * n / sum(n), comma(n)))
    p_pie_stage <- ggplot(by_stage, aes(x = 1, y = n, fill = stage)) +
        geom_col(width = 1, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
        geom_text(aes(label = lab), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
                  colour = "white", size = OVERVIEW_LABEL_SIZE, lineheight = 0.9) +
        coord_polar(theta = "y", direction = -1) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = STAGE_PELLET, guide = "none") +
        void_theme

    # --- E, F: host genera at each stage ----------------------------------------------
    host_panel <- function(s) {
        h <- d |> dplyr::filter(stage == s) |> dplyr::count(host_genus, name = "n") |>
            dplyr::slice_max(n, n = OVERVIEW_TOP_HOSTS, with_ties = FALSE) |>
            dplyr::mutate(host_genus = fct_reorder(host_genus, n))
        ggplot(h, aes(x = n, y = host_genus)) +
            geom_col(fill = STAGE_PELLET[[s]], width = 0.75) +
            geom_text(aes(label = comma(n)), hjust = -0.15, size = OVERVIEW_LABEL_SIZE) +
            scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18)), labels = comma) +
            labs(x = "Samples", y = NULL) +
            panel_theme + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"))
    }

    p <- (p_map + p_pie_country + p_pie_stage +
              patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(3.17, 1.3, 1.3))) /
         # D is wrapped so that its long study names do not push the map above it inwards
         (patchwork::wrap_elements(full = p_study) +
              host_panel(STAGES[1]) + host_panel(STAGES[2]) +
              patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(2.6, 1.25, 1.25))) +
        patchwork::plot_layout(heights = c(1.25, 1.25)) +
        patchwork::plot_annotation(tag_levels = panel_letter("a")) &
        theme(plot.tag = element_text(size = PANEL_LETTER_SIZE, face = "bold", colour = "black"),
              plot.tag.position = c(0, 1), plot.tag.location = "plot")
    print(p)
    # Composite at double-column width (183 mm), wider than the save_nature_figure() sizes.
    # 600 dpi, the resolution journals ask of figures that mix text and line art, and drawn
    # with ragg where it is installed: its text is hinted and anti-aliased, where the
    # default macOS device leaves small type soft.
    ggsave(fig("study_overview"), p, width = 7.2, height = 3.2, dpi = 600,
           device = if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) ragg::agg_tiff else "tiff",
           compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
})
```

## 7. Manuscript figures

Fig 1–4 are the audit's corrected figures. They are **not** recomputed here: the
values of record live in `validation/supplementary/`, and `manuscript_figures.qmd`
regenerates the panels against them. That notebook is kept separate on purpose —
see the independence note in `CLAUDE.md`. This section surfaces the manifest so one
document still accounts for every figure in the project.

## 9. One folder per analysis

```{r fx-analysis-folders}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS - | support code (no analysis)
#   deposit each analysis's tables and figures together in its own folder
# ==========================================================================================
# One folder per analysis under <outputs.directory>/<analysis_folders.directory>/, as the
# config's `analysis_folders` section lists them (paths relative to the outputs directory,
# wildcards allowed), so that an analysis's tables sit beside its figures.
#   Figures live in these folders only. Part 2 writes them there directly (fig() above);
#     Part 1 still writes its own to figures/, and this step moves those across. A figure
#     already in its folder and not redrawn by this run is left where it is.
#   Tables and other results are copied: every later step reads them from tables/. Copies
#     an earlier run deposited are removed first, from the previous index, so nothing
#     stale is left. Anything else in the folders is not touched.
# index.csv records every file in the folders, every listed file that was not found, and
# every file in tables/ and figures/ that no folder claims.
deposit_by_analysis <- function(results_dir, settings) {
    root <- file.path(results_dir, settings$directory)
    dir.create(root, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
    index_path <- file.path(root, "index.csv")
    is_figure <- function(path) startsWith(path, "figures/")
    if (file.exists(index_path)) {
        old <- read_csv(index_path, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
            dplyr::filter(status == "deposited", !is_figure(source))
        unlink(file.path(root, old$folder, old$file))
    }
    relative <- function(path) substring(path, nchar(results_dir) + 2)
    kind_of <- function(path) dplyr::case_when(
        grepl("\\.(tiff|png|pdf)$", path, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "figure",
        grepl("\\.(csv|md)$", path, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "table", TRUE ~ "other")

    index <- purrr::imap(settings$folders, function(entry, folder) {
        found <- purrr::map(entry$files, function(pattern) {
            hits <- Sys.glob(file.path(results_dir, pattern))
            # a figure written or moved here earlier has no file left under figures/
            held <- if (is_figure(pattern)) {
                setdiff(basename(Sys.glob(file.path(root, folder, basename(pattern)))),
                        basename(hits))
            } else character()
            if (!length(hits) && !length(held)) {
                return(tibble(source = file.path(results_dir, pattern),
                              status = "listed but not found", arrival = NA_character_))
            }
            tibble(source = c(hits, file.path(results_dir, "figures", held)),
                   status = "deposited",
                   arrival = c(rep(if (is_figure(pattern)) "moved" else "copied", length(hits)),
                               rep("already in folder", length(held))))
        }) |> purrr::list_rbind() |> dplyr::distinct()
        # two files of one name (the three tree.nwk) take their folder's name in front
        clash <- basename(found$source) %in% basename(found$source)[duplicated(basename(found$source))]
        found |>
            dplyr::mutate(folder = folder, methods_paragraph = entry$methods_paragraph,
                          analysis = entry$analysis,
                          file = ifelse(clash, paste(basename(dirname(source)), basename(source),
                                                     sep = "_"), basename(source)))
    }) |> purrr::list_rbind()

    for (folder in unique(index$folder)) {
        dir.create(file.path(root, folder), showWarnings = FALSE)
    }
    # a folder the config no longer lists goes once it is empty (unlink leaves a full one)
    retired <- setdiff(list.dirs(root, full.names = FALSE, recursive = FALSE), names(settings$folders))
    for (folder in retired[lengths(lapply(file.path(root, retired), list.files, all.files = TRUE,
                                          no.. = TRUE)) == 0]) {
        unlink(file.path(root, folder), recursive = TRUE)
    }
    arriving <- dplyr::filter(index, arrival %in% c("moved", "copied"))
    target <- file.path(root, arriving$folder, arriving$file)
    # Part 1 and Part 2 draw a few figures under one name, and Part 2's is the one to keep.
    # Part 2 writes straight into the folder, after Part 1, so a figure already there and
    # newer than its figures/ namesake stays, and the older one is only cleared away.
    superseded <- arriving$arrival == "moved" & file.exists(target) &
        file.mtime(target) > file.mtime(arriving$source)
    copied <- file.copy(arriving$source[!superseded], target[!superseded], overwrite = TRUE,
                        copy.date = TRUE)
    if (!all(copied)) {
        stop("could not deposit: ", paste(arriving$source[!superseded][!copied], collapse = ", "))
    }
    # the original of a figure goes only once its copy is in place
    unlink(arriving$source[arriving$arrival == "moved" & file.exists(target)])

    produced <- list.files(file.path(results_dir, c("tables", "figures")), full.names = TRUE)
    unclaimed <- setdiff(produced[!grepl("^\\.", basename(produced))], index$source)
    index <- dplyr::bind_rows(
        index, tibble(source = unclaimed, status = "not assigned to a folder",
                      file = basename(unclaimed))) |>
        dplyr::transmute(folder, methods_paragraph, analysis, kind = kind_of(file), file,
                         source = relative(source), status, arrival)
    write_csv(index, index_path)

    counts <- dplyr::filter(index, status == "deposited") |>
        dplyr::summarise(figures = sum(kind == "figure"), tables = sum(kind == "table"),
                         other = sum(kind == "other"),
                         .by = c(folder, methods_paragraph, analysis))
    writeLines(c(
        "# Results by analysis", "",
        "One folder per analysis, with its tables and figures together.", "",
        "- **Figures are kept here and nowhere else.** `figures/` is only a staging folder that",
        "  the pipeline empties into these folders at the end of each run.",
        "- **Tables are copies.** The pipeline reads its tables from `tables/`, and refreshes the",
        "  copies here at the end of each run.", "",
        "`index.csv` lists every file here and where it came from.", "",
        "| Folder | Methodology paragraph | Analysis | Figures | Tables | Other |",
        "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |",
        sprintf("| `%s` | %d | %s | %d | %d | %d |", counts$folder, counts$methods_paragraph,
                counts$analysis, counts$figures, counts$tables, counts$other)),
        file.path(root, "README.md"))
    index
}

if (is.null(config$analysis_folders)) {
    cat("Folders by analysis: skipped, no `analysis_folders` section in the config\n")
} else {
    folder_index <- deposit_by_analysis(RESULTS, config$analysis_folders)
    print(as.data.frame(dplyr::count(folder_index, status)), row.names = FALSE)
    cat("folders by analysis:", file.path(RESULTS, config$analysis_folders$directory), "\n")
}
```

## 10. The four figures of the manuscript

```{r fx-fig-main-figures}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS - | support code (no analysis)
#   the four main figures, each merged from finished figures with patchwork
# ==========================================================================================
# The manuscript carries four figures. Each is a page-sized stack of figures this document
# has already drawn, merged with patchwork at the full column width. The arrangement
# follows the figure plan of the Cell Reports manuscript the user works from (overview;
# host phylogeny and diversity; trees and host breadth; predicted traits), with the
# developmental-stage figure in the place of its clustering figure. Which figures go
# into which, in what row and under what panel letter, is the `main_figures` section of
# the config: change it there. Panels sharing a row are set side by side. A panel that
# carries its own letters (the overview's A-F, the heatmaps' letters) is given none.
# This runs after the folder step, because Part 1's figures reach their analysis folders
# only then. The finished figures are read back as images: Part 1 keeps no plot objects.
# In the supplementary set, figures that carry one message are joined into one figure in
# the same way (config `supplementary_figures`); the letters of a figure joined under
# another are set where it is drawn. The supplementary set holds figures only for data that
# no main figure shows: composition, and the trait and plant-growth-promotion tests, have
# main panels and so no supplementary figure. Their component figures stay in the
# analysis folders.
compose_main_figures <- function(results_dir, folders_dir, settings) {
    root <- file.path(results_dir, folders_dir)
    out_dir <- file.path(root, settings$directory)
    dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
    find_panel <- function(file) {
        hits <- list.files(root, recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
        hits <- hits[basename(hits) == file & dirname(hits) != out_dir]
        if (length(hits) == 1) hits else NA_character_
    }
    purrr::imap(settings$figures, function(panels, name) {
        panels <- tibble::as_tibble(panels)
        if (!"tag" %in% names(panels)) panels$tag <- NA_character_
        # a letter is set bold or plain to match the letters its neighbours already carry
        if (!"tag_face" %in% names(panels)) panels$tag_face <- NA_character_
        paths <- vapply(panels$file, find_panel, character(1))
        if (anyNA(paths)) {
            message("SKIP ", name, " - not found exactly once: ",
                    paste(panels$file[is.na(paths)], collapse = ", "))
            return(tibble(figure = name, status = "skipped",
                          panels = paste(panels$file, collapse = " + "), height_in = NA_real_))
        }
        images <- lapply(paths, magick::image_read)
        # Space: white bands running the full width of a panel are cut back, so that the
        # panels follow one another closely: the bands above and below a panel to
        # `trim_margin_in`, and a band inside it (between a plot and its key, or between two
        # of its rows) to `max_gap_in` (config). No row holding ink is removed, and the width
        # is left alone, which keeps the type of every panel at the size it was drawn.
        squeeze <- function(image) {
            info <- magick::image_info(image)
            grey <- magick::image_data(magick::image_scale(image, "x900"), "gray")
            inked <- apply(matrix(as.integer(grey[1, , ]), nrow = dim(grey)[2]) < 250, 2, any)   # one value per row
            if (!any(inked)) return(image)
            dpi <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sub("x.*$", "", info$density)))
            if (is.na(dpi) || dpi < 72) dpi <- info$width / settings$width_in
            per_row <- info$height / length(inked)
            runs <- rle(inked)
            last <- cumsum(runs$lengths)
            first <- last - runs$lengths + 1
            keep <- rep(TRUE, info$height)
            for (k in which(!runs$values)) {
                at_top <- k == 1
                at_bottom <- k == length(runs$values)
                allowed <- if (at_top || at_bottom) settings$trim_margin_in else settings$max_gap_in
                if (is.null(allowed)) next
                # the band in rows of the full-size image, one scaled row short of the ink
                from <- if (at_top) 1 else floor(first[k] * per_row) + 1
                to <- if (at_bottom) info$height else floor((last[k] - 1) * per_row)
                surplus <- (to - from + 1) - round(allowed * dpi)
                if (surplus <= 0) next
                start <- if (at_top) from else if (at_bottom) to - surplus + 1 else from + (to - from + 1 - surplus) %/% 2
                keep[start:(start + surplus - 1)] <- FALSE
            }
            if (all(keep)) return(image)
            kept <- rle(keep)
            ends <- cumsum(kept$lengths)
            parts <- lapply(which(kept$values), function(s) magick::image_crop(
                image, magick::geometry_area(info$width, kept$lengths[s], 0, ends[s] - kept$lengths[s])))
            magick::image_append(do.call(c, parts), stack = TRUE)
        }
        if (!is.null(settings$trim_margin_in) || !is.null(settings$max_gap_in)) images <- lapply(images, squeeze)
        size <- do.call(rbind, lapply(images, magick::image_info))
        aspect <- size$width / size$height
        # panels sharing a `row` sit side by side, each as wide as makes them equally tall
        if (!"row" %in% names(panels)) panels$row <- NA_integer_
        panels$row <- ifelse(is.na(panels$row), 1000L + seq_len(nrow(panels)), panels$row)
        row_id <- match(panels$row, unique(panels$row))
        drawn <- purrr::pmap(list(images, panels$tag, panels$tag_face), function(image, tag, face) {
            ggplot() +
                annotation_custom(grid::rasterGrob(grDevices::as.raster(image), interpolate = TRUE,
                                                   width = unit(1, "npc"), height = unit(1, "npc"))) +
                labs(tag = if (is.na(tag)) NULL else panel_letter(tag)) +
                theme_void() +
                theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = if (is.na(face)) "bold" else face, size = 8,
                                              hjust = 0, vjust = 1),
                      plot.tag.position = c(0.008, 0.992), plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
        })
        heights <- vapply(split(aspect, row_id), function(a) settings$width_in / sum(a), numeric(1))
        # Each row is a patchwork nested in the column of rows. Wrapped as an element
        # instead, a row kept a margin of its own, which left 0.15 in between the panels.
        rows <- lapply(unique(row_id), function(r) {
            patchwork::wrap_plots(drawn[row_id == r], nrow = 1, widths = aspect[row_id == r])
        })
        # no margin round the rows: the space between panels is what the squeezing left
        merged <- patchwork::wrap_plots(rows, ncol = 1, heights = heights) &
            theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
        ggsave(file.path(out_dir, paste0(name, ".tiff")), merged, width = settings$width_in,
               height = sum(heights), dpi = settings$dpi,
               device = if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) ragg::agg_tiff else "tiff",
               compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
        # Ready to insert: the white round the finished figure is cropped on all four sides,
        # leaving a hair's breadth (config `crop_border_in`). The figure is then a little
        # narrower than the column; its size is recorded with it.
        size_in <- c(width = settings$width_in, height = sum(heights))
        if (!is.null(settings$crop_border_in)) {
            file <- file.path(out_dir, paste0(name, ".tiff"))
            border <- round(settings$crop_border_in * settings$dpi)
            cropped <- magick::image_border(magick::image_trim(magick::image_read(file)), "white",
                                            sprintf("%dx%d", border, border))
            magick::image_write(cropped, file, format = "tiff", compression = "LZW",
                                density = sprintf("%dx%d", settings$dpi, settings$dpi))
            size_in <- unlist(magick::image_info(cropped)[c("width", "height")]) / settings$dpi
        }
        message("OK   ", name)
        tibble(figure = name,
               status = if (size_in[["height"]] > settings$max_height_in) "written, taller than a page" else "written",
               panels = paste(panels$file, collapse = " + "), height_in = round(size_in[["height"]], 2),
               width_in = round(size_in[["width"]], 2))
    }) |> purrr::list_rbind() |>
        # main_figures.csv or supplementary_figures.csv, after the folder
        readr::write_csv(file.path(out_dir, paste0(sub("^[0-9]+_", "", settings$directory), ".csv")))
}

if (is.null(config$main_figures) || is.null(config$analysis_folders)) {
    cat("Main figures: skipped, no `main_figures` section in the config\n")
} else if (!requireNamespace("magick", quietly = TRUE)) {
    cat("Main figures: skipped, the magick package is not installed\n")
} else {
    main_figures <- compose_main_figures(RESULTS, config$analysis_folders$directory, config$main_figures)
    print(as.data.frame(main_figures), row.names = FALSE)
    # the supplementary figures are numbered and gathered the same way, into their own folder
    if (!is.null(config$supplementary_figures)) {
        supplementary_figures <- compose_main_figures(RESULTS, config$analysis_folders$directory,
                                                      config$supplementary_figures)
        print(as.data.frame(supplementary_figures), row.names = FALSE)
    }
}
```



# Part 3 — Manuscript audit figures

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## About this part
Fig 1–4 of the manuscript, as corrected by the 2026-08-04 audit. Fig 1 and Fig 2a are
recomputed from the aligned raw inputs; Fig 2b/2c, 3 and 4 are read from the audit's
tables of record so the panels show published values rather than a fresh permutation
run. The `Validation` section at the end reconciles every recomputed quantity.

The recomputation behind those tables is `validation/verify_manuscript.py`, which
reimplements the statistics independently of Part 1 — that is deliberate, so agreement
between them is evidence rather than tautology. Do not refactor the two to share code.
:::

```{r ms-run-validation}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 9 | Software, statistics and validation
#   validation: optionally rerun validation/verify_manuscript.py
# ==========================================================================================
# Optionally regenerate the audit tables before drawing Fig 1-4. Guarded the same way
# the Python pipeline guards its R step: if the interpreter or script is missing, the
# existing tables are used and the render continues.
run_validation <- isTRUE(as.logical(if (exists("params")) params$run_validation else FALSE))
validation_script <- file.path(base_dir, "validation", "verify_manuscript.py")

if (run_validation) {
    python_bin <- Sys.which("python3")
    if (nzchar(python_bin) && file.exists(validation_script)) {
        message("running ", validation_script)
        status <- system2(python_bin, c(shQuote(validation_script),
                                        "--config", shQuote(config_path)))
        message("verify_manuscript.py exit status: ", status)
    } else {
        message("skipping validation run - python3 or verify_manuscript.py not found")
    }
} else {
    message("run_validation is FALSE - using the audit tables already on disk")
}
```


## What this document does

Regenerates the four corrected figures from the manuscript audit in R. Panels
are built from two kinds of input:

- **Recomputed from raw data** (`asv_sparse.npz`, `metadata_aligned.csv`,
  `taxonomy_aligned.csv`): the filtering cascade, phylum/genus composition
  (Fig 1) and per-sample Shannon (Fig 2a).
- **Read from the audit's result tables** (`TableS1`–`TableS3`, the PERMANOVA /
  PERMDISP files): effect sizes (Fig 2b, 2c), beta diversity (Fig 3) and
  indicator taxa (Fig 4). These are the tables of record, so the figures show
  the published values rather than a fresh permutation run.

The `Validation` section at the end compares every recomputed quantity against
the audit tables.

```{r ms-setup}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 9 | Software, statistics and validation
#   validation: setup; sets MS_READY
# ==========================================================================================
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
library(forcats)
library(patchwork)
library(Matrix)
library(ggtext)

library(jsonlite)

# Paths come from analysis_config.json, resolved relative to the config file --
# the same contract phyloseq_analysis.qmd and validation/verify_manuscript.py use.
resolve_path <- function(base_dir, configured_path) {
  if (startsWith(configured_path, "/")) {
    return(configured_path)
  }
  normalizePath(file.path(base_dir, configured_path), mustWork = FALSE)
}

config_path <- if (exists("params") && !is.null(params$config)) {
  params$config
} else {
  "analysis_config.json"
}
if (!file.exists(config_path)) {
  stop("Configuration file not found: ", config_path)
}
config <- fromJSON(config_path)
base_dir <- dirname(normalizePath(config_path))

# Everything this notebook reads and writes lives under <outputs.directory>/validation,
# produced by: python3 validation/verify_manuscript.py --config <config>
VALID <- file.path(resolve_path(base_dir, config$outputs$directory), "validation")
DATA  <- VALID                                       # aligned raw inputs
SUPP  <- file.path(VALID, "supplementary")           # audit tables of record
OUT   <- file.path(VALID, "figures_R")               # regenerated PNGs land here
dir.create(OUT, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

MS_READY <- all(dir.exists(c(DATA, SUPP)))
if (!MS_READY) {
  message("Part 3 skipped - missing ", paste(c(DATA, SUPP)[!dir.exists(c(DATA, SUPP))],
                                             collapse = ", "),
          "\n  populate it with: python3 validation/verify_manuscript.py --config ",
          config_path, "\n  or re-render with -P run_validation:true")
}

# Palette matched to the Python originals.
RED   <- "#DC0000"   # seed-enriched / stage / recomputed-correct
BLUE  <- "#2166AC"   # seedling-enriched / other
PURPL <- "#6A3D9A"   # batch / provenance
GREY  <- "#6E6E6E"   # annotation text, as-published values
INK   <- "#1A1A1A"

theme_fig <- function(base_size = 9) {
  theme_classic(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = rel(1.05), hjust = 0, colour = INK,
                                margin = margin(b = 6)),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      plot.tag = element_text(size = rel(1.3), face = "bold"),
      axis.text = element_text(colour = INK),
      axis.title = element_text(colour = INK),
      axis.line = element_line(colour = INK, linewidth = 0.4),
      axis.ticks = element_line(colour = INK, linewidth = 0.4),
      legend.background = element_blank(),
      legend.key.height = unit(10, "pt"),
      legend.title = element_blank(),
      plot.margin = margin(6, 10, 6, 6)
    )
}
theme_set(theme_fig())

save_fig <- function(plot, file, width, height) {
  ggsave(file.path(OUT, file), plot, width = width, height = height,
         dpi = 300, bg = "white")
}
```

## Load raw data

`asv_sparse.npz` is a SciPy CSR checkpoint. Rather than add a Python
dependency, the two functions below read the `.npy` members directly: an
`.npy` file is a short ASCII header (dtype, shape) followed by a raw
little-endian buffer.

```{r ms-read-npz, eval = MS_READY}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 9 | Software, statistics and validation
#   validation: load the audit's raw data
# ==========================================================================================
read_npy <- function(path) {
  con <- file(path, "rb"); on.exit(close(con))
  stopifnot(identical(readBin(con, "raw", 6),
                      as.raw(c(0x93, 0x4e, 0x55, 0x4d, 0x50, 0x59))))
  ver  <- readBin(con, "integer", 2, size = 1)
  hlen <- if (ver[1] == 1) readBin(con, "integer", 1, size = 2, signed = FALSE)
          else             readBin(con, "integer", 1, size = 4)
  hdr  <- rawToChar(readBin(con, "raw", hlen))

  descr <- sub(".*'descr': *'([^']+)'.*", "\\1", hdr)
  shp   <- sub(".*'shape': *\\(([^)]*)\\).*", "\\1", hdr)
  dims  <- as.numeric(regmatches(shp, gregexpr("[0-9]+", shp))[[1]])
  n     <- if (length(dims) == 0) 1 else prod(dims)

  switch(descr,
    "<i4" = readBin(con, "integer", n, size = 4),
    # readBin has no 8-byte integer: read hi/lo words and assert the high
    # word is empty (all values here are well under 2^31).
    "<i8" = { w <- readBin(con, "integer", 2 * n, size = 4)
              stopifnot(all(w[c(FALSE, TRUE)] == 0))
              w[c(TRUE, FALSE)] },
    stop("unsupported dtype: ", descr)
  )
}

read_npz_csr <- function(path) {
  dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "npz"); unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE)
  unzip(path, exdir = dir)
  indptr <- read_npy(file.path(dir, "indptr.npy"))
  shape  <- read_npy(file.path(dir, "shape.npy"))
  sparseMatrix(i = rep.int(seq_len(shape[1]), diff(indptr)),
               j = read_npy(file.path(dir, "indices.npy")) + 1L,
               x = as.numeric(read_npy(file.path(dir, "data.npy"))),
               dims = shape)
}

X   <- read_npz_csr(file.path(DATA, "asv_sparse.npz"))
md  <- read_csv(file.path(DATA, "metadata_aligned.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
tax <- read_csv(file.path(DATA, "taxonomy_aligned.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

# Rows of X are aligned to md, columns to tax (both written out pre-aligned).
stopifnot(nrow(md) == nrow(X), nrow(tax) == ncol(X))
c(samples = nrow(X), features = ncol(X), reads = sum(X))
```

## Filtering cascade

Reproduces steps 1–10 of `TableS5`. Order matters: soil samples are dropped
**before** the library-size floor, so the 1,886 retained samples are already
plant-only.

```{r ms-cascade, eval = MS_READY}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 9 | Software, statistics and validation
#   validation: filtering cascade recomputed
# ==========================================================================================
blank_na <- function(v) ifelse(is.na(v), "", v)

fmask <- blank_na(tax$Kingdom) == "Bacteria" &
         blank_na(tax$Order)   != "Chloroplast" &
         blank_na(tax$Family)  != "Mitochondria" &
         !blank_na(tax$Phyla) %in% c("Cyanobacteria", "Cyanobacteriota")

smask <- md$Developmental_Stage != "soil"                      # 48 soil samples
smask <- smask & rowSums(X[, fmask, drop = FALSE]) >= 500      # min_library_size

# Feature filters apply to the surviving columns; lift the predicate back to
# full-matrix positions each time.
lift <- function(pred) {
  out <- logical(ncol(X)); out[which(fmask)[pred]] <- TRUE; out
}
S <- X[smask, fmask, drop = FALSE]; fmask <- lift(colSums(S) > 0)
S <- X[smask, fmask, drop = FALSE]; fmask <- lift(colSums(S > 0) >= 3)
S <- X[smask, fmask, drop = FALSE]; fmask <- lift(colSums(S) >= 10)

# Cap at the 2,000 most abundant features. Five features tie at 220 reads for
# the last three slots, so this cut is NOT uniquely defined -- tie order
# changes which features are kept and therefore the prevalence counts of
# low-abundance phyla. Ties are broken by feature index for determinism.
S  <- X[smask, fmask, drop = FALSE]
ts <- colSums(S)
fmask <- lift(order(-ts, seq_along(ts))[1:2000])

Xf   <- as.matrix(X[smask, fmask, drop = FALSE])
mdf  <- md[smask, ]
taxf <- tax[fmask, ]
c(samples = nrow(Xf), features = ncol(Xf), reads = sum(Xf))
```

```{r ms-aggregate, eval = MS_READY}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 9 | Software, statistics and validation
#   validation: aggregate to genus
# ==========================================================================================
# Sum feature columns within a taxonomic rank; blank/NA -> "Unassigned".
agg_rank <- function(counts, rank_values) {
  g <- blank_na(rank_values); g[g == ""] <- "Unassigned"
  t(rowsum(t(counts), g))
}

phylum_counts <- agg_rank(Xf, taxf$Phyla)
genus_counts  <- agg_rank(Xf, taxf$Genus)
```

## Figure 1 — Composition

```{r ms-fig1-data, eval = MS_READY}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 9 | Software, statistics and validation
#   validation: composition recomputed
# ==========================================================================================
# (a) per-sample relative abundance by phylum
phy_rel <- phylum_counts / pmax(rowSums(phylum_counts), 1)
phy <- tibble(
  phylum     = colnames(phy_rel),
  mean_rel   = colMeans(phy_rel),
  median_rel = apply(phy_rel, 2, median),
  prevalence = colSums(phy_rel > 0) / nrow(phy_rel)
) |>
  dplyr::filter(phylum != "Unassigned") |>
  slice_max(mean_rel, n = 6) |>
  # label sits clear of whichever marker extends further right
  mutate(phylum = fct_reorder(phylum, mean_rel),
         label_x = pmax(mean_rel, median_rel))

# (b) genus read totals. "Seed-enriched" is derived, not asserted: a genus is
# seed-side if its significant indicator ASVs are mostly Seeds-side (TableS3).
s3 <- read_csv(file.path(SUPP, "TableS3_indicator_taxa.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
seed_side <- s3 |>
  dplyr::filter(q_BH < 0.05) |>
  dplyr::count(Genus, group) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  dplyr::filter(Seeds > Seedlings) |>
  pull(Genus)

gen <- tibble(
  genus      = colnames(genus_counts),
  total      = colSums(genus_counts),
  prevalence = colSums(genus_counts > 0)
) |>
  dplyr::filter(genus != "Unassigned") |>
  slice_max(total, n = 8) |>
  mutate(direction = if_else(genus %in% seed_side, "seed-enriched", "other"),
         genus = fct_reorder(genus, total))

top3_pct <- round(100 * sum(sort(gen$total, decreasing = TRUE)[1:3]) / sum(Xf))
```

## Figure 2 — Alpha diversity

```{r ms-fig2-data, eval = MS_READY}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 9 | Software, statistics and validation
#   validation: alpha diversity recomputed
# ==========================================================================================
# (a) per-sample Shannon on the 2,000-feature matrix. Three samples have all
# their reads outside the cap; Shannon is undefined there and they are dropped
# (scoring them 0 is what inflates the published H to 38.2 at n = 1,886).
depth <- rowSums(Xf)
prop  <- Xf / pmax(depth, 1)
shannon <- -rowSums(ifelse(prop > 0, prop * log(prop), 0))
shannon[depth == 0] <- NA_real_

alpha <- tibble(stage = mdf$Developmental_Stage, shannon = shannon) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(shannon)) |>
  mutate(stage = factor(stage, c("Seeds", "Seedlings")))

s1 <- read_csv(file.path(SUPP, "TableS1_alpha_diversity.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
kw <- s1 |> dplyr::filter(variable == "Developmental_Stage", metric == "Shannon")

# (b) Kruskal-Wallis effect sizes, Shannon. Display order puts developmental
# stage first (the paper's focus), then the remaining variables ascending.
eps <- s1 |>
  dplyr::filter(metric == "Shannon") |>
  transmute(variable, epsilon_sq,
            label = recode(variable,
              Developmental_Stage = "Developmental\nstage", Family = "Plant family",
              Scientific_Name = "Host species", Cultivar = "Cultivar",
              Author = "Author", study_alias = "Study"),
            class = case_when(
              variable == "Developmental_Stage" ~ "stage",
              variable %in% c("study_alias", "Author") ~ "batch / provenance",
              TRUE ~ "host biology")) |>
  mutate(label = factor(label, rev(c("Developmental\nstage", "Plant family",
                                     "Host species", "Cultivar", "Author", "Study"))),
         class = factor(class, c("stage", "host biology", "batch / provenance")))

# floor, not round: the published panel states 13x (0.254 / 0.019 = 13.5)
stage_ratio <- floor(max(eps$epsilon_sq) / eps$epsilon_sq[eps$class == "stage"])

# (c) stage coefficient under increasing control
s2 <- read_csv(file.path(SUPP, "TableS2_alpha_depth_models.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::filter(metric == "Shannon") |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, unique(model),
                        labels = c("stage\nonly", "+ depth", "+ depth\n+ study",
                                   "+ depth\n+ study\n+ species")),
         lo = stage_beta - 1.96 * se, hi = stage_beta + 1.96 * se)

shrink <- round(100 * (1 - dplyr::last(s2$stage_beta) / dplyr::first(s2$stage_beta)))
```

```{r ms-fig2, fig.width=7.48, fig.height=3.05, eval = MS_READY}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 9 | Software, statistics and validation
#   validation: audit figure 2
# ==========================================================================================
n_lab <- dplyr::count(alpha, stage)

# p in mantissa/exponent form, taken from TableS1 rather than retyped
p_exp <- floor(log10(kw$p))
p_lab <- sprintf("H = %.1f, p = %.1f×10<sup>%d</sup>",
                 kw$H, kw$p / 10^p_exp, p_exp)

set.seed(42)   # reproducible jitter
p2a <- ggplot(alpha, aes(stage, shannon, colour = stage)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.24, height = 0, size = 0.3, alpha = 0.25) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, fun.min = mean, fun.max = mean, geom = "errorbar",
               width = 0.5, linewidth = 1.1, colour = INK) +
  annotate("text", x = seq_len(nrow(n_lab)), y = 5.5,

  annotate("segment", x = 1, xend = 2, y = 4.9, yend = 4.9,
           colour = INK, linewidth = 0.4) +
  # vjust/padding pinned: richtext padding otherwise floats the label upward
  annotate("richtext", x = 1.5, y = 5.12, label.colour = NA, fill = NA,
           label.padding = unit(rep(0, 4), "pt"), vjust = 0.5, hjust = 0.5,
           size = 2.9, colour = INK, label = p_lab) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Seeds = RED, Seedlings = BLUE), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 5.65), breaks = 0:5) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Stage difference is real but small\n(ε² = %.3f)",
                       kw$epsilon_sq),
       x = NULL, y = "Shannon diversity")

p2b <- ggplot(eps, aes(epsilon_sq, label, colour = class)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = epsilon_sq, yend = label), linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", epsilon_sq),
                colour = if_else(class == "host biology", "grey", as.character(class))),
            hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.008, size = 2.9, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(stage = RED, `host biology` = BLUE,
                                 `batch / provenance` = PURPL, grey = GREY),
                      breaks = c("stage", "host biology", "batch / provenance")) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 0.34), breaks = seq(0, 0.3, 0.1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Study identity explains %d× more\nvariance than stage", stage_ratio),
       x = "Kruskal–Wallis ε²  (variance explained)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "inside", legend.position.inside = c(0.99, 0.86),
        legend.justification = c(1, 0.5), legend.text = element_text(size = 7))

p2c <- ggplot(s2, aes(model, stage_beta)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", colour = INK) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), colour = RED,
                  linewidth = 0.6, size = 0.45) +
  geom_text(data = dplyr::slice(s2, c(1, n())),
            aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", stage_beta)),
            colour = RED, size = 2.9, hjust = c(0, 1),
            nudge_x = c(-0.4, -0.12), nudge_y = c(-0.062, 0.064)) +
  annotate("text", x = 4.4, y = -0.255, label = "95% CI", colour = GREY,
           size = 2.8, hjust = 1) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Effect shrinks %d%% once depth and\nstudy are controlled", shrink),
       x = NULL, y = "Seedling − seed Shannon (β)")

fig2 <- p2a + p2b + p2c + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
fig2
save_fig(fig2, "fig2_alpha_R.png", 7.48, 3.05)
```

## Figure 3 — Beta diversity

All three panels read the audit's PERMANOVA / PERMDISP outputs. The key point
is the basis: the manuscript's Table 4 values reproduce on **ASV-level raw
counts at n = 1,553**, not the genus-level relative abundances at n = 1,883
that the caption claims.

```{r ms-fig3-data, eval = MS_READY}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 9 | Software, statistics and validation
#   validation: beta diversity from the tables of record
# ==========================================================================================
TERMS <- c("Developmental_Stage", "study_alias", "Author",
           "Scientific_Name", "Cultivar")   # published panel order, top to bottom
TERM_LAB <- c(Developmental_Stage = "Developmental\nstage", study_alias = "Study",
              Author = "Author", Scientific_Name = "Host species",
              Cultivar = "Cultivar")

as_term <- function(x) factor(TERM_LAB[x], rev(unname(TERM_LAB[TERMS])))

uni <- read_csv(file.path(SUPP, "permanova_univariate_recomputed.csv"),
                show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(basis = if_else(str_detect(basis, "^ASV"), "asv", "genus"),
         term = as_term(term))

marg <- read_csv(file.path(SUPP, "permanova_marginal_recomputed.csv"),
                 show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::filter(basis == "ASV top100 raw") |>
  mutate(term = as_term(term))

disp <- read_csv(file.path(SUPP, "permdisp_recomputed.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(basis = if_else(str_detect(basis, "^ASV"), "asv", "genus"),
         term = as_term(term))

# (b) univariate vs marginal for the three terms that share a model
pan_b <- marg |>
  transmute(term, marginal = R2) |>
  left_join(uni |> dplyr::filter(basis == "asv") |> transmute(term, univariate = R2),
            by = "term") |>
  pivot_longer(c(univariate, marginal), names_to = "model", values_to = "R2") |>
  mutate(term = factor(term, c("Study", "Developmental\nstage", "Host species"),
                       labels = c("Study", "Stage", "Host\nspecies")),
         model = factor(model, c("univariate", "marginal"),
                        labels = c("univariate (as published)", "marginal (adjusted)")))

stage_drop <- pan_b |>
  dplyr::filter(term == "Stage") |>
  summarise(x = R2[str_starts(model, "univariate")] /
                R2[str_starts(model, "marginal")]) |>
  pull(x) |> round(1)
stage_gap  <- uni |> dplyr::filter(term == "Developmental\nstage") |>
  dplyr::select(basis, R2) |> deframe()
disp_genus <- disp |> dplyr::filter(basis == "genus", term == "Developmental\nstage")
```

```{r ms-fig3, fig.width=7.92, fig.height=3.11, eval = MS_READY}

dumbbell <- function(d, value, xlab, xlim) {

    geom_line(aes(group = term), colour = "#B8C4CE", linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = basis, colour = basis, fill = basis),

    scale_shape_manual(values = c(asv = 21, genus = 22)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(asv = RED, genus = BLUE)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(asv = RED, genus = "transparent")) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = xlim) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = NULL)
}

# legend keys for panel (a): which basis each marker represents
BASIS_LAB <- c(asv = "ASV-level, raw counts\n(reproduces Table 4)",
               genus = "genus-level, relative\n(what caption claims)")

  scale_colour_manual(values = c(asv = RED, genus = BLUE), labels = BASIS_LAB) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(asv = RED, genus = "transparent"),
                    labels = BASIS_LAB) +
  labs(title = "Reported values came from ASV-level\ndistances, not genus-level") +
  theme(legend.position = "inside", legend.position.inside = c(0, 0.2),
        legend.justification = c(0, 0.5),
        legend.key.height = unit(20, "pt"), legend.key.width = unit(8, "pt"),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 5.6))

p3b <- ggplot(pan_b, aes(term, R2, fill = model)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.68) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", R2),
                colour = model == "marginal (adjusted)"),
```

## Figure 4 — Indicator taxa

```{r ms-fig4-data, eval = MS_READY}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 9 | Software, statistics and validation
#   validation: indicator taxa from the tables of record
# ==========================================================================================
sig <- dplyr::filter(s3, q_BH < 0.05)

# Named in the manuscript's indicator-taxa claims, with the direction the text
# reports. Panel (a) shows that four of the six carry significant ASVs in both
# directions, so a single reported direction is not supportable.
NAMED <- tribble(
  ~Genus,            ~reported,
  "Pantoea",         "seedling",
  "Enterobacter",    "seedling",
  "Kosakonia",       "seedling",
  "Pseudomonas",     "seedling",
  "Exiguobacterium", "seed",
  "Erwinia",         "seed"
)

counts <- sig |>
  dplyr::filter(Genus %in% NAMED$Genus) |>
  dplyr::count(Genus, group) |>
  complete(Genus, group, fill = list(n = 0)) |>
  mutate(signed = if_else(group == "Seeds", -n, n),
         Genus = factor(Genus, rev(NAMED$Genus)))

arrows <- NAMED |>
  mutate(Genus = factor(Genus, rev(NAMED$Genus)),
         glyph = if_else(reported == "seedling", "→", "←"))

# Several genera appear more than once, so rank (not genus) is the y position;
# duplicate factor labels would otherwise be merged into one level.
top12 <- sig |>
  slice_max(indval, n = 12) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(indval)) |>
  mutate(rank = row_number(), y = factor(rank, levels = rev(rank)))

top12_labels <- setNames(top12$Genus, as.character(top12$rank))

both_ways <- counts |> group_by(Genus) |> dplyr::filter(all(n > 0)) |> n_groups()
```

```{r ms-fig4, fig.width=7.04, fig.height=3.16, eval = MS_READY}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 9 | Software, statistics and validation
#   validation: audit figure 4
# ==========================================================================================
```

## Validation

Recomputed values against the audit's tables of record.

```{r ms-validate, eval = MS_READY}
# ==========================================================================================
# METHODS 9 | Software, statistics and validation
#   validation: reconcile recomputed values with the tables of record
# ==========================================================================================
s5 <- read_csv(file.path(SUPP, "TableS5_filtering_accounting.csv"),
               show_col_types = FALSE) |> slice_tail(n = 1)

kw_r <- kruskal.test(shannon ~ stage, data = alpha)

checks <- tribble(
  ~quantity,                        ~recomputed,                  ~audit,
  "samples retained",               nrow(Xf),                     s5$n_samples,
  "features retained",              ncol(Xf),                     s5$n_features,
  "reads retained",                 sum(Xf),                      s5$total_reads,
  "Shannon n (stage test)",         nrow(alpha),                  kw$n_samples,
  "Proteobacteria prevalence (n)",  sum(phy_rel[, "Proteobacteria"] > 0), 1770L,
  "Pantoea total reads",            max(colSums(genus_counts[, "Pantoea", drop = FALSE])), 4468686L
) |>
  mutate(across(c(recomputed, audit), as.numeric),
         agrees = recomputed == audit)

knitr::kable(checks)

tibble(statistic = "Kruskal-Wallis H (Shannon ~ stage)",
       recomputed = round(unname(kw_r$statistic), 3),
       audit_TableS1 = kw$H) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

**On the H discrepancy.** The recomputed H differs from `TableS1` in the third
decimal (36.354 vs 36.357). The cause is the tie at the 2,000-feature cut
documented in the cascade chunk: five features tie at 220 reads for three
slots, so the retained feature set — and every per-sample Shannon value
computed from it — depends on sort order. The same tie makes Actinobacteriota
prevalence 937 under index-order tie-breaking (the value the manuscript
reports) and 940 under NumPy's unstable `argsort` (the value the audit script
comments). Neither figure annotation is affected at the precision shown, but
the cap should be made explicitly deterministic in the pipeline.

master document holds the whole project's content — but none of it runs, deliberately:

  They reference `Data/` paths, `alpha_df`, `all_dunn_results`, `TreatmentCode.x` and
  `attach()` on objects that do not exist here. Executing them fails immediately.

- `seedling_meta_analysis.qmd` (Part 4) duplicates Part 1's analyses in an earlier form.
- Part 9 holds library tutorials and a reveal.js deck — a different output format entirely.

Parts 1–3 are the live analysis. To revive anything below, lift the chunk out and adapt it
to this repo's schema (`run_accession`, `Developmental_Stage`, `Datesets/`) first.

### Overview

This document consolidates the overlapping logic from the imported strawberry `.qmd` analyses into a single workflow adapted to the local repository data in `Datesets/`.

The merged workflow covers:

- sample metadata inspection
- construction of a count matrix aligned to metadata and taxonomy
- taxonomic composition summaries
- alpha diversity analysis
- beta diversity ordination and PERMANOVA
- tree-based alpha and beta diversity using `Datesets/tree.nexus`

### Load Data

```{r sma-load-data, eval = FALSE}
metadata_raw <- readr::read_csv("Datesets/metadata.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
counts_raw <- readr::read_csv("Datesets/asv-counts.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
taxonomy_raw <- readr::read_csv("Datesets/taxa.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
tree_raw <- ape::read.nexus("Datesets/tree.nexus")

if (inherits(tree_raw, "multiPhylo")) {
  tree_raw <- tree_raw[[1]]
}

if (names(metadata_raw)[2] == "") {
  names(metadata_raw)[2] <- "blank_column"
}

metadata <- metadata_raw %>%
  rename(sample_id = run_accession) %>%
  select(sample_id, everything()) %>%
  distinct(sample_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# align samples and metadata
sample_ids <- intersect(metadata$sample_id, counts_raw[[1]])
counts_filtered <- counts_raw %>%
  filter(sample_id %in% sample_ids)

count_matrix <- counts_filtered %>%
  dplyr::select(-sample_id) %>%
  as.matrix()
rownames(count_matrix) <- counts_filtered$sample_id
storage.mode(count_matrix) <- "numeric"

feature_ids <- colnames(count_matrix)
tree_feature_ids <- intersect(feature_ids, tree_raw$tip.label)

metadata <- metadata %>%
  filter(sample_id %in% rownames(count_matrix))

taxonomy <- taxonomy_raw %>%
  filter(OTUID %in% feature_ids)
taxonomy <- taxonomy %>%
  mutate(across(c(Kingdom:Species), ~replace_na(.x, "Unassigned")))

common_features <- intersect(colnames(count_matrix), tree_raw$tip.label)
if (length(common_features) == 0) {
  stop("No overlapping OTUs between counts and the tree.")
}

count_matrix <- count_matrix[, common_features, drop = FALSE]
taxonomy <- taxonomy[match(common_features, taxonomy$OTUID), ]
metadata <- metadata[match(rownames(count_matrix), metadata$sample_id), , drop = FALSE]

sample_totals <- rowSums(count_matrix)
keep_samples <- sample_totals > 0

count_matrix <- count_matrix[keep_samples, , drop = FALSE]
metadata <- metadata %>%
  filter(sample_id %in% rownames(count_matrix))

taxonomy <- taxonomy %>%
  filter(OTUID %in% colnames(count_matrix))

count_matrix <- count_matrix[, taxonomy$OTUID, drop = FALSE]
metadata <- metadata[match(rownames(count_matrix), metadata$sample_id), , drop = FALSE]
phylo_tree <- ape::keep.tip(tree_raw, colnames(count_matrix))

saveRDS(count_matrix, "analysis_outputs/objects/count_matrix.rds")
saveRDS(metadata, "analysis_outputs/objects/metadata.rds")
saveRDS(taxonomy, "analysis_outputs/objects/taxonomy.rds")
saveRDS(phylo_tree, "analysis_outputs/objects/phylo_tree.rds")

cat("Samples retained:", nrow(count_matrix), "\n")
cat("Features retained:", ncol(count_matrix), "\n")
cat("Metadata columns:", ncol(metadata), "\n")
cat("Tree tips retained:", length(phylo_tree$tip.label), "\n")

aggregate_by_rank <- function(mat, taxonomy_tbl, rank_col) {
  rank_vals <- taxonomy_tbl[[rank_col]]
  rank_vals[is.na(rank_vals) | rank_vals == ""] <- "Unassigned"
  levels <- unique(rank_vals)
  result <- matrix(
    0,
    nrow = nrow(mat),
    ncol = length(levels),
    dimnames = list(rownames(mat), levels)
  )
  for (lvl in levels) {
    cols <- which(rank_vals == lvl)
    if (length(cols) > 0) {
      result[, lvl] <- rowSums(mat[, cols, drop = FALSE])
    }
  }
  result
}
```

#### Alpha Diversity Statistics

```{r sma-alpha-stats, eval = FALSE}
run_kruskal <- function(df, metric, group_var) {
  subset_df <- df %>%
    select(all_of(c(metric, group_var))) %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[metric]]), !is.na(.data[[group_var]]))

  if (dplyr::n_distinct(subset_df[[group_var]]) < 2) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  test <- kruskal.test(stats::as.formula(paste(metric, "~", group_var)), data = subset_df)
  tibble::tibble(
    metric = metric,
    variable = group_var,
    statistic = unname(test$statistic),
    p_value = test$p.value
  )
}

alpha_stats <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson", "Evenness", "Faith_PD"), function(metric) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(categorical_group_vars, function(group_var) run_kruskal(alpha_df, metric, group_var)))
}))

readr::write_csv(alpha_stats, "analysis_outputs/tables/alpha_diversity_kruskal.csv")
knitr::kable(alpha_stats)
```

### Beta Diversity

```{r sma-beta-diversity, eval = FALSE}
relative_matrix <- sweep(count_matrix, 1, rowSums(count_matrix), "/")
relative_matrix[is.na(relative_matrix)] <- 0
presence_absence_matrix <- ifelse(count_matrix > 0, 1, 0)

bray_dist <- vegan::vegdist(relative_matrix, method = "bray")
jaccard_dist <- vegan::vegdist(presence_absence_matrix, method = "jaccard", binary = TRUE)
phylo_beta_features <- head(
  names(sort(colSums(count_matrix), decreasing = TRUE)),
  n = min(2000, ncol(count_matrix))
)
phylo_beta_matrix <- count_matrix[, phylo_beta_features, drop = FALSE]
phylo_beta_tree <- ape::keep.tip(phylo_tree, phylo_beta_features)
phylo_beta_dist <- GUniFrac::GUniFrac(phylo_beta_matrix, phylo_beta_tree, alpha = 0.5)$unifracs[, , "d_0.5"]

bray_pcoa <- cmdscale(bray_dist, eig = TRUE, k = 2)
jaccard_pcoa <- cmdscale(jaccard_dist, eig = TRUE, k = 2)
phylo_pcoa <- cmdscale(as.dist(phylo_beta_dist), eig = TRUE, k = 2)

bray_df <- metadata %>%
  mutate(
    Axis1 = bray_pcoa$points[, 1],
    Axis2 = bray_pcoa$points[, 2]
  )

jaccard_df <- metadata %>%
  mutate(
    Axis1 = jaccard_pcoa$points[, 1],
    Axis2 = jaccard_pcoa$points[, 2]
  )

phylo_df <- metadata %>%
  mutate(
    Axis1 = phylo_pcoa$points[, 1],
    Axis2 = phylo_pcoa$points[, 2]
  )
```

#### PERMANOVA

```{r sma-permanova, eval = FALSE}
run_permanova <- function(distance_object, metadata_df, group_var, distance_name) {
  subset_df <- metadata_df %>%
    select(sample_id, all_of(group_var)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[group_var]]))

  if (dplyr::n_distinct(subset_df[[group_var]]) < 2) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  sample_keep <- subset_df$sample_id
  subset_dist <- as.dist(as.matrix(distance_object)[sample_keep, sample_keep])
  subset_df <- subset_df[match(sample_keep, subset_df$sample_id), , drop = FALSE]
  formula <- stats::as.formula(paste("subset_dist ~", group_var))
  test <- vegan::adonis2(formula, data = subset_df)

  tibble::tibble(
    distance = distance_name,
    variable = group_var,
    df = test$Df[1],
    r2 = test$R2[1],
    f = test$F[1],
    p_value = test$`Pr(>F)`[1]
  )
}

permanova_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(categorical_group_vars, function(group_var) run_permanova(bray_dist, metadata, group_var, "bray")),
  lapply(categorical_group_vars, function(group_var) run_permanova(jaccard_dist, metadata, group_var, "jaccard")),
  lapply(categorical_group_vars, function(group_var) run_permanova(as.dist(phylo_beta_dist), metadata, group_var, "phylogenetic"))
)

readr::write_csv(permanova_results, "analysis_outputs/tables/permanova_results.csv")
knitr::kable(permanova_results)
```

### Project Scope

- `Developmental_Stage`

It does not assume strawberry-specific variables such as `TreatmentCode`, `EnvZone`, or `Management`.

### Build Analysis Objects

```{r pj1-build-objects, eval = FALSE}
metadata <- readr::read_csv("Datesets/metadata.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
counts <- readr::read_csv("Datesets/asv-counts.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
taxonomy <- readr::read_csv("Datesets/taxa.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
tree <- ape::read.nexus("Datesets/tree.nexus")

if (inherits(tree, "multiPhylo")) {
  tree <- tree[[1]]
}

if (names(metadata)[2] == "") {
  names(metadata)[2] <- "blank_column"
}

metadata <- metadata %>%
  rename(sample_id = run_accession) %>%
  select(-blank_column, -command_to_download_the_reads)

counts_long <- counts %>%
  rename(sample_id = 1) %>%
  pivot_longer(-sample_id, names_to = "OTUID", values_to = "Abundance") %>%
  mutate(Abundance = as.numeric(Abundance))

common_samples <- intersect(metadata$sample_id, unique(counts_long$sample_id))
common_features <- Reduce(intersect, list(unique(counts_long$OTUID), taxonomy$OTUID, tree$tip.label))

metadata <- metadata %>% filter(sample_id %in% common_samples)
taxonomy <- taxonomy %>% filter(OTUID %in% common_features)
counts_long <- counts_long %>% filter(sample_id %in% common_samples, OTUID %in% common_features)

count_matrix <- counts_long %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = OTUID, values_from = Abundance, values_fill = 0) %>%
  as.data.frame()

rownames(count_matrix) <- count_matrix$sample_id
count_matrix$sample_id <- NULL
count_matrix <- as.matrix(count_matrix)
storage.mode(count_matrix) <- "numeric"

count_matrix <- count_matrix[rowSums(count_matrix) > 0, , drop = FALSE]
metadata <- metadata[match(rownames(count_matrix), metadata$sample_id), , drop = FALSE]
tree <- ape::keep.tip(tree, colnames(count_matrix))

saveRDS(metadata, "analysis_outputs/objects/metadata_joined.rds")
saveRDS(taxonomy, "analysis_outputs/objects/taxonomy_joined.rds")
saveRDS(count_matrix, "analysis_outputs/objects/count_matrix_joined.rds")
saveRDS(tree, "analysis_outputs/objects/tree_joined.rds")

cat("Samples:", nrow(count_matrix), "\n")
cat("Features:", ncol(count_matrix), "\n")
cat("Metadata variables:", paste(names(metadata), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

#Filter data at 0.0025 prevalence
#Obtained from: https://f1000research.com/articles/5-1492/v1;#One of the reasons to filter by prevalence is to avoid spending #much time analyzing taxa that were only rarely seen. This also turns out to be a useful filter of noise (taxa that are #actually just artifacts of the data collection process)
### Define prevalence of each taxa; # (in how many samples did each taxa appear at least once)

```{r pj2-c2, echo = FALSE,warning = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
load("phyloseq-objects/ps.RData")

prev0 = apply(X = otu_table(ps),
              MARGIN = ifelse(taxa_are_rows(ps), yes = 1, no = 2),
              FUN = function(x){sum(x > 0)})

prevdf = data.frame(Prevalence = prev0,
                    TotalAbundance = taxa_sums(ps),
                    tax_table(ps))# the most prevalent ASVs present therein the composition

#only for reference, in case we want to filter Phylum that appear less than X times
keepPhylum = table(prevdf$Phylum)[(table(prevdf$Phylum) > 0)]

prevasv = subset(prevdf, Phylum %in% names(keepPhylum))

# Define prevalence threshold as 0.25% of total samples# 
prevalenceThreshold = 0.0025 * nsamples(ps)
prevalenceThreshold

# Execute prevalence filter, using `prune_taxa()` function
prevalence_filter_result <- (prev0 > prevalenceThreshold)
if(sum(prevalence_filter_result) == 0) {
  stop("Error: Prevalence filter would remove all taxa. Consider adjusting the prevalence threshold.")
}

ps1 = prune_taxa(prevalence_filter_result, ps);ps1

# Filter entries with unidentified Phylum.
ps2 = subset_taxa(ps1, Phylum %in% names(keepPhylum));ps2

#Plot prevalence of different Phylum
#https://github.com/joey711/phyloseq/issues/1474

print(paste0("Initial #ASVs:", ntaxa(ps), ". #ASVs after prevalence filtering:", ntaxa(ps2), ". #ASVs removed: ", ntaxa(ps)-ntaxa(ps2)))
```

### Rerefaction curves at different sampling depths and including the lost samples

```{r pj2-alpha-diversity-analysis, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval = FALSE}
# Load the phyloseq object, but only if it doesn't already exist
# Set working directory
setwd("/Users/expeditoolimi/Documents/TUG-schrodinger-Return/FOEKL/EXC_16S_FOE_KOB/Extensive-system-microbiome/")
load("phyloseq-objects/ps2.RData")
library(phyloseq)
library(ggplot2)
library(microbiome)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(FSA)
library(multcompView)
library(kableExtra)

# Define rarefaction depths
depths <- c(500, 1000,2500)

#colour pellets
my_palette <- c("500" = "grey35", "1000" = "#00AFBB", "2500" = "goldenrod")


# Initialize lists
alpha_list <- list()
lost_samples <- data.frame(Depth = integer(), Retained = integer(), Lost = integer())
lost_sample_names <- list()

# Rarefy and compute alpha diversity
alpha_list <- list()
ps <- ps2
total_samples <- nsamples(ps)

for (d in depths) {
  rarefied <- rarefy_even_depth(ps, sample.size = d, rngseed = 123, verbose = FALSE)
  
  retained_samples <- sample_names(rarefied)
  original_samples <- sample_names(ps)
  lost <- setdiff(original_samples, retained_samples)
  
  lost_samples <- rbind(lost_samples, data.frame(Depth = d, Retained = length(retained_samples), Lost = length(lost)))
  lost_sample_names[[as.character(d)]] <- lost
  
  alpha_df <- estimate_richness(rarefied, measures = c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson", "InvSimpson", "Chao1", "ACE"))
  alpha_df$Depth <- d
  alpha_df$SampleID <- rownames(alpha_df)
  alpha_list[[as.character(d)]] <- alpha_df
}

# Combine all alpha diversity dataframes
alpha_all <- do.call(rbind, alpha_list);alpha_all

# Reshape for ggplot (long format)
alpha_long <- alpha_all %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson", "InvSimpson", "Chao1", "ACE"),
               names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Value");alpha_long

# Function to compute significance letters
get_significance_letters <- function(df) {
  if (length(unique(df$Depth)) < 2 || nrow(df) < 2) return(data.frame())
  dunn_res <- dunnTest(Value ~ factor(Depth), data = df, method = "bh")
  pvals <- dunn_res$res$P.adj
  names(pvals) <- dunn_res$res$Comparison
  letters <- multcompLetters(pvals)$Letters
  depth_levels <- sort(unique(df$Depth))
  label_map <- setNames(letters[1:length(depth_levels)], depth_levels)
  df %>%
    group_by(Depth) %>%
    summarise(ypos = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.5) %>%
    mutate(label = label_map[as.character(Depth)],
           Metric = unique(df$Metric)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(label), !is.na(ypos))
}

# Compute annotations for all metrics
annot_all <- alpha_long %>%
  group_by(Metric) %>%
  group_split() %>%
  lapply(get_significance_letters) %>%
  bind_rows();annot_all

p <- ggplot(alpha_long, aes(x = factor(Depth), y = Value)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = factor(Depth))) +   # Depth stays numeric for fill
  geom_text(data = annot_all, aes(x = factor(Depth), y = ypos, label = label),
            color = "black", size = 4) +
  facet_wrap(~ Metric, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = my_palette) +
      labs(
    x = "Sequencing Depth",
    y = "Alpha Diversity",
    title = "Alpha Diversity Metrics Across Sequencing Depths"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

ggsave(
  "alpha_diversity_plot.tiff",
  plot = p,
  width = 4,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)


# Print lost sample summary
print(lost_samples)

# Print lost sample names per depth
for (depth in names(lost_sample_names)) {
  cat("\nDepth:", depth, "\nLost Samples:", paste(lost_sample_names[[depth]], collapse = ", "), "\n")
}
```

```{r pj2-u8, eval = FALSE}
load("phyloseq-objects/ps2.RData")
# --------------------------------------------------
# 1. Normalize and Prepare Data for Plotting
```
